<div class="col-sm order-1">
      <h2 class="chapter_title">CHAPTER 609. CRIMINAL CODE</h2>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.001"><b>609.001</b> MS 2006 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.001">15.001</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">GENERAL PRINCIPLES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.01">
        <h1 class="shn">609.01 NAME AND CONSTRUCTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.01.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Purposes.</span></h2>
          <p>This chapter may be cited as the Criminal Code of 1963. Its provisions shall be construed according to the fair import of its terms, to promote justice, and to effect its purposes which are declared to be:</p>
          <p>(1) to protect the public safety and welfare by preventing the commission of crime through the deterring effect of the sentences authorized, the rehabilitation of those convicted, and their confinement when the public safety and interest requires; and</p>
          <p>(2) to protect the individual against the misuse of the criminal law by fairly defining the acts and omissions prohibited, authorizing sentences reasonably related to the conduct and character of the convicted person, and prescribing fair and reasonable postconviction procedures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.01.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/216/#laws.1.76.0">1983 c 216 art 1 s 76</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.01.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.01</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.015">
        <h1 class="shn">609.015 SCOPE AND EFFECT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.015.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Common law crimes abolished.</span></h2>
          <p>Common law crimes are abolished and no act or omission is a crime unless made so by this chapter or by other applicable statute, but this does not prevent the use of common law rules in the construction or interpretation of the provisions of this chapter or other statute. Crimes committed prior to September 1, 1963, are not affected thereby.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.015.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless expressly stated otherwise, or the context otherwise requires, the provisions of this chapter also apply to crimes created by statute other than in this chapter.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.015.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.015</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.02">
        <h1 class="shn">609.02 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>"Crime" means conduct which is prohibited by statute and for which the actor may be sentenced to imprisonment, with or without a fine.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>"Felony" means a crime for which a sentence of imprisonment for one year or more may be imposed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/194/#laws.0.11.0">1999 c 194 s 11</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Misdemeanor" means a crime for which a sentence of not more than 90 days or a fine of not more than $1,000, or both, may be imposed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Gross misdemeanor" means any crime which is not a felony or misdemeanor. The maximum fine which may be imposed for a gross misdemeanor is $3,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Petty misdemeanor" means a petty offense which is prohibited by statute, which does not constitute a crime and for which a sentence of a fine of not more than $300 may be imposed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Conviction.</span></h2>
          <p>"Conviction" means any of the following accepted and recorded by the court:</p>
          <p>(1) a plea of guilty; or</p>
          <p>(2) a verdict of guilty by a jury or a finding of guilty by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Dangerous weapon.</span></h2>
          <p>"Dangerous weapon" means any firearm, whether loaded or unloaded, or any device designed as a weapon and capable of producing death or great bodily harm, any combustible or flammable liquid or other device or instrumentality that, in the manner it is used or intended to be used, is calculated or likely to produce death or great bodily harm, or any fire that is used to produce death or great bodily harm.</p>
          <p>As used in this subdivision, "flammable liquid" means any liquid having a flash point below 100 degrees Fahrenheit and having a vapor pressure not exceeding 40 pounds per square inch (absolute) at 100 degrees Fahrenheit but does not include intoxicating liquor as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.101">340A.101</a>. As used in this subdivision, "combustible liquid" is a liquid having a flash point at or above 100 degrees Fahrenheit.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>"Bodily harm" means physical pain or injury, illness, or any impairment of physical condition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Substantial bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>"Substantial bodily harm" means bodily injury which involves a temporary but substantial disfigurement, or which causes a temporary but substantial loss or impairment of the function of any bodily member or organ, or which causes a fracture of any bodily member.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Great bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>"Great bodily harm" means bodily injury which creates a high probability of death, or which causes serious permanent disfigurement, or which causes a permanent or protracted loss or impairment of the function of any bodily member or organ or other serious bodily harm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Mental state.</span></h2>
          <p>(1) When criminal intent is an element of a crime in this chapter, such intent is indicated by the term "intentionally," the phrase "with intent to," the phrase "with intent that," or some form of the verbs "know" or "believe."</p>
          <p>(2) "Know" requires only that the actor believes that the specified fact exists.</p>
          <p>(3) "Intentionally" means that the actor either has a purpose to do the thing or cause the result specified or believes that the act performed by the actor, if successful, will cause that result. In addition, except as provided in clause (6), the actor must have knowledge of those facts which are necessary to make the actor's conduct criminal and which are set forth after the word "intentionally."</p>
          <p>(4) "With intent to" or "with intent that" means that the actor either has a purpose to do the thing or cause the result specified or believes that the act, if successful, will cause that result.</p>
          <p>(5) Criminal intent does not require proof of knowledge of the existence or constitutionality of the statute under which the actor is prosecuted or the scope or meaning of the terms used in that statute.</p>
          <p>(6) Criminal intent does not require proof of knowledge of the age of a minor even though age is a material element in the crime in question.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Assault.</span></h2>
          <p>"Assault" is:</p>
          <p>(1) an act done with intent to cause fear in another of immediate bodily harm or death; or</p>
          <p>(2) the intentional infliction of or attempt to inflict bodily harm upon another.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Second or subsequent violation or offense.</span></h2>
          <p>"Second or subsequent violation" or "second or subsequent offense" means that prior to the commission of the violation or offense, the actor has been adjudicated guilty of a specified similar violation or offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.34.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.34.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/263/#laws.0.4.0">2014 c 263 s 4</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Probation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Probation" means a court-ordered sanction imposed upon an offender for a period of supervision no greater than that set by statute. It is imposed as an alternative to confinement or in conjunction with confinement or intermediate sanctions. The purpose of probation is to deter further criminal behavior, punish the offender, help provide reparation to crime victims and their communities, and provide offenders with opportunities for rehabilitation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Qualified domestic violence-related offense.</span></h2>

<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a> (first-degree murder); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a> (second-degree murder); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a>, paragraph (a) (third-degree murder); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a>, clauses (1), (2), and (5) (first-degree manslaughter); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.205">609.205</a>, clauses (1) and (5) (second-degree manslaughter); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a> (first-degree assault); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222 </a>(second-degree assault); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a> (third-degree assault); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a> (fourth-degree assault); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224 </a>(fifth-degree assault); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a> (domestic assault); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2245">609.2245</a> (female genital mutilation); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2247">609.2247</a> (domestic assault by strangulation); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.25">609.25</a> (kidnapping); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255">609.255</a> (false imprisonment); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> (first-degree criminal sexual conduct); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a> (second-degree criminal sexual conduct); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a> (third-degree criminal sexual conduct); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345 </a>(fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a> (sexual extortion); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.377">609.377 </a>(malicious punishment of a child); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a>, clause (c) (burglary in the first degree); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a> (terroristic threats); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.748#stat.609.748.6">609.748, subdivision 6 </a>(violation of harassment restraining order); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749">609.749</a> (harassment or stalking); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.78">609.78</a>, subdivision 2 (interference with an emergency call); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.261">617.261</a> (nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images); and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.75">629.75</a> (violation of domestic abuse no contact order); and similar laws of other states, the United States, the District of Columbia, tribal lands, and United States territories.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Ammunition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Ammunition" means ammunition or cartridge cases, primers, bullets, or propellent powder designed for use in any firearm. Ammunition does not include ornaments, curiosities, or souvenirs constructed from or resembling ammunition or ammunition components that are not operable as ammunition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.02.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Conditional release.</span></h2>
          <p>"Conditional release" means a court-ordered mandatory term of community supervision as prescribed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.276#stat.169A.276.1">169A.276, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (d) (first-degree DWI); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.166#stat.243.166.5a">243.166, subdivision 5a</a> (violating predatory offender registration requirements); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231#stat.609.2231.3a">609.2231, subdivision 3a</a>, paragraph (d) (assault on secure treatment facility staff); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455, subdivisions 6</a> and 7 (criminal sexual conduct); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.246#stat.617.246.7">617.246, subdivision 7 </a>(use of minors in sexual performances); and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.247#stat.617.247.9">617.247, subdivision 9</a> (possession of child pornography). Conditional release is in addition to any applicable supervised release term.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
