      <div class="section" id="stat.609.025">
        <h1 class="shn">609.025 JURISDICTION OF STATE.</h1>
        <p>A person may be convicted and sentenced under the law of this state if the person:</p>
        <p>(1) commits an offense in whole or in part within this state; or</p>
        <p>(2) being without the state, causes, aids or abets another to commit a crime within the state; or</p>
        <p>(3) being without the state, intentionally causes a result within the state prohibited by the criminal laws of this state.</p>
        <p>It is not a defense that the defendant's conduct is also a criminal offense under the laws of another state or of the United States or of another country.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.025.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.025; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.44.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 44</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.03">
        <h1 class="shn">609.03 PUNISHMENT WHEN NOT OTHERWISE FIXED.</h1>
        <p>If a person is convicted of a crime for which no punishment is otherwise provided the person may be sentenced as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) If the crime is a felony, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; or</p>
        <p>(2) If the crime is a gross misdemeanor, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
        <p>(3) If the crime is a misdemeanor, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both; or</p>
        <p>(4) If the crime is other than a misdemeanor and a fine is imposed but the amount is not specified, to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or to imprisonment for a specified term of not more than six months if the fine is not paid.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.03.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.03; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/735/#laws.0.4.0">1969 c 735 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.3.0">1977 c 355 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/331/#laws.0.6.0">1983 c 331 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.5.4.0">2000 c 488 art 5 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.5.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.031"><b>609.031</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/331/#laws.0.11.0">1983 c 331 s 11</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.032"><b>609.032</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/331/#laws.0.11.0">1983 c 331 s 11</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.033">
        <h1 class="shn">609.033 MAXIMUM PENALTIES; MISDEMEANORS.</h1>
        <p>Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $700 as a penalty for a misdemeanor shall, on or after August 1, 2000, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $1,000.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.033.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/331/#laws.0.7.0">1983 c 331 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.5.5.0">2000 c 488 art 5 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.0331">
        <h1 class="shn">609.0331 MAXIMUM PENALTIES; PETTY MISDEMEANORS.</h1>
        <p>A law of this state that provides, on or after August 1, 2000, for a maximum penalty of $200 for a petty misdemeanor is considered to provide for a maximum fine of $300.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.0331.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.4.0">1987 c 329 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/464/#laws.1.49.0">1992 c 464 art 1 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.13.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.5.6.0">2000 c 488 art 5 s 6</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.0332">
        <h1 class="shn">609.0332 MAXIMUM PENALTY; PETTY MISDEMEANOR ORDINANCE VIOLATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.0332.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Increased fine.</span></h2>
          <p>From August 1, 2000, if a state law or municipal charter sets a limit of $200 or less on the fines that a statutory or home rule charter city, town, county, or other political subdivision may prescribe for an ordinance violation that is defined as a petty misdemeanor, that law or charter is considered to provide that the political subdivision has the power to prescribe a maximum fine of $300 for the petty misdemeanor violation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.0332.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.69.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 69</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.0332.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.5.0">1987 c 329 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/199/#laws.2.1.0">1991 c 199 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.14.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.5.7.0">2000 c 488 art 5 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.034">
        <h1 class="shn">609.034 MAXIMUM PENALTY; ORDINANCE VIOLATIONS.</h1>
        <p>Any law of this state or municipal charter which limits the power of any statutory or home rule charter city, town, county, or other political subdivision to prescribe a maximum fine of $700 or less for an ordinance shall on or after August 1, 2000, be deemed to provide that the statutory or home rule charter city, town, county, or other political subdivision has the power to prescribe a maximum fine of $1,000.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.034.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/331/#laws.0.8.0">1983 c 331 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.5.8.0">2000 c 488 art 5 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.0341">
        <h1 class="shn">609.0341 MAXIMUM FINES FOR GROSS MISDEMEANORS; FELONIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.0341.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanors.</span></h2>
          <p>Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $1,000 or for a maximum sentence of imprisonment of one year or which is defined as a gross misdemeanor shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $3,000 and for a maximum sentence of imprisonment of 364 days.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.0341.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felonies.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $2,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $4,000.</p>
          <p>(b) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $3,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $5,000.</p>
          <p>(c) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $5,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $10,000.</p>
          <p>(d) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $7,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $14,000.</p>
          <p>(e) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $10,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $20,000.</p>
          <p>(f) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $15,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $30,000.</p>
          <p>(g) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $20,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $35,000.</p>
          <p>(h) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $25,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $40,000.</p>
          <p>(i) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $30,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $45,000.</p>
          <p>(j) Any law of this state which provides for a maximum fine of $40,000 shall, on or after August 1, 1983, be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $50,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.0341.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.10.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 10</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.0341.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/331/#laws.0.9.0">1983 c 331 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.13.19.0">1993 c 326 art 13 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.0342">
        <h1 class="shn">609.0342 MAXIMUM PUNISHMENT FOR GROSS MISDEMEANORS.</h1>
        <p>(a) Any law of this state that provides for a maximum sentence of imprisonment of one year or is defined as a gross misdemeanor shall be deemed to provide for a maximum fine of $3,000 and a maximum sentence of imprisonment of 364 days.</p>
        <p>(b) Any sentence of imprisonment for one year or 365 days imposed or executed before July 1, 2023, shall be deemed to be a sentence of imprisonment for 364 days. A court may at any time correct or reduce such a sentence pursuant to rule <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/27.03#stat.27.03.9">27.03, subdivision 9</a>, of the Rules of Criminal Procedure and shall issue a corrected sentencing order upon motion of any eligible defendant.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.0342.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.6.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.035">
        <h1 class="shn">609.035 CRIME PUNISHABLE UNDER DIFFERENT PROVISIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.035.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Conduct; multiple crimes; chargeable for one offense.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivisions 2, 3, 4, and 5, and in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114#stat.609.2114.3">609.2114, subdivision 3</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.251">609.251</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2691">609.2691</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.486">609.486</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.494">609.494</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.585">609.585</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.856">609.856</a>, and Minnesota Statutes 2012, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.21#stat.609.21.1b">609.21, subdivision 1b</a>, if a person's conduct constitutes more than one offense under the laws of this state, the person may be punished for only one of the offenses and a conviction or acquittal of any one of them is a bar to prosecution for any other of them. All the offenses, if prosecuted, shall be included in one prosecution which shall be stated in separate counts.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.035.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Consecutive sentences.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a person is being sentenced for a violation of a provision listed in paragraph (e), the court may sentence the person to a consecutive term of imprisonment for a violation of any other provision listed in paragraph (e), notwithstanding the fact that the offenses arose out of the same course of conduct, subject to the limitation on consecutive sentences contained in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.15#stat.609.15.2">609.15, subdivision 2</a>, and except as provided in paragraphs (b), (c), and (f).</p>
          <p>(b) When a person is being sentenced for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.09">171.09</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.20">171.20</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.24">171.24</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.30">171.30</a>, the court may not impose a consecutive sentence for another violation of a provision in chapter 171.</p>
          <p>(c) When a person is being sentenced for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.791">169.791</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.797">169.797</a>, the court may not impose a consecutive sentence for another violation of a provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.79">169.79</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.7995">169.7995</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) This subdivision does not limit the authority of the court to impose consecutive sentences for crimes arising on different dates or to impose a consecutive sentence when a person is being sentenced for a crime and is also in violation of the conditions of a stayed or otherwise deferred sentence under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) This subdivision applies to misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor violations of the following if the offender has two or more prior impaired driving convictions as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03">169A.03</a> within the past ten years:</p>
          <p>(1) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20#stat.169A.20.1">169A.20, subdivision 1</a>, driving while impaired;</p>
          <p>(2) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20#stat.169A.20.2">169A.20, subdivision 2</a>, test refusal;</p>
          <p>(3) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.791">169.791</a>, failure to provide proof of insurance;</p>
          <p>(4) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.797">169.797</a>, failure to provide vehicle insurance;</p>
          <p>(5) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.09">171.09</a>, violation of condition of restricted license;</p>
          <p>(6) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.20#stat.171.20.2">171.20, subdivision 2</a>, operation after revocation, suspension, cancellation, or disqualification;</p>
          <p>(7) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.24">171.24</a>, driving without valid license; and</p>
          <p>(8) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.30">171.30</a>, violation of condition of limited license.</p>
          <p>(f) When a court is sentencing an offender for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a> and a violation of an offense listed in paragraph (e), and the offender has five or more qualified prior impaired driving incidents, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03">169A.03</a>, within the past ten years, the court shall sentence the offender to serve consecutive sentences for the offenses, notwithstanding the fact that the offenses arose out of the same course of conduct.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.035.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Exception; firearms offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.165">609.165</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713#stat.624.713.1">624.713, subdivision 1</a>, clause (2), is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.035.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Exception; arson offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction of a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.563">609.563</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5641">609.5641</a> is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct when the defendant is shown to have violated sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.563">609.563</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5641">609.5641</a> for the purpose of concealing any other crime.</p>
          <p>For purposes of the Sentencing Guidelines, a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.563">609.563</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5641">609.5641</a> is a crime against the person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.035.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exception; fleeing a peace officer.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 1, a prosecution or conviction for violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a> is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct. If an offender is punished for more than one crime as authorized by this subdivision and the court imposes consecutive sentences for the crimes, the consecutive sentences are not a departure from the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.035.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Exception; criminal sexual conduct offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 1, a prosecution or conviction for committing a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a> with force or violence is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct. If an offender is punished for more than one crime as authorized by this subdivision and the court imposes consecutive sentences for the crimes, the consecutive sentences are not a departure from the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.035.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.035; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/139/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 139 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.1.0">1986 c 388 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/111/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 111 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.13.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/615/#laws.0.23.0">1994 c 615 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.4.2.0">1996 c 408 art 4 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.8.28.0">1997 c 239 art 8 s 28</a>,29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/194/#laws.0.6.0">1999 c 194 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/216/#laws.3.4.0">1999 c 216 art 3 s 4</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/311/#laws.4.1.0">2000 c 311 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/478/#laws.2.4.0">2000 c 478 art 2 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.12.16.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 12 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.3.14.0">2007 c 54 art 3 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.2.37.0">2009 c 83 art 2 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.9.0">2014 c 180 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.187.0">2023 c 25 s 187</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE:</b> Subdivision 2, paragraph (f), was found unconstitutional in <i>State v. Blooflat</i>, 671 N.W.2d 591 (Minn. Ct. App. 2003).</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.04">
        <h1 class="shn">609.04 CONVICTION OF LESSER OFFENSE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.04.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Lesser offense prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon prosecution for a crime, the actor may be convicted of either the crime charged or an included offense, but not both. An included offense may be any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a lesser degree of the same crime; or</p>
          <p>(2) an attempt to commit the crime charged; or</p>
          <p>(3) an attempt to commit a lesser degree of the same crime; or</p>
          <p>(4) a crime necessarily proved if the crime charged were proved; or</p>
          <p>(5) a petty misdemeanor necessarily proved if the misdemeanor charge were proved.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.04.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Conviction; bar to prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>A conviction or acquittal of a crime is a bar to further prosecution of any included offense, or other degree of the same crime.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.04.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.04; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/1/27/#laws.0.45.0">Ex1971 c 27 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.041">
        <h1 class="shn">609.041 PROOF OF PRIOR CONVICTIONS.</h1>
        <p>In a criminal prosecution in which the degree of the crime or the penalty for the crime depends, in whole or in part, on proof of the existence of a prior conviction, if the defendant contests the existence of or factual basis for a prior conviction, proof of it is established by competent and reliable evidence, including a certified court record of the conviction.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.041.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/520/#laws.0.2.0">1988 c 520 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.045">
        <h1 class="shn">609.045 FOREIGN CONVICTION OR ACQUITTAL.</h1>
        <p>If an act or omission in this state constitutes a crime under both the laws of this state and the laws of another jurisdiction, a conviction or acquittal of the crime in the other jurisdiction shall not bar prosecution for the crime in this state unless the elements of both law and fact are identical.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.045.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.045; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/152/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 152 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.05">
        <h1 class="shn">609.05 LIABILITY FOR CRIMES OF ANOTHER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.05.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Aiding, abetting; liability.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is criminally liable for a crime committed by another if the person intentionally aids, advises, hires, counsels, or conspires with or otherwise procures the other to commit the crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.05.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Expansive liability.</span></h2>
          <p>A person liable under subdivision 1 is also liable for any other crime committed in pursuance of the intended crime if reasonably foreseeable by the person as a probable consequence of committing or attempting to commit the crime intended.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.05.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Exception.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person may not be held criminally liable for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, paragraph (a), clause (3), for a death caused by another unless the person intentionally aided, advised, hired, counseled, or conspired with or otherwise procured the other with the intent to cause the death of a human being.</p>
          <p>(b) A person may not be held criminally liable for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>, subdivision 2, clause (1), for a death caused by another unless the person was a major participant in the underlying felony and acted with extreme indifference to human life.</p>
          <p>(c) As used in this subdivision, "major participant" means a person who:</p>
          <p>(1) used a deadly weapon during the commission of the underlying felony or provided a deadly weapon to another participant where it was reasonably foreseeable that the weapon would be used in the underlying felony;</p>
          <p>(2) caused substantial bodily harm to another during the commission of the underlying felony;</p>
          <p>(3) coerced or hired a participant to undertake actions in furtherance of the underlying felony that proximately caused the death, and where it was reasonably foreseeable that such actions would cause death or great bodily harm; or</p>
          <p>(4) impeded another person from preventing the death either by physical action or by threat of physical action where it was reasonably foreseeable that death or great bodily harm would result.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.05.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Abandonment of criminal purpose.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally aids, advises, hires, counsels, or conspires with or otherwise procures another to commit a crime and thereafter abandons that purpose and makes a reasonable effort to prevent the commission of the crime prior to its commission is not liable if the crime is thereafter committed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.05.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Circumstances of conviction.</span></h2>
          <p>A person liable under this section may be charged with and convicted of the crime although the person who directly committed it has not been convicted, or has been convicted of some other degree of the crime or of some other crime based on the same act, or if the person is a juvenile who has not been found delinquent for the act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.05.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, a crime also includes an act committed by a juvenile that would be a crime if committed by an adult.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.05.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.05; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/279/#laws.0.22.0">1991 c 279 s 22</a>,23; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.3.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.055">
        <h1 class="shn">609.055 CAPABILITY OF CHILDREN TO COMMIT CRIME.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.055.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General rule.</span></h2>
          <p>Children under the age of 14 years are incapable of committing crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.055.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Adult prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b), children of the age of 14 years or over but under 18 years may be prosecuted for a felony offense if the alleged violation is duly certified for prosecution under the laws and court procedures controlling adult criminal violations or may be designated an extended jurisdiction juvenile in accordance with the provisions of chapter 260B. A child who is 16 years of age or older but under 18 years of age is capable of committing a crime and may be prosecuted for a felony if:</p>
          <p>(1) the child has been previously certified on a felony charge pursuant to a hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.125#stat.260B.125.2">260B.125, subdivision 2</a>, or pursuant to the waiver of the right to such a hearing, or prosecuted pursuant to this subdivision; and</p>
          <p>(2) the child was convicted of the felony offense or offenses for which the child was prosecuted or of a lesser included felony offense.</p>
          <p>(b) A child who is alleged to have committed murder in the first degree after becoming 16 years of age is capable of committing a crime and may be prosecuted for the felony. This paragraph does not apply to a child alleged to have committed attempted murder in the first degree after becoming 16 years of age.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.055.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.055; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.7.12.0">1992 c 571 art 7 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/576/#laws.0.45.0">1994 c 576 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.3.47.0">1995 c 226 art 3 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/139/#laws.4.2.0">1999 c 139 art 4 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.06">
        <h1 class="shn">609.06 AUTHORIZED USE OF FORCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.06.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">When authorized.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as otherwise provided in subdivisions 2 to 4, reasonable force may be used upon or toward the person of another without the other's consent when the following circumstances exist or the actor reasonably believes them to exist:</p>
          <p>(1) when used by a public officer or one assisting a public officer under the public officer's direction:</p>
          <p>(i) in effecting a lawful arrest; or</p>
          <p>(ii) in the execution of legal process; or</p>
          <p>(iii) in enforcing an order of the court; or</p>
          <p>(iv) in executing any other duty imposed upon the public officer by law; or</p>
          <p>(2) when used by a person not a public officer in arresting another in the cases and in the manner provided by law and delivering the other to an officer competent to receive the other into custody; or</p>
          <p>(3) when used by any person in resisting or aiding another to resist an offense against the person; or</p>
          <p>(4) when used by any person in lawful possession of real or personal property, or by another assisting the person in lawful possession, in resisting a trespass upon or other unlawful interference with such property; or</p>
          <p>(5) when used by any person to prevent the escape, or to retake following the escape, of a person lawfully held on a charge or conviction of a crime; or</p>
          <p>(6) when used by a parent, guardian, or other lawful custodian of a child, in the exercise of lawful authority, to restrain or correct such child; or</p>
          <p>(7) when used by a teacher, school principal, school employee, school bus driver, or other agent of a district in the exercise of lawful authority, to restrain a child or pupil to prevent bodily harm or death to the child, pupil, or another; or</p>
          <p>(8) when used by a common carrier in expelling a passenger who refuses to obey a lawful requirement for the conduct of passengers and reasonable care is exercised with regard to the passenger's personal safety; or</p>
          <p>(9) when used to restrain a person with a mental illness or a person with a developmental disability from self-injury or injury to another or when used by one with authority to do so to compel compliance with reasonable requirements for the person's control, conduct, or treatment; or</p>
          <p>(10) when used by a public or private institution providing custody or treatment against one lawfully committed to it to compel compliance with reasonable requirements for the control, conduct, or treatment of the committed person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.06.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Deadly force used against peace officers.</span></h2>
          <p>Deadly force may not be used against peace officers who have announced their presence and are performing official duties at a location where a person is committing a crime or an act that would be a crime if committed by an adult.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.06.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Limitations on the use of certain restraints.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A peace officer may not use any of the following restraints unless section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.066">609.066</a> authorizes the use of deadly force to protect the peace officer or another from death or great bodily harm:</p>
          <p>(1) a choke hold;</p>
          <p>(2) tying all of a person's limbs together behind the person's back to render the person immobile; or</p>
          <p>(3) securing a person in any way that results in transporting the person face down in a vehicle.</p>
          <p>(b) For the purposes of this subdivision, "choke hold" means a method by which a person applies sufficient pressure to a person to make breathing difficult or impossible, and includes but is not limited to any pressure to the neck, throat, or windpipe that may prevent or hinder breathing, or reduce intake of air. Choke hold also means applying pressure to a person's neck on either side of the windpipe, but not to the windpipe itself, to stop the flow of blood to the brain via the carotid arteries.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.06.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Use of force not authorized; reaction to victim's sexual orientation or gender identity.</span></h2>
          <p>Force may not be used against another based on the discovery of, knowledge about, or potential disclosure of the victim's actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.06.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.06; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.4.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.12.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/221/#laws.0.46.0">2002 c 221 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/59/#laws.3.16.0">2013 c 59 art 3 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/62/#laws.0.28.0">2013 c 62 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/2/1/#laws.0.7.0">2Sp2020 c 1 s 7</a>,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/78/#laws.0.7.0">2024 c 78 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.4.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 4</a>,5</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.065">
        <h1 class="shn">609.065 JUSTIFIABLE TAKING OF LIFE.</h1>
        <p>The intentional taking of the life of another is not authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.06">609.06</a>, except when necessary in resisting or preventing an offense which the actor reasonably believes exposes the actor or another to great bodily harm or death, or preventing the commission of a felony in the actor's place of abode.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.065.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.065; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/736/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 736 s 1</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.066">
        <h1 class="shn">609.066 AUTHORIZED USE OF DEADLY FORCE BY PEACE OFFICERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.066.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Deadly force defined.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, "deadly force" means force which the actor uses with the purpose of causing, or which the actor should reasonably know creates a substantial risk of causing, death or great bodily harm. The intentional discharge of a firearm, other than a firearm loaded with less lethal munitions and used by a peace officer within the scope of official duties, in the direction of another person, or at a vehicle in which another person is believed to be, constitutes deadly force. "Less lethal munitions" means projectiles which are designed to stun, temporarily incapacitate, or cause temporary discomfort to a person. "Peace officer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.066.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Legislative intent.</span></h2>
          <p>The legislature hereby finds and declares the following:</p>
          <p>(1) that the authority to use deadly force, conferred on peace officers by this section, is a critical responsibility that shall be exercised judiciously and with respect for human rights and dignity and for the sanctity of every human life. The legislature further finds and declares that every person has a right to be free from excessive use of force by officers acting under color of law;</p>
          <p>(2) as set forth below, it is the intent of the legislature that peace officers use deadly force only when necessary in defense of human life or to prevent great bodily harm. In determining whether deadly force is necessary, officers shall evaluate each situation in light of the particular circumstances of each case;</p>
          <p>(3) that the decision by a peace officer to use deadly force shall be evaluated from the perspective of a reasonable officer in the same situation, based on the totality of the circumstances known to or perceived by the officer at the time, rather than with the benefit of hindsight, and that the totality of the circumstances shall account for occasions when officers may be forced to make quick judgments about using deadly force; and</p>
          <p>(4) that peace officers should exercise special care when interacting with individuals with known physical, mental health, developmental, or intellectual disabilities as an individual's disability may affect the individual's ability to understand or comply with commands from peace officers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.066.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of deadly force.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.06">609.06</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.065">609.065</a>, the use of deadly force by a peace officer in the line of duty is justified only if an objectively reasonable officer would believe, based on the totality of the circumstances known to the officer at the time and without the benefit of hindsight, that such force is necessary:</p>
          <p>(1) to protect the peace officer or another from death or great bodily harm, provided that the threat:</p>
          <p>(i) can be articulated with specificity;</p>
          <p>(ii) is reasonably likely to occur absent action by the law enforcement officer; and</p>
          <p>(iii) must be addressed through the use of deadly force without unreasonable delay; or</p>
          <p>(2) to effect the arrest or capture, or prevent the escape, of a person whom the peace officer knows or has reasonable grounds to believe has committed or attempted to commit a felony and the officer reasonably believes that the person will cause death or great bodily harm to another person under the threat criteria in clause (1), items (i) to (iii), unless immediately apprehended.</p>
          <p>(b) A peace officer shall not use deadly force against a person based on the danger the person poses to self if an objectively reasonable officer would believe, based on the totality of the circumstances known to the officer at the time and without the benefit of hindsight, that the person does not pose a threat of death or great bodily harm to the peace officer or to another under the threat criteria in paragraph (a), clause (1), items (i) to (iii).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.066.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">No defense.</span></h2>
          <p>This section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.06">609.06</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.065">609.065</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.33">629.33</a> may not be used as a defense in a civil action brought by an innocent third party.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.066.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/736/#laws.0.2.0">1978 c 736 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/127/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 127 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/2/1/#laws.0.9.0">2Sp2020 c 1 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.10.8.0">2023 c 52 art 10 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.075">
        <h1 class="shn">609.075 DEFENSES; INTOXICATION, REACTION TO VICTIM'S SEXUAL ORIENTATION OR GENDER IDENTITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.075.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Intoxication as defense.</span></h2>
          <p>An act committed while in a state of voluntary intoxication is not less criminal by reason thereof, but when a particular intent or other state of mind is a necessary element to constitute a particular crime, the fact of intoxication may be taken into consideration in determining such intent or state of mind.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.075.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Reaction to victim's sexual orientation or gender identity.</span></h2>
          <p>It is not a defense to a crime that the defendant acted based on the discovery of, knowledge about, or potential disclosure of the victim's actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.075.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.075; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.6.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 6</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.08">
        <h1 class="shn">609.08 DURESS.</h1>
        <p>Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a>, clause (3), when any crime is committed or participated in by two or more persons, any one of whom participates only under compulsion by another engaged therein, who by threats creates a reasonable apprehension in the mind of such participator that in case of refusal that participator is liable to instant death, such threats and apprehension constitute duress which will excuse such participator from criminal liability.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.08.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.08; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.085">
        <h1 class="shn">609.085 SENDING WRITTEN COMMUNICATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.085.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition of offense.</span></h2>
          <p>When the sending of a letter or other written communication is made an offense, the offense is complete upon deposit of the letter or communication in any official depository of mail or given to another for the purpose of delivery to the receiver.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.085.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>The offense is committed in both the county in which the letter is so deposited or given and the county in which it is received by the person for whom it is intended.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.085.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.085</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.09">
        <h1 class="shn">609.09 COMPELLING TESTIMONY; IMMUNITY FROM PROSECUTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.09.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Conditions of immunity.</span></h2>
          <p>In any criminal proceeding, including a grand jury proceeding, paternity proceeding, or proceeding in juvenile court, if it appears a person may be entitled to refuse to answer a question or produce evidence of any other kind on the ground that the person may be incriminated thereby, and if the prosecuting attorney, in writing, requests the chief judge of the district or a judge of the court in which the proceeding is pending to order that person to answer the question or produce the evidence, the judge, after notice to the witness and hearing, shall so order if the judge finds that to do so would not be contrary to the public interest and would not be likely to expose the witness to prosecution in another state or in the federal courts.</p>
          <p>After complying, and if, but for this section, the witness would have been privileged to withhold the answer given or the evidence produced by the witness, no testimony or other information compelled under the order, or any information directly or indirectly derived from such testimony or other information may be used against the witness in any criminal case, but the witness may be prosecuted or subjected to penalty or forfeiture for any perjury, false swearing or contempt committed in answering, or in failing to answer, or in producing, or failing to produce, evidence in accordance with the order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.09.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Testimony required; no use of testimony for prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>In every case not provided for in subdivision 1 and in which it is provided by law that a witness shall not be excused from giving testimony tending to be self-incriminating, no person shall be excused from testifying or producing any papers or documents on the ground that doing so may tend to criminate the person or subject the person to a penalty or forfeiture; but no testimony or other information directly or indirectly derived from such testimony or other information may be used against the witness in any criminal case, except for perjury committed in such testimony.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.09.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.09; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/661/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 661 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/293/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 293 s 1</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.092">
        <h1 class="shn">609.092 JUVENILE PETTY OFFENDERS; USE OF RESTORATIVE JUSTICE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">First-time juvenile petty offenders; applicability; procedure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) This subdivision applies to a child alleged to be a juvenile petty offender who:</p>
          <p>(1) has not been previously adjudicated delinquent or as a petty offender;</p>
          <p>(2) has not previously participated in or completed a diversion program for an offense;</p>
          <p>(3) has not previously been placed on probation without an adjudication for an offense or received a continuance under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.198#stat.260B.198.7">260B.198, subdivision 7</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) agrees to successfully complete a restorative justice program under this section.</p>
          <p>(b) Subject to subdivision 6, the prosecutor shall refer a child described in paragraph (a) to a restorative justice program or provider that has been included on the approved provider list described in subdivision 4. The program or provider shall arrange an appropriate outcome for the matter using restorative justice concepts. The program or provider shall involve the victim of the offense in the proceedings. If the victim is unwilling or unable to proceed, or if there is no identifiable victim, the program or provider shall ensure that someone serves as a proxy for the victim. The program or provider and child, along with other participants, shall agree in writing to an appropriate sanction for the child. The sanction may include any of the dispositions authorized in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.235">260B.235</a>, if appropriate, along with any other sanctions agreed to.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Failure to comply.</span></h2>
          <p>If a person fails to comply with the settlement agreement, the person shall be referred back to the court for further proceedings.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Dismissal of charge.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon the successful completion by a person of the sanctions agreed to in the settlement agreement, the program or provider shall notify the court and the court shall dismiss the charge against the person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Approved list.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecutor shall maintain a list of approved restorative justice programs and providers to which persons may be referred under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Preference for culturally specific programs.</span></h2>
          <p>If a restorative justice program or provider that is tailored in a more culturally specific manner to the person is on the list of approved providers under subdivision 4, and the prosecutor is referring the person to a restorative justice program or provider under this section, the prosecutor shall refer the person to the more appropriate program or provider.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Exceptions; availability of programs; diversion alternatives; domestic abuse.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies only in jurisdictions where suitable restorative justice programs and providers are available and are able to accept the referral. This section does not apply if a prosecutor has determined that a nonrestorative justice diversion program is more appropriate for the person. In addition, this section does not apply to cases involving domestic violence or domestic assault.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.092.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "restorative justice" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.775">611A.775</a>. The term also includes Native American sentencing circles.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.092.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.2.38.0">2009 c 83 art 2 s 38</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.093"><b>609.093</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.3.48.0">2013 c 108 art 3 s 48</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SENTENCES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.095">
        <h1 class="shn">609.095 LIMITS OF SENTENCES.</h1>
        <p>(a) The legislature has the exclusive authority to define crimes and offenses and the range of the sentences or punishments for their violation. No other or different sentence or punishment shall be imposed for the commission of a crime than is authorized by this chapter or other applicable law.</p>
        <p>(b) Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.18">152.18</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.1056">609.1056</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.375">609.375</a>, or upon agreement of the parties, a court may not refuse to adjudicate the guilt of a defendant who tenders a guilty plea in accordance with Minnesota Rules of Criminal Procedure, rule <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/court_rules/cr/id/15/">15</a>, or who has been found guilty by a court or jury following a trial. A decision by the court to issue a stay of adjudication under this paragraph for a charge of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.166">243.166</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451#stat.609.3451.3">609.3451, subdivision 3</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, must be justified in writing and on the record.</p>
        <p>(c) Paragraph (b) does not supersede Minnesota Rules of Criminal Procedure, rule <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/court_rules/cr/id/26/#26.04">26.04</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.095.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.095; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.1.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/158/#laws.0.6.0">2001 c 158 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/5/#laws.4.1.0">1Sp2019 c 5 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/12/#laws.3.12.0">1Sp2021 c 12 art 3 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.10">
        <h1 class="shn">609.10 SENTENCES AVAILABLE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.10.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Sentences available.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon conviction of a felony and compliance with the other provisions of this chapter the court, if it imposes sentence, may sentence the defendant to the extent authorized by law as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to life imprisonment; or</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for a fixed term of years set by the court; or</p>
          <p>(3) to both imprisonment for a fixed term of years and payment of a fine; or</p>
          <p>(4) to payment of a fine without imprisonment or as an intermediate sanction on a stayed sentence; or</p>
          <p>(5) to payment of court-ordered restitution in addition to either imprisonment or payment of a fine, or both; or</p>
          <p>(6) to payment of a local correctional fee as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.102">609.102</a> in addition to any other sentence imposed by the court.</p>
          <p>(b) If the court imposes a fine or orders restitution under paragraph (a), payment is due on the date imposed unless the court otherwise establishes a due date or a payment plan.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.10.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, "restitution" includes:</p>
          <p>(1) payment of compensation to the victim or the victim's family; and</p>
          <p>(2) if the victim is deceased or already has been fully compensated, payment of money to a victim assistance program or other program directed by the court.</p>
          <p>"Restitution" includes payment of compensation to a government entity that incurs loss as a direct result of a crime.</p>
          <p>(b) When the defendant does not pay the entire amount of court-ordered restitution and the fine at the same time, the court may order that all restitution shall be paid before the fine is paid.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.10.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/723/#laws.1.13.0">1978 c 723 art 1 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/610/#laws.0.1.0">1984 c 610 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.11.12.0">1992 c 571 art 11 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.10.0">1995 c 244 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.7.2.0">1996 c 408 art 7 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.7.16.0">1997 c 239 art 7 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.2.39.0">2009 c 83 art 2 s 39</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.101">
        <h1 class="shn">609.101 SURCHARGE ON FINES, ASSESSMENTS; MINIMUM FINES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.101.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.8.26.0">1998 c 367 art 8 s 26</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.101.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Minimum fines.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any other law, when a court sentences a person convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.267">609.267</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2671">609.2671</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2672">609.2672</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, it must impose a fine of not less than 30 percent of the maximum fine authorized by law nor more than the maximum fine authorized by law.</p>
          <p>The court shall collect the portion of the fine mandated by this subdivision and forward 70 percent of it to a local victim assistance program that provides services locally in the county in which the crime was committed. The court shall forward the remaining 30 percent to the commissioner of management and budget to be credited to the general fund. If more than one victim assistance program serves the county in which the crime was committed, the court may designate on a case-by-case basis which program will receive the fine proceeds, giving consideration to the nature of the crime committed, the types of victims served by the program, and the funding needs of the program. If no victim assistance program serves that county, the court shall forward 100 percent of the fine proceeds to the commissioner of management and budget to be credited to the general fund. Fine proceeds received by a local victim assistance program must be used to provide direct services to crime victims.</p>
          <p>The minimum fine required by this subdivision is in addition to the surcharge or assessment required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/357.021#stat.357.021.6">357.021, subdivision 6</a>, and is in addition to any sentence of imprisonment or restitution imposed or ordered by the court.</p>
          <p>As used in this subdivision, "victim assistance program" means victim witness programs within county attorney offices or any of the following programs: crime victim crisis centers, victim-witness programs, battered women shelters and nonshelter programs, and sexual assault programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.101.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Controlled substance offenses; minimum fines.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding any other law, when a court sentences a person convicted of a controlled substance crime under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.021">152.021</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.025">152.025</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.0262">152.0262</a>, it must impose a fine of not less than 30 percent of the maximum fine authorized by law nor more than the maximum fine authorized by law.</p>
          <p>(b) The minimum fine required by this subdivision is in addition to the surcharge or assessment required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/357.021#stat.357.021.6">357.021, subdivision 6</a>, and is in addition to any sentence of imprisonment or restitution imposed or ordered by the court.</p>
          <p>(c) The court shall collect the fine mandated by this subdivision and forward 70 percent of it to a local drug abuse prevention or intervention program existing or being implemented in the county in which the crime was committed. The court shall forward the remaining 30 percent to the commissioner of management and budget to be credited to the general fund. If more than one drug abuse prevention or intervention program serves the county in which the crime was committed, the court may designate on a case-by-case basis which program will receive the fine proceeds, giving consideration to the community in which the crime was committed, the funding needs of the program, the number of peace officers in each community certified to teach the program, and the number of children served by the program in each community. If no drug abuse prevention or intervention program serves communities in that county, the court shall forward 100 percent of the fine proceeds to the commissioner of management and budget to be credited to the general fund.</p>
          <p>(d) The minimum fines required by this subdivision shall be collected as are other fines. Fine proceeds received by a local drug abuse prevention or intervention program must be used to support that program, and may be used for salaries of program staff or peace officers certified to teach the program. The program must report receipt and use of money generated under this subdivision to the state court administrator by January 15 of each year. The state court administrator must make this information available upon request.</p>
          <p>(e) As used in this subdivision, "drug abuse prevention or intervention program" and "program" include:</p>
          <p>(1) the drug abuse resistance education program described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299A.33">299A.33</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a drug abuse education and prevention program that includes the following components:</p>
          <p>(i) instruction for students enrolled in kindergarten through grade six that is designed to teach students to recognize and resist pressures to experiment with controlled substances and alcohol;</p>
          <p>(ii) provisions for parental involvement;</p>
          <p>(iii) classroom instruction by uniformed law enforcement personnel;</p>
          <p>(iv) the use of positive student leaders to influence younger students not to use drugs; and</p>
          <p>(v) an emphasis on activity-oriented techniques designed to encourage student-generated responses to problem-solving situations; and</p>
          <p>(3) a juvenile court program that:</p>
          <p>(i) provides intervention strategies to reduce drug abuse and criminal behavior in juvenile offenders; and</p>
          <p>(ii) promotes local drug abuse prevention efforts within the community.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.101.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Minimum fines; other crimes.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any other law:</p>
          <p>(1) when a court sentences a person convicted of a felony that is not listed in subdivision 2 or 3, it must impose a fine of not less than 30 percent of the maximum fine authorized by law nor more than the maximum fine authorized by law; and</p>
          <p>(2) when a court sentences a person convicted of a gross misdemeanor or misdemeanor that is not listed in subdivision 2, it must impose a fine of not less than 30 percent of the maximum fine authorized by law nor more than the maximum fine authorized by law, unless the fine is set at a lower amount on a uniform fine schedule established by the Judicial Council in consultation with affected state and local agencies. This schedule shall be promulgated not later than September 1 of each year and shall become effective on January 1 of the next year unless the legislature, by law, provides otherwise.</p>
          <p>The minimum fine required by this subdivision is in addition to the surcharge or assessment required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/357.021#stat.357.021.6">357.021, subdivision 6</a>, and is in addition to any sentence of imprisonment or restitution imposed or ordered by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.101.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Waiver prohibited; reduction and installment payments.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The court may not waive payment of the minimum fine required by this section.</p>
          <p>(b) If the defendant qualifies for the services of a public defender or the court finds on the record that the convicted person is indigent or that immediate payment of the fine would create undue hardship for the convicted person or that person's immediate family, the court may reduce the amount of the minimum fine to not less than $50. Additionally, the court may permit the defendant to perform community work service in lieu of a fine.</p>
          <p>(c) The court also may authorize payment of the fine in installments.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.101.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/360/#laws.2.50.0">1981 c 360 art 2 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/262/#laws.1.6.0">1983 c 262 art 1 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/13/#laws.0.366.0">1Sp1985 c 13 s 366</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/442/#laws.0.15.0">1986 c 442 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/463/#laws.0.2.0">1986 c 463 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/1/#laws.8.15.0">1Sp1986 c 1 art 8 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/244/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 244 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/404/#laws.0.189.0">1987 c 404 s 189</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/264/#laws.0.2.0">1989 c 264 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/335/#laws.4.99.0">1989 c 335 art 4 s 99</a>; art 13 s 20-22; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.2.8.0">1995 c 226 art 2 s 8</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/305/#laws.1.119.0">1996 c 305 art 1 s 119</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.7.21.0">2005 c 136 art 7 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.5.50.0">2006 c 260 art 5 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/277/#laws.1.93.0">2008 c 277 art 1 s 93</a>;
