      <div class="section" id="stat.609.102">
        <h1 class="shn">609.102 CORRECTIONAL FEES; IMPOSITION BY COURT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.102.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, " correctional fee" means a fee for local correctional services established by a probation agency or the commissioner of corrections under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.18">244.18</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.102.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Imposing fee.</span></h2>
          <p>When a court places a person convicted of a crime under the supervision and control of a probation agency, the agency may collect a correctional fee based on the agency's fee schedule adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.18">244.18</a>, subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.102.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Imposing correctional fee.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person convicted of a crime is supervised by the commissioner of corrections, the commissioner may collect a correctional fee based on the commissioner's fee schedule adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.18">244.18</a>, subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.102.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/111/#laws.0.6.0">1999 c 111 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.102.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/111/#laws.0.6.0">1999 c 111 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.102.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.11.13.0">1992 c 571 art 11 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/111/#laws.0.4.0">1999 c 111 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/216/#laws.4.10.0">1999 c 216 art 4 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.4.13.0">2006 c 260 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.17.31.0">2023 c 52 art 17 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.103"><b>609.103</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/299/#laws.0.28.0">2008 c 299 s 28</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.104">
        <h1 class="shn">609.104 FINE AND SURCHARGE COLLECTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.104.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Failure to pay restitution or fine.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any portion of a fine, surcharge, court cost, restitution, or fee that the defendant fails to pay by the due date may be referred for collection under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/480.15#stat.480.15.10c">480.15, subdivision 10c</a>. If the defendant has agreed to a payment plan but fails to pay an installment when due, the entire amount remaining becomes due and payable and may be referred for collection under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/480.15#stat.480.15.10c">480.15, subdivision 10c</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The defendant may contest the referral for collection based on inability to pay by requesting a hearing no later than the due date. The defendant shall be notified in writing at sentencing that under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/480.15#stat.480.15.10c">480.15, subdivision 10c</a>, the court may refer the case for collection for nonpayment, and collection costs may be added to the amount due. The defendant shall also be notified in writing of the right to contest a referral for collection. The state court administrator shall develop the notice language.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.104.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fine and surcharge collection.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A defendant's obligation to pay court-ordered fines, surcharges, court costs, restitution, and fees shall survive after the due date for a period set by the Judicial Council.</p>
          <p>(b) Any change in the collection period established by the Judicial Council shall be effective on court-ordered fines, surcharges, court costs, restitution, and fees imposed on or after July 1, 2009.</p>
          <p>(c) The period relating to a defendant's obligation to pay restitution under paragraph (a) does not limit the victim's right to collect restitution through other means such as a civil judgment.</p>
          <p>(d) Nothing in this subdivision extends the period of a defendant's stay of sentence imposition or execution.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.104.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.2.42.0">2009 c 83 art 2 s 42</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.105">
        <h1 class="shn">609.105 SENTENCE OF IMPRISONMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.105.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Sentence to one year or more.</span></h2>
          <p> A felony sentence to imprisonment for one year or more shall commit the defendant to the custody of the commissioner of corrections.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.105.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.3.24.0">2009 c 83 art 3 s 24</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.105.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.3.24.0">2009 c 83 art 3 s 24</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.105.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Place of confinement.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of corrections shall determine the place of confinement in a prison, reformatory, or other facility of the Department of Corrections established by law for the confinement of convicted persons and prescribe reasonable conditions and rules for their employment, conduct, instruction, and discipline within or without the facility. When the remaining term of imprisonment for a convicted person upon commitment is 90 days or less, the commissioner of corrections may contract with a county for placement of the person in a county jail or detention center for the remainder of the person's term.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.105.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence to less than one year.</span></h2>
          <p>A sentence to imprisonment for a period of less than one year shall be to a workhouse, work farm, county jail, or other place authorized by law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.105.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.105; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/2/#laws.0.61.0">1Sp1997 c 2 s 61</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/126/#laws.0.10.0">1999 c 126 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/194/#laws.0.7.0">1999 c 194 s 7</a>,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.5.7.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 5 s 7</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.3.19.0">2009 c 83 art 3 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/71/#laws.2.11.0">2020 c 71 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.7.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 7</a>,8</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.1055">
        <h1 class="shn">609.1055 OFFENDERS WITH SERIOUS AND PERSISTENT MENTAL ILLNESS; ALTERNATIVE PLACEMENT.</h1>
        <p>When a court intends to commit an offender with a serious and persistent mental illness, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.462#stat.245.462.20">245.462, subdivision 20</a>, paragraph (c), to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for imprisonment at a state correctional facility, either when initially pronouncing a sentence or when revoking an offender's probation, the court, when consistent with public safety, may instead place the offender on probation or continue the offender's probation and require as a condition of the probation that the offender successfully complete an appropriate supervised alternative living program having a mental health treatment component. This section applies only to offenders who would have a remaining term of imprisonment after adjusting for credit for prior imprisonment, if any, of one year or more.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.1055.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.5.10.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 5 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.9.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.1056">
        <h1 class="shn">609.1056 MILITARY VETERANS; CRIMES COMMITTED BECAUSE OF CONDITIONS RESULTING FROM SERVICE; DISCHARGE AND DISMISSAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given:</p>
          <p>(1) "applicable condition" means sexual trauma, traumatic brain injury, posttraumatic stress disorder, substance abuse, or a mental health condition;</p>
          <p>(2) "eligible offense" means any misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor, and any felony that is ranked at severity level 7 or lower or D7 or lower on the Sentencing Guidelines grid; and</p>
          <p>(3) "veterans treatment court program" means a program that has the following essential characteristics:</p>
          <p>(i) the integration of services in the processing of cases in the judicial system;</p>
          <p>(ii) the use of a nonadversarial approach involving prosecutors and defense attorneys to promote public safety and to protect the due process rights of program participants;</p>
          <p>(iii) early identification and prompt placement of eligible participants in the program;</p>
          <p>(iv) access to a continuum of alcohol, controlled substance, mental health, and other related treatment and rehabilitative services;</p>
          <p>(v) careful monitoring of treatment and services provided to program participants;</p>
          <p>(vi) a coordinated strategy to govern program responses to participants' compliance;</p>
          <p>(vii) ongoing judicial interaction with program participants;</p>
          <p>(viii) monitoring and evaluation of program goals and effectiveness;</p>
          <p>(ix) continuing interdisciplinary education to promote effective program planning, implementation, and operations;</p>
          <p>(x) development of partnerships with public agencies and community organizations, including the United States Department of Veterans Affairs; and</p>
          <p>(xi) inclusion of a participant's family members who agree to be involved in the treatment and services provided to the participant under the program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Eligibility assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) At any time before sentencing, a defendant who was, or currently is, a member of the United States military and who is charged with an eligible offense may request that the court determine whether the defendant is eligible for deferred prosecution under this section.</p>
          <p>(b) Upon making a request for an eligibility assessment, the defendant shall release or authorize access to military service reports and records relating to an alleged applicable condition stemming from service in the United States military. The court must file the records as confidential, and the records must remain sealed, except as provided in this paragraph. The defendant, through existing records or licensed professional evaluation, shall establish the diagnosis of the applicable condition and the condition's connection to military service. The court, on its motion or the prosecutor's motion with notice to defense counsel, may order the defendant to furnish to the court for in-camera review or to the prosecutor copies of all medical and military service reports and records previously or subsequently made concerning the defendant's condition and its connection to service.</p>
          <p>(c) The defendant is eligible for deferred prosecution under this section if the court determines by clear and convincing evidence that:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant suffers from an applicable condition;</p>
          <p>(2) the condition stems from service in the United States military; and</p>
          <p>(3) the offense was committed as a result of the applicable condition.</p>
          <p>(d) If the defendant requests an eligibility assessment before a finding of guilty after trial or entry of a guilty plea, the court may make the finding required under paragraph (c), clause (3), based on the information in a citation or complaint and any accompanying police reports.</p>
          <p>(e) Within 15 days of the court's findings, either party may file a challenge and demand a hearing on the defendant's eligibility for deferred prosecution.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Deferred prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the court finds a defendant eligible for deferred prosecution pursuant to subdivision 1a and the defendant is found guilty, after trial or upon a plea of guilty, the court shall defer prosecution as provided in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) Except as provided in paragraph (c), the court shall, without entering a judgment of guilty, defer further proceedings and place a defendant who is eligible for deferred prosecution on probation upon such reasonable conditions as it may require and for a period not to exceed the maximum period provided by law. A court may extend a defendant's term of probation pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135#stat.609.135.2">609.135, subdivision 2</a>, paragraphs (g) and (h). Conditions ordered by the court must include treatment, services, rehabilitation, and education sufficient so that if completed, the defendant would be eligible for discharge and dismissal under subdivision 3. If the court determines that a defendant suffers from a substance use disorder, the court shall order a Rule 25 assessment under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9530.6615">9530.6615</a>, and order the defendant to follow the recommendations contained in the assessment. If the court determines that a defendant suffers from posttraumatic stress disorder, sexual trauma, traumatic brain injury, or other mental health conditions, the court shall order a mental health assessment conducted by a licensed mental health professional and follow the recommendations contained in the examiner's report.</p>
          <p>(c) If the court determines that the defendant is eligible for a deferred sentence but the defendant has previously received a deferred sentence for a felony offense under this subdivision, the court may, but is not required to, impose a deferred sentence. If the court does not impose a deferred sentence, the court may sentence the defendant as otherwise provided in law, including as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(d) Upon violation of a condition of probation, the court may enter an adjudication of guilt and proceed as otherwise provided in law, including as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(e) As a condition of probation, the court may order the defendant to attend a local, state, federal, or private nonprofit treatment program for a period not to exceed the maximum period for which the defendant could have been incarcerated.</p>
          <p>(f) The court, when issuing an order under this subdivision that a defendant attend an established treatment program, shall give preference to a treatment program that has a history of successfully treating veterans who suffer from applicable conditions caused by military service, including but not limited to programs operated by the United States Department of Defense or Veterans Affairs.</p>
          <p>(g) The court and any assigned treatment program shall collaborate with, when available, the county veterans service officer and the United States Department of Veterans Affairs to maximize benefits and services provided to the defendant. If an appropriate treatment provider is not available in the defendant's county of residence or public funding is not available, the Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs shall coordinate with the United States Department of Veterans Affairs to locate an appropriate treatment program and sources to fund the cost of the defendant's participation in the program.</p>
          <p>(h) If available in the county or judicial district having jurisdiction over the case, the defendant may be supervised by a veterans treatment court program under subdivision 5. If there is a veterans treatment court that meets the requirements of subdivision 5 in the county in which the defendant resides or works, supervision of the defendant may be transferred to that county or judicial district veterans treatment court program. Upon the defendant's successful or unsuccessful completion of the program, the veterans treatment court program shall communicate this information to the court of original jurisdiction for further action.</p>
          <p>(i) Sentencing pursuant to this subdivision waives any right to administrative review pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.53#stat.169A.53.1">169A.53, subdivision 1</a>, or judicial review pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.53">169A.53</a>, subdivision 2, for a license revocation or cancellation imposed pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.52">169A.52</a>, and also waives any right to administrative review pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.177">171.177, subdivision </a>10, or judicial review pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.177#stat.171.177.11">171.177, subdivision 11</a>, for a license revocation or cancellation imposed pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.177">171.177</a>, if that license revocation or cancellation is the result of the same incident for which the defendant is being sentenced.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Discharge and dismissal.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon the expiration of the period of the defendant's probation, the court shall hold a hearing to discharge the defendant from probation and determine whether to dismiss the proceedings against a defendant who received a deferred sentence under subdivision 2. The hearing shall be scheduled so that the parties have adequate time to prepare and present arguments regarding the issue of dismissal. The parties may submit written arguments to the court prior to the date of the hearing and may make oral arguments before the court at the hearing. The defendant must be present at the hearing unless excused under Minnesota Rules of Criminal Procedure, rule 26.03, subdivision 1, clause (3).</p>
          <p>(b) The court shall provide notice to any identifiable victim of the offense at least 15 days before the hearing is held. Notice to victims of the offense under this subdivision must specifically inform the victim of the right to submit an oral or written statement to the court at the time of the hearing describing the harm suffered by the victim as a result of the crime and the victim's recommendation on whether dismissal should be granted or denied. The judge shall consider the victim's statement when making a decision. If a victim notifies the prosecutor of an objection to dismissal and is not present at the hearing, the prosecutor shall make the objections known to the court.</p>
          <p>(c) The court shall dismiss proceedings against a defendant if the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that the defendant:</p>
          <p>(1) is in compliance with the conditions of probation;</p>
          <p>(2) has successfully completed court-ordered treatment and services to address the applicable condition caused by military service;</p>
          <p>(3) does not represent a danger to the health or safety of victims or others; and</p>
          <p>(4) has demonstrated significant benefit from court-ordered education, treatment, or rehabilitation to clearly show that a discharge and dismissal under this subdivision is in the interests of justice.</p>
          <p>(d) In determining the interests of justice, the court shall consider, among other factors, all of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant's completion and degree of participation in education, treatment, and rehabilitation as ordered by the court;</p>
          <p>(2) the defendant's progress in formal education;</p>
          <p>(3) the defendant's development of career potential;</p>
          <p>(4) the defendant's leadership and personal responsibility efforts;</p>
          <p>(5) the defendant's contribution of service in support of the community;</p>
          <p>(6) the level of harm to the community from the offense;</p>
          <p>(7) the level of harm to the victim from the offense with the court's determination of harm guided by the factors for evaluating injury and loss contained in the applicable victim's rights provisions of chapter 611A; and</p>
          <p>(8) the statement of the victim, if any.</p>
          <p>(e) If the court finds that the defendant does not qualify for discharge and dismissal under paragraph (c), the court shall enter an adjudication of guilt and proceed as otherwise provided in law, including as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(f) Discharge and dismissal under this subdivision shall be without court adjudication of guilt, but a not public record of the discharge and dismissal shall be retained by the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension for the purpose of use by the courts in determining the merits of subsequent proceedings against the defendant. The not public record may also be opened only upon court order for purposes of a criminal investigation, prosecution, or sentencing. Upon request by law enforcement, prosecution, or corrections authorities, the bureau shall notify the requesting party of the existence of the not public record and the right to seek a court order to open the not public record under this paragraph. The court shall forward a record of any discharge and dismissal under this subdivision to the bureau, which shall make and maintain the not public record of the discharge and dismissal. The discharge and dismissal shall not be deemed a conviction for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law upon conviction of a crime or for any other purpose. For purposes of this paragraph, "not public" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.8a">13.02, subdivision 8a</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the court imposes a deferred sentence under subdivision 2, paragraph (b), the court shall prepare a deferred sentence report containing the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the name of the defendant;</p>
          <p>(2) the case number;</p>
          <p>(3) the underlying charge or charges;</p>
          <p>(4) the fact that proceedings have been deferred pursuant to this section;</p>
          <p>(5) the length of the term of probation ordered by the court;</p>
          <p>(6) the conditions of probation; and</p>
          <p>(7) a copy of the sentencing worksheet prepared pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.115">609.115</a>, if a worksheet was prepared.</p>
          <p>(b) If the defendant violates a condition of probation and the court enters an adjudication of guilt as described in subdivision 2, paragraph (d), the court shall prepare a violation report containing the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the name of the defendant;</p>
          <p>(2) the case number;</p>
          <p>(3) whether the violation was a technical violation as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.195">244.195</a>, subdivision 15, or involved allegation of a subsequent criminal act; and</p>
          <p>(4) the sentence announced by the court.</p>
          <p>(c) The deferred sentence report prepared under paragraph (a), any violation report prepared under paragraph (b), and a record of any discharge and dismissal prepared pursuant to subdivision 3 must be forwarded to the Sentencing Guidelines Commission. By January 15 of each year, the Sentencing Guidelines Commission shall provide a report to the committees and divisions with jurisdiction over public safety finance and policy and veterans and military affairs finance and policy that consists solely of summary data and includes:</p>
          <p>(1) the number of individuals who received a deferred sentence pursuant to subdivision 2, paragraph (b), in the previous year, disaggregated by county;</p>
          <p>(2) the number of individuals who received an adjudication of guilt as described in subdivision 2, paragraph (d), in the previous year, disaggregated by county;</p>
          <p>(3) for the individuals identified in clause (2), the number who committed a technical violation of probation and the number alleged to have committed a subsequent criminal act; and</p>
          <p>(4) the number of proceedings dismissed pursuant to subdivision 3 in the previous year, disaggregated by county.</p>
          <p>(d) The report required under paragraph (c) may be submitted as a section of any other annual report required to be submitted by the Sentencing Guidelines Commission.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Sentencing departure; waiver of mandatory sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) This subdivision applies to defendants who plead or are found guilty of any criminal offense except one for which registration is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.166#stat.243.166.1b">243.166, subdivision 1b</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Prior to sentencing, a defendant described in paragraph (a) may present proof to the court that the defendant has, since the commission of the offense, engaged in rehabilitative efforts consistent with those described in this section. If the court determines that the defendant has engaged in substantial rehabilitative efforts and the defendant establishes by clear and convincing evidence that:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant suffered from an applicable condition at the time of the offense;</p>
          <p>(2) the applicable condition was caused by service in the United States military; and</p>
          <p>(3) the offense was committed as a result of the applicable condition;</p>
          <p class="bl">the court may determine that the defendant is particularly amenable to probation and order a mitigated durational or dispositional sentencing departure or a waiver of any statutory mandatory minimum sentence applicable to the defendant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Optional veterans treatment court program; procedures for eligible defendants.</span></h2>
          <p>A county or judicial district may supervise probation under this section through a veterans treatment court using county veterans service officers appointed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/197.60">197.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/197.606">197.606</a>, United States Department of Veterans Affairs veterans justice outreach specialists, probation agents, and any other rehabilitative resources available to the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Creation of county and city diversion programs; authorization.</span></h2>
          <p>Any county or city may establish and operate a veterans pretrial diversion program for defendants eligible under subdivision 1 without penalty under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/477A.0175">477A.0175</a>. "Pretrial diversion" means the decision of a prosecutor to refer a defendant to a diversion program on the condition that the criminal charges against the defendant shall be dismissed after a specified period of time or the case shall not be charged, if the defendant successfully completes the program of treatment recommended by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs or a local, state, federal, or private nonprofit treatment program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1056.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Exception.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to a person charged with an offense for which registration is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.166#stat.243.166.1b">243.166, subdivision 1b</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.1056.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/12/#laws.3.13.0">1Sp2021 c 12 art 3 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/19/#laws.0.1.0">2023 c 19 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.7.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.106">
        <h1 class="shn">609.106 HEINOUS CRIMES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.106.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Terms.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, "heinous crime" means:</p>
          <p>(1) a violation or attempted violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, if the offense was committed with force or violence.</p>
          <p>(b) "Previous conviction" means a conviction in Minnesota for a heinous crime or a conviction elsewhere for conduct that would have been a heinous crime under this chapter if committed in Minnesota. The term includes any conviction that occurred before the commission of the present offense of conviction, but does not include a conviction if 15 years have elapsed since the person was discharged from the sentence imposed for the offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.106.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Life without release.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivision 3, the court shall sentence a person to life imprisonment without possibility of release under the following circumstances:</p>
          <p>(1) the person is convicted of first-degree murder under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185, paragraph (a)</a>, clause (1), (2), (4), or (7), or murder of unborn child in the first degree under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a>, clause (1) or (2);</p>
          <p>(2) the person is convicted of committing first-degree murder in the course of a kidnapping under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, paragraph (a), clause (3), or murder of unborn child in the first degree in the course of a kidnapping under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a>, clause (3); or</p>
          <p>(3) the person is convicted of first-degree murder under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, paragraph (a), clause (3), (5), or (6), or murder of unborn child in the first degree under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a>, clause (3), and the court determines on the record at the time of sentencing that the person has one or more previous convictions for a heinous crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.106.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Offender under age 18; life imprisonment.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall sentence a person who was under 18 years of age at the time of the commission of an offense under the circumstances described in subdivision 2 to imprisonment for life.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.106.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.6.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 6</a>; art 6 s 3,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/401/#laws.1.13.0">2002 c 401 art 1 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.2.5.0">2005 c 136 art 2 s 5</a>; art 17 s 9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.98.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 98</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.18.8.0">2023 c 52 art 18 s 8</a>,9</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.107">
        <h1 class="shn">609.107 MANDATORY PENALTY FOR CERTAIN MURDERERS.</h1>
        <p>When a person is convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a>, the court shall sentence the person to the statutory maximum sentence for the offense if the person was previously convicted of a heinous crime as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.106">609.106</a> and 15 years have not elapsed since the person was discharged from the sentence imposed for that conviction. The court may not stay the imposition or execution of the sentence, notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.107.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.4.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.609.108">
        <h1>609.108 </h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.108.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.48.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 48</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.108.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.2.23.0">2005 c 136 art 2 s 23</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.108.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.48.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 48</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.108.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.48.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 48</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.108.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.48.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 48</a>]</p>
        </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.1095">
        <h1 class="shn">609.1095 INCREASED SENTENCES FOR CERTAIN DANGEROUS AND REPEAT FELONY OFFENDERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1095.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Conviction" means any of the following accepted and recorded by the court: a plea of guilty, a verdict of guilty by a jury, or a finding of guilty by the court. The term includes a conviction by any court in Minnesota or another jurisdiction.</p>
          <p>(c) "Prior conviction" means a conviction that occurred before the offender committed the next felony resulting in a conviction and before the offense for which the offender is being sentenced under this section.</p>
          <p>(d) "Violent crime" means a violation of or an attempt or conspiracy to violate any of the following laws of this state or any similar laws of the United States or any other state: sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.137">152.137</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.165">609.165</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.205">609.205</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112">609.2112</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113">609.2113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114">609.2114</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.228">609.228</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.235">609.235</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.247">609.247</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.25">609.25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255">609.255</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2662">609.2662</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2663">609.2663</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2664">609.2664</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2665">609.2665</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.267">609.267</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2671">609.2671</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.268">609.268</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.498#stat.609.498.1">609.498, subdivision 1</a> or 1b; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.562">609.562</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.66#stat.609.66.1e">609.66, subdivision 1e</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.687">609.687</a>; and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.855#stat.609.855.5">609.855, subdivision 5</a>; any provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.229">609.229</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.377">609.377</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.378">609.378</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749">609.749</a>; and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713">624.713</a> that is punishable by a felony penalty; or any provision of chapter 152 that is punishable by a maximum sentence of 15 years or more; or Minnesota Statutes 2012, section 609.21.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1095.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Increased sentences for dangerous offender who commits third violent crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever a person is convicted of a violent crime that is a felony, and the judge is imposing an executed sentence based on a Sentencing Guidelines presumptive imprisonment sentence, the judge may impose an aggravated durational departure from the presumptive imprisonment sentence up to the statutory maximum sentence if the offender was at least 18 years old at the time the felony was committed, and:</p>
          <p>(1) the court determines on the record at the time of sentencing that the offender has two or more prior convictions for violent crimes; and</p>
          <p>(2) the fact finder determines that the offender is a danger to public safety. The fact finder may base its determination that the offender is a danger to public safety on the following factors:</p>
          <p>(i) the offender's past criminal behavior, such as the offender's high frequency rate of criminal activity or juvenile adjudications, or long involvement in criminal activity including juvenile adjudications; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the fact that the present offense of conviction involved an aggravating factor that would justify a durational departure under the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1095.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Mandatory sentence for dangerous offender who commits third violent felony.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Unless a longer mandatory minimum sentence is otherwise required by law or the court imposes a longer aggravated durational departure under subdivision 2, a person who is convicted of a violent crime that is a felony must be committed to the commissioner of corrections for a mandatory sentence of at least the length of the presumptive sentence under the Sentencing Guidelines if the court determines on the record at the time of sentencing that the person has two or more prior felony convictions for violent crimes. The court shall impose and execute the prison sentence regardless of whether the guidelines presume an executed prison sentence.</p>
          <p>Any person convicted and sentenced as required by this subdivision is not eligible for probation, parole, discharge, or work release, until that person has served the full term of imprisonment imposed by the court, notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.26">241.26</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/242.19">242.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05">243.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.04">244.04</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.12">609.12</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this subdivision, "violent crime" does not include a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.023">152.023</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.024">152.024</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.1095.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Increased sentence for offender who commits sixth felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever a person is convicted of a felony, and the judge is imposing an executed sentence based on a Sentencing Guidelines presumptive imprisonment sentence, the judge may impose an aggravated durational departure from the presumptive sentence up to the statutory maximum sentence if the factfinder determines that the offender has five or more prior felony convictions and that the present offense is a felony that was committed as part of a pattern of criminal conduct.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.1095.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.7.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.7.16.0">2005 c 136 art 7 s 16</a>; art 16 s 11,12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.9.0">2014 c 180 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.29.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.20.16.0">2023 c 52 art 20 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.8.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.11">
        <h1 class="shn">609.11 MINIMUM SENTENCES OF IMPRISONMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Commitments without minimums.</span></h2>
          <p>All commitments to the commissioner of corrections for imprisonment of the defendant are without minimum terms except when the sentence is to life imprisonment as required by law and except as otherwise provided in this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/723/#laws.2.5.0">1978 c 723 art 2 s 5</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/227/#laws.0.13.0">1981 c 227 s 13</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Dangerous weapon.</span></h2>
          <p>Any defendant convicted of an offense listed in subdivision 9 in which the defendant or an accomplice, at the time of the offense, used, whether by brandishing, displaying, threatening with, or otherwise employing, a dangerous weapon other than a firearm, shall be committed to the commissioner of corrections for not less than one year plus one day, nor more than the maximum sentence provided by law. Any defendant convicted of a second or subsequent offense in which the defendant or an accomplice, at the time of the offense, used a dangerous weapon other than a firearm, shall be committed to the commissioner of corrections for not less than three years nor more than the maximum sentence provided by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Firearm.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b), any defendant convicted of an offense listed in subdivision 9 in which the defendant or an accomplice, at the time of the offense, had in possession or used, whether by brandishing, displaying, threatening with, or otherwise employing, a firearm, shall be committed to the commissioner of corrections for not less than three years, nor more than the maximum sentence provided by law. Any defendant convicted of a second or subsequent offense in which the defendant or an accomplice, at the time of the offense, had in possession or used a firearm shall be committed to the commissioner of corrections for not less than five years, nor more than the maximum sentence provided by law.</p>
          <p>(b) Any defendant convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.165">609.165</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713#stat.624.713.1">624.713, subdivision 1</a>, clause (2), shall be committed to the commissioner of corrections for not less than five years, nor more than the maximum sentence provided by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Drug offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.035">609.035</a>, whenever a defendant is subject to a mandatory minimum sentence for a felony violation of chapter 152, other than a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.021#stat.152.021.2b">152.021, subdivision 2b</a>, clause (1), or a violation of chapter 152 sentenced under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.021#stat.152.021.3">152.021, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (c), and is also subject to this section, the minimum sentence imposed under this section shall be consecutive to that imposed under chapter 152.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">No early release.</span></h2>
          <p>Any defendant convicted and sentenced as required by this section is not eligible for probation, parole, discharge, or supervised release until that person has served the full term of imprisonment as provided by law, notwithstanding the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/242.19">242.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05">243.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.04">244.04</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.12">609.12</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Fact finder shall establish.</span></h2>
          <p>The question of whether the defendant or an accomplice, at the time of commission of an offense listed in subdivision 9, used a firearm or other dangerous weapon or had in possession a firearm shall be determined by the fact finder at the time of a verdict or finding of guilt at trial or the entry of a plea of guilty based upon the record of the trial or the plea of guilty. The fact finder shall also determine whether the defendant has been convicted of a second or subsequent offense in which the defendant or an accomplice, at the time of commission of an offense listed in subdivision 9, used a firearm or other dangerous weapon or had in possession a firearm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Motion by prosecutor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b) and (c), prior to the time of sentencing, the prosecutor may file a motion to have the defendant sentenced without regard to the mandatory minimum sentences established by this section. The motion shall be accompanied by a statement on the record of the reasons for it. When presented with the motion, or on its own motion, the court may sentence the defendant without regard to the mandatory minimum sentences established by this section if the court finds substantial and compelling reasons to do so. A sentence imposed under this subdivision is a departure from the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
          <p>(b) The court may not, on its own motion or the prosecutor's motion, sentence a defendant without regard to the mandatory minimum sentences established by this section if the defendant previously has been convicted of an offense listed in subdivision 9 in which the defendant used or possessed a firearm or other dangerous weapon.</p>
          <p>(c) The court may not, on its own motion or the prosecutor's motion, sentence a defendant without regard to the mandatory minimum sentences established by subdivision 5, if the defendant was convicted of a crime under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.021#stat.152.021.1">152.021, subdivision 1</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.022#stat.152.022.1">152.022, subdivision 1</a>, and the person or an accomplice possessed on their person or within immediate reach, or used, whether by brandishing, displaying, threatening with, or otherwise employing, a firearm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Applicable offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>The crimes for which mandatory minimum sentences shall be served as provided in this section are: murder in the first, second, or third degree; assault in the first, second, or third degree; burglary; kidnapping; false imprisonment; manslaughter in the first or second degree; aggravated robbery; simple robbery; carjacking in the first, second, or third degree; first-degree or aggravated first-degree witness tampering; criminal sexual conduct under the circumstances described in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342#stat.609.342.1">609.342, subdivision 1</a>, and subdivision 1a, clauses (a) to (f) and (i); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343#stat.609.343.1">609.343, subdivision 1</a>, and subdivision 1a, clauses (a) to (f) and (i); and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344#stat.609.344.1">609.344, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (a) to (c) and (d), under the conditions described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.24">609.341, subdivision 24</a>, clause (2), item (i), (ii), or (iii), and subdivision 1a, clauses (a) to (e), (h), and (i), under the conditions described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.24">609.341, subdivision 24</a>, clause (2), item (i), (ii), or (iii); escape from custody; arson in the first, second, or third degree; drive-by shooting under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.66#stat.609.66.1e">609.66, subdivision 1e</a>; harassment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749#stat.609.749.3">609.749, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (a), clause (3); possession or other unlawful use of a firearm or ammunition in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.165#stat.609.165.1b">609.165, subdivision 1b</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713#stat.624.713.1">624.713, subdivision 1</a>, clause (2), a felony violation of chapter <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152">152</a>; or any attempt to commit any of these offenses.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.11.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Report on criminal cases involving firearm.</span></h2>
          <p>Beginning on July 1, 1994, every county attorney shall collect and maintain the following information on criminal complaints and prosecutions within the county attorney's office in which the defendant is alleged to have committed an offense listed in subdivision 9 while possessing or using a firearm:</p>
          <p>(1) whether the case was charged or dismissed;</p>
          <p>(2) whether the defendant was convicted of the offense or a lesser offense; and</p>
          <p>(3) whether the mandatory minimum sentence required under this section was imposed and executed or was waived by the prosecutor or court.</p>
          <p>No later than July 1 of each year, beginning on July 1, 1995, the county attorney shall forward this information to the Sentencing Guidelines commission upon forms prescribed by the commission.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/182/#laws.1.102.0">2018 c 182 art 1 s 102</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/5/#laws.2.29.0">1Sp2019 c 5 art 2 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.20.17.0">2023 c 52 art 20 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.113"><b>609.113</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/216/#laws.3.10.0">1999 c 216 art 3 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.115">
        <h1 class="shn">609.115 PRESENTENCE INVESTIGATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Presentence investigation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a defendant has been convicted of a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor, the court may, and when the defendant has been convicted of a felony, the court shall, before sentence is imposed, cause a presentence investigation and written report to be made to the court concerning the defendant's individual characteristics, circumstances, needs, potentialities, criminal record and social history, the circumstances of the offense and the harm caused by it to others and to the community. At the request of the prosecutor in a gross misdemeanor case, the court shall order that a presentence investigation and report be prepared. The investigation shall be made by a probation officer of the court, if there is one; otherwise it shall be made by the commissioner of corrections. The officer conducting the presentence or predispositional investigation shall make reasonable and good faith efforts to contact and provide the victim with the information required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.037#stat.611A.037.2">611A.037, subdivision 2</a>. Presentence investigations shall be conducted and summary hearings held upon reports and upon the sentence to be imposed upon the defendant in accordance with this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.10">244.10</a>, and the Rules of Criminal Procedure.</p>
          <p>(b) When the crime is a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.563">609.563</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5641">609.5641</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.576">609.576</a> and involves a fire, the report shall include a description of the financial and physical harm the offense has had on the public safety personnel who responded to the fire. For purposes of this paragraph, "public safety personnel" means the state fire marshal; employees of the Division of the State Fire Marshal; firefighters, regardless of whether the firefighters receive any remuneration for providing services; peace officers, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.05#stat.626.05.2">626.05, subdivision 2</a>; individuals providing emergency management services; and individuals providing emergency medical services.</p>
          <p>(c) When the crime is a felony violation of chapter 152 involving the sale or distribution of a controlled substance, the report may include a description of any adverse social or economic effects the offense has had on persons who reside in the neighborhood where the offense was committed.</p>
          <p>(d) The report shall also include the information relating to crime victims required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.037#stat.611A.037.1">611A.037, subdivision 1</a>. If the court directs, the report shall include an estimate of the prospects of the defendant's rehabilitation and recommendations as to the sentence which should be imposed. In misdemeanor cases the report may be oral.</p>
          <p>(e) When a defendant has been convicted of a felony, and before sentencing, the court shall cause a sentencing worksheet to be completed to facilitate the application of the Minnesota Sentencing Guidelines. The worksheet shall be submitted as part of the presentence investigation report.</p>
          <p>(f) When a person is convicted of a felony for which the Sentencing Guidelines presume that the defendant will be committed to the commissioner of corrections under an executed sentence and no motion for a sentencing departure has been made by counsel, the court may, when there is no space available in the local correctional facility, commit the defendant to the custody of the commissioner of corrections, pending completion of the presentence investigation and report. When a defendant is convicted of a felony for which the Sentencing Guidelines do not presume that the defendant will be committed to the commissioner of corrections, or for which the Sentencing Guidelines presume commitment to the commissioner but counsel has moved for a sentencing departure, the court may commit the defendant to the commissioner with the consent of the commissioner, pending completion of the presentence investigation and report. The county of commitment shall return the defendant to the court when the court so orders.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Contents of worksheet.</span></h2>
          <p>The supreme court shall promulgate rules uniformly applicable to all district courts for the form and contents of sentencing worksheets. These rules shall be promulgated by and effective on January 2, 1982.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/331/#laws.0.13.0">1987 c 331 s 13</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/331/#laws.0.13.0">1987 c 331 s 13</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Life imprisonment report.</span></h2>
          <p>If the defendant has been convicted of a crime for which a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment is provided by law, the probation officer of the court, if there is one, otherwise the commissioner of corrections, shall forthwith make a postsentence investigation and make a written report as provided by subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Sentencing worksheet; sentencing guidelines commission.</span></h2>
          <p>If the defendant has been convicted of a felony, including a felony for which a mandatory life sentence is required by law, the court shall cause a sentencing worksheet as provided in subdivision 1 to be completed and forwarded to the Sentencing Guidelines Commission.</p>
          <p>For the purpose of this section, "mandatory life sentence" means a sentence under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.106#stat.609.106.2">609.106, subdivision 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.385#stat.609.385.2">609.385, subdivision 2</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, subdivision 3, and governed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.05">244.05</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Criminal justice agency disclosure requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>All criminal justice agencies shall make available at no cost to the probation officer or the commissioner of corrections the criminal record and other relevant information relating to the defendant which they may have, when requested for the purposes of subdivisions 1 and 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Confidential sources of information.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any report made pursuant to subdivision 1 shall be, if written, provided to counsel for all parties before sentence. The written report shall not disclose confidential sources of information unless the court otherwise directs. On the request of the prosecuting attorney or the defendant's attorney a summary hearing in chambers shall be held on any matter brought in issue, but confidential sources of information shall not be disclosed unless the court otherwise directs. If the presentence report is given orally the defendant or the defendant's attorney shall be permitted to hear the report.</p>
          <p>(b) Any report made under subdivision 1 or 2 shall be provided to counsel for the defendant for purposes of representing the defendant on any appeal or petition for postconviction relief. The reports shall be provided by the court and the commissioner of corrections at no cost to the defendant or the defendant's attorney.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Report to commissioner or local correctional agency.</span></h2>
          <p>If the defendant is sentenced to the commissioner of corrections, a copy of any report made pursuant to this section and not made by the commissioner shall accompany the commitment. If the defendant is sentenced to a local correctional agency or facility, a copy of the report must be provided to that agency or facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Report disclosure prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivisions 4 and 5 or as otherwise directed by the court any report made pursuant to this section shall not be disclosed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Stay of imposition of sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>If imposition of sentence is stayed by reason of an appeal taken or to be taken, the presentence investigation provided for in this section shall not be made until such stay has expired or has otherwise been terminated.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Chemical use assessment required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a person is convicted of a felony, the probation officer shall determine in the report prepared under subdivision 1 whether or not alcohol or drug use was a contributing factor to the commission of the offense. If so, the report shall contain the results of a chemical use assessment conducted in accordance with this subdivision. The probation officer shall make an appointment for the defendant to undergo the chemical use assessment if so indicated.</p>
          <p>(b) The chemical use assessment report must include a recommended level of care for the defendant in accordance with the criteria contained in rules adopted by the commissioner of human services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/254A.03#stat.254A.03.3">254A.03, subdivision 3</a>. The assessment must be conducted by an assessor qualified under rules adopted by the commissioner of human services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/254A.03#stat.254A.03.3">254A.03, subdivision 3</a>. An assessor providing a chemical use assessment may not have any direct or shared financial interest or referral relationship resulting in shared financial gain with a treatment provider, except as authorized under section 254A.19, subdivision 3. If an independent assessor is not available, the probation officer may use the services of an assessor authorized to perform assessments for the county social services agency under a variance granted under rules adopted by the commissioner of human services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/254A.03#stat.254A.03.3">254A.03, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Compulsive gambling assessment required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a person is convicted of theft under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>, embezzlement of public funds under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.54">609.54</a>, or forgery under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>, the probation officer shall determine in the report prepared under subdivision 1 whether or not compulsive gambling contributed to the commission of the offense. If so, the report shall contain the results of a compulsive gambling assessment conducted in accordance with this subdivision. The probation officer shall make an appointment for the offender to undergo the assessment if so indicated.</p>
          <p>(b) The compulsive gambling assessment report must include a recommended level of treatment for the offender if the assessor concludes that the offender is in need of compulsive gambling treatment. The assessment must be conducted by an assessor qualified either under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9585.0040">9585.0040</a>, subpart 1, item C, or qualifications determined to be equivalent by the commissioner, to perform these assessments or to provide compulsive gambling treatment. An assessor providing a compulsive gambling assessment may not have any direct or shared financial interest or referral relationship resulting in shared financial gain with a treatment provider. If an independent assessor is not available, the probation officer may use the services of an assessor with a financial interest or referral relationship as authorized under rules adopted by the commissioner of human services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.98#stat.245.98.2a">245.98, subdivision 2a</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner of human services shall reimburse the assessor for each compulsive gambling assessment at a rate established by the commissioner. To the extent practicable, the commissioner shall standardize reimbursement rates for assessments. The commissioner shall reimburse the assessor after receiving written verification from the probation officer that the assessment was performed and found acceptable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.115.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Military veterans.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) When a defendant appears in court and is convicted of a crime, the court shall inquire whether the defendant is currently serving in or is a veteran of the armed forces of the United States.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) If the defendant is currently serving in the military or is a veteran and has been diagnosed as having a mental illness by a qualified psychiatrist or clinical psychologist or physician, the court may:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) order that the officer preparing the report under subdivision 1 consult with the United States Department of Veterans Affairs, Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs, or another agency or person with suitable knowledge or experience, for the purpose of providing the court with information regarding treatment options available to the defendant, including federal, state, and local programming; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) consider the treatment recommendations of any diagnosing or treating mental health professionals together with the treatment options available to the defendant in imposing sentence.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">
