      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.609.116">
        <h1>609.116 </h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.116.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.25.0">1979 c 258 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.116.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/997/#laws.0.3.0">1969 c 997 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.25.0">1979 c 258 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.117">
        <h1 class="shn">609.117 DNA ANALYSIS OF CERTAIN OFFENDERS REQUIRED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.117.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Upon sentencing.</span></h2>
          <p>If an offender has not already done so, the court shall order an offender to provide a biological specimen for the purpose of DNA analysis as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.155">299C.155</a> when:</p>
          <p>(1) the court sentences a person charged with committing or attempting to commit a felony offense and the person is convicted of that offense or of any offense arising out of the same set of circumstances; or</p>
          <p>(2) the juvenile court adjudicates a person a delinquent child who is petitioned for committing or attempting to commit a felony offense and is adjudicated delinquent for that offense or any offense arising out of the same set of circumstances.</p>
          <p class="bl">The biological specimen or the results of the analysis shall be maintained by the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.155">299C.155</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.117.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Before release.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of corrections or local corrections authority shall order a person to provide a biological specimen for the purpose of DNA analysis before completion of the person's term of imprisonment when the person has not provided a biological specimen for the purpose of DNA analysis and the person:</p>
          <p>(1) was initially charged with committing or attempting to commit a felony offense and was convicted of that offense or of any offense arising out of the same set of circumstances, or the person has a past felony conviction in this or any other state; or</p>
          <p>(2) is serving a term of imprisonment in this state under a reciprocal agreement although convicted in another state of committing or attempting to commit a felony offense or of any offense arising out of the same set of circumstances if the person was initially charged with committing or attempting to commit a felony offense. The commissioner of corrections or local corrections authority shall forward the sample to the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.117.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Offenders from other states.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">When the state accepts an offender from another state under the interstate compact authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.1605">243.1605</a>, the acceptance is conditional on the offender providing a biological specimen for the purposes of DNA analysis as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.155">299C.155</a>, if the offender was initially charged with committing or attempting to commit a felony offense and was convicted of that offense or of any offense arising out of the same set of circumstances. The specimen must be provided under supervision of staff from the Department of Corrections or a Community Corrections Act county within 15 business days after the offender reports to the supervising agent. The cost of obtaining the biological specimen is the responsibility of the agency providing supervision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.117.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">After supervision expires.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon motion of a prosecuting authority, a court shall issue an order to show cause why an offender who should have been ordered or required to provide a biological specimen under this section but did not, should not now be ordered to provide one for the purposes of DNA analysis. This subdivision applies if the offender's sentence or supervision has expired. The prosecuting authority shall provide the court with an affidavit that:</p>
          <p>(1) identifies the offender by name and date of birth;</p>
          <p>(2) identifies the offender's last known address;</p>
          <p>(3) identifies the offender's charged offense, offense of conviction, and date of conviction; and</p>
          <p>(4) indicates that the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension database of biological specimens has been searched and the offender has not previously provided a biological specimen for DNA analysis under this chapter.</p>
          <p>(b) The order to show cause shall direct the offender to appear before the court within 30 days after the order is served. The prosecutor shall serve the order to show cause upon the offender in the same manner as a civil summons. The offender may avoid appearing before the court by appearing at a place and time designated in the order and voluntarily providing the specimen.</p>
          <p>(c) Upon the offender's appearance before the court, and after an opportunity to be heard, the court may issue an order directing the offender to provide the specimen.</p>
          <p>(d) If the offender has failed to provide the specimen or appear before the court and the prosecuting authority makes a sufficient showing that the offender was properly served with the order to show cause, the court may issue an order:</p>
          <p>(1) requiring the offender to submit the specimen within 30 days from the date of the order at a designated location;</p>
          <p>(2) including the designated location's address, telephone number, and regular hours of operation; and</p>
          <p>(3) authorizing, if the offender fails or refuses to comply with the order to provide a specimen, a peace officer to detain and bring the offender before the court as soon as practicable to show cause why the specimen should not be obtained.</p>
          <p>(e) The local corrections authority shall mail the order in paragraph (d) to the offender's last known address.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.117.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.4.16.0">1989 c 290 art 4 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/232/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 232 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/285/#laws.0.11.0">1991 c 285 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.10.15.0">1993 c 326 art 10 s 15</a>; art 13 s 32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.3.12.0">1998 c 367 art 3 s 12</a>,13; art 6 s 15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/216/#laws.3.7.0">1999 c 216 art 3 s 7</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.9.6.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 9 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.12.9.0">2005 c 136 art 12 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/299/#laws.0.19.0">2008 c 299 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/256/#laws.0.1.0">2010 c 256 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.118">
        <h1 class="shn">609.118 FINGERPRINTING REQUIRED.</h1>
        <p>(a) When a person is convicted of a felony, gross misdemeanor, or targeted misdemeanor, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.10#stat.299C.10.1">299C.10, subdivision 1</a>, or is adjudicated delinquent for a felony or gross misdemeanor, the court shall order the offender to immediately report to the law enforcement agency responsible for the collection of fingerprint and other identification data required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.10">299C.10</a>, regardless of the sentence imposed or executed.</p>
        <p>(b) Paragraph (a) does not apply if the person is remanded to the custody of a law enforcement agency or if the identification data was collected prior to the conviction or adjudication for the offense.</p>
        <p>(c) A person who fails to obey a court order under paragraph (a) is subject to probation revocation, contempt of court, or any other appropriate remedy.</p>
        <p>(d) This section does not limit or restrict any other statutory requirements or local policies regarding the collection of identification data.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.118.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.6.7.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 6 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.119"><b>609.119</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.12.12.0">2005 c 136 art 12 s 12</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.12">
        <h1 class="shn">609.12 PAROLE OR DISCHARGE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.12.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority; conditions.</span></h2>
          <p>A person sentenced to the commissioner of corrections for imprisonment for a period less than life may be paroled or discharged at any time without regard to length of the term of imprisonment which the sentence imposes when in the judgment of the Supervised Release Board, and under the conditions the board imposes, the granting of parole or discharge would be most conducive to rehabilitation and would be in the public interest.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.12.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Parole required after certain term.</span></h2>
          <p>If a sentence of more than five years has been imposed on a defendant for a crime authorizing a sentence of not more than ten years, the Supervised Release Board shall grant the defendant parole no later than the expiration of five years of imprisonment, less time granted for good behavior, unless the board determines with or without hearing that the defendant's parole would not be conducive to rehabilitation or would not be in the public interest.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.12.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Parole; board powers.</span></h2>
          <p>All sentences to the Supervised Release Board for the imprisonment of the defendant are subject to the laws relating to parole and the powers of the Supervised Release Board, except as modified in subdivisions 1 and 2, and to all other laws relating to persons in said institutions and their imprisonment.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.12.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/654/#laws.0.15.0">1973 c 654 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/271/#laws.0.6.0">1975 c 271 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/274/#laws.0.18.0">1983 c 274 s 18</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.18.13.0">2023 c 52 art 18 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.125">
        <h1 class="shn">609.125 SENTENCE FOR MISDEMEANOR OR GROSS MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.125.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Sentences available.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon conviction of a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor the court, if sentence is imposed, may, to the extent authorized by law, sentence the defendant:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for a definite term; or</p>
          <p>(2) to payment of a fine without imprisonment or as an intermediate sanction on a stayed sentence; or</p>
          <p>(3) to both imprisonment for a definite term and payment of a fine; or</p>
          <p>(4) to payment of court-ordered restitution in addition to either imprisonment or payment of a fine, or both; or</p>
          <p>(5) to payment of a local correctional fee as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.102">609.102</a> in addition to any other sentence imposed by the court; or</p>
          <p>(6) to perform work service in a restorative justice program in addition to any other sentence imposed by the court.</p>
          <p>(b) If the court imposes a fine or orders restitution under paragraph (a), payment is due on the date imposed unless the court otherwise establishes a due date or a payment plan.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.125.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, "restitution" includes:</p>
          <p>(1) payment of compensation to the victim or the victim's family; and</p>
          <p>(2) if the victim is deceased or already has been fully compensated, payment of money to a victim assistance program or other program directed by the court.</p>
          <p>"Restitution" includes payment of compensation to a government entity that incurs loss as a direct result of a crime.</p>
          <p>(b) When the defendant does not pay the entire amount of court-ordered restitution and the fine at the same time, the court may order that all restitution shall be paid before the fine is paid.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.125.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.125; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/25/#laws.0.91.0">1971 c 25 s 91</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/610/#laws.0.2.0">1984 c 610 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.11.14.0">1992 c 571 art 11 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.11.0">1995 c 244 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.7.3.0">1996 c 408 art 7 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.6.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 6</a>; art 7 s 17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.2.43.0">2009 c 83 art 2 s 43</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.13">
        <h1 class="shn">609.13 CONVICTIONS OF FELONY OR GROSS MISDEMEANOR; WHEN DEEMED MISDEMEANOR OR GROSS MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.13.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding a conviction is for a felony:</p>
          <p>(1) the conviction is deemed to be for a misdemeanor or a gross misdemeanor if the sentence imposed is within the limits provided by law for a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02">609.02</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) the conviction is deemed to be for a misdemeanor if the imposition of the prison sentence is stayed, the defendant is placed on probation, and the defendant is thereafter discharged without a prison sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.13.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding that a conviction is for a gross misdemeanor, the conviction is deemed to be for a misdemeanor if:</p>
          <p>(1) the sentence imposed is within the limits provided by law for a misdemeanor as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02">609.02</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the imposition of the sentence is stayed, the defendant is placed on probation, and the defendant is thereafter discharged without sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.13.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanors.</span></h2>
          <p>If a defendant is convicted of a misdemeanor and is sentenced, or if the imposition of sentence is stayed, and the defendant is thereafter discharged without sentence, the conviction is deemed to be for a misdemeanor for purposes of determining the penalty for a subsequent offense.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.13.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/937/#laws.0.21.0">1971 c 937 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/435/#laws.0.6.0">1986 c 435 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.10.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.131">
        <h1 class="shn">609.131 CERTIFICATION OF MISDEMEANOR AS PETTY MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.131.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General rule.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivision 2, an alleged misdemeanor violation must be treated as a petty misdemeanor if the prosecuting attorney believes that it is in the interest of justice that the defendant not be imprisoned if convicted and certifies that belief to the court at or before the time of arraignment or pretrial hearing, and the court approves of the certification motion. Prior to the appointment of a public defender to represent a defendant charged with a misdemeanor, the court shall inquire of the prosecutor whether the prosecutor intends to certify the case as a petty misdemeanor. The defendant's consent to the certification is not required. When an offense is certified as a petty misdemeanor under this section, the defendant is not eligible for the appointment of a public defender.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.131.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.40.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 40</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.131.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Certain violations excepted.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivision 1 does not apply to a misdemeanor violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.09#stat.171.09.1">171.09, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (g); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.306">171.306</a>, subdivision 6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.226">609.226</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.23">617.23</a>, or an ordinance that conforms in substantial part to any of those sections. A violation described in this subdivision must be treated as a misdemeanor unless the defendant consents to the certification of the violation as a petty misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.131.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Use of conviction for enhancement.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any other law, a conviction for a violation that was originally charged as a misdemeanor and was treated as a petty misdemeanor under subdivision 1 or the Rules of Criminal Procedure may not be used as the basis for charging a subsequent violation as a gross misdemeanor rather than a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.131.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.6.0">1987 c 329 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.4.48.0">1992 c 513 art 4 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.3.8.0">1995 c 259 art 3 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/478/#laws.2.7.0">2000 c 478 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/366/#laws.0.15.0">2010 c 366 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/187/#laws.1.71.0">2012 c 187 art 1 s 71</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/212/#laws.0.8.0">2012 c 212 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.30.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 30</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.132">
        <h1 class="shn">609.132 CONTINUANCE FOR DISMISSAL.</h1>
        <p>The decision to offer or agree to a continuance of a criminal prosecution is an exercise of prosecutorial discretion resting solely with the prosecuting attorney.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.132.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.15.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.133">
        <h1 class="shn">609.133 SENTENCE ADJUSTMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "prosecutor" means the attorney general, county attorney, or city attorney responsible for the prosecution of individuals charged with a crime; and</p>
          <p>(2) "victim" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.01">611A.01</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prosecutor-initiated sentence adjustment.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecutor for the jurisdiction responsible for the prosecution of an individual convicted of a crime may commence a proceeding to adjust the sentence of that individual at any time after the initial sentencing provided the prosecutor does not seek to increase the period of confinement or, if the individual is serving a stayed sentence, increase the period of supervision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Review by prosecutor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A prosecutor may review individual cases at the prosecutor's discretion.</p>
          <p>(b) Prior to filing a petition under this section, a prosecutor shall make a reasonable and good faith effort to seek input from any identifiable victim and shall consider the impact an adjusted sentence would have on the victim.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner of corrections, a supervising agent, or an offender may request that a prosecutor review an individual case. A prosecutor is not required to respond to a request. Inaction by a prosecutor shall not be considered by any court as grounds for an offender, a supervising agent, or the commissioner of corrections to petition for a sentence adjustment under this section or for a court to adjust a sentence without a petition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Petition; contents; fee.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A prosecutor's petition for sentence adjustment shall be filed in the district court where the individual was convicted and include the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the full name of the individual on whose behalf the petition is being brought and, to the extent possible, all other legal names or aliases by which the individual has been known at any time;</p>
          <p>(2) the individual's date of birth;</p>
          <p>(3) the individual's address;</p>
          <p>(4) a brief statement of the reason the prosecutor is seeking a sentence adjustment for the individual;</p>
          <p>(5) the details of the offense for which an adjustment is sought, including:</p>
          <p>(i) the date and jurisdiction of the occurrence;</p>
          <p>(ii) either the names of any victims or that there were no identifiable victims;</p>
          <p>(iii) whether there is a current order for protection, restraining order, or other no contact order prohibiting the individual from contacting the victims or whether there has ever been a prior order for protection or restraining order prohibiting the individual from contacting the victims;</p>
          <p>(iv) the court file number; and</p>
          <p>(v) the date of conviction;</p>
          <p>(6) what steps the individual has taken since the time of the offense toward personal rehabilitation, including treatment, work, good conduct within correctional facilities, or other personal history that demonstrates rehabilitation;</p>
          <p>(7) the individual's criminal conviction record indicating all convictions for misdemeanors, gross misdemeanors, or felonies in this state, and for all comparable convictions in any other state, federal court, or foreign country, whether the convictions occurred before or after the conviction for which an adjustment is sought;</p>
          <p>(8) the individual's criminal charges record indicating all prior and pending criminal charges against the individual in this state or another jurisdiction, including all criminal charges that have been continued for dismissal, stayed for adjudication, or were the subject of pretrial diversion; and</p>
          <p>(9) to the extent known, all prior requests by the individual, whether for the present offense or for any other offenses in this state or any other state or federal court, for pardon, return of arrest records, or expungement or sealing of a criminal record, whether granted or not, and all stays of adjudication or imposition of sentence involving the petitioner.</p>
          <p>(b) The filing fee for a petition brought under this section shall be waived.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding chapter 13 or any other statute related to the classification of government data, a supervising agent or the commissioner of corrections may provide private or confidential data to a prosecutor for purposes of a petition for sentence adjustment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Service of petition.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The prosecutor shall serve the petition for sentence adjustment on the individual on whose behalf the petition is being brought.</p>
          <p>(b) The prosecutor shall make a good faith and reasonable effort to notify any person determined to be a victim of the offense for which adjustment is sought of the existence of a petition. Notification under this paragraph does not constitute a violation of an existing order for protection, restraining order, or other no contact order.</p>
          <p>(c) Notice to victims of the offense under this subdivision must:</p>
          <p>(1) specifically inform the victim of the right to object, orally or in writing, to the proposed adjustment of sentence; and</p>
          <p>(2) inform the victims of the right to be present and to submit an oral or written statement at the hearing described in subdivision 6.</p>
          <p>(d) If a victim notifies the prosecutor of an objection to the proposed adjustment of sentence and is not present when the court considers the sentence adjustment, the prosecutor shall make these objections known to the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The court shall hold a hearing on the petition no sooner than 60 days after service of the petition. The hearing shall be scheduled so that the parties have adequate time to prepare and present arguments regarding the issue of sentence adjustment. The parties may submit written arguments to the court prior to the date of the hearing and may make oral arguments before the court at the hearing. The individual on whose behalf the petition has been brought must be present at the hearing, unless excused under Minnesota Rules of Criminal Procedure, rule <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/26.03#stat.26.03.1">26.03, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3).</p>
          <p>(b) A victim of the offense for which sentence adjustment is sought has a right to submit an oral or written statement to the court at the time of the hearing describing the harm suffered by the victim as a result of the crime and the victim's recommendation on whether adjustment should be granted or denied. The judge shall consider the victim's statement when making a decision.</p>
          <p>(c) Representatives of the Department of Corrections, supervising agents, community treatment providers, and any other individual with relevant information may submit an oral or written statement to the court at the time of the hearing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Nature of remedy; standard.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The court shall determine whether there are substantial and compelling reasons to adjust the individual's sentence. In making this determination, the court shall consider what impact, if any, a sentence adjustment would have on public safety, including whether an adjustment would promote the rehabilitation of the individual, properly reflect the severity of the underlying offense, or reduce sentencing disparities. In making this determination, the court may consider factors relating to both the offender and the offense, including but not limited to:</p>
          <p>(1) the presentence investigation report used at sentencing, if available;</p>
          <p>(2) the individual's performance on probation or supervision;</p>
          <p>(3) the individual's disciplinary record during any period of incarceration;</p>
          <p>(4) records of any rehabilitation efforts made by the individual since the date of offense and any plan to continue those efforts in the community;</p>
          <p>(5) evidence that remorse, age, diminished physical condition, or any other factor has significantly reduced the likelihood that the individual will commit a future offense;</p>
          <p>(6) the amount of time the individual has served in custody or under supervision; and</p>
          <p>(7) significant changes in law or sentencing practice since the date of offense.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, if the court determines by a preponderance of the evidence that there are substantial and compelling reasons to adjust the individual's sentence, the court may modify the sentence in any way provided the adjustment does not:</p>
          <p>(1) increase the period of confinement or, if the individual is serving a stayed sentence, increase the period of supervision;</p>
          <p>(2) reduce or eliminate the amount of court-ordered restitution; or</p>
          <p>(3) reduce or eliminate a term of conditional release required by law when a court commits an offender to the custody of the commissioner of corrections.</p>
          <p class="bl">The court may stay imposition or execution of sentence pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) A sentence adjustment is not a valid basis to vacate the judgment of conviction, enter a judgment of conviction for a different offense, or impose sentence for any other offense.</p>
          <p>(d) The court shall state in writing or on the record the reasons for its decision on the petition. If the court grants a sentence adjustment, the court shall provide the information in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.09#stat.244.09.15">244.09, subdivision 15</a>, to the Sentencing Guidelines Commission.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.133.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Appeals.</span></h2>
          <p>An order issued under this section shall not be considered a final judgment, but shall be treated as an order imposing or staying a sentence.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.133.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.10.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/69/#laws.0.8.0">2023 c 69 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.8.22.0">2024 c 123 art 8 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.135">
        <h1 class="shn">609.135 STAY OF IMPOSITION OR EXECUTION OF SENTENCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Terms and conditions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except when a sentence of life imprisonment is required by law, or when a mandatory minimum sentence is required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.11">609.11</a>, any court may stay imposition or execution of sentence and:</p>
          <p>(1) may order intermediate sanctions without placing the defendant on probation; or</p>
          <p>(2) may place the defendant on probation with or without supervision and on the terms the court prescribes, including intermediate sanctions when practicable. The court may order the supervision to be under the probation officer of the court, or, if there is none and the conviction is for a felony or gross misdemeanor, by the commissioner of corrections, or in any case by some other suitable and consenting person. Unless the court directs otherwise, state parole and probation agents and probation officers may impose community work service or probation violation sanctions, consistent with section 243.05, subdivision 1, or sections 244.197 to 244.199.</p>
          <p>No intermediate sanction may be ordered performed at a location that fails to observe applicable requirements or standards of chapter 181A or 182, or any rule promulgated under them.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this subdivision, subdivision 6, and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.14">609.14</a>, the term "intermediate sanctions" includes but is not limited to incarceration in a local jail or workhouse, home detention, electronic monitoring, intensive probation, sentencing to service, reporting to a day reporting center, chemical dependency or mental health treatment or counseling, restitution, fines, day-fines, community work service, work service in a restorative justice program, work in lieu of or to work off fines and, with the victim's consent, work in lieu of or to work off restitution.</p>
          <p>(c) A court may not stay the revocation of the driver's license of a person convicted of violating the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) If the court orders a fine, day-fine, or restitution as an intermediate sanction, payment is due on the date imposed unless the court otherwise establishes a due date or a payment plan.</p>
          <p>(e) The court may prohibit a defendant from using adult-use cannabis flower as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01#stat.342.01.4">342.01, subdivision 4</a>, or adult-use cannabis products as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01</a>, subdivision 2, if the defendant undergoes a chemical use assessment and abstinence is consistent with a recommended level of care for the defendant in accordance with the criteria under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/254B.04#stat.254B.04.4">254B.04, subdivision 4</a>. The assessment must be conducted by an assessor qualified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245G.11">245G.11, subdivisions 1</a> and 5.</p>
          <p>(f) A court shall not impose an intermediate sanction that has the effect of prohibiting a person from participating in the registry program as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01, subdivision </a>63.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Failure to pay restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>If the court orders payment of restitution as a condition of probation and if the defendant fails to pay the restitution in accordance with the payment schedule or structure established by the court or the probation officer, the prosecutor or the defendant's probation officer may, on the prosecutor's or the officer's own motion or at the request of the victim, ask the court to hold a hearing to determine whether or not the conditions of probation should be changed or probation should be revoked. The defendant's probation officer shall ask for the hearing if the restitution ordered has not been paid prior to 60 days before the term of probation expires. The court shall schedule and hold this hearing and take appropriate action, including action under subdivision 2, paragraph (h), before the defendant's term of probation expires.</p>
          <p>Nothing in this subdivision limits the court's ability to refer the case to collections under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.104">609.104</a> when a defendant fails to pay court-ordered restitution.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/384/#laws.1.52.0">1987 c 384 art 1 s 52</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Failure to complete court-ordered treatment.</span></h2>
          <p>If the court orders a defendant to undergo treatment as a condition of probation and if the defendant fails to successfully complete treatment at least 60 days before the term of probation expires, the prosecutor or the defendant's probation officer may ask the court to hold a hearing to determine whether the conditions of probation should be changed or probation should be revoked. The court shall schedule and hold this hearing and take appropriate action, including action under subdivision 2, paragraph (i), before the defendant's term of probation expires.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Stay of sentence maximum periods.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), if the conviction is for a felony, the stay shall be for not more than five years or the maximum period for which the sentence of imprisonment might have been imposed, whichever is less.</p>
          <p>(b) If the conviction is for a felony violation of, or a felony-level attempt or conspiracy to violate, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112">609.2112</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113#stat.609.2113.2">609.2113, subdivision 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2662">609.2662</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2663">609.2663</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2664">609.2664</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.268">609.268</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749">609.749</a>; or a felony-level attempt or conspiracy to violate section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a>, the stay shall be for not more than four years or the maximum period for which the sentence of imprisonment might have been imposed, whichever is longer.</p>
          <p>(c) If the conviction is for a gross misdemeanor violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113#stat.609.2113.3">609.2113, subdivision 3</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>, the stay shall be for not more than four years. The court shall provide for unsupervised probation for the last year of the stay unless the court finds that the defendant needs supervised probation for all or part of the last year.</p>
          <p>(d) If the conviction is for a gross misdemeanor not specified in paragraph (c), the stay shall be for not more than two years.</p>
          <p>(e) If the conviction is for any misdemeanor under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.746#stat.609.746.1">609.746, subdivision 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.79">609.79</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.23">617.23</a>; or for a misdemeanor under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224#stat.609.224.1">609.224, subdivision 1</a>, in which the victim of the crime was a family or household member as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01">518B.01</a>, the stay shall be for not more than two years. The court shall provide for unsupervised probation for the second year of the stay unless the court finds that the defendant needs supervised probation for all or part of the second year.</p>
          <p>(f) If the conviction is for a misdemeanor not specified in paragraph (e), the stay shall be for not more than one year.</p>
          <p>(g) The defendant shall be discharged six months after the term of the stay expires, unless the stay has been revoked or extended under paragraph (h), or the defendant has already been discharged.</p>
          <p>(h) Notwithstanding the maximum periods specified for stays of sentences under paragraphs (a) to (g), a court may extend a defendant's term of probation for up to one year if it finds, at a hearing conducted under subdivision 1a, that:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant has not paid court-ordered restitution in accordance with the payment schedule or structure; and</p>
          <p>(2) the defendant is likely to not pay the restitution the defendant owes before the term of probation expires.</p>
          <p class="bl">This one-year extension of probation for failure to pay restitution may be extended by the court for up to one additional year if the court finds, at another hearing conducted under subdivision 1a, that the defendant still has not paid the court-ordered restitution that the defendant owes.</p>
          <p>Nothing in this subdivision limits the court's ability to refer the case to collections under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.104">609.104</a>.</p>
          <p>(i) Notwithstanding the maximum periods specified for stays of sentences under paragraphs (a) to (g), a court may extend a defendant's term of probation for up to three years if it finds, at a hearing conducted under subdivision 1c, that:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant has failed to complete court-ordered treatment successfully; and</p>
          <p>(2) the defendant is likely not to complete court-ordered treatment before the term of probation expires.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Motor vehicle offense report.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall report to the commissioner of public safety any stay of imposition or execution granted in the case of a conviction for an offense in which a motor vehicle, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.42">169.011, subdivision 42</a>, is used.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Jail as condition of probation.</span></h2>
          <p>The court may, as a condition of probation, require the defendant to serve up to one year incarceration in a county jail, a county regional jail, a county work farm, county workhouse or other local correctional facility, or require the defendant to pay a fine, or both. The court may allow the defendant the work release privileges of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/631.425">631.425</a> during the period of incarceration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Assaulting spouse stay conditions.</span></h2>
          <p>If a person is convicted of assaulting a spouse or other person with whom the person resides, and the court stays imposition or execution of sentence and places the defendant on probation, the court must condition the stay upon the defendant's participation in counseling or other appropriate programs selected by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Domestic abuse victims; electronic monitoring.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Until a judicial district has adopted standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.72#stat.629.72.2a">629.72, subdivision 2a</a>, paragraph (b), governing electronic monitoring devices used to protect victims of domestic abuse, a court within the judicial district, as a condition of a stay of imposition or execution of a sentence, may not order an offender convicted of a crime described in paragraph (b) to use an electronic monitoring device to protect a victim's safety.</p>
          <p>(b) This subdivision applies to the following crimes, if committed by the defendant against a family or household member as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) violations of orders for protection issued under chapter 518B;</p>
          <p>(2) assault in the first, second, third, or fifth degree under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>; or domestic assault under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) criminal damage to property under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595">609.595</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) disorderly conduct under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.72">609.72</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) harassing telephone calls under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.79">609.79</a>;</p>
          <p>(6) burglary under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582">609.582</a>;</p>
          <p>(7) trespass under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.605">609.605</a>;</p>
          <p>(8) criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, third, fourth, or fifth degree under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>, or sexual extortion under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>;</p>
          <p>(9) terroristic threats under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a>;</p>
          <p>(10) harassment or stalking under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749">609.749</a>;</p>
          <p>(11) violations of harassment restraining orders under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.748">609.748</a>;</p>
          <p>(12) violations of domestic abuse no contact orders under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.75">629.75</a>; and</p>
          <p>(13) interference with an emergency call under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.78#stat.609.78.2">609.78, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The location data associated with the victim and offender are security information as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.37">13.37</a>. Location data maintained by a law enforcement agency, probation authority, prosecutorial agency, or court services department may be shared among those agencies to develop and monitor conditions of a stayed sentence under this section.</p>
          <p>(d) A violation of a location restriction by an offender in a situation involving a victim and offender who are both mobile does not automatically constitute a violation of the conditions of the offender's stayed sentence.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Preference for intermediate sanctions.</span></h2>
          <p>A court staying imposition or execution of a sentence that does not include a term of incarceration as a condition of the stay shall order other intermediate sanctions where practicable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Demand of execution of sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>An offender may not demand execution of sentence in lieu of a stay of imposition or execution of sentence if the offender will serve less than nine months at the state institution. This subdivision does not apply to an offender who will be serving the sentence consecutively or concurrently with a previously imposed executed felony sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.135.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/83/#laws.2.50.0">2009 c 83 art 2 s 50</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
