      <p><b>NOTE: </b> To read the amendments to subdivision 5a that expired August 1, 2017, see Laws 2014, chapter 263, section 1.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.1351">
        <h1 class="shn">609.1351 PETITION FOR CIVIL COMMITMENT.</h1>
        <p>When a court sentences a person under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455#stat.609.3455.3a">609.3455, subdivision 3a</a>, the court shall make a preliminary determination whether in the court's opinion a petition under chapter 253D may be appropriate and include the determination as part of the sentencing order. If the court determines that a petition may be appropriate, the court shall forward its preliminary determination along with supporting documentation to the county attorney.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.1351.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.4.9.0">1989 c 290 art 4 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.3.7.0">1992 c 571 art 3 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/1/1/#laws.2.32.0">1Sp1994 c 1 art 2 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.15.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.4.5.0">2005 c 136 art 4 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.47.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/49/#laws.0.22.0">2013 c 49 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.1352"><b>609.1352</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.16.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 16</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.14">
        <h1 class="shn">609.14 REVOCATION OF STAY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Grounds.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When it appears that the defendant has violated any of the conditions of probation or intermediate sanction, or has otherwise been guilty of misconduct that warrants the adjudication of guilt, or imposition or execution of sentence, the court may without notice revoke the stay and direct that the defendant be taken into immediate custody. Revocation shall only be used as a last resort when rehabilitation has failed.</p>
          <p>(b) When it appears that the defendant violated any of the conditions of probation during the term of the stay, but the term of the stay has since expired, the defendant's probation officer or the prosecutor may ask the court to initiate probation revocation proceedings under the Rules of Criminal Procedure at any time within six months after the expiration of the stay. The court also may initiate proceedings under these circumstances on its own motion. If proceedings are initiated within this six-month period, the court may conduct a revocation hearing and take any action authorized under rule <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/court_rules/cr/id/27/#27.04">27.04</a> at any time during or after the six-month period.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> or any law to the contrary, after proceedings to revoke the stay have been initiated by a court order revoking the stay and directing either that the defendant be taken into custody or that a summons be issued in accordance with paragraph (a), the proceedings to revoke the stay may be concluded and the summary hearing provided by subdivision 2 may be conducted after the expiration of the stay or after the six-month period set forth in paragraph (b). The proceedings to revoke the stay shall not be dismissed on the basis that the summary hearing is conducted after the term of the stay or after the six-month period. The ability or inability to locate or apprehend the defendant prior to the expiration of the stay or during or after the six-month period shall not preclude the court from conducting the summary hearing unless the defendant demonstrates that the delay was purposefully caused by the state in order to gain an unfair advantage.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Violations where policies favor continued rehabilitation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Correctional treatment is better provided through a community resource than through confinement and would not unduly depreciate the seriousness of the violation if probation was not revoked. Policies favoring probation outweigh the need for confinement if a person has not previously violated a condition of probation or intermediate sanction in an open criminal case and does any of the following in violation of a condition imposed by the court:</p>
          <p>(1) fails to abstain from the use of controlled substances without a valid prescription, unless the person is under supervision for a violation of section:</p>
          <p>(i) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a>;</p>
          <p>(ii) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112#stat.609.2112.1">609.2112, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), clauses (2) to (6); or</p>
          <p>(iii) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113#stat.609.2113.1">609.2113, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (2) to (6); 2, clauses (2) to (6); or 3, clauses (2) to (6);</p>
          <p>(2) fails to abstain from the use of alcohol, unless the person is under supervision for a violation of section:</p>
          <p>(i) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a>;</p>
          <p>(ii) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112#stat.609.2112.1">609.2112, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), clauses (2) to (6); or</p>
          <p>(iii) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113#stat.609.2113.1">609.2113, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (2) to (6); 2, clauses (2) to (6); or 3, clauses (2) to (6);</p>
          <p>(3) possesses drug paraphernalia in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.092">152.092</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) fails to obtain or maintain employment;</p>
          <p>(5) fails to pursue a course of study or vocational training;</p>
          <p>(6) fails to report a change in employment, unless the person is prohibited from having contact with minors and the employment would involve such contact;</p>
          <p>(7) violates a curfew;</p>
          <p>(8) fails to report contact with a law enforcement agency, unless the person was charged with a misdemeanor, gross misdemeanor, or felony; or</p>
          <p>(9) commits any offense for which the penalty is a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) A violation by a person described in paragraph (a) does not warrant the imposition or execution of sentence and the court may not direct that the person be taken into immediate custody unless the court receives a written report, signed under penalty of perjury pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/358.116">358.116</a>, showing probable cause to believe the person violated probation and establishing by a preponderance of the evidence that the continued presence of the person in the community would present a risk to public safety. If the court does not direct that the person be taken into custody, the court may request a supplemental report from the supervising agent containing:</p>
          <p>(1) the specific nature of the violation;</p>
          <p>(2) the response of the person under supervision to the violation, if any; and</p>
          <p>(3) the actions the supervising agent has taken or will take to address the violation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notification of grounds for revocation.</span></h2>
          <p>The defendant shall thereupon be notified in writing and in such manner as the court directs of the grounds alleged to exist for revocation of the stay. If such grounds are brought in issue by the defendant, a summary hearing shall be held thereon at which the defendant is entitled to be heard and to be represented by counsel.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Alternatives to incarceration.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A probation agent must present the court with local options to address and correct the violation including, but not limited to, inpatient chemical dependency treatment when the defendant at a summary hearing provided by subdivision 2 is:</p>
          <p>(1) a nonviolent controlled substance offender;</p>
          <p>(2) subject to supervised probation;</p>
          <p>(3) appearing based on a technical violation; and</p>
          <p>(4) admitting or found to have violated any of the conditions of probation.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this subdivision, "nonviolent controlled substance offender" is a person who meets the criteria described under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.0513#stat.244.0513.2">244.0513, subdivision 2</a>, clauses (1), (2), and (5), and "technical violation" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.195">244.195, subdivision </a>15.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>If any of such grounds are found to exist the court may:</p>
          <p>(1) if imposition of sentence was previously stayed, again stay sentence or impose sentence and stay the execution thereof, and in either event place the defendant on probation or order intermediate sanctions pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>, or impose sentence and order execution thereof;</p>
          <p>(2) if sentence was previously imposed and execution thereof stayed, continue such stay and place the defendant on probation or order intermediate sanctions in accordance with the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>, or order execution of the sentence previously imposed; or</p>
          <p>(3) if adjudication was stayed or prosecution was deferred, continue the stay without intermediate sanctions, continue it with intermediate sanctions, or adjudicate guilt and proceed as otherwise provided, including, in the event of a felony conviction, as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.10">244.10</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Restoration to liberty.</span></h2>
          <p>If none of such grounds are found to exist, the defendant shall be restored to liberty under the previous order of the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.14.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, "stay" means a stay of adjudication, a stay of imposition, a stay of execution, or a deferred prosecution.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.14.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/610/#laws.0.5.0">1984 c 610 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/579/#laws.0.5.0">1990 c 579 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.10.14.0">1993 c 326 art 10 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.17.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.3.12.0">2017 c 95 art 3 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.17.32.0">2023 c 52 art 17 s 32</a>-34; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.10.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 10</a>-13</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.145">
        <h1 class="shn">609.145 CREDIT FOR PRIOR IMPRISONMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.145.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Prior imprisonment reduction.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person has been imprisoned pursuant to a conviction which is set aside and is thereafter convicted of a crime growing out of the same act or omission, the period of imprisonment to which the person is sentenced is reduced by the period of the prior imprisonment and the time earned thereby in diminution of sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.145.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Reduction for time served before commitment to commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>A sentence of imprisonment upon conviction of a felony is reduced by the period of confinement of the defendant following the conviction and before the defendant's commitment to the commissioner of corrections for execution of sentence unless the court otherwise directs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.145.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Credit.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is to be committed to the commissioner, the person's probation officer must provide to the court, prior to the sentencing hearing, the amount of time the person has in credit for prior imprisonment. The court must pronounce credit for prior imprisonment at the time of sentencing.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.145.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.145; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/723/#laws.1.14.0">1978 c 723 art 1 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.5.11.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 5 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.15">
        <h1 class="shn">609.15 MULTIPLE SENTENCES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.15.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Concurrent, consecutive sentences; specification requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (c), when separate sentences of imprisonment are imposed on a defendant for two or more crimes, whether charged in a single indictment or information or separately, or when a person who is under sentence of imprisonment in this state is being sentenced to imprisonment for another crime committed prior to or while subject to such former sentence, the court in the later sentences shall specify whether the sentences shall run concurrently or consecutively. If the court does not so specify, the sentences shall run concurrently.</p>
          <p>(b) When a court imposes sentence for a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor offense and specifies that the sentence shall run consecutively to any other sentence, the court may order the defendant to serve time in custody for the consecutive sentence in addition to any time in custody the defendant may be serving for any other offense, including probationary jail time or imprisonment for any felony offense.</p>
          <p>(c) An inmate of a state prison who is convicted of committing an assault within the correctional facility is subject to the consecutive sentencing provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2232">609.2232</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.15.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Limit on sentences; misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>If the court specifies that the sentence shall run consecutively and all of the sentences are for misdemeanors, the total of the sentences shall not exceed one year. If the sentences are for a gross misdemeanor and one or more misdemeanors, the total of the sentences shall not exceed two years. If all of the sentences are for gross misdemeanors, the total of the sentences shall not exceed four years.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.15.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.2.8.0">1992 c 571 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.13.26.0">1993 c 326 art 13 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/615/#laws.0.25.0">1994 c 615 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.8.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 8</a>; art 9 s 35; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/2/#laws.0.63.0">1Sp1997 c 2 s 63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/194/#laws.0.10.0">1999 c 194 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.152"><b>609.152</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.16.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 16</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.153">
        <h1 class="shn">609.153 INCREASED PENALTIES FOR CERTAIN MISDEMEANORS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.153.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies to the following misdemeanor-level crimes: sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.093">152.093</a> (manufacture or delivery of drug paraphernalia prohibited); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.095">152.095</a> (advertisement of drug paraphernalia prohibited); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a> (prostitution); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3243">609.3243</a> (loitering with intent to participate in prostitution); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.546">609.546</a> (motor vehicle tampering); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595">609.595</a> (damage to property); and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.66">609.66</a> (dangerous weapons); misdemeanor-level violations of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.605">609.605</a> (trespass); and violations of local ordinances prohibiting the unlawful sale or possession of controlled substances.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.153.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Custodial arrest.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/court_rules/cr/id/6/#6.01">rule 6.01</a> of the Rules of Criminal Procedure, a peace officer acting without a warrant who has decided to proceed with the prosecution of a person for committing a crime described in subdivision 1 may arrest and take the person into custody if the officer has reason to believe the person has a prior conviction for any crime described in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.153.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Increased penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the statutory maximum penalty otherwise applicable to the offense, a person who commits a misdemeanor-level crime described in subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the court determines at the time of sentencing that the person has two or more prior convictions in this or any other state for any of the crimes described in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.153.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notice to complaining witness.</span></h2>
          <p>A prosecuting authority who is responsible for filing charges against or prosecuting a person arrested under the circumstances described in subdivision 2 shall make reasonable efforts to notify the complaining witness of the final outcome of the criminal proceeding that resulted from the arrest including, where appropriate, the decision to dismiss or not file charges against the arrested person.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.153.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.9.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.14.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.155"><b>609.155</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/723/#laws.1.19.0">1978 c 723 art 1 s 19</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.16"><b>609.16</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/723/#laws.1.19.0">1978 c 723 art 1 s 19</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.165">
        <h1 class="shn">609.165 RESTORATION OF CIVIL RIGHTS; POSSESSION OF FIREARMS AND AMMUNITION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Restoration.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person has been deprived of civil rights by reason of conviction of a crime and is thereafter discharged, such discharge shall restore the person to all civil rights and to full citizenship, the same as if such conviction had not taken place, and the order of discharge shall so provide.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Certain convicted felons ineligible to possess firearms or ammunition.</span></h2>
          <p>The order of discharge must provide that a person who has been convicted of a crime of violence, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.712#stat.624.712.5">624.712, subdivision 5</a>, is not entitled to ship, transport, possess, or receive a firearm or ammunition for the remainder of the person's lifetime. Any person who has received such a discharge and who thereafter has received a relief of disability under United States Code, title 18, section 925, or whose ability to possess firearms and ammunition has been restored under subdivision 1d, shall not be subject to the restrictions of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Violation and penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any person who has been convicted of a crime of violence, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.712#stat.624.712.5">624.712, subdivision 5</a>, and who ships, transports, possesses, or receives a firearm or ammunition, commits a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A conviction and sentencing under this section shall be construed to bar a conviction and sentencing for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713#stat.624.713.2">624.713, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The criminal penalty in paragraph (a) does not apply to any person who has received a relief of disability under United States Code, title 18, section 925, or whose ability to possess firearms and ammunition has been restored under subdivision 1d.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/61/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 61 s 2</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.1d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1d.<span class="headnote">Judicial restoration of ability to possess firearms and ammunition by felon.</span></h2>
          <p>A person prohibited by state law from shipping, transporting, possessing, or receiving a firearm or ammunition because of a conviction or a delinquency adjudication for committing a crime of violence may petition a court to restore the person's ability to possess, receive, ship, or transport firearms and otherwise deal with firearms and ammunition.</p>
          <p>The court may grant the relief sought if the person shows good cause to do so and the person has been released from physical confinement.</p>
          <p>If a petition is denied, the person may not file another petition until three years have elapsed without the permission of the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Discharge.</span></h2>
          <p>The discharge may be:</p>
          <p>(1) by order of the court following stay of sentence or stay of execution of sentence; or</p>
          <p>(2) upon expiration of sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.165.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to a forfeiture of and disqualification for public office as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.42#stat.609.42.2">609.42, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.165.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.165; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/654/#laws.0.15.0">1973 c 654 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/271/#laws.0.6.0">1975 c 271 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/723/#laws.1.15.0">1978 c 723 art 1 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/276/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 276 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.3.9.0">1994 c 636 art 3 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.4.7.0">1996 c 408 art 4 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/376/#laws.0.5.0">1998 c 376 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/28/#laws.3.3.0">2003 c 28 art 3 s 3</a>-5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/83/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 83 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.3.18.0">2015 c 65 art 3 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/12/#laws.0.7.0">2023 c 12 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.166"><b>609.166</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.9.10.0">1996 c 408 art 9 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.167"><b>609.167</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.9.10.0">1996 c 408 art 9 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.168"><b>609.168</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.9.10.0">1996 c 408 art 9 s 10</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">ANTICIPATORY CRIMES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.17">
        <h1 class="shn">609.17 ATTEMPTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.17.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to commit a crime, does an act which is a substantial step toward, and more than preparation for, the commission of the crime is guilty of an attempt to commit that crime, and may be punished as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.17.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Act defined.</span></h2>
          <p>An act may be an attempt notwithstanding the circumstances under which it was performed or the means employed to commit the crime intended or the act itself were such that the commission of the crime was not possible, unless such impossibility would have been clearly evident to a person of normal understanding.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.17.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a defense to a charge of attempt that the crime was not committed because the accused desisted voluntarily and in good faith and abandoned the intention to commit the crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.17.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever attempts to commit a crime may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the maximum sentence provided for the crime is life imprisonment, to not more than 20 years; or</p>
          <p>(2) for any other attempt, to not more than one-half of the maximum imprisonment or fine or both provided for the crime attempted, but such maximum in any case shall not be less than imprisonment for 90 days or a fine of $100.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.17.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.17; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.175">
        <h1 class="shn">609.175 CONSPIRACY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.175.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">To cause arrest or prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever conspires with another to cause a third person to be arrested or prosecuted on a criminal charge knowing the charge to be false is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.175.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">To commit crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever conspires with another to commit a crime and in furtherance of the conspiracy one or more of the parties does some overt act in furtherance of such conspiracy may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the crime intended is a misdemeanor, by a sentence to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $300, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the crime intended is murder in the first degree or treason, to imprisonment for not more than 20 years; or</p>
          <p>(3) if the crime intended is any other felony or a gross misdemeanor, to imprisonment or to payment of a fine of not more than one-half the imprisonment or fine provided for that felony or gross misdemeanor or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.175.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Application of section jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies if:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant in this state conspires with another outside of this state; or</p>
          <p>(2) the defendant outside of this state conspires with another in this state; or</p>
          <p>(3) the defendant outside of this state conspires with another outside of this state and an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy is committed within this state by either of them; or</p>
          <p>(4) the defendant in this state conspires with another in this state.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.175.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.175; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.37.0">1971 c 23 s 37</a>,38; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/279/#laws.0.1.0">1975 c 279 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HOMICIDE; BODILY HARM; SUICIDE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.18">
        <h1 class="shn">609.18 DEFINITION.</h1>
        <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2662">609.2662</a>, "premeditation" means to consider, plan or prepare for, or determine to commit, the act referred to prior to its commission.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.18.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.2.0">1986 c 388 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.184"><b>609.184</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.16.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 16</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.185">
        <h1 class="shn">609.185 MURDER IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>(a) Whoever does any of the following is guilty of murder in the first degree and shall be sentenced to imprisonment for life:</p>
        <p>(1) causes the death of a human being with premeditation and with intent to effect the death of the person or of another;</p>
        <p>(2) causes the death of a human being while committing or attempting to commit criminal sexual conduct in the first or second degree with force or violence, either upon or affecting the person or another;</p>
        <p>(3) causes the death of a human being with intent to effect the death of the person or another, while committing or attempting to commit burglary, aggravated robbery, carjacking in the first or second degree, kidnapping, arson in the first or second degree, a drive-by shooting, tampering with a witness in the first degree, escape from custody, or any felony violation of chapter 152 involving the unlawful sale of a controlled substance;</p>
        <p>(4) causes the death of a peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or a guard employed at a Minnesota state or local correctional facility, with intent to effect the death of that person or another, while the person is engaged in the performance of official duties;</p>
        <p>(5) causes the death of a minor while committing child abuse, when the perpetrator has engaged in a past pattern of child abuse upon a child and the death occurs under circumstances manifesting an extreme indifference to human life;</p>
        <p>(6) causes the death of a human being while committing domestic abuse, when the perpetrator has engaged in a past pattern of domestic abuse upon the victim or upon another family or household member and the death occurs under circumstances manifesting an extreme indifference to human life; or</p>
        <p>(7) causes the death of a human being while committing, conspiring to commit, or attempting to commit a felony crime to further terrorism and the death occurs under circumstances manifesting an extreme indifference to human life.</p>
        <p>(b) For the purposes of paragraph (a), clause (4), "prosecuting attorney" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221,</a> subdivision 6, clause (4).</p>
        <p>(c) For the purposes of paragraph (a), clause (4), "judge" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221,</a> subdivision 6, clause (5).</p>
        <p>(d) For purposes of paragraph (a), clause (5), "child abuse" means an act committed against a minor victim that constitutes a violation of the following laws of this state or any similar laws of the United States or any other state: section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.377">609.377</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.378">609.378</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a>.</p>
        <p>(e) For purposes of paragraph (a), clause (6), "domestic abuse" means an act that:</p>
        <p>(1) constitutes a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a>, or any similar laws of the United States or any other state; and</p>
        <p>(2) is committed against the victim who is a family or household member as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (b).</p>
        <p>(f) For purposes of paragraph (a), clause (7), "further terrorism" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.714#stat.609.714.1">609.714, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.185.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.185; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.1.0">1975 c 374 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/227/#laws.0.9.0">1981 c 227 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/662/#laws.0.2.0">1988 c 662 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.2.11.0">1989 c 290 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/583/#laws.0.4.0">1990 c 583 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.4.5.0">1992 c 571 art 4 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.19.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.12.0">1995 c 244 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.3.12.0">1995 c 259 art 3 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.7.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/437/#laws.0.5.0">2000 c 437 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/401/#laws.1.15.0">2002 c 401 art 1 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.10.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/302/#laws.0.1.0">2014 c 302 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.20.18.0">2023 c 52 art 20 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/85/#laws.0.106.0">2024 c 85 s 106</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.19">
        <h1 class="shn">609.19 MURDER IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.19.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Intentional murder; drive-by shootings.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does either of the following is guilty of murder in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 40 years:</p>
          <p>(1) causes the death of a human being with intent to effect the death of that person or another, but without premeditation; or</p>
          <p>(2) causes the death of a human being while committing or attempting to commit a drive-by shooting in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.66#stat.609.66.1e">609.66, subdivision 1e</a>, under circumstances other than those described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, paragraph (a), clause (3).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.19.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Unintentional murders.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does either of the following is guilty of unintentional murder in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 40 years:</p>
          <p>(1) causes the death of a human being, without intent to effect the death of any person, while committing or attempting to commit a felony offense other than criminal sexual conduct in the first or second degree with force or violence or a drive-by shooting; or</p>
          <p>(2) causes the death of a human being without intent to effect the death of any person, while intentionally inflicting or attempting to inflict bodily harm upon the victim, when the perpetrator is restrained under an order for protection and the victim is a person designated to receive protection under the order. As used in this clause, "order for protection" includes an order for protection issued under chapter 518B; a harassment restraining order issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.748">609.748</a>; a court order setting conditions of pretrial release or conditions of a criminal sentence or juvenile court disposition; a restraining order issued in a marriage dissolution action; and any order issued by a court of another state or of the United States that is similar to any of these orders.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.19.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/227/#laws.0.10.0">1981 c 227 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.4.6.0">1992 c 571 art 4 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.2.16.0">1995 c 226 art 2 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.4.8.0">1996 c 408 art 4 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.8.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.99.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 99</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.195">
        <h1 class="shn">609.195 MURDER IN THE THIRD DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>(a) Whoever, without intent to effect the death of any person, causes the death of another by perpetrating an act eminently dangerous to others and evincing a depraved mind, without regard for human life, is guilty of murder in the third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years.</p>
        <p>(b) Whoever, without intent to cause death, proximately causes the death of a human being by, directly or indirectly, unlawfully selling, giving away, bartering, delivering, exchanging, distributing, or administering a controlled substance classified in Schedule I or II, is guilty of murder in the third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.195.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.195; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/130/#laws.0.3.0">1977 c 130 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/227/#laws.0.11.0">1981 c 227 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/176/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 176 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.196"><b>609.196</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.16.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 16</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.20">
        <h1 class="shn">609.20 MANSLAUGHTER IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of manslaughter in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) intentionally causes the death of another person in the heat of passion provoked by such words or acts of another as would provoke a person of ordinary self-control under like circumstances, provided that the crying of a child does not constitute provocation;</p>
        <p>(2) violates section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a> and causes the death of another or causes the death of another in committing or attempting to commit a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor offense with such force and violence that death of or great bodily harm to any person was reasonably foreseeable, and murder in the first or second degree was not committed thereby;</p>
        <p>(3) intentionally causes the death of another person because the actor is coerced by threats made by someone other than the actor's coconspirator and which cause the actor reasonably to believe that the act performed by the actor is the only means of preventing imminent death to the actor or another;</p>
        <p>(4) proximately causes the death of another, without intent to cause death by, directly or indirectly, unlawfully selling, giving away, bartering, delivering, exchanging, distributing, or administering a controlled substance classified in Schedule III, IV, or V; or</p>
        <p>(5) causes the death of another in committing or attempting to commit a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.377">609.377</a> (malicious punishment of a child), and murder in the first, second, or third degree is not committed thereby.</p>
        <p>As used in this section, a "person of ordinary self-control" does not include a person under the influence of intoxicants or a controlled substance.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.20.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/227/#laws.0.12.0">1981 c 227 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.3.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/176/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 176 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/604/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 604 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.13.0">1995 c 244 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.13.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.205">
        <h1 class="shn">609.205 MANSLAUGHTER IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>A person who causes the death of another by any of the following means is guilty of manslaughter in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) by the person's culpable negligence whereby the person creates an unreasonable risk, and consciously takes chances of causing death or great bodily harm to another; or</p>
        <p>(2) by shooting another with a firearm or other dangerous weapon as a result of negligently believing the other to be a deer or other animal; or</p>
        <p>(3) by setting a spring gun, pit fall, deadfall, snare, or other like dangerous weapon or device; or</p>
        <p>(4) by negligently or intentionally permitting any animal, known by the person to have vicious propensities or to have caused great or substantial bodily harm in the past, to run uncontrolled off the owner's premises, or negligently failing to keep it properly confined; or</p>
        <p>(5) by committing or attempting to commit a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.378">609.378</a> (neglect or endangerment of a child), and murder in the first, second, or third degree is not committed thereby.</p>
        <p>If proven by a preponderance of the evidence, it shall be an affirmative defense to criminal liability under clause (4) that the victim provoked the animal to cause the victim's death.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.205.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.205; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/294/#laws.0.6.0">1985 c 294 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.5.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.14.0">1995 c 244 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
