      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2111">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2111 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <p class="in">(a) For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2111">609.2111</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114">609.2114</a>, the terms defined in this subdivision have the meanings given them.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) "Motor vehicle" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, and includes attached trailers.</p>
        <p class="in">(c) "Controlled substance" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.4">152.01, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        <p class="in">(d) "Intoxicating substance" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03#stat.169A.03.11a">169A.03, subdivision 11a</a>.</p>
        <p class="in">(e) "Qualified prior driving offense" includes a prior conviction:</p>
        <p>(1) for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.20">169A.20</a> under the circumstances described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.24">169A.24</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.25">169A.25</a>;</p>
        <p>(2) under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112#stat.609.2112.1">609.2112, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), clauses (2) to (6); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113">609.2113, subdivision </a>1, clauses (2) to (6); 2, clauses (2) to (6); or 3, clauses (2) to (6); or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114#stat.609.2114.1">609.2114, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), clauses (2) to (6); or 2, clauses (2) to (6);</p>
        <p>(3) under Minnesota Statutes 2012, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.21#stat.609.21.1">609.21, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (2) to (6); or</p>
        <p>(4) under Minnesota Statutes 2006, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.21#stat.609.21.1">609.21, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (2) to (6); 2, clauses (2) to (6); 2a, clauses (2) to (6); 2b, clauses (2) to (6); 3, clauses (2) to (6); or 4, clauses (2) to (6).</p>
        <p>(f) "Artificially derived cannabinoid" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01, subdivision </a>6.</p>
        <p>(g) "Cannabis flower" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01#stat.342.01.16">342.01, subdivision 16</a>.</p>
        <p>(h) "Cannabis product" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01#stat.342.01.20">342.01, subdivision 20</a>.</p>
        <p>(i) "Hemp-derived consumer product" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01</a>, subdivision 37.</p>
        <p>(j) "Lower-potency hemp edible" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01, subdivision </a>50.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2111.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/602/#laws.4.1.0">1990 c 602 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/442/#laws.0.33.0">1996 c 442 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.3.11.0">2007 c 54 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.6.0">2014 c 180 s 6</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/109/#laws.0.1.0">2016 c 109 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/195/#laws.3.18.0">2018 c 195 art 3 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.90.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 90</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.38.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 38</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2112">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2112 CRIMINAL VEHICULAR HOMICIDE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2112.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Criminal vehicular homicide.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), a person is guilty of criminal vehicular homicide and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the person causes the death of a human being not constituting murder or manslaughter as a result of operating a motor vehicle:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in a grossly negligent manner;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in a negligent manner while under the influence of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) alcohol;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(iii) cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) any combination of those elements;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, as measured within two hours of the time of driving;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in a negligent manner while under the influence of an intoxicating substance and the person knows or has reason to know that the substance has the capacity to cause impairment;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in a negligent manner while any amount of a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II, or its metabolite, other than cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols, is present in the person's body;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) where the driver who causes the collision leaves the scene of the collision in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.09#stat.169.09.1">169.09, subdivision 1</a> or 6; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) where the driver had actual knowledge that a peace officer had previously issued a citation or warning that the motor vehicle was defectively maintained, the driver had actual knowledge that remedial action was not taken, the driver had reason to know that the defect created a present danger to others, and the death was caused by the defective maintenance.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) If a person is sentenced under paragraph (a) for a violation under paragraph (a), clauses (2) to (6), occurring within ten years of a qualified prior driving offense, the statutory maximum sentence of imprisonment is 15 years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2112.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defense.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">It shall be an affirmative defense to a charge under subdivision 1, clause (6), that the defendant used the controlled substance according to the terms of a prescription issued for the defendant in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.11">152.11</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.12">152.12</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2112.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.21; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/12/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 12 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/622/#laws.0.24.0">1984 c 622 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.4.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 4</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.6.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 6</a>; art 10 s 7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/602/#laws.4.1.0">1990 c 602 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.14.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/442/#laws.0.33.0">1996 c 442 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/283/#laws.0.13.0">2004 c 283 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.3.7.0">2007 c 54 art 3 s 7</a>,8,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.4.0">2014 c 180 s 4</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/186/#laws.0.2.0">2014 c 186 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/109/#laws.0.2.0">2016 c 109 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/195/#laws.3.19.0">2018 c 195 art 3 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.39.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 39</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2113">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2113 CRIMINAL VEHICULAR OPERATION; BODILY HARM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2113.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Great bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person is guilty of criminal vehicular operation resulting in great bodily harm and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the person causes great bodily harm to another not constituting attempted murder or assault as a result of operating a motor vehicle:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in a grossly negligent manner;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in a negligent manner while under the influence of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) alcohol;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(iii) cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) any combination of those elements;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, as measured within two hours of the time of driving;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in a negligent manner while under the influence of an intoxicating substance and the person knows or has reason to know that the substance has the capacity to cause impairment;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in a negligent manner while any amount of a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II, or its metabolite, other than cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols, is present in the person's body;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) where the driver who causes the accident leaves the scene of the accident in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.09#stat.169.09.1">169.09, subdivision 1</a> or 6; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) where the driver had actual knowledge that a peace officer had previously issued a citation or warning that the motor vehicle was defectively maintained, the driver had actual knowledge that remedial action was not taken, the driver had reason to know that the defect created a present danger to others, and the injury was caused by the defective maintenance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2113.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Substantial bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person is guilty of criminal vehicular operation resulting in substantial bodily harm and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the person causes substantial bodily harm to another as a result of operating a motor vehicle:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in a grossly negligent manner;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in a negligent manner while under the influence of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) alcohol;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(iii) cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) any combination of those elements;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, as measured within two hours of the time of driving;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in a negligent manner while under the influence of an intoxicating substance and the person knows or has reason to know that the substance has the capacity to cause impairment;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in a negligent manner while any amount of a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II, or its metabolite, other than cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols, is present in the person's body;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) where the driver who causes the accident leaves the scene of the accident in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.09#stat.169.09.1">169.09, subdivision 1</a> or 6; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) where the driver had actual knowledge that a peace officer had previously issued a citation or warning that the motor vehicle was defectively maintained, the driver had actual knowledge that remedial action was not taken, the driver had reason to know that the defect created a present danger to others, and the injury was caused by the defective maintenance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2113.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person is guilty of criminal vehicular operation resulting in bodily harm and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the person causes bodily harm to another as a result of operating a motor vehicle:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in a grossly negligent manner;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in a negligent manner while under the influence of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) alcohol;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(iii) cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) any combination of those elements;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, as measured within two hours of the time of driving;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in a negligent manner while under the influence of an intoxicating substance and the person knows or has reason to know that the substance has the capacity to cause impairment;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in a negligent manner while any amount of a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II, or its metabolite, other than cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols, is present in the person's body;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) where the driver who causes the accident leaves the scene of the accident in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.09#stat.169.09.1">169.09, subdivision 1</a> or 6; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) where the driver had actual knowledge that a peace officer had previously issued a citation or warning that the motor vehicle was defectively maintained, the driver had actual knowledge that remedial action was not taken, the driver had reason to know that the defect created a present danger to others, and the injury was caused by the defective maintenance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2113.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be an affirmative defense to a charge under subdivisions 1, clause (6); 2, clause (6); and 3, clause (6), that the defendant used the controlled substance according to the terms of a prescription issued for the defendant in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.11">152.11</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.12">152.12</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2113.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/12/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 12 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/622/#laws.0.25.0">1984 c 622 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.4.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 4</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.7.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 7</a>; art 10 s 7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/602/#laws.4.1.0">1990 c 602 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.15.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 15</a>,16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/442/#laws.0.33.0">1996 c 442 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/283/#laws.0.13.0">2004 c 283 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.3.7.0">2007 c 54 art 3 s 7</a>,8,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.5.0">2014 c 180 s 5</a>,7,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/195/#laws.3.20.0">2018 c 195 art 3 s 20</a>-22; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.40.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 40</a>-42</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2114">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2114 CRIMINAL VEHICULAR OPERATION; UNBORN CHILD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2114.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Death to an unborn child.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), a person is guilty of criminal vehicular operation resulting in death to an unborn child and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the person causes the death of an unborn child as a result of operating a motor vehicle:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in a grossly negligent manner;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in a negligent manner while under the influence of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) alcohol;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(iii) cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) any combination of those elements;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, as measured within two hours of the time of driving;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in a negligent manner while under the influence of an intoxicating substance and the person knows or has reason to know that the substance has the capacity to cause impairment;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in a negligent manner while any amount of a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II, or its metabolite, other than cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols, is present in the person's body;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) where the driver who causes the accident leaves the scene of the accident in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.09#stat.169.09.1">169.09, subdivision 1</a> or 6; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) where the driver had actual knowledge that a peace officer had previously issued a citation or warning that the motor vehicle was defectively maintained, the driver had actual knowledge that remedial action was not taken, the driver had reason to know that the defect created a present danger to others, and the injury was caused by the defective maintenance.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) If a person is sentenced under paragraph (a) for a violation under paragraph (a), clauses (2) to (6), occurring within ten years of a qualified prior driving offense, the statutory maximum sentence of imprisonment is 15 years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2114.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Injury to an unborn child.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person is guilty of criminal vehicular operation resulting in injury to an unborn child and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the person causes the great bodily harm to an unborn child subsequently born alive as a result of operating a motor vehicle:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in a grossly negligent manner;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) in a negligent manner while under the influence of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) alcohol;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(iii) cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) any combination of those elements;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) while having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, as measured within two hours of the time of driving;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in a negligent manner while under the influence of an intoxicating substance and the person knows or has reason to know that the substance has the capacity to cause impairment;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) in a negligent manner while any amount of a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II, or its metabolite, other than cannabis flower, a cannabis product, a lower-potency hemp edible, a hemp-derived consumer product, artificially derived cannabinoids, or tetrahydrocannabinols, is present in the person's body;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) where the driver who causes the accident leaves the scene of the accident in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.09#stat.169.09.1">169.09, subdivision 1</a> or 6; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) where the driver had actual knowledge that a peace officer had previously issued a citation or warning that the motor vehicle was defectively maintained, the driver had actual knowledge that remedial action was not taken, the driver had reason to know that the defect created a present danger to others, and the injury was caused by the defective maintenance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2114.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Conviction not bar to punishment for other crimes.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A prosecution for or a conviction of a crime under this section relating to causing death or injury to an unborn child is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2114.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be an affirmative defense to a charge under subdivisions 1, clause (6), and 2, clause (6), that the defendant used the controlled substance according to the terms of a prescription issued for the defendant in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.11">152.11</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.12">152.12</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2114.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.3.0">1986 c 388 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.10.7.0">1989 c 290 art 10 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/602/#laws.4.1.0">1990 c 602 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.17.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 17</a>,18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/442/#laws.0.33.0">1996 c 442 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/283/#laws.0.13.0">2004 c 283 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.3.8.0">2007 c 54 art 3 s 8</a>,9,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.8.0">2014 c 180 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/109/#laws.0.3.0">2016 c 109 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/195/#laws.3.23.0">2018 c 195 art 3 s 23</a>,24; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.43.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 43</a>,44</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.215">
        <h1 class="shn">609.215 SUICIDE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.215.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Aiding suicide.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally advises, encourages, or assists another in taking the other's own life may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.215.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Aiding attempted suicide.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally advises, encourages, or assists another who attempts but fails to take the other's own life may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than seven years or to payment of a fine of not more than $14,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.215.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Acts or omissions not considered aiding suicide or aiding attempted suicide.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A health care provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145B.02#stat.145B.02.6">145B.02, subdivision 6</a>, who administers, prescribes, or dispenses medications or procedures to relieve another person's pain or discomfort, even if the medication or procedure may hasten or increase the risk of death, does not violate this section unless the medications or procedures are knowingly administered, prescribed, or dispensed to cause death.</p>
          <p>(b) A health care provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145B.02#stat.145B.02.6">145B.02, subdivision 6</a>, who withholds or withdraws a life-sustaining procedure in compliance with chapter 145B or 145C or in accordance with reasonable medical practice does not violate this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.215.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Injunctive relief.</span></h2>
          <p>A cause of action for injunctive relief may be maintained against any person who is reasonably believed to be about to violate or who is in the course of violating this section by any person who is:</p>
          <p>(1) the spouse, parent, child, or sibling of the person who would commit suicide;</p>
          <p>(2) an heir or a beneficiary under a life insurance policy of the person who would commit suicide;</p>
          <p>(3) a health care provider of the person who would commit suicide;</p>
          <p>(4) a person authorized to prosecute or enforce the laws of this state; or</p>
          <p>(5) a legally appointed guardian or conservator of the person who would have committed suicide.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.215.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Civil damages.</span></h2>
          <p>A person given standing by subdivision 4, clause (1), (2), or (5), or the person who would have committed suicide, in the case of an attempt, may maintain a cause of action against any person who violates or who attempts to violate subdivision 1 or 2 for compensatory damages and punitive damages as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/549.20">549.20</a>. A person described in subdivision 4, clause (4), may maintain a cause of action against a person who violates or attempts to violate subdivision 1 or 2 for a civil penalty of up to $50,000 on behalf of the state. An action under this subdivision may be brought whether or not the plaintiff had prior knowledge of the violation or attempt.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.215.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Attorney fees.</span></h2>
          <p>Reasonable attorney fees shall be awarded to the prevailing plaintiff in a civil action brought under subdivision 4 or 5.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.215.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.215; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/577/#laws.0.6.0">1992 c 577 s 6</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/399/#laws.0.37.0">1998 c 399 s 37</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The words "advises" and "encourages" were severed from subdivision 1 as unconstitutional in <i>State v. Melchert-Dinkel</i>, 844 N.W.2d 13 (Minn. 2014).</p>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.22"><b>609.22</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.25.0">1979 c 258 s 25</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST THE PERSON</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.221">
        <h1 class="shn">609.221 ASSAULT IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.221.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Great bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults another and inflicts great bodily harm may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.221.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of deadly force against peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee.</span></h2>
          <p> Whoever assaults a peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee by using or attempting to use deadly force against the officer, attorney, judge, or employee while the person is engaged in the performance of a duty imposed by law, policy, or rule may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.221.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Great bodily harm; peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults a peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee and inflicts great bodily harm on the officer, attorney, judge, or employee while the person is engaged in the performance of a duty imposed by law, policy, or rule may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.221.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Use of dangerous weapon or deadly force resulting in great bodily harm against peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults and inflicts great bodily harm upon a peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee with a dangerous weapon or by using or attempting to use deadly force against the officer, attorney, judge, or employee while the person is engaged in the performance of a duty imposed by law, policy, or rule may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 30 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.221.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Mandatory sentences for assaults against a peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person convicted of assaulting a peace officer, prosecuting attorney, judge, or correctional employee shall be committed to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for not less than:</p>
          <p>(1) ten years, nor more than 20 years, for a violation of subdivision 2;</p>
          <p>(2) 15 years, nor more than 25 years, for a violation of subdivision 3; or</p>
          <p>(3) 25 years, nor more than 30 years, for a violation of subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(b) A defendant convicted and sentenced as required by this subdivision is not eligible for probation, parole, discharge, work release, or supervised release, until that person has served the full term of imprisonment as provided by law, notwithstanding the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.26">241.26</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/242.19">242.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05">243.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.04">244.04</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.12">609.12</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>, the court may not stay the imposition or execution of this sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.221.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p> As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "correctional employee" means an employee of a public or private prison, jail, or workhouse;</p>
          <p>(2) "deadly force" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.066#stat.609.066.1">609.066, subdivision 1</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) "peace officer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) "prosecuting attorney" means an attorney, with criminal prosecution or civil responsibilities, who is the attorney general, a political subdivision's elected or appointed county or city attorney, or a deputy, assistant, or special assistant of any of these; and</p>
          <p>(5) "judge" means a judge or justice of any court of this state that is established by the Minnesota Constitution.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.221.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.4.0">1979 c 258 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.8.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.10.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/302/#laws.0.2.0">2014 c 302 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.222">
        <h1 class="shn">609.222 ASSAULT IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.222.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Dangerous weapon.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults another with a dangerous weapon may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than seven years or to payment of a fine of not more than $14,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.222.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Dangerous weapon; substantial bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults another with a dangerous weapon and inflicts substantial bodily harm may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.222.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.5.0">1979 c 258 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/53/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 53 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.9.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.4.7.0">1992 c 571 art 4 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.223">
        <h1 class="shn">609.223 ASSAULT IN THE THIRD DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.223.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Substantial bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults another and inflicts substantial bodily harm may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.223.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Past pattern of child abuse.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults a minor may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the perpetrator has engaged in a past pattern of child abuse against the minor. As used in this subdivision, "child abuse" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, paragraph (a), clause (5).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.223.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Felony; victim under four.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults a victim under the age of four, and causes bodily harm to the child's head, eyes, or neck, or otherwise causes multiple bruises to the body, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.223.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.6.0">1979 c 258 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.10.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/542/#laws.0.17.0">1990 c 542 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.20.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.100.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 100</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2231">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2231 ASSAULT IN THE FOURTH DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Peace officers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this subdivision, "peace officer" means a person who is licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.845#stat.626.845.1">626.845, subdivision 1</a>, and effecting a lawful arrest or executing any other duty imposed by law.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever physically assaults a peace officer is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) Whoever commits either of the following acts against a peace officer is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $6,000, or both: (1) physically assaults the officer if the assault inflicts demonstrable bodily harm; or (2) intentionally throws or otherwise transfers bodily fluids or feces at or onto the officer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Firefighters and emergency medical personnel.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults any of the following persons and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) a member of a municipal or volunteer fire department or emergency medical services personnel unit in the performance of the member's duties; or</p>
          <p>(2) a physician, nurse, or other person providing health care services in a hospital emergency department.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Certain Department of Natural Resources employees.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm on an employee of the Department of Natural Resources who is engaged in forest fire activities is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Correctional employees; prosecuting attorneys; judges; probation officers.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever commits either of the following acts against an employee of a correctional facility as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.021">241.021,</a> subdivision 1i, against a prosecuting attorney as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221,</a> subdivision 6, clause (4), against a judge as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221,</a> subdivision 6, clause (5), or against a probation officer or other qualified person employed in supervising offenders while the person is engaged in the performance of a duty imposed by law, policy, or rule is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults the person and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally throws or otherwise transfers bodily fluids or feces at or onto the person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Secure treatment facility personnel.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this subdivision, "secure treatment facility" includes facilities listed in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.02#stat.253B.02.18a">253B.02, subdivision 18a</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253D.02#stat.253D.02.13">253D.02, subdivision 13</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever, while committed under chapter 253D, Minnesota Statutes 2012, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.185">253B.185</a>, or Minnesota Statutes 1992, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/526.10">526.10</a>, commits either of the following acts against an employee or other individual who provides care or treatment at a secure treatment facility while the person is engaged in the performance of a duty imposed by law, policy, or rule is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults the person and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally throws or otherwise transfers bodily fluids or feces at or onto the person.</p>
          <p>(c) Whoever, while committed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.18">253B.18</a>, or admitted under the provision of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.10#stat.253B.10.1">253B.10, subdivision 1</a>, commits either of the following acts against an employee or other individual who supervises and works directly with patients at a secure treatment facility while the person is engaged in the performance of a duty imposed by law, policy, or rule, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults the person and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally throws or otherwise transfers urine, blood, semen, or feces onto the person.</p>
          <p>(d) The court shall commit a person convicted of violating paragraph (b) to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for not less than one year and one day. The court may not, on its own motion or the prosecutor's motion, sentence a person without regard to this paragraph. A person convicted and sentenced as required by this paragraph is not eligible for probation, parole, discharge, work release, or supervised release, until that person has served the full term of imprisonment as provided by law, notwithstanding the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.26">241.26</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/242.19">242.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05">243.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.04">244.04</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.12">609.12</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) Notwithstanding the statutory maximum sentence provided in paragraph (b), when a court sentences a person to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for a violation of paragraph (b), the court shall provide that after the person has been released from prison, the commissioner shall place the person on conditional release for five years. The terms of conditional release are governed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.05">244.05</a> and 609.3455, subdivision 6, 7, or 8; and Minnesota Statutes 2004, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.109">609.109</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Assaults motivated by bias.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever assaults another in whole or in substantial part because of the victim's or another's actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>, or because of the victim's actual or perceived association with another person or group of a certain actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates the provisions of paragraph (a) within five years of a previous conviction under paragraph (a) is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than one year and a day or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">School official.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults a school official while the official is engaged in the performance of the official's duties, and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. As used in this subdivision, "school official" includes teachers, school administrators, and other employees of a public or private school.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Public employees with mandated duties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults an agricultural inspector, occupational safety and health investigator, child protection worker, public health nurse, animal control officer, or probation or parole officer while the employee is engaged in the performance of a duty mandated by law, court order, or ordinance;</p>
          <p>(2) knows that the victim is a public employee engaged in the performance of the official public duties of the office; and</p>
          <p>(3) inflicts demonstrable bodily harm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Community crime prevention group members.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults a community crime prevention group member while the member is engaged in neighborhood patrol;</p>
          <p>(2) should reasonably know that the victim is a community crime prevention group member engaged in neighborhood patrol; and</p>
          <p>(3) inflicts demonstrable bodily harm.</p>
          <p>(b) As used in this subdivision, "community crime prevention group" means a community group focused on community safety and crime prevention that:</p>
          <p>(1) is organized for the purpose of discussing community safety and patrolling community neighborhoods for criminal activity;</p>
          <p>(2) is designated and trained by the local law enforcement agency as a community crime prevention group; or</p>
          <p>(3) interacts with local law enforcement regarding community safety issues.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Vulnerable adults.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this subdivision, "vulnerable adult" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.232#stat.609.232.11">609.232, subdivision 11</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever assaults and inflicts demonstrable bodily harm on a vulnerable adult, knowing or having reason to know that the person is a vulnerable adult, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Reserve officer.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults a reserve officer as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (e), who is engaged in the performance of official public duties at the direction of, under the control of, or on behalf of a peace officer or supervising law enforcement officer or agency; and</p>
          <p>(2) should reasonably know that the victim is a reserve officer engaged in the performance of official public duties of the peace officer, or supervising law enforcement officer or agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Utility and postal service employees and contractors.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who:</p>
          <p>(1) assaults an employee or contractor of a utility or the United States Postal Service while the employee or contractor is engaged in the performance of the employee's or contractor's duties;</p>
          <p>(2) should reasonably know that the victim is an employee or contractor of a utility or the postal service who is:</p>
          <p>(i) performing duties of the victim's employment; or</p>
          <p>(ii) fulfilling the victim's contractual obligations; and</p>
          <p>(3) inflicts demonstrable bodily harm.</p>
          <p>(b) As used in this subdivision, "utility" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.594">609.594</a>, subdivision 1, clause (3).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2231.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Transit operators.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if (1) the person assaults a transit operator, or intentionally throws or otherwise transfers bodily fluids onto a transit operator; and (2) the transit operator is acting in the course of the operator's duties and is operating a transit vehicle, aboard a transit vehicle, or otherwise responsible for a transit vehicle. A person convicted under this paragraph may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) For the purposes of this subdivision, "transit operator" means a driver or operator of a transit vehicle that is used to provide any of the following services:</p>
          <p>(1) public transportation, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/174.22#stat.174.22.7">174.22, subdivision 7</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) light rail transit service;</p>
          <p>(3) special transportation service under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.386">473.386</a>, whether provided by the Metropolitan Council or by other providers under contract with the council; or</p>
          <p>(4) commuter rail service.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2231.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/169/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 169 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>;       <div class="section" id="stat.609.2232">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2232 CONSECUTIVE SENTENCES FOR ASSAULTS COMMITTED BY STATE PRISON INMATES.</h1>
        <p>If an inmate of a state correctional facility is convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, while confined in the facility, the sentence imposed for the assault shall be executed and run consecutively to any unexpired portion of the offender's earlier sentence. The inmate is not entitled to credit against the sentence imposed for the assault for time served in confinement for the earlier sentence. The inmate shall serve the sentence for the assault in a state correctional facility even if the assault conviction was for a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2232.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.9.37.0">1997 c 239 art 9 s 37</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2233">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2233 FELONY ASSAULT MOTIVATED BY BIAS; INCREASED STATUTORY MAXIMUM SENTENCE.</h1>
        <p>A person who violates section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223 in whole or in substantial part</a> because of the victim's or another person's actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>, or because of the victim's actual or perceived association with another person or group of a certain actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>, is subject to a statutory maximum penalty of 25 percent longer than the maximum penalty otherwise applicable.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2233.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.4.14.0">2016 c 189 art 4 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.5.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.224">
        <h1 class="shn">609.224 ASSAULT IN THE FIFTH DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.224.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following commits an assault and is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) commits an act with intent to cause fear in another of immediate bodily harm or death; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally inflicts or attempts to inflict bodily harm upon another.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.224.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever violates the provisions of subdivision 1 against the same victim within ten years of a previous qualified domestic violence-related offense conviction or adjudication of delinquency is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates the provisions of subdivision 1 within three years of a previous qualified domestic violence-related offense conviction or adjudication of delinquency is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.224.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Firearms.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a person is convicted of a violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, the court shall determine and make written findings on the record as to whether:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant owns or possesses a firearm; and</p>
          <p>(2) the firearm was used in any way during the commission of the assault.</p>
          <p>(b) Except as otherwise provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242#stat.609.2242.3">609.2242, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (c), a person is not entitled to possess a pistol if the person has been convicted after August 1, 1992, of assault in the fifth degree if the offense was committed within three years of a previous conviction under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, unless three years have elapsed from the date of conviction and, during that time, the person has not been convicted of any other violation of this section. Property rights may not be abated but access may be restricted by the courts. A person who possesses a pistol in violation of this paragraph is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.224.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever violates the provisions of subdivision 1 against the same victim within ten years of the first of any combination of two or more previous qualified domestic violence-related offense convictions or adjudications of delinquency is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates the provisions of subdivision 1 within three years of the first of any combination of two or more previous qualified domestic violence-related offense convictions or adjudications of delinquency is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.224.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.7.0">1979 c 258 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/169/#laws.0.2.0">1983 c 169 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/159/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 159 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.7.0">1987 c 329 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/537/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 537 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.6.13.0">1992 c 571 art 6 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.11.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 11</a>,12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/5/#laws.0.2.0">1Sp1993 c 5 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.3.10.0">1994 c 636 art 3 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.2.1.0">1995 c 229 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.3.13.0">1995 c 259 art 3 s 13</a>,14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.21.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 21</a>,22; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/437/#laws.0.6.0">2000 c 437 s 6</a>,7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.10.8.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 10 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.16.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 16</a>,17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/28/#laws.0.8.0">2011 c 28 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.91.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 91</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2241">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2241 KNOWING TRANSFER OF COMMUNICABLE DISEASE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2241.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given:</p>
          <p>(a) "Communicable disease" means a disease or condition that causes serious illness, serious disability, or death; the infectious agent of which may pass or be carried from the body of one person to the body of another through direct transmission.</p>
          <p>(b) "Direct transmission" means predominately sexual or blood-borne transmission.</p>
          <p>(c) "A person who knowingly harbors an infectious agent" refers to a person who receives from a physician or other health professional:</p>
          <p>(1) advice that the person harbors an infectious agent for a communicable disease;</p>
          <p>(2) educational information about behavior which might transmit the infectious agent; and</p>
          <p>(3) instruction of practical means of preventing such transmission.</p>
          <p>(d) "Transfer" means to engage in behavior that has been demonstrated epidemiologically to be a mode of direct transmission of an infectious agent which causes the communicable disease.</p>
          <p>(e) "Sexual penetration" means any of the acts listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.12">609.341, subdivision 12</a>, when the acts described are committed without the use of a latex or other effective barrier.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2241.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a crime, which may be prosecuted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.17">609.17</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, for a person who knowingly harbors an infectious agent to transfer, if the crime involved:</p>
          <p>(1) sexual penetration with another person without having first informed the other person that the person has a communicable disease;</p>
          <p>(2) transfer of blood, sperm, organs, or tissue, except as deemed necessary for medical research or if disclosed on donor screening forms; or</p>
          <p>(3) sharing of nonsterile syringes or needles for the purpose of injecting drugs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2241.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It is an affirmative defense to prosecution, if it is proven by a preponderance of the evidence, that:</p>
          <p>(1) the person who knowingly harbors an infectious agent for a communicable disease took practical means to prevent transmission as advised by a physician or other health professional; or</p>
          <p>(2) the person who knowingly harbors an infectious agent for a communicable disease is a health care provider who was following professionally accepted infection control procedures.</p>
          <p>Nothing in this section shall be construed to be a defense to a criminal prosecution that does not allege a violation of subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2241.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Health Department data.</span></h2>
          <p>Data protected by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.3805#stat.13.3805.1">13.3805, subdivision 1</a>, and information collected as part of a Health Department investigation under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a> may not be accessed or subpoenaed by law enforcement authorities or prosecutors without the consent of the subject of the data.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2241.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.2.17.0">1995 c 226 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/227/#laws.0.22.0">1999 c 227 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2242">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2242 DOMESTIC ASSAULT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2242.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following against a family or household member as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>, commits an assault and is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) commits an act with intent to cause fear in another of immediate bodily harm or death; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally inflicts or attempts to inflict bodily harm upon another.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2242.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 1 within ten years of a previous qualified domestic violence-related offense conviction or an adjudication of delinquency is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2242.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Domestic assaults; firearms.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a person is convicted of a violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2247">609.2247</a>, the court shall determine and make written findings on the record as to whether:</p>
          <p>(1) the assault was committed against a family or household member, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) the defendant owns or possesses a firearm; and</p>
          <p>(3) the firearm was used in any way during the commission of the assault.</p>
          <p>(b) If the court determines that the assault was of a family or household member, and that the offender owns or possesses a firearm and used it in any way during the commission of the assault, it shall order that the firearm be summarily forfeited under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5316#stat.609.5316.3">609.5316, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) When a person is convicted of assaulting a family or household member and is determined by the court to have used a firearm in any way during commission of the assault, the court may order that the person is prohibited from possessing any type of firearm for any period longer than three years or for the remainder of the person's life. A person who violates this paragraph is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. At the time of the conviction, the court shall inform the defendant for how long the defendant is prohibited from possessing a firearm and that it is a gross misdemeanor to violate this paragraph. The failure of the court to provide this information to a defendant does not affect the applicability of the firearm possession prohibition or the gross misdemeanor penalty to that defendant.</p>
          <p>(d) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (c), when a person is convicted of a violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a> and the court determines that the victim was a family or household member, the court shall inform the defendant that the defendant is prohibited from possessing a firearm for three years from the date of conviction and that it is a gross misdemeanor offense to violate this prohibition. The failure of the court to provide this information to a defendant does not affect the applicability of the firearm possession prohibition or the gross misdemeanor penalty to that defendant.</p>
          <p>(e) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (c), a person is not entitled to possess a pistol if the person has been convicted after August 1, 1992, or a firearm if a person has been convicted on or after August 1, 2014, of domestic assault under this section or assault in the fifth degree under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a> and the assault victim was a family or household member as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>, unless three years have elapsed from the date of conviction and, during that time, the person has not been convicted of any other violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>. Property rights may not be abated but access may be restricted by the courts. A person who possesses a firearm in violation of this paragraph is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(f) Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b) and (h), when a person is convicted of a violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2247">609.2247 </a>and the court determines that the assault was against a family or household member, the court shall order the defendant to transfer any firearms that the person possesses, within three business days, to a federally licensed firearms dealer, a law enforcement agency, or a third party who may lawfully receive them. The transfer may be permanent or temporary, unless the court prohibits the person from possessing a firearm for the remainder of the person's life under paragraph (c). A temporary firearm transfer only entitles the receiving party to possess the firearm. A temporary transfer does not transfer ownership or title. A defendant may not transfer firearms to a third party who resides with the defendant. If a defendant makes a temporary transfer, a federally licensed firearms dealer or law enforcement agency may charge the defendant a reasonable fee to store the person's firearms and may establish policies for disposal of abandoned firearms, provided such policies require that the person be notified by certified mail prior to disposal of abandoned firearms. For temporary firearms transfers under this paragraph, a law enforcement agency, federally licensed firearms dealer, or third party shall exercise due care to preserve the quality and function of the transferred firearms and shall return the transferred firearms to the person upon request after the expiration of the prohibiting time period imposed under this subdivision, provided the person is not otherwise prohibited from possessing firearms under state or federal law. The return of temporarily transferred firearms to a person shall comply with state and federal law. If a defendant permanently transfers the defendant's firearms to a law enforcement agency, the agency is not required to compensate the defendant and may charge the defendant a reasonable processing fee. A law enforcement agency is not required to accept a person's firearm under this paragraph. The court shall order that the person surrender all permits to carry and purchase firearms to the sheriff.</p>
          <p>(g) A defendant who is ordered to transfer firearms under paragraph (f) must file proof of transfer as provided for in this paragraph. If the transfer is made to a third party, the third party must sign an affidavit under oath before a notary public either acknowledging that the defendant permanently transferred the defendant's firearms to the third party or agreeing to temporarily store the defendant's firearms until such time as the defendant is legally permitted to possess firearms. The affidavit shall indicate the serial number, make, and model of all firearms transferred by the defendant to the third party. The third party shall acknowledge in the affidavit that the third party may be held criminally and civilly responsible under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.7144">624.7144</a> if the defendant gains access to a transferred firearm while the firearm is in the custody of the third party. If the transfer is to a law enforcement agency or federally licensed firearms dealer, the law enforcement agency or federally licensed firearms dealer shall provide proof of transfer to the defendant. The proof of transfer must specify whether the firearms were permanently or temporarily transferred and include the name of the defendant, date of transfer, and the serial number, make, and model of all transferred firearms. The defendant shall provide the court with a signed and notarized affidavit or proof of transfer as described in this section within two business days of the firearms transfer. The court shall seal affidavits and proofs of transfer filed pursuant to this paragraph.</p>
          <p>(h) When a person is convicted of a violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2247">609.2247</a>, and the court determines that the assault was against a family or household member, the court shall determine by a preponderance of the evidence if the person poses an imminent risk of causing another person substantial bodily harm. Upon a finding of imminent risk, the court shall order that the local law enforcement agency take immediate possession of all firearms in the person's possession. The local law enforcement agency shall exercise due care to preserve the quality and function of the defendant's firearms and shall return the firearms to the person upon request after the expiration of the prohibiting time period, provided the person is not otherwise prohibited from possessing firearms under state or federal law. The local law enforcement agency shall, upon written notice from the person, transfer the firearms to a federally licensed firearms dealer or a third party who may lawfully receive them.
