Before a local law enforcement agency transfers a firearm under this paragraph, the agency shall require the third party or federally licensed firearms dealer receiving the firearm to submit an affidavit or proof of transfer that complies with the requirements for affidavits or proofs of transfer established in paragraph (g). The agency shall file all affidavits or proofs of transfer received with the court within two business days of the transfer. The court shall seal all affidavits or proofs of transfer filed pursuant to this paragraph. A federally licensed firearms dealer or third party who accepts a firearm transfer pursuant to this paragraph shall comply with paragraphs (f) and (g) as if accepting transfer from the defendant. If the law enforcement agency does not receive written notice from the defendant within three business days, the agency may charge a reasonable fee to store the defendant's firearms. A law enforcement agency may establish policies for disposal of abandoned firearms, provided such policies require that the person be notified via certified mail prior to disposal of abandoned firearms.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2242.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates the provisions of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224#stat.609.224.1">609.224, subdivision 1</a>, within ten years of the first of any combination of two or more previous qualified domestic violence-related offense convictions or adjudications of delinquency is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2242.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.3.15.0">1995 c 259 art 3 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/437/#laws.0.8.0">2000 c 437 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.10.10.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 10 s 10</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.12.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.18.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 18</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/47/#laws.0.3.0">2013 c 47 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/213/#laws.0.3.0">2014 c 213 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2243">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2243 SENTENCING; REPEAT DOMESTIC ASSAULT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2243.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted of gross misdemeanor domestic assault under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242#stat.609.2242.2">609.2242, subdivision 2</a>, shall be sentenced to a minimum of 20 days imprisonment, at least 96 hours of which must be served consecutively. The court may stay execution of the minimum sentence required under this subdivision on the condition that the person sentenced complete anger therapy or counseling and fulfill any other condition, as ordered by the court; provided, however, that the court shall revoke the stay of execution and direct the person to be taken into immediate custody if it appears that the person failed to attend or complete the ordered therapy or counseling, or violated any other condition of the stay of execution. If the court finds at the revocation hearing required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.14#stat.609.14.2">609.14, subdivision 2</a>, that the person failed to attend or complete the ordered therapy, or violated any other condition of the stay of execution, the court shall order execution of the sentence previously imposed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2243.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b), in determining an appropriate disposition for felony domestic assault under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242#stat.609.2242.4">609.2242, subdivision 4</a>, the court shall presume that a stay of execution with at least a 45-day period of incarceration as a condition of probation shall be imposed. If the court imposes a stay of execution with a period of incarceration as a condition of probation, at least 15 days must be served consecutively.</p>
          <p>(b) If the defendant's criminal history score, determined according to the Sentencing Guidelines, indicates a presumptive executed sentence, that sentence shall be imposed unless the court departs from the Sentencing Guidelines pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.10">244.10</a>. A stay of imposition of sentence under this paragraph may be granted only if accompanied by a statement on the record of the reasons for it.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2243.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.23.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 23</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2244">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2244 PRESENTENCE DOMESTIC ABUSE INVESTIGATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2244.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Investigation.</span></h2>
          <p>A presentence domestic abuse investigation must be conducted and a report submitted to the court by the corrections agency responsible for conducting the investigation when:</p>
          <p>(1) a defendant is convicted of an offense described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a defendant is arrested for committing an offense described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>, but is convicted of another offense arising out of the same circumstances surrounding the arrest; or</p>
          <p>(3) a defendant is convicted of a violation against a family or household member of: (a) an order for protection under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01">518B.01</a>; (b) a harassment restraining order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.748">609.748</a>; (c) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.79#stat.609.79.1">609.79, subdivision 1</a>; or (d) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713#stat.609.713.1">609.713, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2244.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Report.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The Department of Corrections shall establish minimum standards for the report, including the circumstances of the offense, impact on the victim, the defendant's prior record, characteristics and history of alcohol and chemical use problems, and amenability to domestic abuse programs. The report is classified as private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>. Victim impact statements are confidential.</p>
          <p>(b) The report must include:</p>
          <p>(1) a recommendation on any limitations on contact with the victim and other measures to ensure the victim's safety;</p>
          <p>(2) a recommendation for the defendant to enter and successfully complete domestic abuse programming and any aftercare found necessary by the investigation, including a specific recommendation for the defendant to complete a domestic abuse counseling program or domestic abuse educational program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.02">518B.02</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) a recommendation for chemical dependency evaluation and treatment as determined by the evaluation whenever alcohol or drugs were found to be a contributing factor to the offense;</p>
          <p>(4) recommendations for other appropriate remedial action or care or a specific explanation why no level of care or action is recommended; and</p>
          <p>(5) consequences for failure to abide by conditions set up by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2244.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Corrections agents standards; rules; investigation time limits.</span></h2>
          <p>A domestic abuse investigation required by this section must be conducted by the local Corrections Department or the commissioner of corrections. The corrections agent shall have access to any police reports or other law enforcement data relating to the current offense or previous offenses that are necessary to complete the evaluation. A corrections agent conducting an investigation under this section may not have any direct or shared financial interest or referral relationship resulting in shared financial gain with a treatment provider. An appointment for the defendant to undergo the investigation must be made by the court, a court services probation officer, or court administrator as soon as possible.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2244.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.10.20.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 10 s 20</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2244.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.24.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.7.18.0">1997 c 239 art 7 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.5.6.0">1998 c 367 art 5 s 6</a>,7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.10.12.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 10 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2245">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2245 FEMALE GENITAL MUTILATION; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2245.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as otherwise permitted in subdivision 2, whoever knowingly circumcises, excises, or infibulates, in whole or in part, the labia majora, labia minora, or clitoris of another is guilty of a felony. Consent to the procedure by a minor on whom it is performed or by the minor's parent is not a defense to a violation of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2245.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Permitted activities.</span></h2>
          <p>A surgical procedure is not a violation of subdivision 1 if the procedure:</p>
          <p>(1) is necessary to the health of the person on whom it is performed and is performed by: (i) a physician licensed under chapter 147; (ii) a physician in training under the supervision of a licensed physician; or (iii) a certified nurse midwife practicing within the nurse midwife's legal scope of practice; or</p>
          <p>(2) is performed on a person who is in labor or who has just given birth and is performed for medical purposes connected with that labor or birth: (i) by a physician licensed under chapter 147; (ii) a physician in training under the supervision of a licensed physician; or (iii) a certified nurse midwife practicing within the nurse midwife's legal scope of practice.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2245.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.22.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.11.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.2246"><b>609.2246</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/43/#laws.0.32.0">2013 c 43 s 32</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2247">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2247 DOMESTIC ASSAULT BY STRANGULATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2247.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Family or household members" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.2">518B.01, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) "Strangulation" means intentionally impeding normal breathing or circulation of the blood by applying pressure on the throat or neck or by blocking the nose or mouth of another person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2247.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless a greater penalty is provided elsewhere, whoever assaults a family or household member by strangulation is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2247.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.13.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.225"><b>609.225</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.25.0">1979 c 258 s 25</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.226">
        <h1 class="shn">609.226 HARM CAUSED BY DOG.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.226.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Great or substantial bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who causes great or substantial bodily harm to another by negligently or intentionally permitting any dog to run uncontrolled off the owner's premises, or negligently failing to keep it properly confined is guilty of a misdemeanor. A person who is convicted of a second or subsequent violation of this section involving the same dog is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.226.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Dangerous dogs.</span></h2>
          <p>If the owner of a dangerous dog, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/347.50#stat.347.50.2">347.50, subdivision 2</a>, has been convicted of a misdemeanor under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/347.55">347.55</a>, and the same dog causes bodily injury to a person other than the owner, the owner is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.226.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>If proven by a preponderance of the evidence, it shall be an affirmative defense to liability under subdivision 1 or 2 that the victim provoked the dog to cause the victim's bodily harm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.226.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Harm to service animal caused by dog; crime, mandatory restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this subdivision, "service animal" means an animal individually trained or being trained to do work or perform tasks for the benefit of an individual with a disability.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who negligently or intentionally (1) permits the person's dog to run uncontrolled off the person's premises, or (2) fails to keep the person's dog properly confined or controlled; and as a result the dog causes bodily harm to a service animal or otherwise renders a service animal unable to perform its duties, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) The court shall order a person convicted of violating this subdivision to pay restitution for the costs and expenses resulting from the crime. Costs and expenses include, but are not limited to, the service animal user's loss of income, veterinary expenses, transportation costs, and other expenses of temporary replacement assistance services, and service animal replacement or retraining costs incurred by a school, agency, or individual. If the court finds that the convicted person is indigent, the court may reduce the amount of restitution to a reasonable level or order it paid in installments.</p>
          <p>(d) This subdivision does not preclude a person from seeking any available civil remedies for an act that violates this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.226.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/294/#laws.0.7.0">1985 c 294 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/711/#laws.0.8.0">1988 c 711 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/37/#laws.0.13.0">1989 c 37 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/159/#laws.0.1.0">2004 c 159 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.227">
        <h1 class="shn">609.227 DANGEROUS ANIMALS DESTROYED.</h1>
        <p>When a person has been charged with a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.205">609.205</a>, clause (4), or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.226#stat.609.226.2">609.226, subdivision 2</a> or 3, or a gross misdemeanor violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.226#stat.609.226.1">609.226, subdivision 1</a>, the court shall order that the animal which caused the death or injury be seized by the appropriate local law enforcement agency. The animal shall be killed in a proper and humane manner if the person has been convicted of the crime for which the animal was seized. The owner of the animal shall pay the cost of confining and killing the animal. This section shall not preempt local ordinances with more restrictive provisions.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.227.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/294/#laws.0.8.0">1985 c 294 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/711/#laws.0.9.0">1988 c 711 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.228">
        <h1 class="shn">609.228 GREAT BODILY HARM CAUSED BY DISTRIBUTION OF DRUGS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever proximately causes great bodily harm by, directly or indirectly, unlawfully selling, giving away, bartering, delivering, exchanging, distributing, or administering a controlled substance classified in Schedule I or II may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.228.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/176/#laws.0.3.0">1987 c 176 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.229">
        <h1 class="shn">609.229 CRIME COMMITTED FOR BENEFIT OF GANG.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.229.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "criminal gang" means any ongoing organization, association, or group of three or more persons, whether formal or informal, that:</p>
          <p>(1) has, as one of its primary activities, the commission of one or more of the offenses listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.11#stat.609.11.9">609.11, subdivision 9</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) has a common name or common identifying sign or symbol; and</p>
          <p>(3) includes members who individually or collectively engage in or have engaged in a pattern of criminal activity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.229.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crimes.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who commits a crime for the benefit of, at the direction of, in association with, or motivated by involvement with a criminal gang, with the intent to promote, further, or assist in criminal conduct by gang members is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.229.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the crime committed in violation of subdivision 2 is a felony, the statutory maximum for the crime is five years longer than the statutory maximum for the underlying crime. If the crime committed in violation of subdivision 2 is a felony, and the victim of the crime is a child under the age of 18 years, the statutory maximum for the crime is ten years longer than the statutory maximum for the underlying crime.</p>
          <p>(b) If the crime committed in violation of subdivision 2 is a misdemeanor, the person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) If the crime committed in violation of subdivision 2 is a gross misdemeanor, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $15,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.229.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Mandatory minimum sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Unless a longer mandatory minimum sentence is otherwise required by law, or the court imposes a longer aggravated durational departure, or a longer prison sentence is presumed under the Sentencing Guidelines and imposed by the court, a person convicted of a crime described in subdivision 3, paragraph (a), shall be committed to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for not less than one year plus one day.</p>
          <p>(b) Any person convicted and sentenced as required by paragraph (a) is not eligible for probation, parole, discharge, work release, or supervised release until that person has served the full term of imprisonment as provided by law, notwithstanding the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/242.19">242.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05">243.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.04">244.04</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.12">609.12</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.229.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/279/#laws.0.30.0">1991 c 279 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.13.29.0">1993 c 326 art 13 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.9.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 9</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.14.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.23">
        <h1 class="shn">609.23 MISTREATMENT OF PERSONS CONFINED.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, being in charge of or employed in any institution, whether public or private, intentionally abuses or ill-treats any person confined therein who is mentally or physically disabled or who is involuntarily confined therein by order of court or other duly constituted authority may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.23.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.23; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.231">
        <h1 class="shn">609.231 MISTREATMENT OF RESIDENTS OR PATIENTS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, being in charge of or employed in any facility required to be licensed under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.02">144A.02</a>, intentionally abuses, ill-treats, or culpably neglects any patient or resident therein to the patient's or resident's physical detriment may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.231.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/688/#laws.0.9.0">1973 c 688 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.60.0">1976 c 173 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.232">
        <h1 class="shn">609.232 CRIMES AGAINST VULNERABLE ADULTS; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2325">609.2325</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.233">609.233</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2335">609.2335</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.234">609.234</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Caregiver.</span></h2>
          <p>"Caregiver" means an individual or facility who has responsibility for the care of a vulnerable adult as a result of a family relationship, or who has assumed responsibility for all or a portion of the care of a vulnerable adult voluntarily, by contract, or by agreement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Facility.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Facility" means a hospital or other entity required to be licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>; a nursing home required to be licensed to serve adults under section 144A.02; a home care provider licensed or required to be licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.43">144A.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.482">144A.482</a>; a residential or nonresidential facility required to be licensed to serve adults under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.01">245A.01</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.16">245A.16</a>; or a person or organization that exclusively offers, provides, or arranges for personal care assistance services under the medical assistance program as authorized under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0651">256B.0651</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0653">256B.0653</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) For home care providers and personal care attendants, the term "facility" refers to the provider or person or organization that exclusively offers, provides, or arranges for personal care services, and does not refer to the client's home or other location at which services are rendered.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Immediately.</span></h2>
          <p>"Immediately" means as soon as possible, but no longer than 24 hours from the time of initial knowledge that the incident occurred has been received.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Legal authority.</span></h2>
          <p>"Legal authority" includes, but is not limited to:</p>
          <p>(1) a fiduciary obligation recognized elsewhere in law, including pertinent regulations;</p>
          <p>(2) a contractual obligation; or</p>
          <p>(3) documented consent by a competent person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Maltreatment.</span></h2>
          <p>"Maltreatment" means any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) abuse under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2325">609.2325</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) neglect under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.233">609.233</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) financial exploitation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2335">609.2335</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Operator.</span></h2>
          <p>"Operator" means any person whose duties and responsibilities evidence actual control of administrative activities or authority for the decision making of or by a facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Person" means any individual, corporation, firm, partnership, incorporated and unincorporated association, or any other legal, professional, or commercial entity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Report.</span></h2>
          <p>"Report" means a statement concerning all the circumstances surrounding the alleged or suspected maltreatment, as defined in this section, of a vulnerable adult which are known to the reporter at the time the statement is made.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Therapeutic conduct.</span></h2>
          <p>"Therapeutic conduct" means the provision of program services, health care, or other personal care services done in good faith in the interests of the vulnerable adult by: (1) an individual, facility or employee, or person providing services in a facility under the rights, privileges, and responsibilities conferred by state license, certification, or registration; or (2) a caregiver.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.232.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Vulnerable adult.</span></h2>
          <p>"Vulnerable adult" means any person 18 years of age or older who:</p>
          <p>(1) is a resident inpatient of a facility;</p>
          <p>(2) receives services at or from a facility required to be licensed to serve adults under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.01">245A.01</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.15">245A.15</a>, except that a person receiving outpatient services for treatment of chemical dependency or mental illness, or one who is committed as a sexual psychopathic personality or as a sexually dangerous person under chapter 253B, is not considered a vulnerable adult unless the person meets the requirements of clause (4);</p>
          <p>(3) receives services from a home care provider required to be licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.43">144A.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.482">144A.482</a>; or from a person or organization that exclusively offers, provides, or arranges for personal care assistance services under the medical assistance program as authorized under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0651">256B.0651</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>; or</p>
          <p>(4) regardless of residence or whether any type of service is received, possesses a physical or mental infirmity or other physical, mental, or emotional dysfunction:</p>
          <p>(i) that impairs the individual's ability to provide adequately for the individual's own care without assistance, including the provision of food, shelter, clothing, health care, or supervision; and</p>
          <p>(ii) because of the dysfunction or infirmity and the need for assistance, the individual has an impaired ability to protect the individual from maltreatment.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.232.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.2.2.0">1995 c 229 art 2 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.6.19.0">2009 c 79 art 6 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/262/#laws.4.9.0">2014 c 262 art 4 s 9</a>; art 5 s 6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.202.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 202</a>,203</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2325">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2325 CRIMINAL ABUSE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2325.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crimes.</span></h2>
          <p> A caregiver who, with intent to produce physical or mental pain or injury to a vulnerable adult, subjects a vulnerable adult to any aversive or deprivation procedure, unreasonable confinement, or involuntary seclusion, is guilty of criminal abuse and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
          <p>This subdivision does not apply to therapeutic conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2325.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exemptions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, a vulnerable adult is not abused for the sole reason that:</p>
          <p>(1) the vulnerable adult or a person with authority to make health care decisions for the vulnerable adult under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.651">144.651</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.44">144A.44</a>, chapter 145B, 145C, or 252A, or sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.03">253B.03</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-101">524.5-101</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-502">524.5-502</a>, refuses consent or withdraws consent, consistent with that authority and within the boundary of reasonable medical practice, to any therapeutic conduct, including any care, service, or procedure to diagnose, maintain, or treat the physical or mental condition of the vulnerable adult or, where permitted under law, to provide nutrition and hydration parenterally or through intubation; this paragraph does not enlarge or diminish rights otherwise held under law by:</p>
          <p>(i) a vulnerable adult or a person acting on behalf of a vulnerable adult, including an involved family member, to consent to or refuse consent for therapeutic conduct; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a caregiver to offer or provide or refuse to offer or provide therapeutic conduct; or</p>
          <p>(2) the vulnerable adult, a person with authority to make health care decisions for the vulnerable adult, or a caregiver in good faith selects and depends upon spiritual means or prayer for treatment or care of disease or remedial care of the vulnerable adult in lieu of medical care, provided that this is consistent with the prior practice or belief of the vulnerable adult or with the expressed intentions of the vulnerable adult.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2325.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p> A person who violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the act results in the death of a vulnerable adult, imprisonment for not more than 15 years or payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the act results in great bodily harm, imprisonment for not more than ten years or payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(3) if the act results in substantial bodily harm or the risk of death, imprisonment for not more than five years or payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(4) in other cases, imprisonment for not more than 364 days or payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2325.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.2.3.0">1995 c 229 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.10.11.0">1996 c 408 art 10 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/146/#laws.3.43.0">2004 c 146 art 3 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.4.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.233">
        <h1 class="shn">609.233 CRIMINAL NEGLECT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.233.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A caregiver or operator who intentionally neglects a vulnerable adult or knowingly permits conditions to exist that result in the abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. For purposes of this section, "abuse" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572#stat.626.5572.2">626.5572, subdivision 2</a>, and "neglect" means a failure to provide a vulnerable adult with necessary food, clothing, shelter, health care, or supervision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.233.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Felony deprivation.</span></h2>
          <p>A caregiver or operator who intentionally deprives a vulnerable adult of necessary food, clothing, shelter, health care, or supervision, when the caregiver or operator is reasonably able to make the necessary provisions, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3 if:</p>
          <p>(1) the caregiver or operator knows or has reason to know the deprivation could likely result in substantial bodily harm or great bodily harm to the vulnerable adult; or</p>
          <p>(2) the deprivation occurred over an extended period of time.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.233.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exemptions.</span></h2>
          <p>A vulnerable adult is not neglected or deprived under subdivision 1 or 1a for the sole reason that:</p>
          <p>(1) the vulnerable adult or a person with authority to make health care decisions for the vulnerable adult under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.651">144.651</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.44">144A.44</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.03">253B.03</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-101">524.5-101</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-502">524.5-502</a>, or chapter 145B, 145C, or 252A, refuses consent or withdraws consent, consistent with that authority and within the boundary of reasonable medical practice, to any therapeutic conduct, including any care, service, or procedure to diagnose, maintain, or treat the physical or mental condition of the vulnerable adult or, where permitted under law, to provide nutrition and hydration parenterally or through intubation; this paragraph does not enlarge or diminish rights otherwise held under law by:</p>
          <p>(i) a vulnerable adult or a person acting on behalf of a vulnerable adult, including an involved family member, to consent to or refuse consent for therapeutic conduct; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a caregiver to offer or provide or refuse to offer or provide therapeutic conduct;</p>
          <p>(2) the vulnerable adult, a person with authority to make health care decisions for the vulnerable adult, or a caregiver in good faith selects and depends upon spiritual means or prayer for treatment or care of disease or remedial care of the vulnerable adult in lieu of medical care, provided that this is consistent with the prior practice or belief of the vulnerable adult or with the expressed intentions of the vulnerable adult; or</p>
          <p>(3) the vulnerable adult, who is not impaired in judgment or capacity by mental or emotional dysfunction or undue influence, engages in consensual sexual contact with: (i) a person including a facility staff person when a consensual sexual personal relationship existed prior to the caregiving relationship; or (ii) a personal care attendant, regardless of whether the consensual sexual personal relationship existed prior to the caregiving relationship.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.233.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1a may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the conduct results in great bodily harm to the vulnerable adult, imprisonment for not more than ten years or payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the conduct results in substantial bodily harm to the vulnerable adult, imprisonment for not more than five years or payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.233.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defenses.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be an affirmative defense to a prosecution under subdivision 1 or 1a, if proven by a preponderance of evidence, that:</p>
          <p>(1) the defendant is an individual employed by a facility or operator and does not have managerial or supervisory authority, and was unable to reasonably make the necessary provisions because of inadequate staffing levels, inadequate supervision, or institutional policies;</p>
          <p>(2) the defendant is a facility, an operator, or an employee of a facility or operator in a position of managerial or supervisory authority, and did not knowingly, intentionally, or recklessly permit criminal acts by its employees or agents that resulted in the harm to the vulnerable adult; or</p>
          <p>(3) the defendant is a caregiver and failed to perform acts necessary to prevent the applicable level of harm, if any, to the vulnerable adult because the caregiver was acting reasonably and necessarily to provide care to another identified vulnerable adult.</p>
          <p>For these affirmative defenses, a defendant bears only the burden of production. A defendant's failure to meet the burden of production does not relieve the state of its burden of persuasion as to all elements of the offense.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.233.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.2.4.0">1995 c 229 art 2 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/146/#laws.3.44.0">2004 c 146 art 3 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/175/#laws.0.1.0">2012 c 175 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/125/#laws.1.85.0">2013 c 125 art 1 s 85</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2335">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2335 FINANCIAL EXPLOITATION OF VULNERABLE ADULT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2335.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following acts commits the crime of financial exploitation:</p>
          <p>(1) in breach of a fiduciary obligation recognized elsewhere in law, including pertinent regulations, contractual obligations, documented consent by a competent person, or the obligations of a responsible party under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.6501">144.6501</a> intentionally:</p>
          <p>(i) fails to use the real or personal property or other financial resources of the vulnerable adult to provide food, clothing, shelter, health care, therapeutic conduct, or supervision for the vulnerable adult;</p>
          <p>(ii) uses, manages, or takes either temporarily or permanently the real or personal property or other financial resources of the vulnerable adult, whether held in the name of the vulnerable adult or a third party, for the benefit of someone other than the vulnerable adult; or</p>
          <p>(iii) deprives either temporarily or permanently a vulnerable adult of the vulnerable adult's real or personal property or other financial resources, whether held in the name of the vulnerable adult or a third party, for the benefit of someone other than the vulnerable adult; or</p>
          <p>(2) in the absence of legal authority:</p>
          <p>(i) acquires possession or control of an interest in real or personal property or other financial resources of a vulnerable adult, whether held in the name of the vulnerable adult or a third party, through the use of undue influence, harassment, or duress;</p>
          <p>(ii) forces, compels, coerces, or entices a vulnerable adult against the vulnerable adult's will to perform services for the profit or advantage of another; or</p>
          <p>(iii) establishes a relationship with a fiduciary obligation to a vulnerable adult by use of undue influence, harassment, duress, force, compulsion, coercion, or other enticement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2335.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Defenses.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Nothing in this section requires a facility or caregiver to provide financial management or supervise financial management for a vulnerable adult except as otherwise required by law.</p>
          <p>(b) If the actor knew or had reason to know that the vulnerable adult lacked capacity to consent, consent is not a defense to a violation of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2335.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Criminal penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1, clause (1) or (2), item (i), may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>. A person who violates subdivision 1, clause (2), item (ii) or (iii), may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2335.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Aggregation.</span></h2>
          <p>In any prosecution under this section, the value of the money or property or services received by the defendant within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of subdivision 3; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2335.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/627.01">627.01</a>, an offense committed under this section may be prosecuted in: (1) the county where any part of the offense occurred; or (2) the county of residence of the victim or one of the victims.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2335.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.2.5.0">1995 c 229 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/119/#laws.0.8.0">2009 c 119 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/5/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 5 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2336">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2336 DECEPTIVE OR UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES; ELDERLY OR DISABLED VICTIMS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2336.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "charitable solicitation law violation" means a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/309.50">309.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/309.61">309.61</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) "consumer fraud law violation" means a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.68">325F.68</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.70">325F.70</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) "deceptive trade practices law violation" means a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325D.43">325D.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325D.48">325D.48</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) "false advertising law violation" means a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.67">325F.67</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) "disabled person" means a person who has an impairment of physical or mental function or emotional status that substantially limits one or more major life activities;</p>
          <p>(6) "major life activities" means functions such as caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, and working; and</p>
          <p>(7) "senior citizen" means a person who is 65 years of age or older.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2336.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a gross misdemeanor for any person to commit a charitable solicitation law violation, a consumer fraud law violation, a deceptive trade practices law violation, or a false advertising law violation if the person knows or has reason to know that the person's conduct:</p>
          <p>(1) is directed at one or more disabled persons or senior citizens; and</p>
          <p>(2) will cause or is likely to cause a disabled person or a senior citizen to suffer loss or encumbrance of a primary residence, principal employment or other major source of income, substantial loss of property set aside for retirement or for personal or family care and maintenance, substantial loss of pension, retirement plan, or government benefits, or substantial loss of other assets essential to the victim's health or welfare.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.2336.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prosecutorial jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>The attorney general has statewide jurisdiction to prosecute violations of this section. This jurisdiction is concurrent with that of the local prosecuting authority responsible for prosecuting gross misdemeanors in the place where the violation was committed.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2336.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.12.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.234">
        <h1 class="shn">609.234 FAILURE TO REPORT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.234.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Any mandated reporter who is required to report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a>, who knows or has reason to believe that a vulnerable adult is being or has been maltreated, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572#stat.626.5572.15">626.5572, subdivision 15</a>, and who does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally fails to make a report;</p>
          <p>(2) knowingly provides information which is false, deceptive, or misleading; or</p>
          <p>(3) intentionally fails to provide all of the material circumstances surrounding the incident which are known to the reporter when the report is made.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.234.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Increased penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a gross misdemeanor for a person who is mandated to report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a>, who knows or has reason to believe that a vulnerable adult is being or has been maltreated, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572#stat.626.5572.15">626.5572, subdivision 15</a>, to intentionally fail to make a report if:</p>
          <p>(1) the person knows the maltreatment caused or contributed to the death or great bodily harm of a vulnerable adult; and</p>
          <p>(2) the failure to report causes or contributes to the death or great bodily harm of a vulnerable adult or protects the mandated reporter's interests.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.234.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.2.6.0">1995 c 229 art 2 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.235">
        <h1 class="shn">609.235 USE OF DRUGS TO INJURE OR FACILITATE CRIME.</h1>
        <p>Whoever administers to another or causes another to take any poisonous, stupefying, overpowering, narcotic or anesthetic substance with intent thereby to injure or to facilitate the commission of a crime may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.235.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.235; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.24">
        <h1 class="shn">609.24 SIMPLE ROBBERY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, having knowledge of not being entitled thereto, takes personal property from the person or in the presence of another and uses or threatens the imminent use of force against any person to overcome the person's resistance or powers of resistance to, or to compel acquiescence in, the taking or carrying away of the property is guilty of robbery and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.24.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.24; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.245">
        <h1 class="shn">609.245 AGGRAVATED ROBBERY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.245.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">First degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, while committing a robbery, is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the victim to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon, or inflicts bodily harm upon another, is guilty of aggravated robbery in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.245.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, while committing a robbery, implies, by word or act, possession of a dangerous weapon, is guilty of aggravated robbery in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.245.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.245; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.5.0">1988 c 712 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.23.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 23</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.247">
        <h1 class="shn">609.247 CARJACKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.247.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Carjacking" means taking a motor vehicle from the person or in the presence of another while having knowledge of not being entitled to the motor vehicle and using or threatening the imminent use of force against any person to overcome the person's resistance or powers of resistance to, or to compel acquiescence in, the taking of the motor vehicle.</p>
          <p>(c) "Motor vehicle" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, clause (10).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.247.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">First degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, while committing a carjacking, is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the victim to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon, or inflicts bodily harm upon another, is guilty of carjacking in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.247.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, while committing a carjacking, implies, by word or act, possession of a dangerous weapon, is guilty of carjacking in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.247.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Third degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever commits carjacking under any other circumstances is guilty of carjacking in the third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.247.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.6.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.25">
        <h1 class="shn">609.25 KIDNAPPING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.25.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, for any of the following purposes, confines or removes from one place to another, any person without the person's consent or, if the person is under the age of 16 years, without the consent of the person's parents or other legal custodian, is guilty of kidnapping and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2:</p>
          <p>(1) to hold for ransom or reward for release, or as shield or hostage; or</p>
          <p>(2) to facilitate commission of any felony or flight thereafter; or</p>
          <p>(3) to commit great bodily harm or to terrorize the victim or another; or</p>
          <p>(4) to hold in involuntary servitude.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.25.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the victim is released in a safe place without great bodily harm, to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than 40 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both if:</p>
          <p>(i) the victim is not released in a safe place;</p>
          <p>(ii) the victim suffers great bodily harm during the course of the kidnapping; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the person kidnapped is under the age of 16.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.25.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.8.0">1979 c 258 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.24.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.7.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.251">
        <h1 class="shn">609.251 DOUBLE JEOPARDY; KIDNAPPING.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction of the crime of kidnapping is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed during the time of the kidnapping.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.251.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/139/#laws.0.2.0">1983 c 139 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.16.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.255">
        <h1 class="shn">609.255 FALSE IMPRISONMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.255.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, the following term has the meaning given it unless specific content indicates otherwise.</p>
          <p>"Caretaker" means an individual who has responsibility for the care of a child as a result of a family relationship, or who has assumed responsibility for all or a portion of the care of a child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.255.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Intentional restraint.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, knowingly lacking lawful authority to do so, intentionally confines or restrains someone else's child under the age of 18 years without consent of the child's parent or legal custodian, or any other person without the person's consent, is guilty of false imprisonment and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.255.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Unreasonable restraint of children.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A parent, legal guardian, or caretaker who intentionally subjects a child under the age of 18 years to unreasonable physical confinement or restraint by means including but not limited to, tying, locking, caging, or chaining for a prolonged period of time and in a cruel manner which is excessive under the circumstances, is guilty of unreasonable restraint of a child and, except as provided in paragraph (b) or (c), may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) If the confinement or restraint results in demonstrable bodily harm, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) If the confinement or restraint results in substantial bodily harm, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.255.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.255; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/217/#laws.0.2.0">1983 c 217 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/655/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 655 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.12.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/175/#laws.0.2.0">2012 c 175 s 2</a>; 2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.26">
        <h1 class="shn">609.26 DEPRIVING ANOTHER OF CUSTODIAL OR PARENTAL RIGHTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Prohibited acts.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally does any of the following acts may be charged with a felony and, upon conviction, may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 6:</p>
          <p>(1) conceals a minor child from the child's parent where the action manifests an intent substantially to deprive that parent of parental rights or conceals a minor child from another person having the right to parenting time or custody where the action manifests an intent to substantially deprive that person of rights to parenting time or custody;</p>
          <p>(2) takes, obtains, retains, or fails to return a minor child in violation of a court order which has transferred legal custody under chapter 260, 260B, or 260C to the commissioner of human services, a child-placing agency, or the local social services agency;</p>
          <p>(3) takes, obtains, retains, or fails to return a minor child from or to the parent in violation of a court order, where the action manifests an intent substantially to deprive that parent of rights to parenting time or custody;</p>
          <p>(4) takes, obtains, retains, or fails to return a minor child from or to a parent after commencement of an action relating to child parenting time or custody but prior to the issuance of an order determining custody or parenting time rights, where the action manifests an intent substantially to deprive that parent of parental rights;</p>
          <p>(5) retains a child in this state with the knowledge that the child was removed from another state in violation of any of the above provisions;</p>
          <p>(6) refuses to return a minor child to a parent or lawful custodian and is at least 18 years old and more than 24 months older than the child;</p>
          <p>(7) causes or contributes to a child being a habitual truant as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.19">260C.007, subdivision 19</a>, and is at least 18 years old and more than 24 months older than the child;</p>
          <p>(8) causes or contributes to a child being a runaway as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.28">260C.007, subdivision 28</a>, and is at least 18 years old and more than 24 months older than the child; or</p>
          <p>(9) is at least 18 years old and resides with a minor under the age of 16 without the consent of the minor's parent or lawful custodian.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Defenses.</span></h2>
          <p>It is an affirmative defense if a person charged under subdivision 1 proves that:</p>
          <p>(1) the person reasonably believed the action taken was necessary to protect the child from physical or sexual assault or substantial emotional harm;</p>
          <p>(2) the person reasonably believed the action taken was necessary to protect the person taking the action from physical or sexual assault;</p>
          <p>(3) the action taken is consented to by the parent, stepparent, or legal custodian seeking prosecution, but consent to custody or specific parenting time is not consent to the action of failing to return or concealing a minor child; or</p>
          <p>(4) the action taken is otherwise authorized by a court order issued prior to the violation of subdivision 1.</p>
          <p>The defenses provided in this subdivision are in addition to and do not limit other defenses available under this chapter or chapter 611.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Original intent clarified.</span></h2>
          <p>To the extent that it states that subdivision 2 creates affirmative defenses to a charge under this section, subdivision 2 clarifies the original intent of the legislature in enacting Laws 1984, chapter 484, section 2, and does not change the substance of this section. Subdivision 2 does not modify or alter any convictions entered under this section before August 1, 1988.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates this section may be prosecuted and tried either in the county in which the child was taken, concealed, or detained or in the county of lawful residence of the child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Return of child; costs.</span></h2>
          <p>A child who has been concealed, obtained, or retained in violation of this section shall be returned to the person having lawful custody of the child or shall be taken into custody pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.175#stat.260C.175.1">260C.175, subdivision 1</a>, clause (2), item (ii). In addition to any sentence imposed, the court may assess any expense incurred in returning the child against any person convicted of violating this section. The court may direct the appropriate county welfare agency to provide counseling services to a child who has been returned pursuant to this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Dismissal of charge.</span></h2>
          <p>A felony charge brought under this section shall be dismissed if:</p>
          <p>(a) the person voluntarily returns the child within 48 hours after taking, detaining, or failing to return the child in violation of this section; or</p>
          <p>(b)(1) the person taking the action and the child have not left the state of Minnesota; and (2) within a period of seven days after taking the action, (i) a motion or proceeding under chapter 518, 518A, 518B, 518C, or 518D is commenced by the person taking the action, or (ii) the attorney representing the person taking the action has consented to service of process by the party whose rights are being deprived, for any motion or action pursuant to chapter 518, 518A, 518B, 518C, or 518D.</p>
          <p>Clause (a) does not apply if the person returns the child as a result of being located by law enforcement authorities.</p>
          <p>This subdivision does not prohibit the filing of felony charges or an offense report before the expiration of the 48 hours.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) and subdivision 5, whoever violates this section may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than four years or to payment of a fine of not more than $8,000, or both, if the court finds that:</p>
          <p>(i) the defendant committed the violation while possessing a dangerous weapon or caused substantial bodily harm to effect the taking;</p>
          <p>(ii) the defendant abused or neglected the child during the concealment, detention, or removal of the child;</p>
          <p>(iii) the defendant inflicted or threatened to inflict physical harm on a parent or lawful custodian of the child or on the child with intent to cause the parent or lawful custodian to discontinue criminal prosecution;</p>
          <p>(iv) the defendant demanded payment in exchange for return of the child or demanded to be relieved of the financial or legal obligation to support the child in exchange for return of the child; or</p>
          <p>(v) the defendant has previously been convicted under this section or a similar statute of another jurisdiction.</p>
          <p>(b) A violation of subdivision 1, clause (7), is a gross misdemeanor. The county attorney shall prosecute violations of subdivision 1, clause (7).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.26.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Reporting of deprivation of parental rights.</span></h2>
          <p>Any violation of this section shall be reported pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.11#stat.260E.11.2">260E.11, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.26.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/570/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 570 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/263/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 263 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/484/#laws.0.2.0">1984 c 484 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.5.58.0">1984 c 654 art 5 s 58</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/227/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 227 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/445/#laws.0.1.0">1986 c 445 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/463/#laws.0.4.0">1986 c 463 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/246/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 246 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/523/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 523 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.3.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/285/#laws.0.10.0">1991 c 285 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/631/#laws.0.31.0">1994 c 631 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.25.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 25</a>,26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/86/#laws.1.78.0">1999 c 86 art 1 s 78</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/139/#laws.4.2.0">1999 c 139 art 4 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/444/#laws.2.45.0">2000 c 444 art 2 s 45</a>,46; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/178/#laws.1.44.0">2001 c 178 art 1 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.105.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 105</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/164/#laws.0.29.0">2005 c 164 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/7/#laws.0.28.0">1Sp2005 c 7 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.137.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 137</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.265">
        <h1 class="shn">609.265 ABDUCTION.</h1>
