        <p>Whoever, for the purpose of marriage, takes a person under the age of 18 years, without the consent of the parents, guardian, or other person having legal custody of such person is guilty of abduction and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.265.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.265; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST UNBORN CHILDREN</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.266">
        <h1 class="shn">609.266 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <p>The definitions in this section apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114">609.2114, subdivisions 1 </a>and 2, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2691">609.2691</a>:</p>
        <p>(a) "Unborn child" means the unborn offspring of a human being conceived, but not yet born.</p>
        <p>(b) "Whoever" does not include the pregnant woman.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.266.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.5.0">1986 c 388 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.3.14.0">2007 c 54 art 3 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.9.0">2014 c 180 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.101.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 101</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2661">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2661 MURDER OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of murder of an unborn child in the first degree and must be sentenced to imprisonment for life:</p>
        <p>(1) causes the death of an unborn child with premeditation and with intent to effect the death of the unborn child or of another;</p>
        <p>(2) causes the death of an unborn child while committing or attempting to commit criminal sexual conduct in the first or second degree with force or violence, either upon or affecting the mother of the unborn child or another; or</p>
        <p>(3) causes the death of an unborn child with intent to effect the death of the unborn child or another while committing or attempting to commit burglary, aggravated robbery, carjacking in the first or second degree, kidnapping, arson in the first or second degree, tampering with a witness in the first degree, or escape from custody.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2661.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.6.0">1986 c 388 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.20.19.0">2023 c 52 art 20 s 19</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2662">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2662 MURDER OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does either of the following is guilty of murder of an unborn child in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 40 years:</p>
        <p>(1) causes the death of an unborn child with intent to effect the death of that unborn child or another, but without premeditation; or</p>
        <p>(2) causes the death of an unborn child, without intent to effect the death of any unborn child or person, while committing or attempting to commit a felony offense other than criminal sexual conduct in the first or second degree with force or violence.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2662.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.7.0">1986 c 388 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2663">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2663 MURDER OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE THIRD DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, without intent to effect the death of any unborn child or person, causes the death of an unborn child by perpetrating an act eminently dangerous to others and evincing a depraved mind, without regard for human or fetal life, is guilty of murder of an unborn child in the third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2663.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.8.0">1986 c 388 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2664">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2664 MANSLAUGHTER OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of manslaughter of an unborn child in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) intentionally causes the death of an unborn child in the heat of passion provoked by such words or acts of another as would provoke a person of ordinary self-control under like circumstances;</p>
        <p>(2) causes the death of an unborn child in committing or attempting to commit a misdemeanor or gross misdemeanor offense with such force or violence that death of or great bodily harm to any person or unborn child was reasonably foreseeable, and murder of an unborn child in the first or second degree was not committed thereby; or</p>
        <p>(3) intentionally causes the death of an unborn child because the actor is coerced by threats made by someone other than the actor's coconspirator and which cause the actor to reasonably believe that the act performed by the actor is the only means of preventing imminent death to the actor or another.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2664.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.9.0">1986 c 388 s 9</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2665">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2665 MANSLAUGHTER OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>A person who causes the death of an unborn child by any of the following means is guilty of manslaughter of an unborn child in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) by the actor's culpable negligence whereby the actor creates an unreasonable risk and consciously takes chances of causing death or great bodily harm to an unborn child or a person;</p>
        <p>(2) by shooting the mother of the unborn child with a firearm or other dangerous weapon as a result of negligently believing her to be a deer or other animal;</p>
        <p>(3) by setting a spring gun, pit fall, deadfall, snare, or other like dangerous weapon or device; or</p>
        <p>(4) by negligently or intentionally permitting any animal, known by the person to have vicious propensities or to have caused great or substantial bodily harm in the past, to run uncontrolled off the owner's premises, or negligently failing to keep it properly confined.</p>
        <p>If proven by a preponderance of the evidence, it shall be an affirmative defense to criminal liability under clause (4) that the mother of the unborn child provoked the animal to cause the unborn child's death.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2665.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.10.0">1986 c 388 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.13.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.267">
        <h1 class="shn">609.267 ASSAULT OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever assaults a pregnant woman and inflicts great bodily harm on an unborn child who is subsequently born alive may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.267.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.11.0">1986 c 388 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.14.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2671">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2671 ASSAULT OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever assaults a pregnant woman and inflicts substantial bodily harm on an unborn child who is subsequently born alive may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        <p>As used in this section, "substantial bodily harm" includes the birth of the unborn child prior to 37 weeks gestation if the child weighs 2,500 grams or less at the time of birth. "Substantial bodily harm" does not include the inducement of the unborn child's birth when done for bona fide medical purposes.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2671.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.12.0">1986 c 388 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/20/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 20 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2672">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2672 ASSAULT OF UNBORN CHILD IN THE THIRD DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following commits an assault of an unborn child in the third degree and is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
        <p>(1) commits an act with intent to cause fear in a pregnant woman of immediate bodily harm or death to the unborn child; or</p>
        <p>(2) intentionally inflicts or attempts to inflict bodily harm on an unborn child who is subsequently born alive.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2672.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.13.0">1986 c 388 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.268">
        <h1 class="shn">609.268 INJURY OR DEATH OF UNBORN CHILD IN COMMISSION OF CRIME.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.268.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Death of unborn child.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, in the commission of a felony or in a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.23">609.23</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.231">609.231</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2325">609.2325</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.233">609.233</a>, causes the death of an unborn child is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine not more than $30,000, or both. As used in this subdivision, "felony" does not include a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114">609.2114</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2665">609.2665</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.268.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Injury to unborn child.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, in the commission of a felony or in a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.23">609.23</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.231">609.231</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2325">609.2325</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.233">609.233</a>, causes great or substantial bodily harm to an unborn child who is subsequently born alive, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both. As used in this subdivision, "felony" does not include a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112">609.2112</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114">609.2114</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.267">609.267</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2672">609.2672</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.268.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.14.0">1986 c 388 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.4.17.0">1995 c 229 art 4 s 17</a>,18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.3.16.0">1995 c 259 art 3 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/180/#laws.0.9.0">2014 c 180 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.269">
        <h1 class="shn">609.269 EXCEPTION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.268">609.268</a> do not apply to a person providing reproductive health care offered, arranged, or furnished:</p>
        <p>(1) for the purpose of terminating a pregnancy; and</p>
        <p>(2) with the consent of the pregnant individual or the pregnant individual's representative, except in a medical emergency in which consent cannot be obtained.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.269.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.15.0">1986 c 388 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.8.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.2691">
        <h1 class="shn">609.2691 OTHER CONVICTIONS NOT BARRED.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2661">609.2661</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.268">609.268</a> is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.2691.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/388/#laws.0.16.0">1986 c 388 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES OF COMPULSION</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.27">
        <h1 class="shn">609.27 COERCION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.27.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever orally or in writing makes any of the following threats and thereby causes another against the other's will to do any act or forbear doing a lawful act is guilty of coercion and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2:</p>
          <p>(1) a threat to unlawfully inflict bodily harm upon, or hold in confinement, the person threatened or another, when robbery or attempt to rob is not committed thereby; or</p>
          <p>(2) a threat to unlawfully inflict damage to the property of the person threatened or another; or</p>
          <p>(3) a threat to unlawfully injure a trade, business, profession, or calling; or</p>
          <p>(4) a threat to expose a secret or deformity, publish a defamatory statement, or otherwise to expose any person to disgrace or ridicule; or</p>
          <p>(5) a threat to make or cause to be made a criminal charge, whether true or false; provided, that a warning of the consequences of a future violation of law given in good faith by a peace officer or prosecuting attorney to any person shall not be deemed a threat for the purposes of this section; or</p>
          <p>(6) a threat to commit a violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.261">617.261</a>.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.27.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both if neither the pecuniary gain received by the violator nor the loss suffered by the person threatened or another as a result of the threat exceeds $300, or the benefits received or harm sustained are not susceptible of pecuniary measurement; or</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if such pecuniary gain or loss is more than $300 but less than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(3) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if such pecuniary gain or loss is $2,500, or more.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.27.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.27; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.40.0">1971 c 23 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.7.0">1977 c 355 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.87.0">1983 c 359 s 87</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/126/#laws.0.4.0">2016 c 126 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE:</b> Subdivision 1, clause (4), was found to violate the First Amendment to the United States Constitution as facially overbroad in <i>State v. Jorgenson</i>, 946 N.W.2d 596 (Minn. 2020).</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.275">
        <h1 class="shn">609.275 ATTEMPT TO COERCE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever makes a threat within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27#stat.609.27.1">609.27, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (1) to (6), but fails to cause the intended act or forbearance, commits an attempt to coerce and may be punished as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.17">609.17</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.275.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.275; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/126/#laws.0.5.0">2016 c 126 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.28">
        <h1 class="shn">609.28 INTERFERING WITH RELIGIOUS OBSERVANCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.28.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Interference.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, by threats or violence, intentionally prevents another person from performing any lawful act enjoined upon or recommended to the person by the religion which the person professes is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.28.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Physical interference prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who intentionally and physically obstructs any individual's access to or egress from a religious establishment. This subdivision does not apply to the exclusion of a person from the establishment at the request of an official of the religious organization.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.28.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of subdivision 2, a "religious establishment" is a building used for worship services by a religious organization and clearly identified as such by a posted sign or other means.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.28.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.28; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.41.0">1971 c 23 s 41</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.27.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 27</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SEX AND LABOR TRAFFICKING CRIMES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.281">
        <h1 class="shn">609.281 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Generally.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.281">609.281</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.284">609.284</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/27/#laws.0.15.0">2023 c 27 s 15</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Debt bondage.</span></h2>
          <p>"Debt bondage" occurs when a person provides labor or services of any kind to pay a real or alleged debt of the person or another, if the value of the labor or services as reasonably assessed is not applied toward the liquidation of the debt or the length and nature of the labor or services are not respectively limited and defined.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Forced or coerced labor or services.</span></h2>
          <p>"Forced or coerced labor or services" means labor or services of any kind that are performed or provided by another person and are obtained or maintained through an actor's:</p>
          <p>(1) threat, either implicit or explicit, scheme, plan, pattern, or other action or statement intended to cause a person to believe that, if the person did not perform or provide the labor or services, that person or another would suffer physical restraint; sexual contact, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.11">609.341, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (b); or bodily, psychological, demonstrable economic, or demonstrable reputational harm that is sufficiently serious, under all the surrounding circumstances, to compel a reasonable person of the same background and in the same circumstances to perform or to continue performing labor or services in order to avoid incurring that harm;</p>
          <p>(2) sexual contact, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.11">609.341, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (b), with a person;</p>
          <p>(3) physical restraint of a person;</p>
          <p>(4) infliction of bodily, psychological, demonstrable economic, or demonstrable reputational harm that is sufficiently serious, under all the surrounding circumstances, to compel a reasonable person of the same background and in the same circumstances to perform or to continue performing labor or services in order to avoid incurring that harm;</p>
          <p>(5) abuse or threatened abuse of the legal process, including the use or threatened use of a law or legal process, whether administrative, civil, or criminal; or</p>
          <p>(6) destruction, concealment, removal, confiscation, withholding, or possession of any actual or purported passport or other immigration document, or any other actual or purported government identification document, of another person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Labor trafficking.</span></h2>
          <p>"Labor trafficking" means:</p>
          <p>(1) the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, enticement, provision, obtaining, or receipt of a person by any means, in furtherance of:</p>
          <p>(i) debt bondage;</p>
          <p>(ii) forced or coerced labor or services;</p>
          <p>(iii) slavery or practices similar to slavery; or</p>
          <p>(iv) the removal of organs through the use of coercion or intimidation; or</p>
          <p>(2) receiving profit or anything of value, knowing or having reason to know it is derived from an act described in clause (1).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Labor trafficking victim.</span></h2>
          <p>"Labor trafficking victim" means a person subjected to the practices in subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.281.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Psychological harm.</span></h2>
          <p>"Psychological harm" means harm that causes mental distress, mental suffering, or mental anguish as demonstrated by a victim's response to an act, including but not limited to seeking psychotherapy as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604.20">604.20</a>, losing sleep or appetite, being diagnosed with a mental health condition, experiencing suicidal ideation, or having difficulty concentrating on tasks resulting in a loss of productivity.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.281.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.15.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/137/#laws.0.2.0">2009 c 137 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/27/#laws.0.3.0">2023 c 27 s 3</a>-6</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.282">
        <h1 class="shn">609.282 LABOR TRAFFICKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.282.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Labor trafficking resulting in death.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever knowingly engages in the labor trafficking of an individual is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both if the labor trafficking victim dies and the death was proximately caused by the labor trafficking conduct of the offender and murder in the first or second degree was not committed thereby.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.282.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Individuals under age 18; extended period of time; great bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever knowingly engages in the labor trafficking of an individual is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both if any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(1) the labor trafficking victim is under the age of 18;</p>
          <p>(2) the labor trafficking occurs over an extended period of time; or</p>
          <p>(3) the labor trafficking victim suffers great bodily harm and the harm was proximately caused by the labor trafficking conduct of the offender.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.282.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Other offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever knowingly engages in the labor trafficking of another is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.282.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Consent or age of victim not a defense.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under this section the consent or age of the victim is not a defense.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.282.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.16.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.20.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/27/#laws.0.7.0">2023 c 27 s 7</a>,8</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.283">
        <h1 class="shn">609.283 UNLAWFUL CONDUCT WITH RESPECT TO DOCUMENTS IN FURTHERANCE OF LABOR OR SEX TRAFFICKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.283.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless the person's conduct constitutes a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a>, a person who knowingly destroys, conceals, removes, confiscates, or possesses any actual or purported passport or other immigration document, or any other actual or purported government identification document, of another person:</p>
          <p>(1) in the course of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) with intent to violate section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) to prevent or restrict or to attempt to prevent or restrict, without lawful authority, a person's liberty to move or travel, in order to maintain the labor or services of that person, when the person is or has been a victim of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>;</p>
          <p class="bl">is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.283.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalties. </span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the crime involves a victim under the age of 18, to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of $20,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) in other cases, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.283.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Consent or age of victim not a defense.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under this section the consent or age of the victim is not a defense.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.283.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.17.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.21.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.284">
        <h1 class="shn">609.284 LABOR OR SEX TRAFFICKING CRIMES; DEFENSES; CIVIL LIABILITY; CORPORATE LIABILITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.284.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Consent or age of victim not a defense.</span></h2>
          <p>In an action under this section the consent or age of the victim is not a defense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.284.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Civil liability.</span></h2>
          <p>A labor trafficking victim may bring a cause of action against a person who violates section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.283">609.283</a>. The court may award damages, including punitive damages, reasonable attorney fees, and other litigation costs reasonably incurred by the victim. This remedy is in addition to potential criminal liability.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.284.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Corporate liability.</span></h2>
          <p>If a corporation or other business enterprise is convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.283">609.283</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>, in addition to the criminal penalties described in those sections and other remedies provided elsewhere in law, the court may, when appropriate:</p>
          <p>(1) order its dissolution or reorganization;</p>
          <p>(2) order the suspension or revocation of any license, permit, or prior approval granted to it by a state agency; or</p>
          <p>(3) order the surrender of its charter if it is organized under Minnesota law or the revocation of its certificate to conduct business in Minnesota if it is not organized under Minnesota law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.284.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.18.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 18</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.29"><b>609.29</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.13.0">1975 c 374 s 13</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.291"><b>609.291</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.13.0">1975 c 374 s 13</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.292"><b>609.292</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.13.0">1975 c 374 s 13</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SEX CRIMES</h1>
      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.609.293">
        <h1>609.293 </h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.293.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.25.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.293.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/130/#laws.0.10.0">1977 c 130 s 10</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.293.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/130/#laws.0.10.0">1977 c 130 s 10</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.293.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/130/#laws.0.10.0">1977 c 130 s 10</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.293.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.25.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.294">
        <h1 class="shn">609.294 BESTIALITY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever carnally knows a dead body or an animal or bird is guilty of bestiality, which is a misdemeanor. If knowingly done in the presence of another the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000 or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.294.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/507/#laws.0.5.0">1967 c 507 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.42.0">1971 c 23 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.295"><b>609.295</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.13.0">1975 c 374 s 13</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.296"><b>609.296</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.13.0">1975 c 374 s 13</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.31">
        <h1 class="shn">609.31 LEAVING STATE TO EVADE ESTABLISHMENT OF PATERNITY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever with intent to evade proceedings to establish his paternity leaves the state knowing that a woman with whom he has had sexual intercourse is pregnant or has given birth within the previous 60 days to a living child may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.31.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/507/#laws.0.8.0">1967 c 507 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.32"><b>609.32</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/255/#laws.0.9.0">1979 c 255 s 9</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.321">
        <h1 class="shn">609.321 PROSTITUTION AND SEX TRAFFICKING; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.321">609.321</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.325">609.325</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Business of prostitution.</span></h2>
          <p>"Business of prostitution" means any arrangement between or organization of two or more persons, acting other than as prostitutes or patrons, who commit acts punishable under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.321">609.321</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 33</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Patron.</span></h2>
          <p>"Patron" means an individual who engages in prostitution by hiring, offering to hire, or agreeing to hire another individual to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Place of prostitution.</span></h2>
          <p>"Place of prostitution" means a house or other place where prostitution is practiced.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 33</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Promotes the prostitution of an individual.</span></h2>
          <p>"Promotes the prostitution of an individual" means any of the following wherein the person knowingly:</p>
          <p>(1) solicits or procures patrons for a prostitute;</p>
          <p>(2) provides, leases or otherwise permits premises or facilities owned or controlled by the person to aid the prostitution of an individual;</p>
          <p>(3) owns, manages, supervises, controls, keeps or operates, either alone or with others, a place of prostitution to aid the prostitution of an individual;</p>
          <p>(4) owns, manages, supervises, controls, operates, institutes, aids or facilitates, either alone or with others, a business of prostitution to aid the prostitution of an individual;</p>
          <p>(5) admits a patron to a place of prostitution to aid the prostitution of an individual; or</p>
          <p>(6) transports an individual from one point within this state to another point either within or without this state, or brings an individual into this state to aid the prostitution of the individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Sex trafficking.</span></h2>
          <p>"Sex trafficking" means:</p>
          <p>(1) receiving, recruiting, enticing, harboring, providing, or obtaining by any means an individual to aid in the prostitution of the individual; or</p>
          <p>(2) receiving profit or anything of value, knowing or having reason to know it is derived from an act described in clause (1).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.7b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7b.<span class="headnote">Sex trafficking victim.</span></h2>
          <p>"Sex trafficking victim" means a person subjected to the practices in subdivision 7a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Prostitute.</span></h2>
          <p>"Prostitute" means an individual who engages in prostitution by being hired, offering to be hired, or agreeing to be hired by another individual to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Prostitution.</span></h2>
          <p>"Prostitution" means hiring, offering to hire, or agreeing to hire another individual to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact, or being hired, offering to be hired, or agreeing to be hired by another individual to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Sexual contact.</span></h2>
          <p>"Sexual contact" means any of the following acts, if the acts can reasonably be construed as being for the purpose of satisfying the actor's sexual impulses:</p>
          <p>(i) the intentional touching by an individual of a prostitute's intimate parts; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the intentional touching by a prostitute of another individual's intimate parts.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Sexual penetration.</span></h2>
          <p>"Sexual penetration" means any of the following acts, if for the purpose of satisfying sexual impulses: sexual intercourse, cunnilingus, fellatio, anal intercourse, or any intrusion however slight into the genital or anal openings of an individual's body by any part of another individual's body or any object used for the purpose of satisfying sexual impulses. Emission of semen is not necessary.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Public place.</span></h2>
          <p>A "public place" means a public street or sidewalk, a pedestrian skyway system as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/469.125#stat.469.125.4">469.125, subdivision 4</a>, a hotel, motel, steam room, sauna, massage parlor, shopping mall and other public shopping areas, or other place of public accommodation, a place licensed to sell intoxicating liquor, wine, nonintoxicating malt beverages, or food, or a motor vehicle located on a public street, alley, or parking lot ordinarily used by or available to the public though not used as a matter of right and a driveway connecting such a parking lot with a street or highway.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Place of public accommodation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Place of public accommodation" means a business, accommodation, refreshment, entertainment, recreation, or transportation facility of any kind, whether licensed or not, whose goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations are extended, offered, sold, or otherwise made available to the public.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Prior qualified human trafficking-related offense.</span></h2>
          <p>A "prior qualified human trafficking-related offense" means a conviction or delinquency adjudication within the ten years from the discharge from probation or parole immediately preceding the current offense for a violation of or an attempt to violate section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322#stat.609.322.1">609.322, subdivision 1</a> (solicitation, inducement, and promotion of prostitution; sex trafficking in the first degree); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322#stat.609.322.1a">609.322, subdivision 1a</a> (solicitation, inducement, and promotion of prostitution; sex trafficking in the second degree); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a> (labor trafficking); or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.283">609.283</a> (unlawful conduct with respect to documents in furtherance of labor or sex trafficking).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Debt bondage.</span></h2>
          <p>"Debt bondage" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.281">609.281</a>, subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Forced or coerced labor or services.</span></h2>
          <p>"Forced or coerced labor or services" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.281#stat.609.281.4">609.281, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.321.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Labor trafficking victim.</span></h2>
          <p>"Labor trafficking victim" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.281#stat.609.281.6">609.281, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.321.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/255/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 255 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/291/#laws.0.242.0">1987 c 291 s 242</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.19.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 19</a>-23; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/137/#laws.0.3.0">2009 c 137 s 3</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/170/#laws.0.1.0">2009 c 170 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/1/#laws.5.1.0">1Sp2011 c 1 art 5 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/27/#laws.0.9.0">2023 c 27 s 9</a>-11</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.322">
        <h1 class="shn">609.322 SOLICITATION, INDUCEMENT, AND PROMOTION OF PROSTITUTION; SEX TRAFFICKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.322.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Solicitation, inducement, and promotion of prostitution; sex trafficking in the first degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever, while acting other than as a prostitute or patron, intentionally does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) solicits or induces an individual under the age of 18 years to practice prostitution;</p>
          <p>(2) promotes the prostitution of an individual under the age of 18 years;</p>
          <p>(3) receives profit, knowing or having reason to know that it is derived from the prostitution, or the promotion of the prostitution, of an individual under the age of 18 years; or</p>
          <p>(4) engages in the sex trafficking of an individual under the age of 18 years.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates paragraph (a) or subdivision 1a may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 30 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $60,000, or both, if one or more of the following aggravating factors are present:</p>
          <p>(1) the offender has committed a prior qualified human trafficking-related offense;</p>
          <p>(2) the offense involved a sex trafficking victim who suffered bodily harm during the commission of the offense;</p>
          <p>(3) the time period that a sex trafficking victim was held in debt bondage or forced or coerced labor or services exceeded 180 days; or</p>
          <p>(4) the offense involved more than one sex trafficking victim.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.322.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Solicitation, inducement, and promotion of prostitution; sex trafficking in the second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, while acting other than as a prostitute or patron, intentionally does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) solicits or induces an individual to practice prostitution;</p>
          <p>(2) promotes the prostitution of an individual;</p>
          <p>(3) receives profit, knowing or having reason to know that it is derived from the prostitution, or the promotion of the prostitution, of an individual; or</p>
          <p>(4) engages in the sex trafficking of an individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.322.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivisions 1, paragraph (a), clause (3), and 1a, clause (3), do not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) a minor who is dependent on an individual acting as a prostitute and who may have benefited from or been supported by the individual's earnings derived from prostitution; or</p>
          <p>(2) a parent over the age of 55 who is dependent on an individual acting as a prostitute, who may have benefited from or been supported by the individual's earnings derived from prostitution, and who did not know that the earnings were derived from prostitution; or</p>
          <p>(3) the sale of goods or services to a prostitute in the ordinary course of a lawful business.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.322.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Aggregation of cases.</span></h2>
          <p>Acts by the defendant in violation of any one or more of the provisions in this section within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this section; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.322.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 33</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.322.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 33</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.322.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/255/#laws.0.2.0">1979 c 255 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/448/#laws.0.2.0">1986 c 448 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.4.9.0">1992 c 571 art 4 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.12.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 12</a>-14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/431/#laws.0.2.0">2000 c 431 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.10.1.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 10 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/137/#laws.0.7.0">2009 c 137 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.32.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 32</a>,33; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/27/#laws.0.12.0">2023 c 27 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.323"><b>609.323</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 33</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3232">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3232 PROTECTIVE ORDER AUTHORIZED; PROCEDURES; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Order for protection.</span></h2>
          <p>Any parent or guardian who knows or has reason to believe that a person, while acting as other than a prostitute or patron, is inducing, coercing, soliciting, or promoting the prostitution of the parent or guardian's minor child, or is offering or providing food, shelter, or other subsistence for the purpose of enabling the parent or guardian's minor child to engage in prostitution, may seek an order for protection in the manner provided in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Court jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>An application for relief under this section shall be filed in the juvenile court. Actions under this section shall be given docket priority by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Contents of petition.</span></h2>
          <p>A petition for relief shall allege the existence of a circumstance or circumstances described in subdivision 1, and shall be accompanied by an affidavit made under oath stating the specific facts and circumstances from which relief is sought. The court shall provide simplified forms and clerical assistance to help with the writing and filing of a petition under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Hearing on application; notice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Upon receipt of the petition, the court shall order a hearing which shall be held no later than 14 days from the date of the order. Personal service shall be made upon the respondent not less than five days before the hearing. In the event that personal service cannot be completed in time to give the respondent the minimum notice required under this paragraph, the court may set a new hearing date.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (a), service may be made by one week published notice, as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/645.11">645.11</a>, provided the petitioner files with the court an affidavit stating that an attempt at personal service made by a sheriff was unsuccessful because the respondent is avoiding service by concealment or otherwise, and that a copy of the petition and notice of hearing has been mailed to the respondent at the respondent's residence or that the residence is not known to the petitioner. Service under this paragraph is complete seven days after publication. The court shall set a new hearing date if necessary to allow the respondent the five-day minimum notice required under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Relief by the court.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon notice and hearing, the court may order the respondent to return the minor child to the residence of the child's parents or guardian, and may order that the respondent cease and desist from committing further acts described in subdivision 1 and cease to have further contact with the minor child. Any relief granted by the court in the order for protection shall be for a fixed period of time determined by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Service of order.</span></h2>
          <p>Any order issued under this section shall be served personally on the respondent. Upon the request of the petitioner, the court shall order the sheriff to assist in the execution or service of the order for protection.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3232.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Violation of order for protection.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A violation of an order for protection shall constitute contempt of court and be subject to the penalties provided under chapter 588.</p>
          <p>(b) Any person who willfully fails to return a minor child as required by an order for protection issued under this section commits an act which manifests an intent substantially to deprive the parent or guardian of custodial rights within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.26">609.26</a>, clause (3).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3232.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/448/#laws.0.4.0">1986 c 448 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.324">
        <h1 class="shn">609.324 PATRONS; PROSTITUTES; HOUSING INDIVIDUALS ENGAGED IN PROSTITUTION; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Engaging in, hiring, or agreeing to hire minor to engage in prostitution; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever intentionally does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) engages in prostitution with an individual under the age of 14 years;</p>
          <p>(2) hires or offers or agrees to hire an individual under the age of 14 years to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact; or</p>
          <p>(3) hires or offers or agrees to hire an individual who the actor reasonably believes to be under the age of 14 years to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever intentionally does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) engages in prostitution with an individual under the age of 16 years but at least 14 years;</p>
          <p>(2) hires or offers or agrees to hire an individual under the age of 16 years but at least 14 years to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact; or</p>
          <p>(3) hires or offers or agrees to hire an individual who the actor reasonably believes to be under the age of 16 years but at least 14 years to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
          <p>(c) Whoever intentionally does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) engages in prostitution with an individual under the age of 18 years but at least 16 years;</p>
          <p>(2) hires or offers or agrees to hire an individual under the age of 18 years but at least 16 years to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact; or</p>
          <p>(3) hires or offers or agrees to hire an individual who the actor reasonably believes to be under the age of 18 years but at least 16 years to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Housing unrelated minor engaged in prostitution; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person, other than one related by blood, adoption, or marriage to the minor, who permits a minor to reside, temporarily or permanently, in the person's dwelling without the consent of the minor's parents or guardian, knowing or having reason to know that the minor is engaging in prostitution may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; except that, this subdivision does not apply to residential placements made, sanctioned, or supervised by a public or private social service agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Patrons of prostitution; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever, while acting as a patron, intentionally does any of the following is guilty of a gross misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) engages in prostitution with an individual 18 years of age or older; or</p>
          <p>(2) hires, offers to hire, or agrees to hire an individual 18 years of age or older to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
          <p class="bl">Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 4, a person who is convicted of violating this subdivision must, at a minimum, be sentenced to pay a fine of at least $1,500.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates the provisions of this subdivision within ten years of a previous conviction for violating this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.57.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 57</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Community service in lieu of minimum fine.</span></h2>
          <p>The court may order a person convicted of violating subdivision 2 to perform community work service in lieu of all or a portion of the minimum fine required under those subdivisions if the court makes specific, written findings that the convicted person is indigent or that payment of the fine would create undue hardship for the convicted person or that person's immediate family. Community work service ordered under this subdivision is in addition to any mandatory community work service ordered under subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Use of motor vehicle to patronize prostitutes; driving record notation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a court sentences a person convicted of violating this section while acting as a patron, the court shall determine whether the person used a motor vehicle during the commission of the offense and whether the person has previously been convicted of violating this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>. If the court finds that the person used a motor vehicle during the commission of the offense, it shall forward its finding along with an indication of whether the person has previously been convicted of a prostitution offense to the commissioner of public safety who shall record the finding on the person's driving record. Except as provided in paragraph (b), the finding is classified as private data on individuals, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, but is accessible for law enforcement purposes.</p>
          <p>(b) If the person has previously been convicted of a violation of this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>, the finding is public data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Prostitution in public place; penalty for prostitutes.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, while acting as a prostitute, intentionally does any of the following while in a public place is guilty of a gross misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) engages in prostitution with an individual 18 years of age or older; or</p>
          <p>(2) is hired, offers to be hired, or agrees to be hired by an individual 18 years of age or older to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.324.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">General prostitution crimes; penalties for prostitutes.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever, while acting as a prostitute, intentionally does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) engages in prostitution with an individual 18 years of age or older; or</p>
          <p>(2) is hired, offers to be hired, or agrees to be hired by an individual 18 years of age or older to engage in sexual penetration or sexual contact.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates the provisions of this subdivision within two years of a previous prostitution conviction for violating this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.324.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/255/#laws.0.4.0">1979 c 255 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/448/#laws.0.5.0">1986 c 448 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/463/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 463 s 1</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.10.5.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 10 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/137/#laws.0.8.0">2009 c 137 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/170/#laws.0.2.0">2009 c 170 s 2</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/1/#laws.5.4.0">1Sp2011 c 1 art 5 s 4</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.6.11.0">2015 c 65 art 6 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.4.15.0">2016 c 189 art 4 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.34.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 34</a>,35; art 4 s 5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.14.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3241">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3241 PENALTY ASSESSMENT AUTHORIZED.</h1>
        <p>(a) When a court sentences an adult convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27">609.27</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.283">609.283</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.33">609.33</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.352">609.352</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.246">617.246</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.247">617.247</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.293">617.293</a>, while acting other than as a prostitute, the court shall impose an assessment of not less than $500 and not more than $750 for a misdemeanor violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27">609.27</a>, a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324#stat.609.324.2">609.324, subdivision 2</a>, a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.33">609.33</a>, or a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.293">617.293</a>; otherwise the court shall impose an assessment of not less than $750 and not more than $1,000. The assessment shall be distributed as provided in paragraph (c) and is in addition to the surcharge required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/357.021#stat.357.021.6">357.021, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) The court may not waive payment of the minimum assessment required by this section. If the defendant qualifies for the services of a public defender or the court finds on the record that the convicted person is indigent or that immediate payment of the assessment would create undue hardship for the convicted person or that person's immediate family, the court may reduce the amount of the minimum assessment to not less than $100. The court also may authorize payment of the assessment in installments.</p>
        <p>(c) The assessment collected under paragraph (a) must be distributed as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) 40 percent of the assessment shall be forwarded to the political subdivision that employs the arresting officer for use in enforcement, training, and education activities related to combating sexual exploitation of youth, or if the arresting officer is an employee of the state, this portion shall be forwarded to the commissioner of public safety for those purposes identified in clause (3);</p>
        <p>(2) 20 percent of the assessment shall be forwarded to the prosecuting agency that handled the case for use in training and education activities relating to combating sexual exploitation activities of youth; and</p>
        <p>(3) 40 percent of the assessment must be forwarded to the commissioner of health to be deposited in the safe harbor for youth account in the special revenue fund and are appropriated to the commissioner for distribution to crime victims services organizations that provide services to sexually exploited youth, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.31">260C.007, subdivision 31</a>.</p>
        <p>(d) A safe harbor for youth account is established as a special account in the state treasury.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3241.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/448/#laws.0.7.0">1986 c 448 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/463/#laws.0.5.0">1990 c 463 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.28.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.32.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 32</a>; art 8 s 11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.10.2.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 10 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/1/1/#laws.14.17.0">1Sp2010 c 1 art 14 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/1/#laws.4.7.0">1Sp2011 c 1 art 4 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.15.23.0">2016 c 189 art 15 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/144/#laws.0.2.0">2018 c 144 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.36.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 36</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3242">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3242 PROSTITUTION CRIMES COMMITTED IN SCHOOL OR PARK ZONES; INCREASED PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3242.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "park zone" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.12a">152.01, subdivision 12a</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) "school zone" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.14a">152.01, subdivision 14a</a>, and also includes school bus stops established by a school board under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/123B.88">123B.88</a>, while school children are waiting for the bus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3242.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Increased penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who commits a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a> while acting other than as a prostitute while in a school or park zone may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the crime committed is a felony, the statutory maximum for the crime is three years longer than the statutory maximum for the underlying crime;</p>
          <p>(2) if the crime committed is a gross misdemeanor, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both; and</p>
          <p>(3) if the crime committed is a misdemeanor, the person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3242.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.15.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3243">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3243 LOITERING WITH INTENT TO PARTICIPATE IN PROSTITUTION.</h1>
        <p>A person who loiters in a public place with intent to participate in prostitution is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3243.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.24.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 24</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.325">
        <h1 class="shn">609.325 DEFENSES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.325.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">No defense; solicited; not engaged.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be no defense to a prosecution under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> that an individual solicited or induced to practice prostitution or whose prostitution was promoted, did not actually engage in prostitution.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.325.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Consent no defense.</span></h2>
          <p>Consent or mistake as to age shall be no defense to prosecutions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.325.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">No defense; prior prostitution.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be no defense to actions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> that the individual solicited or induced to practice prostitution, or whose prostitution was promoted, had engaged in prostitution prior to that solicitation, inducement, or promotion.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.325.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">No defense; undercover operative.</span></h2>
          <p>The fact that an undercover operative or law enforcement officer was involved in the detection or investigation of an offense shall not be a defense to a prosecution under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.325.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defense.</span></h2>
