          <p>It is an affirmative defense to a charge under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>, subdivision 6 or 7, if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant is a labor trafficking victim or a sex trafficking victim and that the defendant committed the acts underlying the charge as a result of being a labor trafficking or sex trafficking victim.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.325.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/255/#laws.0.5.0">1979 c 255 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.29.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.32.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.25.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.6.12.0">2015 c 65 art 6 s 12</a>,13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/27/#laws.0.13.0">2023 c 27 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.326">
        <h1 class="shn">609.326 EVIDENCE.</h1>
        <p>The marital privilege provided for in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/595.02">595.02</a> shall not apply in any proceeding under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.326.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/255/#laws.0.6.0">1979 c 255 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.32.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 32</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.33">
        <h1 class="shn">609.33 DISORDERLY HOUSE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.33.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of this section, "disorderly house" means a building, dwelling, place, establishment, or premises in which actions or conduct habitually occur in violation of laws relating to:</p>
          <p>(1) the sale of intoxicating liquor or 3.2 percent malt liquor;</p>
          <p>(2) gambling;</p>
          <p>(3) prostitution as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.321#stat.609.321.9">609.321, subdivision 9</a>, or acts relating to prostitution; or</p>
          <p>(4) the sale or possession of controlled substances as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.4">152.01, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.33.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibiting owning or operating disorderly house.</span></h2>
          <p>No person may own, lease, operate, manage, maintain, or conduct a disorderly house, or invite or attempt to invite others to visit or remain in the disorderly house. A violation of this subdivision is a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.33.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Mandatory minimum penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a person is convicted of a first violation of subdivision 2, in addition to any sentence of imprisonment authorized by subdivision 2 which the court may impose, the court shall impose a fine of not less than $300 nor more than $3,000.</p>
          <p>(b) If a person is convicted of a second violation of subdivision 2, in addition to any sentence of imprisonment authorized by subdivision 2 which the court may impose, the court shall impose a fine of not less than $500 nor more than $3,000.</p>
          <p>(c) If a person is convicted of a third or subsequent violation of subdivision 2, in addition to any sentence of imprisonment authorized by subdivision 2 which the court may impose, the court shall impose a fine of not less than $1,000 nor more than $3,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.33.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>Evidence of unlawful sales of intoxicating liquor or 3.2 percent malt liquor, of unlawful possession or sale of controlled substances, of prostitution or acts relating to prostitution, or of gambling or acts relating to gambling, is prima facie evidence of the existence of a disorderly house. Evidence of sales of intoxicating liquor or 3.2 percent malt liquor between the hours of 1:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m., while a person is within a disorderly house, is prima facie evidence that the person knew it to be a disorderly house.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.33.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Local regulation.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivisions 1 to 4 do not prohibit or restrict a local governmental unit from imposing more restrictive provisions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.33.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Pretrial release.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is charged under this section with owning or leasing a disorderly house, the court may require as a condition of pretrial release that the defendant bring an eviction action against a lessee who has violated the covenant not to allow drugs established by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/504B.171">504B.171</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.33.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/507/#laws.0.10.0">1967 c 507 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/277/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 277 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/77/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 77 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/193/#laws.0.3.0">1991 c 193 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/249/#laws.0.31.0">1991 c 249 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/199/#laws.2.33.0">1999 c 199 art 2 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/2/#laws.2.18.0">2003 c 2 art 2 s 18</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.34"><b>609.34</b> MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.25.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 25</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.341">
        <h1 class="shn">609.341 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341">609.341</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.351">609.351</a>, the terms in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Actor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Actor" means a person accused of criminal sexual conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Force.</span></h2>
          <p>"Force" means either: (1) the infliction by the actor of bodily harm; or (2) the attempted infliction, or threatened infliction by the actor of bodily harm or commission or threat of any other crime by the actor against the complainant or another, which causes the complainant to reasonably believe that the actor has the present ability to execute the threat.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Consent.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Consent" means words or overt actions by a person indicating a freely given present agreement to perform a particular sexual act with the actor. Consent does not mean the existence of a prior or current social relationship between the actor and the complainant or that the complainant failed to resist a particular sexual act.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who is mentally incapacitated or physically helpless as defined by this section cannot consent to a sexual act.</p>
          <p>(c) Corroboration of the victim's testimony is not required to show lack of consent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Intimate parts.</span></h2>
          <p>"Intimate parts" includes the primary genital area, groin, inner thigh, buttocks, or breast of a human being.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Mentally impaired.</span></h2>
          <p>"Mentally impaired" means that a person, as a result of inadequately developed or impaired intelligence or a substantial psychiatric disorder of thought or mood, lacks the judgment to give a reasoned consent to sexual contact or to sexual penetration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Mentally incapacitated.</span></h2>
          <p>"Mentally incapacitated" means:</p>
          <p>(1) that a person under the influence of alcohol, a narcotic, anesthetic, or any other substance, administered to that person without the person's agreement, lacks the judgment to give a reasoned consent to sexual contact or sexual penetration; or</p>
          <p>(2) that a person is under the influence of any substance or substances to a degree that renders them incapable of consenting or incapable of appreciating, understanding, or controlling the person's conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Personal injury.</span></h2>
          <p>"Personal injury" means bodily harm as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02#stat.609.02.7">609.02, subdivision 7</a>, or severe mental anguish or pregnancy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Physically helpless.</span></h2>
          <p>"Physically helpless" means that a person is (a) asleep or not conscious, (b) unable to withhold consent or to withdraw consent because of a physical condition, or (c) unable to communicate nonconsent and the condition is known or reasonably should have been known to the actor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Current or recent position of authority.</span></h2>
          <p>"Current or recent position of authority" includes but is not limited to any person who is a parent or acting in the place of a parent and charged with or assumes any of a parent's rights, duties or responsibilities to a child, or a person who is charged with or assumes any duty or responsibility for the health, welfare, or supervision of a child, either independently or through another, no matter how brief, at the time of or within 120 days immediately preceding the act. For the purposes of subdivision 11, "current or recent position of authority" includes a psychotherapist.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Sexual contact.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) "Sexual contact," for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343#stat.609.343.1">609.343, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (a) to (e), and subdivision 1a, clauses (a) to (f) and (i), and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345#stat.609.345.1">609.345, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (a) to (d) and (i), and subdivision 1a, clauses (a) to (e), (h), and (i), includes any of the following acts committed without the complainant's consent, except in those cases where consent is not a defense, and committed with sexual or aggressive intent:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the intentional touching by the actor of the complainant's intimate parts, or</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the touching by the complainant of the actor's, the complainant's, or another's intimate parts effected by a person in a current or recent position of authority, or by coercion, or by inducement if the complainant is under 14 years of age or mentally impaired, or</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the touching by another of the complainant's intimate parts effected by coercion or by a person in a current or recent position of authority, or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) in any of the cases above, the touching of the clothing covering the immediate area of the intimate parts, or</p>
          <p>(v) the intentional touching with seminal fluid or sperm by the actor of the complainant's body or the clothing covering the complainant's body.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Sexual contact," for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343, subdivision</a> 1a, clauses (g) and (h), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345, subdivision</a> 1a, clauses (f) and (g), and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, includes any of the following acts committed with sexual or aggressive intent:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the intentional touching by the actor of the complainant's intimate parts;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the touching by the complainant of the actor's, the complainant's, or another's intimate parts;</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the touching by another of the complainant's intimate parts;</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) in any of the cases listed above, touching of the clothing covering the immediate area of the intimate parts; or</p>
          <p>(v) the intentional touching with seminal fluid or sperm by the actor of the complainant's body or the clothing covering the complainant's body.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "Sexual contact with a person under 14" means the intentional touching of the complainant's bare genitals or anal opening by the actor's bare genitals or anal opening with sexual or aggressive intent or the touching by the complainant's bare genitals or anal opening of the actor's or another's bare genitals or anal opening with sexual or aggressive intent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Sexual penetration.</span></h2>
          <p>"Sexual penetration" means any of the following acts committed without the complainant's consent, except in those cases where consent is not a defense, whether or not emission of semen occurs:</p>
          <p>(1) sexual intercourse, cunnilingus, fellatio, or anal intercourse; or</p>
          <p>(2) any intrusion however slight into the genital or anal openings:</p>
          <p>(i) of the complainant's body by any part of the actor's body or any object used by the actor for this purpose;</p>
          <p>(ii) of the complainant's body by any part of the body of the complainant, by any part of the body of another person, or by any object used by the complainant or another person for this purpose, when effected by a person in a current or recent position of authority, or by coercion, or by inducement if the child is under 14 years of age or mentally impaired; or</p>
          <p>(iii) of the body of the actor or another person by any part of the body of the complainant or by any object used by the complainant for this purpose, when effected by a person in a current or recent position of authority, or by coercion, or by inducement if the child is under 14 years of age or mentally impaired.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Complainant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Complainant" means a person alleged to have been subjected to criminal sexual conduct, but need not be the person who signs the complaint.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Coercion.</span></h2>
          <p>"Coercion" means the use by the actor of words or circumstances that cause the complainant reasonably to fear the infliction of bodily harm upon the complainant or another, or the use by the actor of confinement, or superior size or strength, against the complainant to accomplish the act. Proof of coercion does not require proof of a specific act or threat.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Significant relationship.</span></h2>
          <p>"Significant relationship" means a situation in which the actor is:</p>
          <p>(1) the complainant's parent, stepparent, or guardian;</p>
          <p>(2) any of the following persons related to the complainant by blood, marriage, or adoption: brother, sister, stepbrother, stepsister, first cousin, aunt, uncle, nephew, niece, grandparent, great-grandparent, great-uncle, great-aunt;</p>
          <p>(3) an adult who jointly resides intermittently or regularly in the same dwelling as the complainant and who is not the complainant's spouse; or</p>
          <p>(4) an adult who is or was involved in a significant romantic or sexual relationship with the parent of a complainant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Patient.</span></h2>
          <p>"Patient" means a person who seeks or obtains psychotherapeutic services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Psychotherapist.</span></h2>
          <p>"Psychotherapist" means a person who is or purports to be a physician, psychologist, nurse, physician assistant, chemical dependency counselor, social worker, marriage and family therapist, licensed professional counselor, or other mental health service provider; or any other person, whether or not licensed by the state, who performs or purports to perform psychotherapy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Psychotherapy.</span></h2>
          <p>"Psychotherapy" means the professional treatment, assessment, or counseling of a mental or emotional illness, symptom, or condition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Emotionally dependent.</span></h2>
          <p>"Emotionally dependent" means that the nature of the former patient's emotional condition and the nature of the treatment provided by the psychotherapist are such that the psychotherapist knows or has reason to know that the former patient is unable to withhold consent to sexual contact or sexual penetration by the psychotherapist.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Therapeutic deception.</span></h2>
          <p>"Therapeutic deception" means a representation by a psychotherapist that sexual contact or sexual penetration by the psychotherapist is consistent with or part of the patient's treatment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.21">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.<span class="headnote">Special transportation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Special transportation service" means motor vehicle transportation provided on a regular basis by a public or private entity or person that is intended exclusively or primarily to serve individuals who are vulnerable adults or disabled. Special transportation service includes, but is not limited to, service provided by buses, vans, taxis, and volunteers driving private automobiles.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.22">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22.<span class="headnote">Predatory crime.</span></h2>
          <p>"Predatory crime" means a felony violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a> (first-degree murder), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a> (second-degree murder), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a> (third-degree murder), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a> (first-degree manslaughter), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.205">609.205</a> (second-degree manslaughter), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221 </a>(first-degree assault), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a> (second-degree assault), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a> (third-degree assault), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a> (simple robbery), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a> (aggravated robbery), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.247">609.247</a> (carjacking), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.25">609.25 </a>(kidnapping), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255">609.255</a> (false imprisonment), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.498">609.498</a> (tampering with a witness), <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561 </a>(first-degree arson), or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a> (first-degree burglary).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.23">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 23.<span class="headnote">Secure treatment facility.</span></h2>
          <p>"Secure treatment facility" has the meaning given in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.02#stat.253B.02.18a">253B.02, subdivision 18a</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253D.02#stat.253D.02.13">253D.02, subdivision 13</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.24">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 24.<span class="headnote">Prohibited occupational relationship.</span></h2>
          <p>A "prohibited occupational relationship" exists when the actor is in one of the following occupations and the act takes place under the specified circumstances:</p>
          <p>(1) the actor performed massage or other bodywork for hire, the sexual penetration or sexual contact occurred during or immediately before or after the actor performed or was hired to perform one of those services for the complainant, and the sexual penetration or sexual contact was nonconsensual; or</p>
          <p>(2) the actor and the complainant were in one of the following occupational relationships at the time of the act. Consent by the complainant is not a defense:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor was a psychotherapist, the complainant was the actor's patient, and the sexual penetration or sexual contact occurred during a psychotherapy session or during a period of time when the psychotherapist-patient relationship was ongoing;</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor was a psychotherapist and the complainant was the actor's former patient who was emotionally dependent on the actor;</p>
          <p>(iii) the actor was or falsely impersonated a psychotherapist, the complainant was the actor's patient or former patient, and the sexual penetration or sexual contact occurred by means of therapeutic deception;</p>
          <p>(iv) the actor was or falsely impersonated a provider of medical services to the complainant and the sexual penetration or sexual contact occurred by means of deception or false representation that the sexual penetration or sexual contact was for a bona fide medical purpose;</p>
          <p>(v) the actor was or falsely impersonated a member of the clergy, the complainant was not married to the actor, the complainant met with the actor in private seeking or receiving religious or spiritual advice, aid, or comfort from the actor, and the sexual penetration or sexual contact occurred during the course of the meeting or during a period of time when the meetings were ongoing;</p>
          <p>(vi) the actor provided special transportation service to the complainant and the sexual penetration or sexual contact occurred during or immediately before or after the actor transported the complainant;</p>
          <p>(vii) the actor was or falsely impersonated a peace officer, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84">626.84</a>, the actor physically or constructively restrained the complainant or the complainant did not reasonably feel free to leave the actor's presence, and the sexual penetration or sexual contact was not pursuant to a lawful search or lawful use of force;</p>
          <p>(viii) the actor was an employee, independent contractor, or volunteer of a state, county, city, or privately operated adult or juvenile correctional system, or secure treatment facility, or treatment facility providing services to clients civilly committed as mentally ill and dangerous, sexually dangerous persons, or sexual psychopathic personalities, including but not limited to jails, prisons, detention centers, or work release facilities, and the complainant was a resident of a facility or under supervision of the correctional system;</p>
          <p>(ix) the complainant was enrolled in a secondary school and:</p>
          <p>(A) the actor was a licensed educator employed or contracted to provide service for the school at which the complainant was a student;</p>
          <p>(B) the actor was age 18 or older and at least 48 months older than the complainant and was employed or contracted to provide service for the secondary school at which the complainant was a student; or</p>
          <p>(C) the actor was age 18 or older and at least 48 months older than the complainant, and was a licensed educator employed or contracted to provide services for an elementary, middle, or secondary school;</p>
          <p>(x) the actor was a caregiver, facility staff person, or person providing services in a facility, and the complainant was a vulnerable adult who was a resident, patient, or client of the facility who was impaired in judgment or capacity by mental or emotional dysfunction or undue influence; or</p>
          <p>(xi) the actor was a caregiver, facility staff person, or person providing services in a facility, and the complainant was a resident, patient, or client of the facility. This clause does not apply if a consensual sexual personal relationship existed prior to the caregiving relationship or if the actor was a personal care attendant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.25">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 25.<span class="headnote">Caregiver.</span></h2>
          <p>"Caregiver" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.232">609.232, subdivision </a>2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.26">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26.<span class="headnote">Facility.</span></h2>
          <p>"Facility" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.232#stat.609.232.3">609.232, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.341.27">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 27.<span class="headnote">Vulnerable adult.</span></h2>
          <p>"Vulnerable adult" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.232#stat.609.232.11">609.232, subdivision 11</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.342">
        <h1 class="shn">609.342 CRIMINAL SEXUAL CONDUCT IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.342.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Adult victim; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who engages in sexual penetration with another person is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the first degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(a) circumstances existing at the time of the act cause the complainant to have a reasonable fear of imminent great bodily harm to the complainant or another;</p>
          <p>(b) the actor is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor causes personal injury to the complainant, and any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the act;</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(iii) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p>(d) the actor uses force as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (1); or</p>
          <p>(e) the actor is aided or abetted by one or more accomplices within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.05">609.05</a>, and either of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor or an accomplice uses force or coercion to cause the complainant to submit; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor or an accomplice is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant reasonably to believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.342.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Victim under the age of 18; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who engages in penetration with anyone under 18 years of age or sexual contact with a person under 14 years of age as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.11">609.341, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (c), is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the first degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(a) circumstances existing at the time of the act cause the complainant to have a reasonable fear of imminent great bodily harm to the complainant or another;</p>
          <p>(b) the actor is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor causes personal injury to the complainant, and any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the act;</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(iii) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p>(d) the actor is aided or abetted by one or more accomplices within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.05">609.05</a>, and either of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor or an accomplice uses force or coercion to cause the complainant to submit; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor or an accomplice is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(e) the complainant is under 14 years of age and the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p>(f) the complainant is at least 14 years of age but less than 16 years of age and:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant; and</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor is in a current or recent position of authority over the complainant.</p>
          <p class="bl">Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p>(g) the complainant was under 16 years of age at the time of the act and the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p>(h) the complainant was under 16 years of age at the time of the act, and the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant and any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor or an accomplice used force or coercion to accomplish the act;</p>
          <p>(ii) the complainant suffered personal injury; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the sexual abuse involved multiple acts committed over an extended period of time.</p>
          <p class="bl">Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense; or</p>
          <p>(i) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (1).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.342.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, a person convicted under subdivision 1 or subdivision 1a may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 30 years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $40,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Unless a longer mandatory minimum sentence is otherwise required by law or the Sentencing Guidelines provide for a longer presumptive executed sentence, the court shall presume that an executed sentence of 144 months must be imposed on an offender convicted of violating this section. Sentencing a person in a manner other than that described in this paragraph is a departure from the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
          <p>(c) A person convicted under this section is also subject to conditional release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.342.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Stay.</span></h2>
          <p>Except when imprisonment is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, if a person is convicted under subdivision 1a, clause (g), the court may stay imposition or execution of the sentence if it finds that:</p>
          <p>(a) a stay is in the best interest of the complainant or the family unit; and</p>
          <p>(b) a professional assessment indicates that the offender has been accepted by and can respond to a treatment program.</p>
          <p>If the court stays imposition or execution of sentence, it shall include the following as conditions of probation:</p>
          <p>(1) incarceration in a local jail or workhouse;</p>
          <p>(2) a requirement that the offender complete a treatment program; and</p>
          <p>(3) a requirement that the offender have no unsupervised contact with the complainant until the offender has successfully completed the treatment program unless approved by the treatment program and the supervising correctional agent.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.342.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.3.0">1975 c 374 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/51/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 51 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/204/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 204 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/24/#laws.0.5.0">1985 c 24 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.15.0">1985 c 286 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.4.12.0">1989 c 290 art 4 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.1.14.0">1992 c 571 art 1 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.34.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/186/#laws.0.99.0">1995 c 186 s 99</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.3.7.0">1998 c 367 art 3 s 7</a>; art 6 s 15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/311/#laws.4.2.0">2000 c 311 art 4 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/437/#laws.0.10.0">2000 c 437 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.2.12.0">2005 c 136 art 2 s 12</a>,13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/13/#laws.3.37.0">2007 c 13 art 3 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/5/#laws.4.5.0">1Sp2019 c 5 art 4 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.16.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.343">
        <h1 class="shn">609.343 CRIMINAL SEXUAL CONDUCT IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.343.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Adult victim; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who engages in sexual contact with another person is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the second degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(a) circumstances existing at the time of the act cause the complainant to have a reasonable fear of imminent great bodily harm to the complainant or another;</p>
          <p>(b) the actor is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the dangerous weapon to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor causes personal injury to the complainant, and any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the sexual contact;</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(iii) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p>(d) the actor uses force as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (1); or</p>
          <p>(e) the actor is aided or abetted by one or more accomplices within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.05">609.05</a>, and either of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor or an accomplice uses force or coercion to cause the complainant to submit; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor or an accomplice is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.343.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Victim under the age of 18; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who engages in sexual contact with anyone under 18 years of age is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the second degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(a) circumstances existing at the time of the act cause the complainant to have a reasonable fear of imminent great bodily harm to the complainant or another;</p>
          <p>(b) the actor is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the dangerous weapon to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor causes personal injury to the complainant, and any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the sexual contact;</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(iii) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p>(d) the actor is aided or abetted by one or more accomplices within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.05">609.05</a>, and either of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor or an accomplice uses force or coercion to cause the complainant to submit; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor or an accomplice is armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and uses or threatens to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(e) the complainant is under 14 years of age and the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense. In a prosecution under this clause, the state is not required to prove that the sexual contact was coerced;</p>
          <p>(f) the complainant is at least 14 but less than 16 years of age and the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant and in a current or recent position of authority over the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p>(g) the complainant was under 16 years of age at the time of the sexual contact and the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p>(h) the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant, the complainant was under 16 years of age at the time of the sexual contact, and:</p>
          <p>(i) the actor or an accomplice used force or coercion to accomplish the contact;</p>
          <p>(ii) the complainant suffered personal injury; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the sexual abuse involved multiple acts committed over an extended period of time.</p>
          <p class="bl">Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense; or</p>
          <p>(i) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (1).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.343.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, a person convicted under subdivision 1 or subdivision 1a may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Unless a longer mandatory minimum sentence is otherwise required by law or the Sentencing Guidelines provide for a longer presumptive executed sentence, the court shall presume that an executed sentence of 90 months must be imposed on an offender convicted of violating subdivision 1, clause (a), (b), (c), (d), or (e), or subdivision 1a, clause (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), or (i). Sentencing a person in a manner other than that described in this paragraph is a departure from the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
          <p>(c) A person convicted under this section is also subject to conditional release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.343.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Stay.</span></h2>
          <p>Except when imprisonment is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, if a person is convicted under subdivision 1a, clause (g), the court may stay imposition or execution of the sentence if it finds that:</p>
          <p>(a) a stay is in the best interest of the complainant or the family unit; and</p>
          <p>(b) a professional assessment indicates that the offender has been accepted by and can respond to a treatment program.</p>
          <p>If the court stays imposition or execution of sentence, it shall include the following as conditions of probation:</p>
          <p>(1) incarceration in a local jail or workhouse;</p>
          <p>(2) a requirement that the offender complete a treatment program; and</p>
          <p>(3) a requirement that the offender have no unsupervised contact with the complainant until the offender has successfully completed the treatment program unless approved by the treatment program and the supervising correctional agent.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.343.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.4.0">1975 c 374 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.12.0">1979 c 258 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/51/#laws.0.3.0">1981 c 51 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/204/#laws.0.2.0">1983 c 204 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/24/#laws.0.6.0">1985 c 24 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.16.0">1985 c 286 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.4.13.0">1989 c 290 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.1.15.0">1992 c 571 art 1 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.3.8.0">1998 c 367 art 3 s 8</a>; art 6 s 15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/437/#laws.0.11.0">2000 c 437 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/381/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 381 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.2.14.0">2005 c 136 art 2 s 14</a>,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/13/#laws.3.37.0">2007 c 13 art 3 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/5/#laws.4.6.0">1Sp2019 c 5 art 4 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.17.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.344">
        <h1 class="shn">609.344 CRIMINAL SEXUAL CONDUCT IN THE THIRD DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.344.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Adult victim; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person who engages in sexual penetration with another person is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the third degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p class="in">(a) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the penetration;</p>
          <p class="in">(b) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(d) at the time of the act, the actor is in a prohibited occupational relationship with the complainant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.344.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Victim under the age of 18; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who engages in sexual penetration with anyone under 18 years of age is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the third degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(a) the complainant is under 14 years of age and the actor is no more than 36 months older than the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant shall be a defense;</p>
          <p>(b) the complainant is at least 14 but less than 16 years of age and the actor is more than 24 months older than the complainant. In any such case if the actor is no more than 60 months older than the complainant, it shall be an affirmative defense, which must be proved by a preponderance of the evidence, that the actor reasonably believes the complainant to be 16 years of age or older. In all other cases, mistake as to the complainant's age shall not be a defense. Consent by the complainant is not a defense;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the penetration;</p>
          <p>(d) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p class="in">(e) the complainant is at least 16 but less than 18 years of age and the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant and in a current or recent position of authority over the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p class="in">(f) the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant and the complainant was at least 16 but under 18 years of age at the time of the sexual penetration. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p class="in">(g) the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant, the complainant was at least 16 but under 18 years of age at the time of the sexual penetration, and:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the actor or an accomplice used force or coercion to accomplish the penetration;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the complainant suffered personal injury; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the sexual abuse involved multiple acts committed over an extended period of time.</p>
          <p class="in">Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p class="in">(h) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341">609.341</a>, subdivision 3, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(i) at the time of the act, the actor is in a prohibited occupational relationship with the complainant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.344.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as otherwise provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>, a person convicted under subdivision 1 or subdivision 1a may be sentenced:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the person was convicted under subdivision 1a, paragraph (b), and if the actor was no more than 36 months but more than 24 months older than the complainant, to imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
          <p>A person convicted under this section is also subject to conditional release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.344.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Stay.</span></h2>
          <p>Except when imprisonment is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, if a person is convicted under subdivision 1a, clause (f), the court may stay imposition or execution of the sentence if it finds that:</p>
          <p>(a) a stay is in the best interest of the complainant or the family unit; and</p>
          <p>(b) a professional assessment indicates that the offender has been accepted by and can respond to a treatment program.</p>
          <p>If the court stays imposition or execution of sentence, it shall include the following as conditions of probation:</p>
          <p>(1) incarceration in a local jail or workhouse;</p>
          <p>(2) a requirement that the offender complete a treatment program; and</p>
          <p>(3) a requirement that the offender have no unsupervised contact with the complainant until the offender has successfully completed the treatment program unless approved by the treatment program and the supervising correctional agent.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">

      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.345">
        <h1 class="shn">609.345 CRIMINAL SEXUAL CONDUCT IN THE FOURTH DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.345.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Adult victim; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person who engages in sexual contact with another person is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the fourth degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p class="in">(a) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the sexual contact;</p>
          <p class="in">(b) the actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.3">609.341, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(d) at the time of the act, the actor is in a prohibited occupational relationship with the complainant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.345.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Victim under the age of 18; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who engages in sexual contact with anyone under 18 years of age is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the fourth degree if any of the following circumstances exists:</p>
          <p>(a) the complainant is under 14 years of age and the actor is no more than 36 months older than the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age or consent to the act by the complainant is a defense. In a prosecution under this clause, the state is not required to prove that the sexual contact was coerced;</p>
          <p>(b) the complainant is at least 14 but less than 16 years of age and the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant or in a current or recent position of authority over the complainant. Consent by the complainant to the act is not a defense.</p>
          <p class="bl">Mistake of age is not a defense unless actor is less than 60 months older. In any such case, if the actor is no more than 60 months older than the complainant, it shall be an affirmative defense which must be proved by a preponderance of the evidence that the actor reasonably believes the complainant to be 16 years of age or older. In all other cases, mistake as to the complainant's age shall not be a defense;</p>
          <p>(c) the actor uses coercion to accomplish the sexual contact;</p>
          <p>(d) The actor knows or has reason to know that the complainant is mentally impaired, mentally incapacitated, or physically helpless;</p>
          <p class="in">(e) the complainant is at least 16 but less than 18 years of age and the actor is more than 36 months older than the complainant and in a current or recent position of authority over the complainant. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p class="in">(f) the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant and the complainant was at least 16 but under 18 years of age at the time of the sexual contact. Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p class="in">(g) the actor has a significant relationship to the complainant, the complainant was at least 16 but under 18 years of age at the time of the sexual contact, and:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the actor or an accomplice used force or coercion to accomplish the contact;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the complainant suffered personal injury; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the sexual abuse involved multiple acts committed over an extended period of time.</p>
          <p class="in">Neither mistake as to the complainant's age nor consent to the act by the complainant is a defense;</p>
          <p class="in">(h) the actor uses force, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341">609.341</a>, subdivision 3, clause (2); or</p>
          <p>(i) at the time of the act, the actor is in a prohibited occupational relationship with the complainant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.345.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as otherwise provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>, a person convicted under subdivision 1 or subdivision 1a may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both. A person convicted under this section is also subject to conditional release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.345.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Stay.</span></h2>
          <p>Except when imprisonment is required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, if a person is convicted under subdivision 1a, clause (f), the court may stay imposition or execution of the sentence if it finds that:</p>
          <p>(a) a stay is in the best interest of the complainant or the family unit; and</p>
          <p>(b) a professional assessment indicates that the offender has been accepted by and can respond to a treatment program.</p>
          <p>If the court stays imposition or execution of sentence, it shall include the following as conditions of probation:</p>
          <p>(1) incarceration in a local jail or workhouse;</p>
          <p>(2) a requirement that the offender complete a treatment program; and</p>
          <p>(3) a requirement that the offender have no unsupervised contact with the complainant until the offender has successfully completed the treatment program unless approved by the treatment program and the supervising correctional agent.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3451">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3451 CRIMINAL SEXUAL CONDUCT IN THE FIFTH DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3451.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Sexual penetration; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the fifth degree if the person engages in nonconsensual sexual penetration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3451.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Sexual contact; child present; crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of criminal sexual conduct in the fifth degree if:</p>
          <p>(1) the person engages in nonconsensual sexual contact; or</p>
          <p>(2) the person engages in masturbation or lewd exhibition of the genitals in the presence of a minor under the age of 16, knowing or having reason to know the minor is present.</p>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "sexual contact" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.11">609.341, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (a), clauses (i), (iv), and (v). Sexual contact also includes the intentional removal or attempted removal of clothing covering the complainant's intimate parts or undergarments, and the nonconsensual touching by the complainant of the actor's intimate parts, effected by the actor, if the action is performed with sexual or aggressive intent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3451.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted under subdivision 1a may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to a payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3451.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the person violates subdivision 1.</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than seven years or to payment of a fine of not more than $14,000, or both, if the person violates subdivision 1 or 1a within ten years of:</p>
          <p>(1) a conviction under subdivision 1;</p>
          <p>(2) a previous conviction for violating subdivision 1a, clause (2), a crime described in paragraph (c), or a statute from another state in conformity with any of these offenses; or</p>
          <p>(3) the first of two or more previous convictions for violating subdivision 1a, clause (1), or a statute from another state in conformity with this offense.</p>
          <p>(c) A previous conviction for violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.23#stat.617.23.2">617.23, subdivision 2</a>, clause (2), or subdivision 3; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.247">617.247</a> may be used to enhance a criminal penalty as provided in paragraph (b).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3451.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/529/#laws.0.2.0">1988 c 529 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/492/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 492 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.2.19.0">1995 c 226 art 2 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.26.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 26</a>,27; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.3.11.0">1998 c 367 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/270/#laws.0.2.0">2014 c 270 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.6.14.0">2015 c 65 art 6 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/5/#laws.4.9.0">1Sp2019 c 5 art 4 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.20.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.3452"><b>609.3452</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3457">609.3457</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3453">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3453 CRIMINAL SEXUAL PREDATORY CONDUCT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3453.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of criminal sexual predatory conduct if the person commits a predatory crime that was motivated by the offender's sexual impulses or was part of a predatory pattern of behavior that had criminal sexual conduct as its goal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3453.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>, the statutory maximum sentence for a violation of subdivision 1 is: (1) 25 percent longer than for the underlying predatory crime; or (2) 50 percent longer than for the underlying predatory crime, if the violation is committed by a person with a previous sex offense conviction, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455#stat.609.3455.1">609.3455, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) In addition to the sentence imposed under paragraph (a), the person may also be sentenced to the payment of a fine of not more than $20,000.</p>
          <p>(c) A person convicted under this section is also subject to conditional release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3453.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.2.20.0">2005 c 136 art 2 s 20</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3455">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3455 DANGEROUS SEX OFFENDERS; LIFE SENTENCES; CONDITIONAL RELEASE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Conviction" includes a conviction as an extended jurisdiction juvenile under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.130">260B.130</a> for a violation of, or an attempt to violate, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, if the adult sentence has been executed.</p>
          <p>(c) "Extreme inhumane conditions" mean situations where, either before or after the sexual penetration or sexual contact, the offender knowingly causes or permits the complainant to be placed in a situation likely to cause the complainant severe ongoing mental, emotional, or psychological harm, or causes the complainant's death.</p>
          <p>(d) A "heinous element" includes:</p>
          <p>(1) the offender tortured the complainant;</p>
          <p>(2) the offender intentionally inflicted great bodily harm upon the complainant;</p>
          <p>(3) the offender intentionally mutilated the complainant;</p>
          <p>(4) the offender exposed the complainant to extreme inhumane conditions;</p>
          <p>(5) the offender was armed with a dangerous weapon or any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the complainant to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon and used or threatened to use the weapon or article to cause the complainant to submit;</p>
          <p>(6) the offense involved sexual penetration or sexual contact with more than one victim;</p>
          <p>(7) the offense involved more than one perpetrator engaging in sexual penetration or sexual contact with the complainant; or</p>
          <p>(8) the offender, without the complainant's consent, removed the complainant from one place to another and did not release the complainant in a safe place.</p>
          <p>(e) "Mutilation" means the intentional infliction of physical abuse designed to cause serious permanent disfigurement or permanent or protracted loss or impairment of the functions of any bodily member or organ, where the offender relishes the infliction of the abuse, evidencing debasement or perversion.</p>
          <p>(f) A conviction is considered a "previous sex offense conviction" if the offender was convicted and sentenced for a sex offense before the commission of the present offense.</p>
          <p>(g) A conviction is considered a "prior sex offense conviction" if the offender was convicted of committing a sex offense before the offender has been convicted of the present offense, regardless of whether the offender was convicted for the first offense before the commission of the present offense, and the convictions involved separate behavioral incidents.</p>
          <p>(h) "Sex offense" means any violation of, or attempt to violate, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, or any similar statute of the United States, this state, or any other state.</p>
          <p>(i) "Torture" means the intentional infliction of extreme mental anguish, or extreme psychological or physical abuse, when committed in an especially depraved manner.</p>
          <p>(j) An offender has "two previous sex offense convictions" only if the offender was convicted and sentenced for a sex offense committed after the offender was earlier convicted and sentenced for a sex offense and both convictions preceded the commission of the present offense of conviction.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Mandatory life sentence without release; egregious first-time and repeat offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (c), notwithstanding the statutory maximum penalty otherwise applicable to the offense, the court shall sentence a person convicted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342#stat.609.342.1">609.342, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d), or (e), or subdivision 1a, clause (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), or (i); or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343#stat.609.343.1">609.343, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d), or (e), or subdivision 1a, clause (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), or (i), to life without the possibility of release if:</p>
          <p>(1) the fact finder determines that two or more heinous elements exist; or</p>
          <p>(2) the person has a previous sex offense conviction for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458#stat.609.3458.1">609.3458, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b), and the fact finder determines that a heinous element exists for the present offense.</p>
          <p>(b) A fact finder may not consider a heinous element if it is an element of the underlying specified violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>. In addition, when determining whether two or more heinous elements exist, the fact finder may not use the same underlying facts to support a determination that more than one element exists.</p>
          <p>(c) The court shall sentence a person who was under 18 years of age at the time of the commission of an offense described in paragraph (a) to imprisonment for life.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Mandatory life sentence for egregious first-time offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding the statutory maximum penalty otherwise applicable to the offense, the court shall sentence a person to imprisonment for life if the person is convicted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342#stat.609.342.1">609.342, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d), or (e), or subdivision 1a, clause (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), or (i); or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343#stat.609.343.1">609.343, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d), or (e), or subdivision 1a, clause (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), or (i); and the fact finder determines that a heinous element exists.</p>
          <p>(b) The fact finder may not consider a heinous element if it is an element of the underlying specified violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Mandatory sentence for certain engrained offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A court shall commit a person to the commissioner of corrections for a period of time that is not less than double the presumptive sentence under the sentencing guidelines and not more than the statutory maximum, or if the statutory maximum is less than double the presumptive sentence, for a period of time that is equal to the statutory maximum, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the court is imposing an executed sentence on a person convicted of committing or attempting to commit a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) the fact finder determines that the offender is a danger to public safety; and</p>
          <p>(3) the fact finder determines that the offender's criminal sexual behavior is so engrained that the risk of reoffending is great without intensive psychotherapeutic intervention or other long-term treatment or supervision extending beyond the presumptive term of imprisonment and supervised release.</p>
          <p>(b) The fact finder shall base its determination that the offender is a danger to public safety on any of the following factors:</p>
          <p>(1) the crime involved an aggravating factor that would justify a durational departure from the presumptive sentence under the sentencing guidelines;</p>
          <p>(2) the offender previously committed or attempted to commit a predatory crime or a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>, including:</p>
          <p>(i) an offense committed as a juvenile that would have been a predatory crime or a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a> if committed by an adult; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a violation or attempted violation of a similar law of any other state or the United States; or</p>
          <p>(3) the offender planned or prepared for the crime prior to its commission.</p>
          <p>(c) As used in this section, "predatory crime" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341">609.341</a>, subdivision 22.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Mandatory life sentence; repeat offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding the statutory maximum penalty otherwise applicable to the offense, the court shall sentence a person to imprisonment for life if the person is convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a> and:</p>
          <p>(1) the person has two previous sex offense convictions;</p>
          <p>(2) the person has a previous sex offense conviction and:</p>
          <p>(i) the fact finder determines that the present offense involved an aggravating factor that would provide grounds for an upward durational departure under the sentencing guidelines other than the aggravating factor applicable to repeat criminal sexual conduct convictions;</p>
