          <p>(ii) the person received an upward durational departure from the sentencing guidelines for the previous sex offense conviction; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the person was sentenced under this section or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.108, for the previous sex offense conviction; or</p>
          <p>(3) the person has two prior sex offense convictions, and the fact finder determines that the prior convictions and present offense involved at least three separate victims, and:</p>
          <p>(i) the fact finder determines that the present offense involved an aggravating factor that would provide grounds for an upward durational departure under the sentencing guidelines other than the aggravating factor applicable to repeat criminal sexual conduct convictions;</p>
          <p>(ii) the person received an upward durational departure from the sentencing guidelines for one of the prior sex offense convictions; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the person was sentenced under this section or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.108, for one of the prior sex offense convictions.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a court may not sentence a person to imprisonment for life for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, unless the person's previous or prior sex offense convictions that are being used as the basis for the sentence are for violations of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, or any similar statute of the United States, this state, or any other state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Life sentences; minimum term of imprisonment.</span></h2>
          <p>At the time of sentencing under subdivision 3 or 4, the court shall specify a minimum term of imprisonment, based on the sentencing guidelines or any applicable mandatory minimum sentence, that must be served before the offender may be considered for supervised release. If the offender was under 18 years of age at the time of the commission of the offense, the minimum term of imprisonment specified by the court shall not exceed the applicable minimum term of imprisonment described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.05">244.05</a>, subdivision 4b.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Mandatory ten-year conditional release term.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the statutory maximum sentence otherwise applicable to the offense and unless a longer conditional release term is required in subdivision 7, when a court commits an offender to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, the court shall provide that, after the offender has been released from prison, the commissioner shall place the offender on conditional release for ten years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Mandatory lifetime conditional release term.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When a court sentences an offender under subdivision 3 or 4, the court shall provide that, if the offender is released from prison, the commissioner of corrections shall place the offender on conditional release for the remainder of the offender's life.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding the statutory maximum sentence otherwise applicable to the offense, when the court commits an offender to the custody of the commissioner of corrections for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, and the offender has a previous or prior sex offense conviction, the court shall provide that, after the offender has been released from prison, the commissioner shall place the offender on conditional release for the remainder of the offender's life.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), an offender may not be placed on lifetime conditional release for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, unless the offender's previous or prior sex offense conviction is for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (b), or any similar statute of the United States, this state, or any other state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Terms of conditional release; applicable to all sex offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The provisions of this subdivision relating to conditional release apply to all sex offenders sentenced to prison for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>. Except as provided in this subdivision, conditional release of sex offenders is governed by provisions relating to supervised release. The commissioner of corrections may not dismiss an offender on conditional release from supervision until the offender's conditional release term expires.</p>
          <p>(b) The conditions of release may include successful completion of treatment and aftercare in a program approved by the commissioner, satisfaction of the release conditions specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.05#stat.244.05.6">244.05, subdivision 6</a>, and any other conditions the commissioner considers appropriate. The commissioner shall develop a plan to pay the cost of treatment of a person released under this subdivision. The plan may include co-payments from offenders, third-party payers, local agencies, or other funding sources as they are identified. This section does not require the commissioner to accept or retain an offender in a treatment program. Before the offender is placed on conditional release, the commissioner shall notify the sentencing court and the prosecutor in the jurisdiction where the offender was sentenced of the terms of the offender's conditional release. The commissioner also shall make reasonable efforts to notify the victim of the offender's crime of the terms of the offender's conditional release.</p>
          <p>(c) If the offender fails to meet any condition of release, the commissioner may revoke the offender's conditional release and order that the offender serve all or a part of the remaining portion of the conditional release term in prison. An offender, while on supervised release, is not entitled to credit against the offender's conditional release term for time served in confinement for a violation of release.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The provisions of this section do not affect the applicability of Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.108, to crimes committed before August 1, 2005, or the validity of sentences imposed under Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.108.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3455.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Presumptive executed sentence for repeat sex offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in subdivision 2, 3, 3a, or 4, if a person is convicted under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a> within 15 years of a previous sex offense conviction, the court shall commit the defendant to the commissioner of corrections for not less than three years, nor more than the maximum sentence provided by law for the offense for which convicted, notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/242.19">242.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05">243.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.11">609.11</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.12">609.12</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a>. The court may stay the execution of the sentence imposed under this subdivision only if it finds that a professional assessment indicates the offender is accepted by and can respond to treatment at a long-term inpatient program exclusively treating sex offenders and approved by the commissioner of corrections. If the court stays the execution of a sentence, it shall include the following as conditions of probation:</p>
          <p>(1) incarceration in a local jail or workhouse; and</p>
          <p>(2) a requirement that the offender successfully complete the treatment program and aftercare as directed by the court.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3455.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.2.21.0">2005 c 136 art 2 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.22.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 22</a>,23; art 4 s 14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.6.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/86/#laws.3.10.0">2013 c 86 art 3 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/96/#laws.0.3.0">2013 c 96 s 3</a>-5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.21.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.18.10.0">2023 c 52 art 18 s 10</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.4.12.0">2024 c 123 art 4 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3456">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3456 USE OF POLYGRAPHS FOR SEX OFFENDERS ON PROBATION OR CONDITIONAL RELEASE.</h1>
        <p>(a) A court may order as an intermediate sanction under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> and the commissioner of corrections may order as a condition of release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.05">244.05</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a> that an offender under supervision for a sex offense submit to polygraphic examinations to ensure compliance with the terms of probation or conditions of release.</p>
        <p>(b) The court or commissioner may order the offender to pay all or a portion of the costs of the examinations. The fee may be waived if the offender is indigent or if payment would result in an economic hardship to the offender's immediate family.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3456.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.3.24.0">2005 c 136 art 3 s 24</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3457">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3457 SEX OFFENDER ASSESSMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3457.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Assessment required.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is convicted of a sex offense, the court shall order an independent professional assessment of the offender's need for sex offender treatment to be completed before sentencing. The court may waive the assessment if: (1) the Sentencing Guidelines provide a presumptive prison sentence for the offender, or (2) an adequate assessment was conducted prior to the conviction. An assessor providing an assessment for the court must be experienced in the evaluation and treatment of sex offenders.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3457.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Repeat offenders; mandatory assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is convicted of a felony-level sex offense, and the person has previously been convicted of a sex offense regardless of the penalty level, the court shall order a sex offender assessment to be completed by the Minnesota security hospital. The assessment must contain the facts upon which the assessment conclusion is based, with reference to the offense history of the offender or the severity of the current offense, the social history of the offender, and the results of an examination of the offender's mental status unless the offender refuses to be examined. The assessment conclusion may not be based on testing alone. Upon completion, the assessment must be forwarded to the court and the commissioner of corrections. The court shall consider the assessment when sentencing the offender and, if applicable, when making the preliminary determination regarding the appropriateness of a civil commitment petition under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.1351">609.1351</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3457.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Access to data.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.384">13.384</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.85">13.85</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.171">260B.171</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.171">260C.171</a>, or chapter 260E, the assessor has access to the following private or confidential data on the person if access is relevant and necessary for the assessment:</p>
          <p>(1) medical data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.384">13.384</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) corrections and detention data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.85">13.85</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) health records under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) juvenile court records under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.171">260B.171</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.171">260C.171</a>; and</p>
          <p>(5) local welfare agency records under chapter 260E.</p>
          <p>Data disclosed under this section may be used only for purposes of the assessment and may not be further disclosed to any other person, except as authorized by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3457.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Treatment order.</span></h2>
          <p>If the assessment indicates that the offender is in need of and amenable to sex offender treatment, the court shall include in the sentence a requirement that the offender undergo treatment, unless the court sentences the offender to prison.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3457.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "sex offense" means a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.746#stat.609.746.1">609.746, subdivision 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.79">609.79</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.23">617.23</a>; or another offense arising out of a charge based on one or more of those sections.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3457.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.1.20.0">1992 c 571 art 1 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/139/#laws.4.2.0">1999 c 139 art 4 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/227/#laws.0.22.0">1999 c 227 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/210/#laws.0.24.0">2001 c 210 s 24</a>-26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.66.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 66</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.3.23.0">2005 c 136 art 3 s 23</a>; art 4 s 11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.138.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 138</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3458">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3458 SEXUAL EXTORTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3458.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who engages in sexual contact with another person and compels the other person to submit to the contact by making any of the following threats, directly or indirectly, is guilty of sexual extortion:</p>
          <p>(1) a threat to withhold or harm the complainant's trade, business, profession, position, employment, or calling;</p>
          <p>(2) a threat to make or cause to be made a criminal charge against the complainant, whether true or false;</p>
          <p>(3) a threat to report the complainant's immigration status to immigration or law enforcement authorities;</p>
          <p>(4) a threat to disseminate private sexual images of the complainant as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.261">617.261</a>, nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images;</p>
          <p>(5) a threat to expose information that the actor knows the complainant wishes to keep confidential; or</p>
          <p>(6) a threat to withhold complainant's housing, or to cause complainant a loss or disadvantage in the complainant's housing, or a change in the cost of complainant's housing.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who engages in sexual penetration with another person and compels the other person to submit to such penetration by making any of the following threats, directly or indirectly, is guilty of sexual extortion:</p>
          <p>(1) a threat to withhold or harm the complainant's trade, business, profession, position, employment, or calling;</p>
          <p>(2) a threat to make or cause to be made a criminal charge against the complainant, whether true or false;</p>
          <p>(3) a threat to report the complainant's immigration status to immigration or law enforcement authorities;</p>
          <p>(4) a threat to disseminate private sexual images of the complainant as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.261">617.261</a>, nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images;</p>
          <p>(5) a threat to expose information that the actor knows the complainant wishes to keep confidential; or</p>
          <p>(6) a threat to withhold complainant's housing, or to cause complainant a loss or disadvantage in the complainant's housing, or a change in the cost of complainant's housing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3458.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the person violates subdivision 1, paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both, if the person violates subdivision 1, paragraph (b).</p>
          <p>(c) A person convicted under this section is also subject to conditional release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3455">609.3455</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3458.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">No attempt charge.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.17">609.17</a>, no person may be charged with or convicted of an attempt to commit a violation of this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3458.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.22.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 22</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3459">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3459 LAW ENFORCEMENT; REPORTS OF SEXUAL ASSAULTS.</h1>
        <p>(a) A victim of any violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a> may initiate a law enforcement investigation by contacting any law enforcement agency, regardless of where the crime may have occurred. The agency must prepare a summary of the allegation and provide the person with a copy of it. The agency must begin an investigation of the facts, or, if the suspected crime was committed in a different jurisdiction, refer the matter along with the summary to the law enforcement agency where the suspected crime was committed for an investigation of the facts. If the agency learns that both the victim and the accused are members of the Minnesota National Guard, the agency receiving the report must refer the matter along with the summary to the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension for investigation pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.80">299C.80</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) If a law enforcement agency refers the matter to the law enforcement agency where the crime was committed, it need not include the allegation as a crime committed in its jurisdiction for purposes of information that the agency is required to provide to the commissioner of public safety pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.06">299C.06</a>, but must confirm that the other law enforcement agency has received the referral.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3459.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/5/#laws.4.10.0">1Sp2019 c 5 art 4 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.37.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 37</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.346"><b>609.346</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.16.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 16</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.3461"><b>609.3461</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.117">609.117</a>]
</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3469">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3469 VOLUNTARY INTOXICATION DEFENSE.</h1>
        <p>(a) The "knows or has reason to know" mental state requirement for violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a> involving a complainant who is mentally incapacitated, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341#stat.609.341.7">609.341, subdivision 7</a>, clause (2), involves specific intent for purposes of determining the applicability of the voluntary intoxication defense described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.075">609.075</a>. This defense may be raised by a defendant if the defense is otherwise applicable under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.075">609.075</a> and related case law.</p>
        <p>(b) Nothing in paragraph (a) may be interpreted to change the application of the defense to other crimes.</p>
        <p>(c) Nothing in paragraph (a) is intended to change the scope or limitations of the defense or case law interpreting it beyond clarifying that the defense is available to a defendant described in paragraph (a).</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3469.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.23.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 23</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.347">
        <h1 class="shn">609.347 EVIDENCE IN CRIMINAL SEXUAL CONDUCT CASES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Victim testimony; corroboration unnecessary.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, the testimony of a victim need not be corroborated.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Showing of resistance unnecessary.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, there is no need to show that the victim resisted the accused.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Previous sexual conduct.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.365">609.365</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, evidence of the victim's previous sexual conduct shall not be admitted nor shall any reference to such conduct be made in the presence of the jury, except by court order under the procedure provided in subdivision 4. The evidence can be admitted only if the probative value of the evidence is not substantially outweighed by its inflammatory or prejudicial nature and only in the circumstances set out in paragraphs (a) and (b). For the evidence to be admissible under paragraph (a), subsection (i), the judge must find by a preponderance of the evidence that the facts set out in the accused's offer of proof are true. For the evidence to be admissible under paragraph (a), subsection (ii) or paragraph (b), the judge must find that the evidence is sufficient to support a finding that the facts set out in the accused's offer of proof are true, as provided under Rule 901 of the Rules of Evidence.</p>
          <p>(a) When consent of the victim is a defense in the case, the following evidence is admissible:</p>
          <p>(i) evidence of the victim's previous sexual conduct tending to establish a common scheme or plan of similar sexual conduct under circumstances similar to the case at issue. In order to find a common scheme or plan, the judge must find that the victim made prior allegations of sexual assault which were fabricated; and</p>
          <p>(ii) evidence of the victim's previous sexual conduct with the accused.</p>
          <p>(b) When the prosecution's case includes evidence of semen, pregnancy, or disease at the time of the incident or, in the case of pregnancy, between the time of the incident and trial, evidence of specific instances of the victim's previous sexual conduct is admissible solely to show the source of the semen, pregnancy, or disease.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Accused offer of evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>The accused may not offer evidence described in subdivision 3 except pursuant to the following procedure:</p>
          <p>(a) A motion shall be made by the accused at least three business days prior to trial, unless later for good cause shown, setting out with particularity the offer of proof of the evidence that the accused intends to offer, relative to the previous sexual conduct of the victim;</p>
          <p>(b) If the court deems the offer of proof sufficient, the court shall order a hearing out of the presence of the jury, if any, and in such hearing shall allow the accused to make a full presentation of the offer of proof;</p>
          <p>(c) At the conclusion of the hearing, if the court finds that the evidence proposed to be offered by the accused regarding the previous sexual conduct of the victim is admissible under subdivision 3 and that its probative value is not substantially outweighed by its inflammatory or prejudicial nature, the court shall make an order stating the extent to which evidence is admissible. The accused may then offer evidence pursuant to the order of the court;</p>
          <p>(d) If new information is discovered after the date of the hearing or during the course of trial, which may make evidence described in subdivision 3 admissible, the accused may make an offer of proof pursuant to clause (a) and the court shall order an in camera hearing to determine whether the proposed evidence is admissible by the standards herein.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Prohibiting instructing jury on certain points.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, the court shall not instruct the jury to the effect that:</p>
          <p>(a) it may be inferred that a victim who has previously consented to sexual intercourse with persons other than the accused would be therefore more likely to consent to sexual intercourse again; or</p>
          <p>(b) the victim's previous or subsequent sexual conduct in and of itself may be considered in determining the credibility of the victim; or</p>
          <p>(c) criminal sexual conduct is a crime easily charged by a victim but very difficult to disprove by an accused because of the heinous nature of the crime; or</p>
          <p>(d) the jury should scrutinize the testimony of the victim any more closely than it should scrutinize the testimony of any witness in any felony prosecution.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Psychotherapy evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In a prosecution under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, involving a psychotherapist and patient, evidence of the patient's personal or medical history is not admissible except when:</p>
          <p>(1) the accused requests a hearing at least three business days prior to trial and makes an offer of proof of the relevancy of the history; and</p>
          <p>(2) the court finds that the history is relevant and that the probative value of the history outweighs its prejudicial value.</p>
          <p>(b) The court shall allow the admission only of specific information or examples of conduct of the victim that are determined by the court to be relevant. The court's order shall detail the information or conduct that is admissible and no other evidence of the history may be introduced.</p>
          <p>(c) Violation of the terms of the order is grounds for mistrial but does not prevent the retrial of the accused.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.347.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Effect of statute on rules.</span></h2>
          <p>Rule 412 of the Rules of Evidence is superseded to the extent of its conflict with this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.347.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.8.0">1975 c 374 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/588/#laws.0.10.0">1984 c 588 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/297/#laws.0.8.0">1985 c 297 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/351/#laws.0.12.0">1986 c 351 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.1.72.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/114/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 114 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.5.10.0">1997 c 239 art 5 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.8.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 8</a>-12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.4.6.0">2005 c 136 art 4 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/13/#laws.3.37.0">2007 c 13 art 3 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3471">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3471 RECORDS PERTAINING TO VICTIM IDENTITY CONFIDENTIAL.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, no data contained in records or reports relating to petitions, complaints, or indictments issued pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, which specifically identifies a victim who is a minor shall be accessible to the public, except by order of the court. Nothing in this section authorizes denial of access to any other data contained in the records or reports, including the identity of the defendant.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3471.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/573/#laws.0.9.0">1984 c 573 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/119/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 119 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/351/#laws.0.13.0">1986 c 351 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.1.73.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 1 s 73</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/331/#laws.0.9.0">1987 c 331 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.1.26.0">1992 c 571 art 1 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/13/#laws.1.49.0">1993 c 13 art 1 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.4.7.0">2005 c 136 art 4 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.6.15.0">2015 c 65 art 6 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.348">
        <h1 class="shn">609.348 MEDICAL PURPOSES; EXCLUSION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>; and Minnesota Statutes 2004, section 609.109, do not apply to sexual penetration or sexual contact when done for a bona fide medical purpose.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.348.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.9.0">1975 c 374 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/273/#laws.0.5.0">1981 c 273 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/351/#laws.0.14.0">1986 c 351 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.6.13.0">1998 c 367 art 6 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.4.8.0">2005 c 136 art 4 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/13/#laws.3.37.0">2007 c 13 art 3 s 37</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.349"><b>609.349</b> MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/16/#laws.0.1.0">2019 c 16 s 1</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.35">
        <h1 class="shn">609.35 COSTS OF MEDICAL EXAMINATION.</h1>
        <p>(a) Costs incurred by a hospital or other emergency medical facility or by a physician, sexual assault nurse examiner, forensic nurse, or other licensed health care provider for the examination of a victim of criminal sexual conduct that occurred in the state shall be paid by the state. These costs include, but are not limited to, the cost of the medical forensic examination, associated tests and treatments relating to sexually transmitted infection, and pregnancy status, including emergency contraception. A hospital, emergency medical facility, or health care provider shall submit the costs for examination and any associated tests and treatment to the Office of Justice Programs for payment. Upon receipt of the costs, the commissioner shall provide payment to the facility or health care provider. Reimbursement for an examination and any associated test and treatments shall not exceed $1,400. Beginning on January 1, 2024, the maximum amount of an award shall be adjusted annually by the inflation rate.</p>
        <p>(b) Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the duties, responsibilities, or liabilities of any insurer, whether public or private. The hospital or other licensed health care provider performing the examination may seek insurance reimbursement from the victim's insurer only if authorized by the victim. This authorization may only be sought after the examination is performed. When seeking this authorization, the hospital or other licensed health care provider shall inform the victim that if the victim does not authorize this, the state is required by law to pay for the examination and that the victim is in no way liable for these costs or obligated to authorize the reimbursement.</p>
        <p>(c) The applicability of this section does not depend upon whether the victim reports the offense to law enforcement or the existence or status of any investigation or prosecution.</p>
        <p>(d) Requests for reimbursement and supporting documents are private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.35.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.11.0">1975 c 374 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/273/#laws.0.6.0">1981 c 273 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/351/#laws.0.16.0">1986 c 351 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.1.75.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 1 s 75</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/381/#laws.0.6.0">2002 c 381 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/116/#laws.0.3.0">2003 c 116 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.5.46.0">2023 c 52 art 5 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.2.5.0">2024 c 123 art 2 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.351">
        <h1 class="shn">609.351 APPLICABILITY TO PAST AND PRESENT PROSECUTIONS.</h1>
        <p>Except for section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.347">609.347</a>, crimes committed prior to August 1, 1975, are not affected by its provisions.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.351.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/374/#laws.0.12.0">1975 c 374 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.352">
        <h1 class="shn">609.352 SOLICITATION OF CHILDREN TO ENGAGE IN SEXUAL CONDUCT; COMMUNICATION OF SEXUALLY EXPLICIT MATERIALS TO CHILDREN.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.352.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">As used in this section:</p>
          <p class="in">(a) "child" means a person 15 years of age or younger;</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "sexual conduct" means sexual contact of the individual's primary genital area, sexual penetration as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.341">609.341</a>, or sexual performance as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.246">617.246</a>; and</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "solicit" means commanding, entreating, or attempting to persuade a specific person in person, by telephone, by letter, or by computerized or other electronic means.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.352.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibited act.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person 18 years of age or older who solicits a child or someone the person reasonably believes is a child to engage in sexual conduct with intent to engage in sexual conduct is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.352.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Electronic solicitation of children.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person 18 years of age or older who uses the Internet, a computer, computer program, computer network, computer system, an electronic communications system, or a telecommunications, wire, or radio communications system, or other electronic device capable of electronic data storage or transmission to commit any of the following acts, with the intent to arouse the sexual desire of any person, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) soliciting a child or someone the person reasonably believes is a child to engage in sexual conduct;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) engaging in communication with a child or someone the person reasonably believes is a child, relating to or describing sexual conduct; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) distributing any material, language, or communication, including a photographic or video image, that relates to or describes sexual conduct to a child or someone the person reasonably believes is a child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.352.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person may be convicted of an offense under subdivision 2a if the transmission that constitutes the offense either originates within this state or is received within this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.352.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Defenses.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Mistake as to age is not a defense to a prosecution under this section.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The fact that an undercover operative or law enforcement officer was involved in the detection or investigation of an offense under this section does not constitute a defense to a prosecution under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.352.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person convicted under subdivision 2 or 2a is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.352.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/445/#laws.0.3.0">1986 c 445 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/311/#laws.4.3.0">2000 c 311 art 4 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.7.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/59/#laws.1.6.0">2009 c 59 art 1 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.38.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 38</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.353">
        <h1 class="shn">609.353 JURISDICTION.</h1>
        <p>A violation or attempted violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3453">609.3453</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3458">609.3458</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.352">609.352</a> may be prosecuted in any jurisdiction in which the violation originates or terminates.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.353.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/311/#laws.4.5.0">2000 c 311 art 4 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.4.9.0">2005 c 136 art 4 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST THE FAMILY</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.355">
        <h1 class="shn">609.355 BIGAMY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.355.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>In this section "cohabit" means to live together under the representation or appearance of being married.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.355.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of bigamy and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) knowingly having a prior marriage that is not dissolved, contracts a marriage in this state; or</p>
          <p>(2) contracts a marriage with another in this state with knowledge that the prior marriage of the other is not dissolved; or</p>
          <p>(3) marries another outside this state with knowledge that either of them has a prior marriage that has not been dissolved, and then cohabits with the other in this state.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.355.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.355; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.36"><b>609.36</b> MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.25.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 25</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.364"><b>609.364</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.24.0">1985 c 286 s 24</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.3641"><b>609.3641</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.24.0">1985 c 286 s 24</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.3642"><b>609.3642</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.24.0">1985 c 286 s 24</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.3643"><b>609.3643</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.24.0">1985 c 286 s 24</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.3644"><b>609.3644</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/286/#laws.0.24.0">1985 c 286 s 24</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.365">
        <h1 class="shn">609.365 INCEST.</h1>
        <p>Whoever has sexual intercourse with another nearer of kin to the actor than first cousin, computed by rules of the civil law, whether of the half or the whole blood, with knowledge of the relationship, is guilty of incest and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.365.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.365; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.37"><b>609.37</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/340/#laws.0.60.0">1993 c 340 s 60</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.375">
        <h1 class="shn">609.375 NONSUPPORT OF SPOUSE OR CHILD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever is legally obligated to provide court-ordered support to a spouse or child, whether or not the child's custody has been granted to another, and knowingly omits and fails to do so is guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor violation.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the violation continues for a period in excess of 90 days but not more than 180 days; or</p>
          <p>(2) the person is in arrears in court-ordered child support or maintenance payments, or both, in an amount equal to or greater than six times but less than nine times the person's total monthly support and maintenance payments.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Felony violation.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a felony and upon conviction may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the violation continues for a period in excess of 180 days; or</p>
          <p>(2) the person is in arrears in court-ordered child support or maintenance payments, or both, in an amount equal to or greater than nine times the person's total monthly support and maintenance payments.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Attempt to obtain contempt order as prerequisite to prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>A person may not be charged with violating this section unless there has been an attempt to obtain a court order holding the person in contempt for failing to pay support or maintenance under chapter 518 or 518A. This requirement is satisfied by a showing that reasonable attempts have been made at service of the order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.6.93.0">1997 c 203 art 6 s 93</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/245/#laws.1.34.0">1997 c 245 art 1 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.6.93.0">1997 c 203 art 6 s 93</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/245/#laws.1.34.0">1997 c 245 art 1 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates this section may be prosecuted and tried in the county in which the support obligor resides or in the county in which the obligee or the child resides.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.6.93.0">1997 c 203 art 6 s 93</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/245/#laws.1.34.0">1997 c 245 art 1 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Conditions of work release; probation violation.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon conviction under this section, a defendant may obtain work release only upon the imposition of an automatic income withholding order, and may be required to post a bond in avoidance of jail time and conditioned upon payment of all court-ordered support owed. Nonpayment of court-ordered support is a violation of any probation granted following conviction under subdivision 2a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.375.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It is an affirmative defense to criminal liability under this section if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the omission and failure to provide court-ordered support were with lawful excuse.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.375.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.375; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.44.0">1971 c 23 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/507/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 507 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/2/#laws.0.151.0">1976 c 2 s 151</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/31/#laws.0.19.0">1981 c 31 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/340/#laws.0.54.0">1993 c 340 s 54</a>,55; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/630/#laws.11.17.0">1994 c 630 art 11 s 17</a>-20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/257/#laws.3.15.0">1995 c 257 art 3 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/245/#laws.1.31.0">1997 c 245 art 1 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/158/#laws.0.7.0">2001 c 158 s 7</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/164/#laws.0.29.0">2005 c 164 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/7/#laws.0.28.0">1Sp2005 c 7 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/242/#laws.0.1.0">2014 c 242 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3751">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3751 DISCHARGE AND DISMISSAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3751.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is eligible for a discharge and dismissal under this section, if the person:</p>
          <p>(1) has not been previously convicted of a felony under the laws of this state or elsewhere;</p>
          <p>(2) has not been previously convicted of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.375">609.375</a> or of a similar offense in this state or elsewhere;</p>
          <p>(3) has not previously participated in or completed a diversion program relating to a charge of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.375">609.375</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) has not previously been placed on probation without a judgment of guilty for violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.375">609.375</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3751.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Procedure.</span></h2>
          <p>For a person eligible under subdivision 1 who is charged with violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.375">609.375</a>, the court may after trial or upon a plea of guilty, without entering a judgment of guilty and with the consent of the person, defer further proceedings and place the person on probation upon such reasonable conditions as it may require and for a period not to exceed the maximum sentence provided for the violation. At a minimum, the conditions must require the defendant to:</p>
          <p>(1) provide the public authority responsible for child support enforcement with an affidavit attesting to the defendant's present address, occupation, employer, current income, assets, and account information, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13B.06">13B.06</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) execute a written payment agreement regarding both current support and arrearages that is approved by the court.</p>
          <p>In determining whether to approve a payment agreement under clause (2), the court shall apply the provisions of chapter 518A consistent with the obligor's ability to pay.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3751.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Violation.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon violation of a condition of the probation, including a failure to comply with the written payment agreement approved by the court under subdivision 2, clause (2), the court may enter an adjudication of guilt and proceed as otherwise provided in law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3751.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Early dismissal.</span></h2>
          <p>The court may, in its discretion, dismiss the proceedings against the person and discharge the person from probation before the expiration of the maximum period prescribed for the person's probation but may do so only if the full amount of any arrearages has been brought current.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3751.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Dismissal; record.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, "not public" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.8a">13.02, subdivision 8a</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) If during the period of probation the person does not violate any of the conditions of the probation, then upon expiration of the period the court shall discharge the person and dismiss the proceedings against that person. Discharge and dismissal under this subdivision shall be without court adjudication of guilt, but a not public record of it shall be retained by the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension for the purpose of use by the courts in determining the merits of subsequent proceedings against the person. The not public record may also be opened only upon court order for purposes of a criminal investigation, prosecution, or sentencing. Upon request by law enforcement, prosecution, or corrections authorities, the bureau shall notify the requesting party of the existence of the not public record and the right to seek a court order to open it pursuant to this section. The court shall forward a record of any discharge and dismissal under this section to the bureau which shall make and maintain the not public record of it as provided under this section. The discharge or dismissal shall not be deemed a conviction for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law upon conviction of a crime or for any other purpose.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3751.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/158/#laws.0.12.0">2001 c 158 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/164/#laws.0.29.0">2005 c 164 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/7/#laws.0.28.0">1Sp2005 c 7 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.376">
        <h1 class="shn">609.376 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.376.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Terms defined.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255">609.255</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.376">609.376</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.38">609.38</a>, the following terms have the meanings given unless specific content indicates otherwise.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.376.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Child.</span></h2>
          <p>"Child" means any person under the age of 18 years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.376.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Caretaker.</span></h2>
          <p>"Caretaker" means an individual who has responsibility for the care of a child as a result of a family relationship or who has assumed responsibility for all or a portion of the care of a child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.376.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Complainant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Complainant" means a person alleged to have been a victim of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255#stat.609.255.3">609.255, subdivision 3</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.377">609.377</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.378">609.378</a>, but need not be the person who signs the complaint.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.376.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/217/#laws.0.3.0">1983 c 217 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.377">
        <h1 class="shn">609.377 MALICIOUS PUNISHMENT OF CHILD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.377.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Malicious punishment.</span></h2>
          <p>A parent, legal guardian, or caretaker who, by an intentional act or a series of intentional acts with respect to a child, evidences unreasonable force or cruel discipline that is excessive under the circumstances is guilty of malicious punishment of a child and may be sentenced as provided in subdivisions 2 to 6.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.377.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>If the punishment results in less than substantial bodily harm, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.377.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Enhancement to a felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates the provisions of subdivision 2 during the time period between a previous conviction or adjudication for delinquency under this section or sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.224">609.224</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2242">609.2242</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a>, and the end of five years following discharge from sentence or disposition for that conviction or adjudication may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine of $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.377.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Felony; child under age four.</span></h2>
          <p>If the punishment is to a child under the age of four and causes bodily harm to the head, eyes, neck, or otherwise causes multiple bruises to the body, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine of $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.377.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Felony; substantial bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>If the punishment results in substantial bodily harm, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.377.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Felony; great bodily harm.</span></h2>
          <p>If the punishment results in great bodily harm, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.377.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/217/#laws.0.4.0">1983 c 217 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/655/#laws.0.2.0">1988 c 655 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.16.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/542/#laws.0.18.0">1990 c 542 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.37.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/437/#laws.0.14.0">2000 c 437 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3775">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3775 CHILD TORTURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3775.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "torture" means the intentional infliction of extreme mental anguish, or extreme psychological or physical abuse, when committed in an especially depraved manner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3775.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who tortures a child is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 25 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.3775.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Proof; evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Expert testimony as to the existence or extent of mental anguish or psychological abuse is not a requirement for a conviction under this section.</p>
          <p>(b) A child's special susceptibility to mental anguish or psychological abuse does not constitute an independent cause of the condition so that a defendant is exonerated from criminal liability.</p>
          <p>(c) Proof that a victim suffered pain is not an element of a violation of this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3775.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.39.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 39</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.378">
        <h1 class="shn">609.378 NEGLECT OR ENDANGERMENT OF CHILD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.378.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Persons guilty of neglect or endangerment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a)(1) A parent, legal guardian, or caretaker who willfully deprives a child of necessary food, clothing, shelter, health care, or supervision appropriate to the child's age, when the parent, guardian, or caretaker is reasonably able to make the necessary provisions and the deprivation harms or is likely to substantially harm the child's physical, mental, or emotional health is guilty of neglect of a child and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both. If the deprivation results in substantial harm to the child's physical, mental, or emotional health, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both. If a parent, guardian, or caretaker responsible for the child's care in good faith selects and depends upon spiritual means or prayer for treatment or care of disease or remedial care of the child, this treatment or care is "health care," for purposes of this clause.</p>
          <p>(2) A parent, legal guardian, or caretaker who knowingly permits the continuing physical or sexual abuse of a child is guilty of neglect of a child and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A parent, legal guardian, or caretaker who endangers the child's person or health by:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally or recklessly causing or permitting a child to be placed in a situation likely to substantially harm the child's physical, mental, or emotional health or cause the child's death; or</p>
          <p>(2) knowingly causing or permitting the child to be present where any person is selling, manufacturing, possessing immediate precursors or chemical substances with intent to manufacture, or possessing a controlled substance, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.4">152.01, subdivision 4</a>, in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.021">152.021</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.022">152.022</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.023">152.023</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.024">152.024</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.0262">152.0262</a>; is guilty of child endangerment and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>If the endangerment results in substantial harm to the child's physical, mental, or emotional health, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>This paragraph does not prevent a parent, legal guardian, or caretaker from causing or permitting a child to engage in activities that are appropriate to the child's age, stage of development, and experience, or from selecting health care as defined in subdivision 1, paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) A person who intentionally or recklessly causes a child under 14 years of age to be placed in a situation likely to substantially harm the child's physical health or cause the child's death as a result of the child's access to a loaded firearm is guilty of child endangerment and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>If the endangerment results in substantial harm to the child's physical health, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.378.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Defenses.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a defense to a prosecution under subdivision 1, paragraph (a), clause (2), or paragraph (b), that at the time of the neglect or endangerment there was a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the defendant that acting to stop or prevent the neglect or endangerment would result in substantial bodily harm to the defendant or the child in retaliation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.378.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/217/#laws.0.5.0">1983 c 217 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.2.199.0">1989 c 282 art 2 s 199</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/571/#laws.4.11.0">1992 c 571 art 4 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.22.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/314/#laws.0.6.0">2002 c 314 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.7.21.0">2005 c 136 art 7 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.3785">
        <h1 class="shn">609.3785 UNHARMED NEWBORNS LEFT AT A SAFE PLACE; AVOIDANCE OF PROSECUTION.</h1>
        <p>A person may leave a newborn with an employee at a safe place, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.902">145.902</a>, in this state pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.139#stat.260C.139.4">260C.139, subdivision 4</a>, without being subjected to prosecution for that act, provided that:</p>
        <p>(1) the newborn was born within seven days of being left at the safe place, as determined within a reasonable degree of medical certainty;</p>
        <p>(2) the newborn is left in an unharmed condition; and</p>
        <p>(3) in cases where the person leaving the newborn is not the newborn's mother, the person has the mother's approval to do so.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.3785.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/421/#laws.0.3.0">2000 c 421 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.2.3.0">2012 c 216 art 2 s 3; art 6 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.379">
        <h1 class="shn">609.379 PERMITTED ACTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.379.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reasonable force.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Reasonable force may be used upon or toward the person of a child without the child's consent when the following circumstance exists or the actor reasonably believes it to exist:</p>
          <p>(1) when used by a parent, legal guardian, or other caretaker of a child, in the exercise of lawful authority, to restrain or correct the child; or</p>
