          <p>(2) when used by a teacher, school principal, school employee, school bus driver, other agent of a district, or other member of the instructional, support, or supervisory staff of a public or nonpublic school upon or toward a child or pupil when necessary to restrain the child or pupil to prevent bodily harm or death to the child, pupil, or another.</p>
          <p>(b) Nothing in this section limits any other authorization to use reasonable force including but not limited to authorizations under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/121A.582#stat.121A.582.1">121A.582, subdivision 1</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.06">609.06</a>, subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.379.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.425">260B.425</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.425">260C.425</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255">609.255</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.376">609.376</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.378">609.378</a> and chapter 260E.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.379.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/217/#laws.0.6.0">1983 c 217 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/266/#laws.0.4.0">1985 c 266 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/542/#laws.0.19.0">1990 c 542 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/139/#laws.4.2.0">1999 c 139 art 4 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.139.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 139</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/78/#laws.0.8.0">2024 c 78 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.38">
        <h1 class="shn">609.38 STAYED SENTENCE.</h1>
        <p>For any violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.255#stat.609.255.3">609.255, subdivision 3</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.377">609.377</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.378">609.378</a> for which the Sentencing Guidelines establish a presumptive executed sentence, the court may stay imposition or execution of the sentence if it finds that a stay is in the best interest of the complainant or the family unit and that the defendant is willing to participate in any necessary or appropriate treatment. In determining an appropriate sentence when there is a family relationship between the complainant and the defendant, the court shall be guided by the policy of preserving and strengthening the family unit whenever possible.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.38.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/217/#laws.0.7.0">1983 c 217 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.385">
        <h1 class="shn">609.385 TREASON.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.385.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Levying war" includes an act of war or an insurrection of several persons with intent to prevent, by force and intimidation, the execution of a statute of the state, or to force its repeal. It does not include either a conspiracy to commit an act of war or a single instance of resistance for a private purpose to the execution of a law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.385.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person owing allegiance to this state who does either of the following is guilty of treason against this state and shall be sentenced to life imprisonment:</p>
          <p>(1) levies war against this state; or</p>
          <p>(2) adheres to the enemies of this state, giving them aid and comfort.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.385.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Testimony required.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall be convicted of treason except on the testimony of two witnesses to the same overt act, or on the person's confession in open court.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.385.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.385; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.39">
        <h1 class="shn">609.39 MISPRISION OF TREASON.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, owing allegiance to this state and having knowledge of the commission of treason against this state, does not, as soon as may be, disclose and make it known to the governor or a judge of the supreme court, court of appeals, or district court, is guilty of misprision of treason against this state and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.39.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/247/#laws.0.208.0">1983 c 247 s 208</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.395">
        <h1 class="shn">609.395 STATE MILITARY FORCES; INTERFERING WITH, OBSTRUCTING, OR OTHER.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, when the United States is at war, does either of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) intentionally makes or conveys false reports or statements with intent to interfere with the operation or success of the military or naval forces of this state; or</p>
        <p>(2) intentionally causes or incites insubordination, disloyalty, mutiny, or refusal of duty in the military or naval forces of this state, or obstructs the recruiting or enlistment service of this state.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.395.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.395; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.396">
        <h1 class="shn">609.396 UNAUTHORIZED PRESENCE ON MILITARY INSTALLATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.396.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor if the person intentionally and without the authorization of the adjutant general or a duly appointed commander in accordance with federal regulations enters or is present on or in any campground, any military reservation, any armory, any installation, or any facility owned or controlled by the state or federal government for military purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.396.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to not more than five years imprisonment or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the person intentionally enters or is present in an area that is posted by order of the adjutant general as restricted for weapon firing or other hazardous military activity; and</p>
          <p>(2) the person knows that doing so creates a risk of death, bodily harm, or serious property damage.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.396.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.3.0">1989 c 5 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.12.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/100/#laws.0.21.0">2024 c 100 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.40">
        <h1 class="shn">609.40 FLAGS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.40.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>In this section "flag" means anything which is or purports to be the Stars and Stripes, the United States shield, the United States coat of arms, the Minnesota state flag, or a copy, picture, or representation of any of them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.40.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally and publicly mutilates, defiles, or casts contempt upon the flag; or</p>
          <p>(2) places on or attaches to the flag any word, mark, design, or advertisement not properly a part of such flag or exposes to public view a flag so altered; or</p>
          <p>(3) manufactures or exposes to public view an article of merchandise or a wrapper or receptacle for merchandise upon which the flag is depicted; or</p>
          <p>(4) uses the flag for commercial advertising purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.40.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to flags depicted on written or printed documents or periodicals or on stationery, ornaments, pictures, or jewelry, provided there are not unauthorized words or designs on such flags and provided the flag is not connected with any advertisement.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.40.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.40; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.45.0">1971 c 23 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.405"><b>609.405</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/10/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 10 s 1</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.41">
        <h1 class="shn">609.41 FALSE TAX STATEMENT.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, in making any statement, oral or written, which is required or authorized by law to be made as a basis of imposing, reducing, or abating any tax or assessment, intentionally makes any statement as to any material matter which the maker of the statement knows is false may be sentenced, unless otherwise provided by law, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.41.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.41; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AFFECTING PUBLIC<br>OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.415">
        <h1 class="shn">609.415 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.415.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.415">609.415</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.465">609.465</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.515">609.515</a>,</p>
          <p>(1) "Public officer" means:</p>
          <p>(a) an executive or administrative officer of the state or of a county, municipality or other subdivision or agency of the state;</p>
          <p>(b) a member of the legislature or of a governing board of a county, municipality, or other subdivision of the state, or other governmental instrumentality within the state;</p>
          <p>(c) a judicial officer;</p>
          <p>(d) a hearing officer;</p>
          <p>(e) a law enforcement officer; or</p>
          <p>(f) any other person exercising the functions of a public officer.</p>
          <p>(2) "Public employee" means a person employed by or acting for the state or a county, municipality, or other subdivision or governmental instrumentality of the state for the purpose of exercising their respective powers and performing their respective duties, and who is not a public officer. Public employee includes a member of a charter commission.</p>
          <p>(3) "Judicial officer" means a judge, court commissioner, referee, or any other person appointed by a judge or court to hear or determine a cause or controversy.</p>
          <p>(4) "Hearing officer" means any person authorized by law or private agreement to hear or determine a cause or controversy who is not a judicial officer.</p>
          <p>(5) "Political subdivision" means a county, town, statutory or home rule charter city, school district, special service district, or other municipal corporation of the state of Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.415.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Deemed officer or employee.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who has been elected, appointed, or otherwise designated as a public officer or public employee is deemed such officer or employee although the person has not yet qualified therefor or entered upon the duties thereof.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.415.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.415; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.88.0">1983 c 359 s 88</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/592/#laws.0.16.0">1992 c 592 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/352/#laws.0.13.0">2002 c 352 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.42">
        <h1 class="shn">609.42 BRIBERY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.42.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of bribery and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) offers, gives, or promises to give, directly or indirectly, to any person who is a public officer or employee any benefit, reward or consideration to which the person is not legally entitled with intent thereby to influence the person's performance of the powers or duties as such officer or employee; or</p>
          <p>(2) being a public officer or employee, requests, receives or agrees to receive, directly or indirectly, any such benefit, reward or consideration upon the understanding that it will have such an influence; or</p>
          <p>(3) offers, gives, or promises to give, directly or indirectly any such benefit, reward, or consideration to a person who is a witness or about to become a witness in a proceeding before a judicial or hearing officer, with intent that the person's testimony be influenced thereby, or that the person will not appear at the proceeding; or</p>
          <p>(4) as a person who is, or is about to become such witness requests, receives, or agrees to receive, directly or indirectly, any such benefit, reward, or consideration upon the understanding that the person's testimony will be so influenced, or that the person will not appear at the proceeding; or</p>
          <p>(5) accepts directly or indirectly a benefit, reward or consideration upon an agreement or understanding, express or implied, that the acceptor will refrain from giving information that may lead to the prosecution of a crime or purported crime or that the acceptor will abstain from, discontinue, or delay prosecution therefor, except in a case where a compromise is allowed by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.42.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture of office.</span></h2>
          <p>Any public officer who is convicted of violating or attempting to violate subdivision 1 shall forfeit the public officer's office and be forever disqualified from holding public office under the state.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.42.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.42; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/178/#laws.0.2.0">1976 c 178 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.425">
        <h1 class="shn">609.425 CORRUPTLY INFLUENCING LEGISLATOR.</h1>
        <p>Whoever by menace, deception, concealment of facts, or other corrupt means, attempts to influence the vote or other performance of duty of any member of the legislature or person elected thereto may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.425.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.425; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.43">
        <h1 class="shn">609.43 MISCONDUCT OF PUBLIC OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE.</h1>
        <p>A public officer or employee who does any of the following, for which no other sentence is specifically provided by law, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) intentionally fails or refuses to perform a known mandatory, nondiscretionary, ministerial duty of the office or employment within the time or in the manner required by law; or</p>
        <p>(2) in the capacity of such officer or employee, does an act knowing it is in excess of lawful authority or knowing it is forbidden by law to be done in that capacity; or</p>
        <p>(3) under pretense or color of official authority intentionally and unlawfully injures another in the other's person, property, or rights; or</p>
        <p>(4) in the capacity of such officer or employee, makes a return, certificate, official report, or other like document having knowledge it is false in any material respect.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.43.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.43; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.435">
        <h1 class="shn">609.435 OFFICER NOT FILING SECURITY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever intentionally performs the functions of a public officer without having executed and duly filed the required security is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.435.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.435; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.46.0">1971 c 23 s 46</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.44">
        <h1 class="shn">609.44 PUBLIC OFFICE; ILLEGALLY ASSUMING; NONSURRENDER.</h1>
        <p>Whoever intentionally and without lawful right thereto, exercises a function of a public office or, having held such office and the right thereto having ceased, refuses to surrender the office or its seal, books, papers, or other incidents to a successor or other authority entitled thereto may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.44.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.44; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.445">
        <h1 class="shn">609.445 FAILURE TO PAY OVER STATE FUNDS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever receives money on behalf of or for the account of the state or any of its agencies or subdivisions and intentionally refuses or omits to pay the same to the state or its agency or subdivision entitled thereto, or to an officer or agent authorized to receive the same, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.445.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.445; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.17.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.45">
        <h1 class="shn">609.45 PUBLIC OFFICER; UNAUTHORIZED COMPENSATION.</h1>
        <p>Whoever is a public officer or public employee and under color of office or employment intentionally asks, receives, or agrees to receive a fee or other compensation in excess of that allowed by law or where no such fee or compensation is allowed, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.45.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.45; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.47.0">1971 c 23 s 47</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.455">
        <h1 class="shn">609.455 PERMITTING FALSE CLAIMS AGAINST GOVERNMENT.</h1>
        <p>A public officer or employee who audits, allows, or pays any claim or demand made upon the state or subdivision thereof or other governmental instrumentality within the state which the public officer or employee knows is false or fraudulent in whole or in part, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.455.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.455; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.456">
        <h1 class="shn">609.456 REPORTING TO STATE AUDITOR AND LEGISLATIVE AUDITOR REQUIRED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.456.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">State auditor; police; firefighters; teachers.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever a public employee or public officer of a political subdivision, charter commission, or local public pension plan governed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/424A.091">424A.091</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/424A.096">424A.096</a> or chapter 354A, discovers evidence of theft, embezzlement, unlawful use of public funds or property, or misuse of public funds by a charter commission or any person authorized to expend public funds, the employee or officer shall promptly report to law enforcement and shall promptly report in writing to the state auditor a detailed description of the alleged incident or incidents. Notwithstanding chapter 13 or any other statute related to the classification of government data, the public employee or public officer shall provide data or information related to the alleged incident or incidents to the state auditor and law enforcement, including data classified as not public.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.456.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Legislative auditor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever an employee or officer of the state, University of Minnesota, or other organization listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/3.971#stat.3.971.6">3.971, subdivision 6</a>, discovers evidence of theft, embezzlement, or unlawful use of public funds or property, the employee or officer shall, except when to do so would knowingly impede or otherwise interfere with an ongoing criminal investigation, promptly report in writing to the legislative auditor a detailed description of the alleged incident or incidents.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.456.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/592/#laws.0.17.0">1992 c 592 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/99/#laws.0.21.0">1999 c 99 s 21</a>,23; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/352/#laws.0.14.0">2002 c 352 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/35/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 35 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/111/#laws.5.80.0">2013 c 111 art 5 s 80</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.46"><b>609.46</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/359/#laws.0.151.0">1983 c 359 s 151</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.465">
        <h1 class="shn">609.465 PRESENTING FALSE CLAIMS TO PUBLIC OFFICER OR BODY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, presents a claim or demand, with knowledge that it is false in whole or in part, for audit, allowance or payment to a public officer or body authorized to make such audit, allowance or payment is guilty of an attempt to commit theft of public funds and may be sentenced accordingly.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.465.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.465; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.466">
        <h1 class="shn">609.466 MEDICAL ASSISTANCE FRAUD.</h1>
        <p>Any person who, with the intent to defraud, presents a claim for reimbursement, a cost report or a rate application, relating to the payment of medical assistance funds pursuant to chapter 256B, to the state agency, which is false in whole or in part, is guilty of an attempt to commit theft of public funds and may be sentenced accordingly.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.466.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/188/#laws.0.5.0">1976 c 188 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.47">
        <h1 class="shn">609.47 INTERFERENCE WITH PROPERTY IN OFFICIAL CUSTODY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever intentionally takes, damages, or destroys any personal property held in custody by an officer or other person under process of law may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.47.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.47; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.475">
        <h1 class="shn">609.475 IMPERSONATING A MILITARY SERVICE MEMBER, VETERAN, OR PUBLIC OFFICIAL.</h1>
        <p>Whoever falsely impersonates an active or reserve component military service member, veteran, or public official with intent to wrongfully obtain money, property, or any other tangible benefit is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.475.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.475; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.49.0">1971 c 23 s 49</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.3.13.0">2017 c 95 art 3 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.4751">
        <h1 class="shn">609.4751 IMPERSONATING A PEACE OFFICER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.4751.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever falsely impersonates a peace officer with intent to mislead another into believing that the impersonator is actually an officer is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.4751.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 1 while committing any of the following acts is guilty of a gross misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) gaining access to a public building or government facility that is not open to the public;</p>
          <p>(2) without legal authority, directing or ordering another person to act or refrain from acting;</p>
          <p>(3) violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.64#stat.169.64.2">169.64, subdivision 2</a>, 3, or 4, or the siren provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.68">169.68</a>; or</p>
          <p>(4) operating a motor vehicle marked:</p>
          <p>(i) with the word or words "police," "patrolman," "sheriff," "deputy," "trooper," "state patrol," "conservation officer," "agent," or "marshal"; or</p>
          <p>(ii) with any lettering, marking, or insignia, or colorable imitation thereof, including, but not limited to, stars, badges, or shields identifying the vehicle as a law enforcement vehicle, and which a reasonable person would believe is a law enforcement vehicle governed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.98#stat.169.98.1">169.98, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.4751.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates this section within five years of a previous violation of this section is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.4751.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.3.14.0">2017 c 95 art 3 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.476">
        <h1 class="shn">609.476 PUBLISHING PERSONAL INFORMATION OF JUDICIAL OFFICIAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.476.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, the terms "personal information" and "judicial official" have the meanings given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/480.40">480.40, subdivision </a>1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.476.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>It is unlawful to knowingly publish the personal information of any judicial official in any publicly available publication, website, or media with the intent to threaten, intimidate, harass, or physically injure. A person convicted of violating this subdivision is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.476.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>If a person's violation of subdivision 2 also causes bodily harm as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02#stat.609.02.7">609.02, subdivision 7</a>, the person is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.476.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.12.4.0">2024 c 123 art 12 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST THE<br>ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.48">
        <h1 class="shn">609.48 PERJURY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.48.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever makes a false material statement not believing it to be true in any of the following cases is guilty of perjury and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4:</p>
          <p>(1) in or for an action, hearing or proceeding of any kind in which the statement is required or authorized by law to be made under oath or affirmation;</p>
          <p>(2) in any writing which is required or authorized by law to be under oath or affirmation;</p>
          <p>(3) in any writing made according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/358.115">358.115</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) in any writing made according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/358.116">358.116</a>; or</p>
          <p>(5) in any other case in which the penalties for perjury are imposed by law and no specific sentence is otherwise provided.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.48.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Defenses not available.</span></h2>
          <p>It is not a defense to a violation of this section that:</p>
          <p>(1) the oath or affirmation was taken or administered in an irregular manner; or</p>
          <p>(2) the declarant was not competent to give the statement; or</p>
          <p>(3) the declarant did not know that the statement was material or believed it to be immaterial; or</p>
          <p>(4) the statement was not used or, if used, did not affect the proceeding for which it was made; or</p>
          <p>(5) the statement was inadmissible under the law of evidence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.48.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Inconsistent statements.</span></h2>
          <p>When the declarant has made two inconsistent statements under such circumstances that one or the other must be false and not believed by the declarant when made, it shall be sufficient for conviction under this section to charge and the jury to find that, without determining which, one or the other of such statements was false and not believed by the declarant. The period of limitations for prosecution under this subdivision runs from the first such statement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.48.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates this section may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the false statement was made upon the trial of a felony charge, or upon an application for an explosives license or use permit, to imprisonment for not more than seven years or to payment of a fine of not more than $14,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) in all other cases, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.48.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>A violation of subdivision 1, clause (4), may be prosecuted in the county where the statement, under penalty of perjury, was signed, or the county of the district court in which the statement was filed.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.48.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.48; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/845/#laws.0.16.0">1971 c 845 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.18.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/295/#laws.0.2.0">2010 c 295 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/204/#laws.0.9.0">2014 c 204 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.2.15.0">2017 c 95 art 2 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.485">
        <h1 class="shn">609.485 ESCAPE FROM CUSTODY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.485.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Escape" includes departure without lawful authority and failure to return to custody following temporary leave granted for a specific purpose or limited period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.485.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4:</p>
          <p>(1) escapes while held pursuant to a lawful arrest, in lawful custody on a charge or conviction of a crime, or while held in lawful custody on an allegation or adjudication of a delinquent act;</p>
          <p>(2) transfers to another, who is in lawful custody on a charge or conviction of a crime, or introduces into an institution in which the latter is confined, anything usable in making such escape, with intent that it shall be so used;</p>
          <p>(3) having another in lawful custody on a charge or conviction of a crime, intentionally permits the other to escape;</p>
          <p>(4) escapes while in a facility designated under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.18#stat.253B.18.1">253B.18, subdivision 1</a>, pursuant to a court commitment order after a finding of not guilty by reason of mental illness or mental deficiency of a crime against the person, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.02#stat.253B.02.4e">253B.02, subdivision 4e</a>. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.17">609.17</a>, no person may be charged with or convicted of an attempt to commit a violation of this clause;</p>
          <p>(5) escapes while in or under the supervision of a facility designated under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/246B.01#stat.246B.01.2a">246B.01, subdivision 2a</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/246C.13">246C.13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.18#stat.253B.18.1">253B.18, subdivision 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253D.07#stat.253D.07.3">253D.07, subdivision 3</a>; or Minnesota Statutes 1992, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/526.10">526.10</a>;</p>
          <p>(6) escapes while on pass status or provisional discharge according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.18">253B.18</a> or chapter 253D; or</p>
          <p>(7) escapes while a civilly committed sex offender in the Minnesota Sex Offender Program as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/246B.01#stat.246B.01.1a">246B.01, subdivision 1a</a>, or subject to a court hold order under chapter 253D.</p>
          <p>For purposes of clauses (1) and (7), "escapes while held in lawful custody" or "escapes while a civilly committed sex offender in the Minnesota Sex Offender Program" includes absconding from electronic monitoring or removing an electronic monitoring device from the person's body.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.485.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to a person who is free on bail or who is on parole or probation, or subject to a stayed sentence or stayed execution of sentence, unless the person (1) has been taken into actual custody upon revocation of the parole, probation, or stay of the sentence or execution of sentence, (2) is in custody in a county jail or workhouse as a condition of a stayed sentence, or (3) is subject to electronic monitoring as a condition of parole, probation, or supervised release.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.485.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Dismissal of charge.</span></h2>
          <p>A felony charge brought under subdivision 2, clause (4) shall be dismissed if the person charged voluntarily returns to the facility within 30 days after a reasonable effort has been made to provide written notice to the person that failure to return within 30 days may result in felony charges being filed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.485.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 3a, whoever violates this section may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the person who escapes is in lawful custody for a felony, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the person who escapes is in lawful custody after a finding of not guilty by reason of mental illness or mental deficiency of a crime against the person, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.02#stat.253B.02.4e">253B.02, subdivision 4e</a>, to imprisonment for not more than one year and one day or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(3) if the person who escapes is in lawful custody for a gross misdemeanor or misdemeanor, or if the person who escapes is in lawful custody on an allegation or adjudication of a delinquent act, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(4) if the person who escapes is under civil commitment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.18">253B.18</a>, to imprisonment for not more than one year and one day or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(5) if the person who escapes is under a court hold, civil commitment, or supervision under chapter 253D, Minnesota Statutes 2012, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.185">253B.185</a>, or Minnesota Statutes 1992, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/526.10">526.10</a>, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) If the escape was a violation of subdivision 2, clause (1), (2), or (3), and was effected by violence or threat of violence against a person, the sentence may be increased to not more than twice those permitted in paragraph (a), clauses (1) and (3).</p>
          <p>(c) Unless a concurrent term is specified by the court, a sentence under this section shall be consecutive to any sentence previously imposed or which may be imposed for any crime or offense for which the person was in custody when the person escaped.</p>
          <p>(d) Notwithstanding paragraph (c), if a person who was committed to the commissioner of corrections under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.198">260B.198</a> escapes from the custody of the commissioner while 18 years of age, the person's sentence under this section shall commence on the person's 19th birthday or on the person's date of discharge by the commissioner of corrections, whichever occurs first. However, if the person described in this clause is convicted under this section after becoming 19 years old and after having been discharged by the commissioner, the person's sentence shall commence upon imposition by the sentencing court.</p>
          <p>(e) Notwithstanding paragraph (c), if a person who is in lawful custody on an allegation or adjudication of a delinquent act while 18 years of age escapes from a local juvenile correctional facility, the person's sentence under this section begins on the person's 19th birthday or on the person's date of discharge from the jurisdiction of the juvenile court, whichever occurs first. However, if the person described in this paragraph is convicted after becoming 19 years old and after discharge from the jurisdiction of the juvenile court, the person's sentence begins upon imposition by the sentencing court.</p>
          <p>(f) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), any person who escapes or absconds from electronic monitoring or removes an electric monitoring device from the person's body is guilty of a crime and shall be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to a payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both. A person in lawful custody for a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.205">609.205</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2112">609.2112</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2113">609.2113</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2114">609.2114</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.3451">609.3451</a>, or civil commitment under chapter 253D, or Minnesota Statutes 2012, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.21">609.21</a>, and who escapes or absconds from electronic monitoring or removes an electronic monitoring device while under sentence may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.485.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.486">
        <h1 class="shn">609.486 COMMISSION OF CRIME WHILE WEARING OR POSSESSING BULLET-RESISTANT VEST.</h1>
        <p>A person who commits or attempts to commit a gross misdemeanor or felony while wearing or possessing a bullet-resistant vest is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, shall be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction under this section is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
        <p>As used in this section, "bullet-resistant vest" means a bullet-resistant garment that provides ballistic and trauma protection.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.486.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/439/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 439 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.487">
        <h1 class="shn">609.487 FLEEING PEACE OFFICER; MOTOR VEHICLE; OTHER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Flee; definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, the term "flee" means to increase speed, extinguish motor vehicle headlights or taillights, refuse to stop the vehicle, or use other means with intent to attempt to elude a peace officer following a signal given by any peace officer to the driver of a motor vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Peace officer; definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "peace officer" means:</p>
          <p>(1) an employee of a political subdivision or state law enforcement agency who is licensed by the Minnesota Board of Peace Officer Standards and Training, charged with the prevention and detection of crime and the enforcement of the general criminal laws of the state and who has the full power of arrest, and shall also include the Minnesota State Patrol and Minnesota conservation officers;</p>
          <p>(2) an employee of a law enforcement agency of a federally recognized tribe, as defined in United States Code, title 25, section 450b(e), who is licensed by the Minnesota Board of Peace Officer Standards and Training; or</p>
          <p>(3) a member of a duly organized state, county, or municipal law enforcement unit of another state charged with the duty to prevent and detect crime and generally enforce criminal laws, and granted full powers of arrest.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Motor vehicle; definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "motor vehicle" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.42">169.011, subdivision 42</a>, and includes a snowmobile, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/84.81">84.81</a>, off-road recreational vehicles as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03#stat.169A.03.16">169A.03, subdivision 16</a>, and motorboats as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03#stat.169A.03.13">169A.03, subdivision 13</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Fleeing officer; motor vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever by means of a motor vehicle flees or attempts to flee a peace officer who is acting in the lawful discharge of an official duty, and the perpetrator knows or should reasonably know the same to be a peace officer, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years and one day or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Fleeing officer; death; bodily injury.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever flees or attempts to flee by means of a motor vehicle a peace officer who is acting in the lawful discharge of an official duty, and the perpetrator knows or should reasonably know the same to be a peace officer, and who in the course of fleeing in a motor vehicle or subsequently by other means causes the death of a human being not constituting murder or manslaughter or any bodily injury to any person other than the perpetrator may be sentenced to imprisonment as follows:</p>
          <p>(a) if the course of fleeing results in death, to imprisonment for not more than 40 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $80,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(b) if the course of fleeing results in great bodily harm, to imprisonment for not more than seven years or to payment of a fine of not more than $14,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(c) if the course of fleeing results in substantial bodily harm, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Revocation; fleeing peace officer offense.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is convicted of operating a motor vehicle in violation of subdivision 3 or 4, or an ordinance in conformity with those subdivisions, the court shall notify the commissioner of public safety and order the commissioner to revoke the driver's license of the person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.487.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Fleeing, other than vehicle.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, for the purpose of avoiding arrest, detention, or investigation, or in order to conceal or destroy potential evidence related to the commission of a crime, attempts to evade or elude a peace officer, who is acting in the lawful discharge of an official duty, by means of running, hiding, or by any other means except fleeing in a motor vehicle, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.487.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/37/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 37 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/312/#laws.0.4.0">1981 c 312 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/445/#laws.0.2.0">1984 c 445 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/655/#laws.1.78.0">1984 c 655 art 1 s 78</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.6.0">1988 c 712 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.19.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/449/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 449 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.30.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/226/#laws.0.44.0">1997 c 226 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.13.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/2/#laws.0.64.0">1Sp1997 c 2 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/411/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 411 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/478/#laws.2.7.0">2000 c 478 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.8.23.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 8 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.28.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/32/#laws.0.1.0">2011 c 32 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.49">
        <h1 class="shn">609.49 RELEASE, FAILURE TO APPEAR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.49.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Felony offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person charged with or convicted of a felony and released from custody, with or without bail or recognizance, who intentionally fails to appear when required after having been notified that a failure to appear for a court appearance is a criminal offense, or after having been released on an order or condition that the releasee personally appear when required with respect to the charge or conviction, is guilty of a crime for failure to appear and may be sentenced to not more than one-half of the maximum term of imprisonment or fine, or both, provided for the underlying crime for which the person failed to appear, but this maximum sentence shall, in no case, be less than a term of imprisonment of one year and one day or a fine of $1,500, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A felony charge under this subdivision may be filed upon the person's nonappearance. However, the charge must be dismissed if the person who fails to appear voluntarily surrenders within 48 hours after the time required for appearance. This paragraph does not apply if the offender appears as a result of being apprehended by law enforcement authorities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.49.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Juvenile offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who intentionally fails to appear for a juvenile court disposition is guilty of a felony if:</p>
          <p>(1) the person was prosecuted in juvenile court for an offense that would have been a felony if committed by an adult;</p>
          <p>(2) the juvenile court made findings pursuant to an admission in court or after trial;</p>
          <p>(3) the person was released from custody on condition that the person appear in the juvenile court for a disposition in connection with the offense; and</p>
          <p>(4) the person was notified that failure to appear is a criminal offense.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates the provisions of this subdivision is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.49.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor and misdemeanor offenders.</span></h2>
          <p>A person charged with a gross misdemeanor or misdemeanor who intentionally fails to appear in court for trial on the charge after having been notified that a failure to appear for a court appearance is a criminal offense, or after having been released on an order or condition that the releasee personally appear for trial when required with respect to the charge, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.49.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Affirmative defense.</span></h2>
          <p>If proven by a preponderance of the evidence, it is an affirmative defense to a violation of subdivision 1, 1a, or 2 that the person's failure to appear in court as required was due to circumstances beyond the person's control.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.49.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>A violation of this section is prosecuted by the prosecuting authority who was responsible for prosecuting the offense in connection with which the person failed to appear in court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.49.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Reimbursement for costs.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon conviction of a defendant for a violation of subdivision 1 or 2, the court may order as part of the sentence that the defendant pay the costs incurred by the prosecuting authority or governmental agency due to the defendant's failure to appear. The court may order this payment in addition to any other penalty authorized by law which it may impose. A defendant shall pay the entire amount of any restitution ordered and fine imposed before paying costs ordered under this subdivision. The order for payment of these costs may be enforced in the same manner as the sentence, or by execution against property. When collected, the costs must be paid into the treasury of the county of conviction.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.49.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.49; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/333/#laws.0.4.0">1989 c 333 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/576/#laws.0.47.0">1994 c 576 s 47</a>,48; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.16.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/28/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 28 s 1</a>-3</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.491">
        <h1 class="shn">609.491 FAILURE TO APPEAR; PETTY MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.491.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Considered guilty plea.</span></h2>
          <p>If a person fails to appear in court on a charge that is a petty misdemeanor, the failure to appear is considered a plea of guilty and waiver of the right to trial, unless the person appears in court within ten days and shows that the person's failure to appear was due to circumstances beyond the person's control.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.491.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>A complaint charging a person with a petty misdemeanor must include a conspicuous notice of the provisions of subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.491.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/333/#laws.0.5.0">1989 c 333 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.493">
        <h1 class="shn">609.493 SOLICITATION OF MENTALLY IMPAIRED PERSONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.493.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2 if the person solicits a mentally impaired person to commit a criminal act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.493.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor if the intended criminal act is a misdemeanor, and is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the intended criminal act is a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a felony if the intended criminal act is a felony, and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than one-half the statutory maximum term for the intended criminal act or to payment of a fine of not more than one-half the maximum fine for the intended criminal act, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.493.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "mentally impaired person" means a person who, as a result of inadequately developed or impaired intelligence or a substantial psychiatric disorder of thought or mood, lacks the judgment to give a reasoned consent to commit the criminal act; and</p>
          <p>(2) "solicit" means commanding, entreating, or attempting to persuade a specific person.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.493.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.23.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 23</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.494">
        <h1 class="shn">609.494 SOLICITATION OF JUVENILES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.494.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2 if the person is an adult and solicits or conspires with a minor to commit a crime or delinquent act or is an accomplice to a minor in the commission of a crime or delinquent act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.494.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor if the intended criminal act is a misdemeanor or would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, and is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the intended criminal act is a gross misdemeanor or would be a gross misdemeanor if committed by an adult.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a felony if the intended criminal act is a felony or would be a felony if committed by an adult, and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than one-half the statutory maximum term for the intended criminal act or to payment of a fine of not more than one-half the maximum fine for the intended criminal act, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.494.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Multiple sentences.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction under this section is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.494.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Consecutive sentences.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any provision of the Sentencing Guidelines, the court may provide that a sentence imposed for a violation of this section shall run consecutively to any sentence imposed for the intended criminal act. A decision by the court to impose consecutive sentences under this subdivision is not a departure from the Sentencing Guidelines.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.494.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Solicit" means commanding, entreating, or attempting to persuade a specific person.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.494.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/279/#laws.0.31.0">1991 c 279 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.24.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 24</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.495">
        <h1 class="shn">609.495 AIDING AN OFFENDER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.495.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition of crime.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever harbors, conceals, aids, or assists by word or acts another whom the actor knows or has reason to know has committed a crime under the laws of this or another state or of the United States with intent that such offender shall avoid or escape from arrest, trial, conviction, or punishment, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both if the crime committed or attempted by the other person is a felony.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever knowingly harbors, conceals, or aids a person who is on probation, parole, or supervised release because of a felony level conviction and for whom an arrest and detention order has been issued, with intent that the person evade or escape being taken into custody under the order, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both. As used in this paragraph, "arrest and detention order" means a written order to take and detain a probationer, parolee, or supervised releasee that is issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/243.05#stat.243.05.1">243.05, subdivision 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.195">244.195</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/401.025">401.025</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.495.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.40.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 40</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.495.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Obstructing investigation.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally aids another person whom the actor knows or has reason to know has committed a criminal act, by destroying or concealing evidence of that crime, providing false or misleading information about that crime, receiving the proceeds of that crime, or otherwise obstructing the investigation or prosecution of that crime is an accomplice after the fact and may be sentenced to not more than one-half of the statutory maximum sentence of imprisonment or to payment of a fine of not more than one-half of the maximum fine that could be imposed on the principal offender for the crime of violence. For purposes of this subdivision, "criminal act" means an act that is a crime listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.11#stat.609.11.9">609.11, subdivision 9</a>, under the laws of this or another state, or of the United States, and also includes an act that would be a criminal act if committed by an adult.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.495.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Taking responsibility for criminal acts.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Unless the person is convicted of the underlying crime, a person who assumes responsibility for a criminal act with the intent to obstruct, impede, or prevent a criminal investigation may be sentenced to not more than one-half of the statutory maximum sentence of imprisonment or to payment of a fine of not more than one-half of the maximum fine that could be imposed on the principal offender for the criminal act.</p>
          <p>(b) Nothing in this subdivision shall be construed to impair the right of any individual or group to engage in speech protected by the United States Constitution or the Minnesota Constitution.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.495.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>An offense committed under subdivision 1 or 3 may be prosecuted in:</p>
          <p>(1) the county where the aiding or obstructing behavior occurred; or</p>
          <p>(2) the county where the underlying criminal act occurred.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.495.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.495; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.25.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.14.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 14</a>; art 9 s 51; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.8.24.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 8 s 24</a>,25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/348/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 348 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.26.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.204.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 204</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.496">
        <h1 class="shn">609.496 CONCEALING CRIMINAL PROCEEDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.496.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced under subdivision 2 if the person:</p>
          <p>(1) conducts a transaction involving a monetary instrument or instruments with a value exceeding $5,000; and</p>
          <p>(2) knows or has reason to know that the monetary instrument or instruments represent the proceeds of, or are derived from the proceeds of, the commission of a felony under this chapter or chapter 152 or an offense in another jurisdiction that would be a felony under this chapter or chapter 152 if committed in Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.496.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted under subdivision 1 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.496.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Monetary instrument.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "monetary instrument" means United States currency and coin; the currency and coin of a foreign country; a bank check, cashier's check, traveler's check, money order, stock, investment security, or negotiable instrument in bearer form or otherwise in the form by which title to the instrument passes upon delivery; gold, silver, or platinum bullion or coins; and diamonds, emeralds, rubies, or sapphires.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.496.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Payment of reasonable attorney fees.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivision 1 does not preclude the payment or receipt of reasonable attorney fees.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.496.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.3.0">1989 c 286 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.497">
        <h1 class="shn">609.497 ENGAGING IN BUSINESS OF CONCEALING CRIMINAL PROCEEDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.497.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced under subdivision 2 if the person knowingly initiates, organizes, plans, finances, directs, manages, supervises, or otherwise engages in a business that has as a primary or secondary purpose concealing money or property that was gained as a direct result of the commission of a felony under this chapter or chapter 152, or of an offense committed in another jurisdiction that would be a felony under this chapter or chapter 152 if committed in Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.497.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted under subdivision 1 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.497.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.4.0">1989 c 286 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.4971">
        <h1 class="shn">609.4971 WARNING SUBJECT OF INVESTIGATION.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, having knowledge that a subpoena has been issued under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/8.16">8.16</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/388.23">388.23</a>, and with intent to obstruct, impede, or prevent the investigation for which the subpoena was issued, gives notice or attempts to give notice of the issuance of the subpoena or the production of the documents to a person, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.4971.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/336/#laws.2.4.0">1989 c 336 art 2 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.4975">
        <h1 class="shn">609.4975 WARNING SUBJECT OF SURVEILLANCE OR SEARCH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.4975.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Electronic communication.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, having knowledge that an investigative or law enforcement officer has been authorized or has applied for authorization under chapter 626A to intercept a wire, oral, or electronic communication, and with intent to obstruct, impede, or prevent interception, gives notice or attempts to give notice of the possible interception to a person, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.4975.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Pen register.</span></h2>
