          <p>Whoever, having knowledge that an investigative or law enforcement officer has been authorized or has applied for authorization under chapter 626A to install and use a pen register or a trap and trace device, and with intent to obstruct, impede, or prevent the purposes for which the installation and use is being made, gives notice or attempts to give notice of the installation or use to any person, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.4975.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Search warrant.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, having knowledge that a peace officer has been issued or has applied for the issuance of a search warrant, and with intent to obstruct, impede, or prevent the search, gives notice or attempts to give notice of the search or search warrant to any person, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.4975.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/336/#laws.2.3.0">1989 c 336 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/426/#laws.2.1.0">1990 c 426 art 2 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.498">
        <h1 class="shn">609.498 TAMPERING WITH WITNESS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Tampering with witness in the first degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of tampering with a witness in the first degree and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 1a:</p>
          <p>(a) intentionally prevents or dissuades or intentionally attempts to prevent or dissuade by means of force or threats of injury to any person or property, a person who is or may become a witness from attending or testifying at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law;</p>
          <p>(b) by means of force or threats of injury to any person or property, intentionally coerces or attempts to coerce a person who is or may become a witness to testify falsely at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law;</p>
          <p>(c) intentionally causes injury or threatens to cause injury to any person or property in retaliation against a person who was summoned as a witness at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law, within a year following that trial, proceeding, or inquiry or within a year following the actor's release from incarceration, whichever is later;</p>
          <p>(d) intentionally prevents or dissuades or attempts to prevent or dissuade, by means of force or threats of injury to any person or property, a person from providing information to law enforcement authorities concerning a crime;</p>
          <p>(e) by means of force or threats of injury to any person or property, intentionally coerces or attempts to coerce a person to provide false information concerning a crime to law enforcement authorities; or</p>
          <p>(f) intentionally causes injury or threatens to cause injury to any person or property in retaliation against a person who has provided information to law enforcement authorities concerning a crime within a year of that person providing the information or within a year of the actor's release from incarceration, whichever is later.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine not to exceed $10,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Aggravated first-degree witness tampering.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of aggravated first-degree witness tampering if the person causes or, by means of an implicit or explicit credible threat, threatens to cause great bodily harm or death to another in the course of committing any of the following acts intentionally:</p>
          <p>(1) preventing or dissuading or attempting to prevent or dissuade a person who is or may become a witness from attending or testifying at any criminal trial or proceeding;</p>
          <p>(2) coercing or attempting to coerce a person who is or may become a witness to testify falsely at any criminal trial or proceeding;</p>
          <p>(3) retaliating against a person who was summoned as a witness at any criminal trial or proceeding within a year following that trial or proceeding or within a year following the actor's release from incarceration, whichever is later;</p>
          <p>(4) preventing or dissuading or attempting to prevent or dissuade a person from providing information to law enforcement authorities concerning a crime;</p>
          <p>(5) coercing or attempting to coerce a person to provide false information concerning a crime to law enforcement authorities; or</p>
          <p>(6) retaliating against any person who has provided information to law enforcement authorities concerning a crime within a year of that person providing the information or within a year of the actor's release from incarceration, whichever is later.</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted of committing any act prohibited by paragraph (a) may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $30,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Tampering with a witness in the second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of tampering with a witness in the second degree and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p>(a) intentionally prevents or dissuades or intentionally attempts to prevent or dissuade by means of any act described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27#stat.609.27.1">609.27, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3), (4), or (5), a person who is or may become a witness from attending or testifying at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law;</p>
          <p>(b) by means of any act described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27#stat.609.27.1">609.27, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3), (4), or (5), intentionally coerces or attempts to coerce a person who is or may become a witness to testify falsely at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law;</p>
          <p>(c) intentionally prevents or dissuades or attempts to prevent or dissuade by means of any act described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27#stat.609.27.1">609.27, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3), (4), or (5), a person from providing information to law enforcement authorities concerning a crime; or</p>
          <p>(d) by means of any act described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27#stat.609.27.1">609.27, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3), (4), or (5), intentionally coerces or attempts to coerce a person to provide false information concerning a crime to law enforcement authorities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Tampering with a witness in the third degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Unless a greater penalty is applicable under subdivision 1, 1b, or 2, whoever does any of the following is guilty of tampering with a witness in the third degree and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally prevents or dissuades or intentionally attempts to prevent or dissuade by means of intimidation, a person who is or may become a witness from attending or testifying at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law;</p>
          <p>(2) by means of intimidation, intentionally influences or attempts to influence a person who is or may become a witness to testify falsely at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry authorized by law;</p>
          <p>(3) intentionally prevents or dissuades or attempts to prevent or dissuade by means of intimidation, a person from providing information to law enforcement authorities concerning a crime; or</p>
          <p>(4) by means of intimidation, intentionally influences or attempts to influence a person to provide false information concerning a crime to law enforcement authorities.</p>
          <p>(b) In a prosecution under this subdivision, proof of intimidation may be based on a specific act or on the totality of the circumstances.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates subdivision 2a is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.498.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">No bar to conviction.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.035">609.035</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction of the crime of aggravated first-degree witness tampering is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.498.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/178/#laws.0.1.0">1976 c 178 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/262/#laws.2.6.0">1983 c 262 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/194/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 194 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.18.0">1995 c 244 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.15.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 15</a>,16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/299/#laws.0.6.0">2010 c 299 s 6</a>,7</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.50">
        <h1 class="shn">609.50 OBSTRUCTING LEGAL PROCESS, ARREST, OR FIREFIGHTING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.50.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally does any of the following may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2:</p>
          <p>(1) obstructs, hinders, or prevents the lawful execution of any legal process, civil or criminal, or apprehension of another on a charge or conviction of a criminal offense;</p>
          <p>(2) obstructs, resists, or interferes with a peace officer while the officer is engaged in the performance of official duties;</p>
          <p>(3) interferes with or obstructs a firefighter while the firefighter is engaged in the performance of official duties;</p>
          <p>(4) interferes with or obstructs a member of an ambulance service personnel crew, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144E.001#stat.144E.001.3a">144E.001, subdivision 3a</a>, who is providing, or attempting to provide, emergency care; or</p>
          <p>(5) by force or threat of force endeavors to obstruct any employee of the Department of Revenue, Department of Public Safety Driver and Vehicle Services Division, a driver's license agent appointed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.061">171.061</a>, or a deputy registrar appointed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.33">168.33</a> while the employee is lawfully engaged in the performance of official duties for the purpose of deterring or interfering with the performance of those duties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.50.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted of violating subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if (i) the person knew or had reason to know that the act created a risk of death, substantial bodily harm, or serious property damage; or (ii) the act caused death, substantial bodily harm, or serious property damage; to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the act was accompanied by force or violence or the threat thereof, and is not otherwise covered by clause (1), to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(3) in other cases, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.50.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.50; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/1013/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 1013 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.51.0">1971 c 23 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/470/#laws.0.18.0">1986 c 470 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/584/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 584 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.4.0">1989 c 5 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/103/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 103 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.17.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.29.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/304/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 304 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.5.51.0">2023 c 68 art 5 s 51</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.501">
        <h1 class="shn">609.501 FUNERAL OR BURIAL SERVICE; PROHIBITED ACTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.501.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions. </span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Family or household" has the meaning given to family or household member in section 518B.01, subdivision 2.</p>
          <p>(c) "Funeral ceremony" has the meaning given in section 149A.02, subdivision 18.</p>
          <p>(d) "Funeral procession" means two or more motor vehicles that identify themselves by using regular lights and by keeping themselves in close formation, one of which contains the body of a deceased person, enroute to or from a funeral ceremony or a graveside service.</p>
          <p>(e) "Graveside service" has the meaning given in section 149A.02, subdivision 24.</p>
          <p>(f) "Memorial service" has the meaning given in section 149A.02, subdivision 28.</p>
          <p>(g) "Targeted residential picketing" has the meaning given in section 609.748, subdivision 1, paragraph (c), but does not require more than one act or that acts be committed on more than one occasion.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.501.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime to disrupt.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) with intent to disrupt a funeral ceremony, graveside service, or memorial service, protests or pickets within 500 feet of the burial site or the entrance to a facility or location being used for the service or ceremony, within one hour prior to, during, or one hour following the service or ceremony;</p>
          <p>(2) with intent to disrupt a funeral procession, impedes or attempts to impede a vehicle that is part of the procession;</p>
          <p>(3) intentionally blocks or attempts to block access to a funeral ceremony, graveside service, or memorial service; or</p>
          <p>(4) knowingly engages in targeted residential picketing at the home or domicile of any surviving member of the deceased person's family or household on the date of the funeral ceremony, graveside service, or memorial service.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever is convicted of a violation of paragraph (a) following a previous conviction for a violation of paragraph (a) or a similar statute from another state or the United States is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.501.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Civil remedy. </span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 2 is liable to a surviving member of the deceased person's family or household for damages caused by the violation. A surviving member of the deceased person's family or household may also bring an action for injunctive relief and other appropriate relief or remedial compensation. In an action brought under this subdivision, a prevailing plaintiff may recover attorney fees.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.501.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/195/#laws.0.1.0">2006 c 195 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.502">
        <h1 class="shn">609.502 INTERFERENCE WITH DEAD BODY; REPORTING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.502.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Concealing evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced under subdivision 1a if the person interferes with the body or scene of death with intent to:</p>
          <p>(1) conceal the body;</p>
          <p>(2) conceal evidence; or</p>
          <p>(3) otherwise mislead the coroner or medical examiner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.502.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted under subdivision 1, clause (2) or (3), is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. A person convicted under subdivision 1, clause (1), may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $5,000 or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.502.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Failure to report.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person in charge of a cemetery who has knowledge that the body of a deceased person interred in the cemetery has been unlawfully removed shall:</p>
          <p>(1) immediately report the occurrence to local law enforcement authorities; and</p>
          <p>(2) inform the next of kin of the deceased person, if known, within three business days of the discovery of the body's removal unless the person making the report has been instructed in writing by law enforcement authorities that informing the next of kin would compromise an active law enforcement investigation.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates paragraph (a), clause (1) or (2), is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.502.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/257/#laws.0.2.0">1976 c 257 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/402/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 402 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/175/#laws.0.1.0">2016 c 175 s 1</a>,2</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.504">
        <h1 class="shn">609.504 DISARMING PEACE OFFICER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.504.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "defensive device" includes a firearm; a dangerous weapon; an authorized tear gas compound, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.731#stat.624.731.1">624.731, subdivision 1</a>; an electronic incapacitation device, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.731">624.731</a>, subdivision 1; a club or baton; and any item issued by a peace officer's employer to the officer to assist in the officer's protection.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.504.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime described.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally takes possession of a defensive device being carried by a peace officer or from the area within the officer's immediate control, without the officer's consent while the officer is engaged in the performance of official duties, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.504.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates this section is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years, payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.504.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/304/#laws.0.2.0">2008 c 304 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.505">
        <h1 class="shn">609.505 FALSELY REPORTING CRIME.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.505.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">False reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever informs a law enforcement officer that a crime has been committed or otherwise provides information to an on-duty peace officer, knowing that the person is a peace officer, regarding the conduct of others, knowing that it is false and intending that the officer shall act in reliance upon it, is guilty of a misdemeanor. A person who is convicted a second or subsequent time under this section is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.505.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Reporting police misconduct.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever informs, or causes information to be communicated to, a peace officer, whose responsibilities include investigating or reporting police misconduct, that a peace officer, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c), has committed an act of police misconduct, knowing that the information is false, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) up to the maximum provided for a misdemeanor if the false information does not allege a criminal act; or</p>
          <p>(2) up to the maximum provided for a gross misdemeanor if the false information alleges a criminal act.</p>
          <p>(b) The court shall order any person convicted of a violation of this subdivision to make full restitution of all reasonable expenses incurred in the investigation of the false allegation unless the court makes a specific written finding that restitution would be inappropriate under the circumstances. A restitution award may not exceed $3,000.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.505.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.505; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.52.0">1971 c 23 s 52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.26.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.30.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 30</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5051">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5051 CRIMINAL ALERT NETWORK; FALSE OR MISLEADING INFORMATION PROHIBITED.</h1>
        <p>Whoever uses the criminal alert network under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299A.61">299A.61</a> to disseminate information regarding the commission of a crime knowing that it is false or misleading, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5051.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.4.22.0">1995 c 226 art 4 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.19.0">1995 c 244 s 19</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.506">
        <h1 class="shn">609.506 PROHIBITING GIVING PEACE OFFICER FALSE NAME.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.506.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever with intent to obstruct justice gives a fictitious name other than a nickname, or gives a false date of birth, or false or fraudulently altered identification card to a peace officer, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c), when that officer makes inquiries incident to a lawful investigatory stop or lawful arrest, or inquiries incident to executing any other duty imposed by law, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.506.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Name of another; gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever with intent to obstruct justice gives the name and date of birth of another person to a peace officer, as defined in subdivision 1, when the officer makes inquiries incident to a lawful investigatory stop or lawful arrest, or inquiries incident to executing any other duty imposed by law, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.506.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Fictitious name; gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever in any criminal proceeding with intent to obstruct justice gives a fictitious name, other than a nickname, or gives a false date of birth to a court official is guilty of a misdemeanor. Whoever in any criminal proceeding with intent to obstruct justice gives the name and date of birth of another person to a court official is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. "Court official" includes a judge, referee, court administrator, or any employee of the court.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.506.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/127/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 127 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/681/#laws.0.17.0">1988 c 681 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/209/#laws.1.45.0">1989 c 209 art 1 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.40.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 40</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.507">
        <h1 class="shn">609.507 FALSELY REPORTING CHILD ABUSE.</h1>
        <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor who:</p>
        <p>(1) informs another person that a person has committed sexual abuse, physical abuse, or neglect of a child, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.03">260E.03</a>;</p>
        <p>(2) knows that the allegation is false or is without reason to believe that the alleged abuser committed the abuse or neglect; and</p>
        <p>(3) has the intent that the information influence a child custody hearing.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.507.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/662/#laws.0.3.0">1988 c 662 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.140.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 140</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.508">
        <h1 class="shn">609.508 FALSE INFORMATION TO FINANCIAL INSTITUTION.</h1>
        <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor if the person informs a financial institution, orally or in writing, that one or more of the person's blank checks or debit cards have been lost or stolen, knowing or having reason to know that the information is false.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.508.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/354/#laws.0.2.0">2000 c 354 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.51">
        <h1 class="shn">609.51 SIMULATING LEGAL PROCESS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.51.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) sends or delivers to another any document which simulates a summons, complaint, or court process with intent thereby to induce payment of a claim; or</p>
          <p>(2) prints, distributes, or offers for sale any such document knowing or intending that it shall be so used.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.51.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not prohibit the printing, distribution or sale of blank forms of legal documents for use in judicial proceedings.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.51.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.51; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.53.0">1971 c 23 s 53</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.515">
        <h1 class="shn">609.515 MISCONDUCT OF JUDICIAL OR HEARING OFFICER.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following, when the act is not in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.42">609.42</a>, is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
        <p>(1) being a judicial or hearing officer, does either of the following:</p>
        <p>(a) agrees with or promises another to determine a cause or controversy or issue pending or to be brought before the officer for or against any party; or</p>
        <p>(b) intentionally obtains or receives and uses information relating thereto contrary to the regular course of the proceeding; and</p>
        <p>(2) induces a judicial or hearing officer to act contrary to the provisions of this section.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.515.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.515; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.54.0">1971 c 23 s 54</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5151">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5151 DISSEMINATION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ABOUT LAW ENFORCEMENT PROHIBITED; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5151.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "family or household member" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01">518B.01, subdivision </a>2;</p>
          <p>(2) "law enforcement official" means both peace officers as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84">626.84</a>, subdivision 1, and persons employed by a law enforcement agency; and</p>
          <p>(3) "personal information" means a home telephone number, personal cell number, personal email address, name of the official's minor child, photographs of the official's minor child, home address, directions to a home, or photographs of a home.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5151.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime described.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) It is a misdemeanor for a person to knowingly and without consent make publicly available, including but not limited to through the Internet, personal information about a law enforcement official or an official's family or household member, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the public availability of information poses an imminent and serious threat to the official's safety or the safety of an official's family or household member; and</p>
          <p>(2) the person making the information publicly available knows or reasonably should know of the imminent and serious threat.</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the person violates paragraph (a) and a law enforcement official or an official's family or household member suffers great bodily harm or death as a result of the violation.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who is convicted of a second or subsequent violation of this section is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5151.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.40.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/112/#laws.2.74.0">2024 c 112 art 2 s 74</a>,75</p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">THEFT AND RELATED CRIMES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.52">
        <h1 class="shn">609.52 THEFT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.52.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>In this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "Property" means all forms of tangible property, whether real or personal, without limitation including documents of value, electricity, gas, water, corpses, domestic animals, dogs, pets, fowl, and heat supplied by pipe or conduit by municipalities or public utility companies and articles, as defined in clause (4), representing trade secrets, which articles shall be deemed for the purposes of Extra Session Laws 1967, chapter 15 to include any trade secret represented by the article.</p>
          <p>(2) "Movable property" is property whose physical location can be changed, including without limitation things growing on, affixed to, or found in land.</p>
          <p>(3) "Value" means the retail market value at the time of the theft, or if the retail market value cannot be ascertained, the cost of replacement of the property within a reasonable time after the theft, or in the case of a theft or the making of a copy of an article representing a trade secret, where the retail market value or replacement cost cannot be ascertained, any reasonable value representing the damage to the owner which the owner has suffered by reason of losing an advantage over those who do not know of or use the trade secret. For a check, draft, or other order for the payment of money, "value" means the amount of money promised or ordered to be paid under the terms of the check, draft, or other order. For a theft committed within the meaning of subdivision 2, paragraph (a), clause (5), items (i) and (ii), if the property has been restored to the owner, "value" means the value of the use of the property or the damage which it sustained, whichever is greater, while the owner was deprived of its possession, but not exceeding the value otherwise provided herein. For a theft committed within the meaning of subdivision 2, clause (9), if the property has been restored to the owner, "value" means the rental value of the property, determined at the rental rate contracted by the defendant or, if no rental rate was contracted, the rental rate customarily charged by the owner for use of the property, plus any damage that occurred to the property while the owner was deprived of its possession, but not exceeding the total retail value of the property at the time of rental. For a theft committed within the meaning of subdivision 2, clause (19), "value" means the difference between wages legally required to be reported or paid to an employee and the amount actually reported or paid to the employee.</p>
          <p>(4) "Article" means any object, material, device or substance, including any writing, record, recording, drawing, sample specimen, prototype, model, photograph, microorganism, blueprint or map, or any copy of any of the foregoing.</p>
          <p>(5) "Representing" means describing, depicting, containing, constituting, reflecting or recording.</p>
          <p>(6) "Trade secret" means information, including a formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, method, technique, or process, that:</p>
          <p>(i) derives independent economic value, actual or potential, from not being generally known to, and not being readily ascertainable by proper means by, other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use, and</p>
          <p>(ii) is the subject of efforts that are reasonable under the circumstances to maintain its secrecy.</p>
          <p>(7) "Copy" means any facsimile, replica, photograph or other reproduction of an article, and any note, drawing, or sketch made of or from an article while in the presence of the article.</p>
          <p>(8) "Property of another" includes property in which the actor is co-owner or has a lien, pledge, bailment, or lease or other subordinate interest, property transferred by the actor in circumstances which are known to the actor and which make the transfer fraudulent as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/513.44">513.44</a>, property possessed pursuant to a short-term rental contract, and property of a partnership of which the actor is a member, unless the actor and the victim are spouses. It does not include property in which the actor asserts in good faith a claim as a collection fee or commission out of property or funds recovered, or by virtue of a lien, setoff, or counterclaim.</p>
          <p>(9) "Services" include but are not limited to labor, professional services, transportation services, electronic computer services, the supplying of hotel accommodations, restaurant services, entertainment services, advertising services, telecommunication services, and the supplying of equipment for use including rental of personal property or equipment.</p>
          <p>(10) "Motor vehicle" means a self-propelled device for moving persons or property or pulling implements from one place to another, whether the device is operated on land, rails, water, or in the air.</p>
          <p>(11) "Motor fuel" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604.15#stat.604.15.1">604.15, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
          <p>(12) "Retailer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604.15#stat.604.15.1">604.15, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
          <p>(13) "Wage theft" occurs when an employer with intent to defraud:</p>
          <p>(i) fails to pay an employee all wages, salary, gratuities, earnings, or commissions at the employee's rate or rates of pay or at the rate or rates required by law, including any applicable statute, regulation, rule, ordinance, government resolution or policy, contract, or other legal authority, whichever rate of pay is greater;</p>
          <p>(ii) directly or indirectly causes any employee to give a receipt for wages for a greater amount than that actually paid to the employee for services rendered;</p>
          <p>(iii) directly or indirectly demands or receives from any employee any rebate or refund from the wages owed the employee under contract of employment with the employer; or</p>
          <p>(iv) makes or attempts to make it appear in any manner that the wages paid to any employee were greater than the amount actually paid to the employee.</p>
          <p>(14) "Employer" means any individual, partnership, association, corporation, business trust, or any person or group of persons acting directly or indirectly in the interest of an employer in relation to an employee.</p>
          <p>(15) "Employee" means any individual employed by an employer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.52.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting theft.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever does any of the following commits theft and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally and without claim of right takes, uses, transfers, conceals or retains possession of movable property of another without the other's consent and with intent to deprive the owner permanently of possession of the property; or</p>
          <p>(2) with or without having a legal interest in movable property, intentionally and without consent, takes the property out of the possession of a pledgee or other person having a superior right of possession, with intent thereby to deprive the pledgee or other person permanently of the possession of the property; or</p>
          <p>(3) obtains for the actor or another the possession, custody, or title to property of or performance of services by a third person by intentionally deceiving the third person with a false representation which is known to be false, made with intent to defraud, and which does defraud the person to whom it is made. "False representation" includes without limitation:</p>
          <p>(i) the issuance of a check, draft, or order for the payment of money, except a forged check as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>, or the delivery of property knowing that the actor is not entitled to draw upon the drawee therefor or to order the payment or delivery thereof; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a promise made with intent not to perform. Failure to perform is not evidence of intent not to perform unless corroborated by other substantial evidence; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the preparation or filing of a claim for reimbursement, a rate application, or a cost report used to establish a rate or claim for payment for medical care provided to a recipient of medical assistance under chapter 256B, which intentionally and falsely states the costs of or actual services provided by a vendor of medical care; or</p>
          <p>(iv) the preparation or filing of a claim for reimbursement for providing treatment or supplies required to be furnished to an employee under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/176.135">176.135</a> which intentionally and falsely states the costs of or actual treatment or supplies provided; or</p>
          <p>(v) the preparation or filing of a claim for reimbursement for providing treatment or supplies required to be furnished to an employee under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/176.135">176.135</a> for treatment or supplies that the provider knew were medically unnecessary, inappropriate, or excessive; or</p>
          <p>(4) by swindling, whether by artifice, trick, device, or any other means, obtains property or services from another person; or</p>
          <p>(5) intentionally commits any of the acts listed in this subdivision but with intent to exercise temporary control only and:</p>
          <p>(i) the control exercised manifests an indifference to the rights of the owner or the restoration of the property to the owner; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the actor pledges or otherwise attempts to subject the property to an adverse claim; or</p>
          <p>(iii) the actor intends to restore the property only on condition that the owner pay a reward or buy back or make other compensation; or</p>
          <p>(6) finds lost property and, knowing or having reasonable means of ascertaining the true owner, appropriates it to the finder's own use or to that of another not entitled thereto without first having made reasonable effort to find the owner and offer and surrender the property to the owner; or</p>
          <p>(7) intentionally obtains property or services, offered upon the deposit of a sum of money or tokens in a coin or token operated machine or other receptacle, without making the required deposit or otherwise obtaining the consent of the owner; or</p>
          <p>(8) intentionally and without claim of right converts any article representing a trade secret, knowing it to be such, to the actor's own use or that of another person or makes a copy of an article representing a trade secret, knowing it to be such, and intentionally and without claim of right converts the same to the actor's own use or that of another person. It shall be a complete defense to any prosecution under this clause for the defendant to show that information comprising the trade secret was rightfully known or available to the defendant from a source other than the owner of the trade secret; or</p>
          <p>(9) leases or rents personal property under a written instrument and who:</p>
          <p>(i) with intent to place the property beyond the control of the lessor conceals or aids or abets the concealment of the property or any part thereof; or</p>
          <p>(ii) sells, conveys, or encumbers the property or any part thereof without the written consent of the lessor, without informing the person to whom the lessee sells, conveys, or encumbers that the same is subject to such lease or rental contract with intent to deprive the lessor of possession thereof; or</p>
          <p>(iii) does not return the property to the lessor at the end of the lease or rental term, plus agreed-upon extensions, with intent to wrongfully deprive the lessor of possession of the property; or</p>
          <p>(iv) returns the property to the lessor at the end of the lease or rental term, plus agreed-upon extensions, but does not pay the lease or rental charges agreed upon in the written instrument, with intent to wrongfully deprive the lessor of the agreed-upon charges.</p>
          <p class="bl">For the purposes of items (iii) and (iv), the value of the property must be at least $100.</p>
          <p class="bl">Evidence that a lessee used a false, fictitious, or not current name, address, or place of employment in obtaining the property or fails or refuses to return the property or pay the rental contract charges to lessor within five days after written demand for the return has been served personally in the manner provided for service of process of a civil action or sent by certified mail to the last known address of the lessee, whichever shall occur later, shall be evidence of intent to violate this clause. Service by certified mail shall be deemed to be complete upon deposit in the United States mail of such demand, postpaid and addressed to the person at the address for the person set forth in the lease or rental agreement, or, in the absence of the address, to the person's last known place of residence; or</p>
          <p>(10) alters, removes, or obliterates numbers or symbols placed on movable property for purpose of identification by the owner or person who has legal custody or right to possession thereof with the intent to prevent identification, if the person who alters, removes, or obliterates the numbers or symbols is not the owner and does not have the permission of the owner to make the alteration, removal, or obliteration; or</p>
          <p>(11) with the intent to prevent the identification of property involved, so as to deprive the rightful owner of possession thereof, alters or removes any permanent serial number, permanent distinguishing number or manufacturer's identification number on personal property or possesses, sells or buys any personal property knowing or having reason to know that the permanent serial number, permanent distinguishing number or manufacturer's identification number has been removed or altered; or</p>
          <p>(12) intentionally deprives another of a lawful charge for cable television service by:</p>
          <p>(i) making or using or attempting to make or use an unauthorized external connection outside the individual dwelling unit whether physical, electrical, acoustical, inductive, or other connection; or by</p>
          <p>(ii) attaching any unauthorized device to any cable, wire, microwave, or other component of a licensed cable communications system as defined in chapter 238. Nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit the electronic video rerecording of program material transmitted on the cable communications system by a subscriber for fair use as defined by Public Law 94-553, section 107; or</p>
          <p>(13) except as provided in clauses (12) and (14), obtains the services of another with the intention of receiving those services without making the agreed or reasonably expected payment of money or other consideration; or</p>
          <p>(14) intentionally deprives another of a lawful charge for telecommunications service by:</p>
          <p>(i) making, using, or attempting to make or use an unauthorized connection whether physical, electrical, by wire, microwave, radio, or other means to a component of a local telecommunication system as provided in chapter 237; or</p>
          <p>(ii) attaching an unauthorized device to a cable, wire, microwave, radio, or other component of a local telecommunication system as provided in chapter 237.</p>
          <p>The existence of an unauthorized connection is prima facie evidence that the occupier of the premises:</p>
          <p>(A) made or was aware of the connection; and</p>
          <p>(B) was aware that the connection was unauthorized;</p>
          <p>(15) with intent to defraud, diverts corporate property other than in accordance with general business purposes or for purposes other than those specified in the corporation's articles of incorporation; or</p>
          <p>(16) with intent to defraud, authorizes or causes a corporation to make a distribution in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/302A.551">302A.551</a>, or any other state law in conformity with it; or</p>
          <p>(17) takes or drives a motor vehicle without the consent of the owner or an authorized agent of the owner, knowing or having reason to know that the owner or an authorized agent of the owner did not give consent; or</p>
          <p>(18) intentionally, and without claim of right, takes motor fuel from a retailer without the retailer's consent and with intent to deprive the retailer permanently of possession of the fuel by driving a motor vehicle from the premises of the retailer without having paid for the fuel dispensed into the vehicle; or</p>
          <p>(19) commits wage theft under subdivision 1, clause (13).</p>
          <p>(b) Proof that the driver of a motor vehicle into which motor fuel was dispensed drove the vehicle from the premises of the retailer without having paid for the fuel permits the factfinder to infer that the driver acted intentionally and without claim of right, and that the driver intended to deprive the retailer permanently of possession of the fuel. This paragraph does not apply if: (1) payment has been made to the retailer within 30 days of the receipt of notice of nonpayment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604.15">604.15</a>; or (2) a written notice as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604.15#stat.604.15.4">604.15, subdivision 4</a>, disputing the retailer's claim, has been sent. This paragraph does not apply to the owner of a motor vehicle if the vehicle or the vehicle's license plate has been reported stolen before the theft of the fuel.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.52.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever commits theft may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both, if the property is a firearm, or the value of the property or services stolen is more than $35,000 and the conviction is for a violation of subdivision 2, clause (3), (4), (15), (16), or (19), or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2335#stat.609.2335.1">609.2335, subdivision 1</a>, clause (1) or (2), item (i); or</p>
          <p class="in">(2) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the value of the property or services stolen exceeds $5,000, or if the property stolen was an article representing a trade secret, an explosive or incendiary device, or a controlled substance listed in Schedule I or II pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.02">152.02 </a>with the exception of marijuana; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p class="in">(a) the value of the property or services stolen is more than $1,000 but not more than $5,000; or</p>
          <p class="in">(b) the property stolen was a controlled substance listed in Schedule III, IV, or V pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.02">152.02</a>; or</p>
          <p class="in">(c) the value of the property or services stolen is more than $500 but not more than $1,000 and the person has been convicted within the preceding five years for an offense under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.98">256.98</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/268.182">268.182</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.247">609.247</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.522">609.522</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a>, 2, or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, or a statute from another state, the United States, or a foreign jurisdiction, in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence for the offense, or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow imposition of a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence; or</p>
          <p class="in">(d) the value of the property or services stolen is not more than $1,000, and any of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the property is taken from the person of another or from a corpse, or grave or coffin containing a corpse; or</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) the property is a record of a court or officer, or a writing, instrument or record kept, filed or deposited according to law with or in the keeping of any public officer or office; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the property is taken from a burning, abandoned, or vacant building or upon its removal therefrom, or from an area of destruction caused by civil disaster, riot, bombing, or the proximity of battle; or</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) the property consists of public funds belonging to the state or to any political subdivision or agency thereof; or</p>
          <p class="in">(v) the property stolen is a motor vehicle; or</p>
          <p class="in">(4) to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the value of the property or services stolen is more than $500 but not more than $1,000; or</p>
          <p class="in">(5) in all other cases where the value of the property or services stolen is $500 or less, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both, provided, however, in any prosecution under subdivision 2, clauses (1), (2), (3), (4), (13), and (19), the value of the money or property or services received by the defendant in violation of any one or more of the above provisions within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this subdivision; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.52.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Enhanced penalty.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">If a violation of this section creates a reasonably foreseeable risk of bodily harm to another, the penalties described in subdivision 3 are enhanced as follows:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) if the penalty is a misdemeanor or a gross misdemeanor, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) if the penalty is a felony, the statutory maximum sentence for the offense is 50 percent longer than for the underlying crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.52.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Wrongfully obtained public assistance; consideration of disqualification.</span></h2>
          <p>When determining the sentence for a person convicted of theft by wrongfully obtaining public assistance, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.98#stat.256.98.1">256.98, subdivision 1</a>, the court shall consider the fact that, under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.98#stat.256.98.8">256.98, subdivision 8</a>, the person will be disqualified from receiving public assistance as a result of the person's conviction.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">
