<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.7.0">1988 c 712 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.5.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/279/#laws.0.32.0">1991 c 279 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.5.80.0">1991 c 292 art 5 s 80</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/510/#laws.2.14.0">1992 c 510 art 2 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.41.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 41</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.20.0">1995 c 244 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.31.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 31</a>,32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/66/#laws.0.79.0">1997 c 66 s 79</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.17.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.18.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/76/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 76 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/218/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 218 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.31.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.8.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/119/#laws.0.9.0">2009 c 119 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/173/#laws.0.5.0">2012 c 173 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/7/#laws.3.14.0">1Sp2019 c 7 art 3 s 14</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.92.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 92</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.9.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 9</a>; art 6 s 16; art 20 s 21; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/101/#laws.3.2.0">2024 c 101 art 3 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.521">
        <h1 class="shn">609.521 POSSESSION OF SHOPLIFTING GEAR.</h1>
        <p>(a) As used in this section, an "electronic article surveillance system" means any electronic device or devices that are designed to detect the unauthorized removal of marked merchandise from a store.</p>
        <p>(b) Whoever has in possession any device, gear, or instrument designed to assist in shoplifting or defeating an electronic article surveillance system with intent to use the same to shoplift and thereby commit theft may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.521.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/314/#laws.0.1.0">1975 c 314 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.8.26.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 8 s 26</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.522">
        <h1 class="shn">609.522 ORGANIZED RETAIL THEFT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.522.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Pattern of retail theft" means acts committed or directed by the defendant on at least two separate occasions in the preceding six months that would constitute a violation of:</p>
          <p>(1) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (1), (3), or (4), involving retail merchandise;</p>
          <p>(2) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.521">609.521</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53#stat.609.53.1">609.53, subdivision 1</a>, involving retail merchandise;</p>
          <p>(4) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582">609.582</a> when the building was a retail establishment; or</p>
          <p>(5) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.59">609.59</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) "Retail establishment" means the building where a retailer sells retail merchandise.</p>
          <p>(d) "Retail merchandise" means all forms of tangible property, without limitation, held out for sale by a retailer.</p>
          <p>(e) "Retail theft enterprise" means a group of two or more individuals with a shared goal involving the unauthorized removal of retail merchandise from a retailer. Retail theft enterprise does not require the membership of the enterprise to remain the same or that the same individuals participate in each offense committed by the enterprise.</p>
          <p>(f) "Retailer" means a person or entity that sells retail merchandise.</p>
          <p>(g) "Value" means the retail market value at the time of the theft or, if the retail market value cannot be ascertained, the cost of replacement of the property within a reasonable time after the theft.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.522.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Organized retail theft.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of organized retail theft if:</p>
          <p>(1) the person is employed by or associated with a retail theft enterprise;</p>
          <p>(2) the person has previously engaged in a pattern of retail theft and intentionally commits an act or directs another member of the retail theft enterprise to commit an act involving retail merchandise that would constitute a violation of:</p>
          <p>(i) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (1), (3), or (4); or</p>
          <p>(ii) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53#stat.609.53.1">609.53, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) the person or another member of the retail theft enterprise:</p>
          <p>(i) resells or intends to resell the stolen retail merchandise;</p>
          <p>(ii) advertises or displays any item of the stolen retail merchandise for sale; or</p>
          <p>(iii) returns any item of the stolen retail merchandise to a retailer for anything of value.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.522.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever commits organized retail theft may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than 15 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both, if the value of the property stolen exceeds $5,000;</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than seven years or to payment of a fine of not more than $14,000, or both, if either of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the value of the property stolen is more than $1,000 but not more than $5,000; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the value of the property is more than $500 but not more than $1,000 and the person commits the offense within ten years of the first of two or more convictions under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.98">256.98</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/268.182">268.182</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582">609.582, subdivision </a>1, 2, or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, or a statute from another state, the United States, or a foreign jurisdiction, in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence for the offense, or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow imposition of a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence;</p>
          <p>(3) to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both, if either of the following circumstances exist:</p>
          <p>(i) the value of the property stolen is more than $500 but not more than $1,000; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the value of the property is $500 or less and the person commits the offense within ten years of a previous conviction under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.98">256.98</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/268.182">268.182</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a>, 2, or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, or a statute from another state, the United States, or a foreign jurisdiction, in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence for the offense, or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow imposition of a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence; or</p>
          <p>(4) to imprisonment of not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the value of the property stolen is $500 or less.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.522.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Aggregation.</span></h2>
          <p>The value of the retail merchandise received by the defendant in violation of this section within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this subdivision; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.522.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Enhanced penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>If a violation of this section creates a reasonably foreseeable risk of bodily harm to another, the penalties described in subdivision 3 are enhanced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the penalty is a gross misdemeanor, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both; and</p>
          <p>(2) if the penalty is a felony, the statutory maximum sentence for the offense is 50 percent longer than for the underlying crime.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.522.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.10.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 10</a>; art 6 s 16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.15.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 15</a>,16</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.523">
        <h1 class="shn">609.523 RETURN OF STOLEN PROPERTY TO OWNERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.523.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Photographic record.</span></h2>
          <p>Photographs of property, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, over which a person is alleged to have exerted unauthorized control or to have otherwise obtained unlawfully, are competent evidence if the photographs are admissible into evidence under all rules of law governing the admissibility of photographs into evidence. The photographic record, when satisfactorily identified, is as admissible in evidence as the property itself.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.523.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Record of property.</span></h2>
          <p>The photographs may bear a written description of the property alleged to have been wrongfully taken, the name of the owner of the property taken, the name of the accused, the name of the arresting law enforcement officer, the date of the photograph, and the signature of the photographer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.523.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Return of property.</span></h2>
          <p>A law enforcement agency which is holding property over which a person is alleged to have exerted unauthorized control or to have otherwise obtained unlawfully may return that property to its owner if:</p>
          <p>(1) the appropriately identified photographs are filed and retained by the law enforcement agency;</p>
          <p>(2) satisfactory proof of ownership of the property is shown by the owner;</p>
          <p>(3) a declaration of ownership is signed under penalty of perjury; and</p>
          <p>(4) a receipt for the property is obtained from the owner upon delivery by the law enforcement agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.523.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Examination of property.</span></h2>
          <p>If the recovered property has a value in excess of $150, then the owner shall retain possession for at least 14 days to allow the defense attorney to examine the property.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.523.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/539/#laws.0.1.0">1982 c 539 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.525">
        <h1 class="shn">609.525 BRINGING STOLEN GOODS INTO STATE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.525.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever brings property into the state which the actor has stolen outside the state, or received outside of the state knowing it to have been stolen, may be sentenced in accordance with the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>. The actor may be charged, indicted, and tried in any county, but not more than one county, into or through which the actor has brought such property.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.525.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Defining stolen property.</span></h2>
          <p>Property is stolen within the meaning of this section if the act by which the owner was deprived of property was a criminal offense under the laws of the state in which the act was committed and would constitute a theft under this chapter if the act had been committed in this state.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.525.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.525; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.526">
        <h1 class="shn">609.526 PRECIOUS METAL AND SCRAP METAL DEALERS; RECEIVING STOLEN PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.526.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) "precious metal dealer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.731#stat.325F.731.2">325F.731, subdivision 2</a>; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) "scrap metal dealer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325E.21#stat.325E.21.1">325E.21, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.526.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime described.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Any precious metal dealer or scrap metal dealer or any person employed by a dealer, who receives, possesses, transfers, buys, or conceals any stolen property or property obtained by robbery or carjacking, knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen or obtained by robbery or carjacking, may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) if the value of the property received, bought, or concealed is $1,000 or more, to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) if the value of the property received, bought, or concealed is less than $1,000 but more than $500, to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) if the value of the property received, bought, or concealed is $500 or less, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
          <p class="in">Any person convicted of violating this section a second or subsequent time within a period of one year may be sentenced as provided in clause (1).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.526.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.6.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.10.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.20.22.0">2023 c 52 art 20 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.527">
        <h1 class="shn">609.527 IDENTITY THEFT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given them in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) "Direct victim" means any person or entity described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.01">611A.01, paragraph (b)</a>, whose identity has been transferred, used, or possessed in violation of this section.</p>
          <p>(c) "False pretense" means any false, fictitious, misleading, or fraudulent information or pretense or pretext depicting or including or deceptively similar to the name, logo, website address, email address, postal address, telephone number, or any other identifying information of a for-profit or not-for-profit business or organization or of a government agency, to which the user has no legitimate claim of right.</p>
          <p>(d) "Financial institution" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13A.01#stat.13A.01.2">13A.01, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) "Identity" means any name, number, or data transmission that may be used, alone or in conjunction with any other information, to identify a specific individual or entity, including any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a name, Social Security number, date of birth, official government-issued driver's license or identification number, government passport number, or employer or taxpayer identification number;</p>
          <p>(2) unique electronic identification number, address, account number, or routing code; or</p>
          <p>(3) telecommunication identification information or access device.</p>
          <p>(f) "Indirect victim" means any person or entity described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.01">611A.01, paragraph (b)</a>, other than a direct victim.</p>
          <p>(g) "Loss" means value obtained, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3), and expenses incurred by a direct or indirect victim as a result of a violation of this section.</p>
          <p>(h) "Unlawful activity" means:</p>
          <p>(1) any felony violation of the laws of this state or any felony violation of a similar law of another state or the United States; and</p>
          <p>(2) any nonfelony violation of the laws of this state involving theft, theft by swindle, forgery, fraud, or giving false information to a public official, or any nonfelony violation of a similar law of another state or the United States.</p>
          <p>(i) "Scanning device" means a scanner, reader, or any other electronic device that is used to access, read, scan, obtain, memorize, or store, temporarily or permanently, information encoded on a computer chip or magnetic strip or stripe of a payment card, driver's license, or state-issued identification card.</p>
          <p>(j) "Reencoder" means an electronic device that places encoded information from the computer chip or magnetic strip or stripe of a payment card, driver's license, or state-issued identification card, onto the computer chip or magnetic strip or stripe of a different payment card, driver's license, or state-issued identification card, or any electronic medium that allows an authorized transaction to occur.</p>
          <p>(k) "Payment card" means a credit card, charge card, debit card, or any other card that:</p>
          <p>(1) is issued to an authorized card user; and</p>
          <p>(2) allows the user to obtain, purchase, or receive credit, money, a good, a service, or anything of value.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who transfers, possesses, or uses an identity that is not the person's own, with the intent to commit, aid, or abet any unlawful activity is guilty of identity theft and may be punished as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the offense involves a single direct victim and the total, combined loss to the direct victim and any indirect victims is $250 or less, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (5);</p>
          <p>(2) if the offense involves a single direct victim and the total, combined loss to the direct victim and any indirect victims is more than $250 but not more than $500, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (4);</p>
          <p>(3) if the offense involves two or three direct victims or the total, combined loss to the direct and indirect victims is more than $500 but not more than $2,500, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (3);</p>
          <p>(4) if the offense involves more than three but not more than seven direct victims, or if the total combined loss to the direct and indirect victims is more than $2,500, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2);</p>
          <p>(5) if the offense involves eight or more direct victims, or if the total, combined loss to the direct and indirect victims is more than $35,000, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (1); and</p>
          <p>(6) if the offense is related to possession or distribution of pornographic work in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.246">617.246</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.247">617.247</a>, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (1).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Restitution; items provided to victim.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A direct or indirect victim of an identity theft crime shall be considered a victim for all purposes, including any rights that accrue under chapter 611A and rights to court-ordered restitution.</p>
          <p>(b) The court shall order a person convicted of violating subdivision 2 to pay restitution of not less than $1,000 to each direct victim of the offense.</p>
          <p>(c) Upon the written request of a direct victim or the prosecutor setting forth with specificity the facts and circumstances of the offense in a proposed order, the court shall provide to the victim, without cost, a certified copy of the complaint filed in the matter, the judgment of conviction, and an order setting forth the facts and circumstances of the offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who has learned or reasonably suspects that a person is a direct victim of a crime under subdivision 2 may initiate a law enforcement investigation by contacting the local law enforcement agency that has jurisdiction where the person resides, regardless of where the crime may have occurred. The agency must prepare a police report of the matter, provide the complainant with a copy of that report, and may begin an investigation of the facts, or, if the suspected crime was committed in a different jurisdiction, refer the matter to the law enforcement agency where the suspected crime was committed for an investigation of the facts.</p>
          <p>(b) If a law enforcement agency refers a report to the law enforcement agency where the crime was committed, it need not include the report as a crime committed in its jurisdiction for purposes of information that the agency is required to provide to the commissioner of public safety pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.06">299C.06</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Crime of electronic use of false pretense to obtain identity.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who, with intent to obtain the identity of another, uses a false pretense in an email to another person or in a web page, electronic communication, advertisement, or any other communication on the Internet, is guilty of a crime.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever commits such offense may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) In a prosecution under this subdivision, it is not a defense that:</p>
          <p>(1) the person committing the offense did not obtain the identity of another;</p>
          <p>(2) the person committing the offense did not use the identity; or</p>
          <p>(3) the offense did not result in financial loss or any other loss to any person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.5b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Unlawful possession or use of scanning device or reencoder.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who uses a scanning device or reencoder without permission of the cardholder of the card from which the information is being scanned or reencoded, with the intent to commit, aid, or abet any unlawful activity, is guilty of a crime.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who possesses, with the intent to commit, aid, or abet any unlawful activity, any device, apparatus, equipment, software, material, good, property, or supply that is designed or adapted for use as a scanning device or a reencoder is guilty of a crime.</p>
          <p>(c) Whoever commits an offense under paragraph (a) or (b) may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/627.01">627.01</a>, an offense committed under subdivision 2, 5a, or 5b may be prosecuted in:</p>
          <p>(1) the county where the offense occurred;</p>
          <p>(2) the county of residence or place of business of the direct victim or indirect victim; or</p>
          <p>(3) in the case of a violation of subdivision 5a or 5b, the county of residence of the person whose identity was obtained or sought.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Aggregation.</span></h2>
          <p>In any prosecution under subdivision 2, the value of the money or property or services the defendant receives or the number of direct or indirect victims within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of subdivision 3; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.527.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Release of limited account information to law enforcement authorities.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A financial institution may release the information described in paragraph (b) to a law enforcement or prosecuting authority that certifies in writing that it is investigating or prosecuting a crime of identity theft under this section. The certification must describe with reasonable specificity the nature of the suspected identity theft that is being investigated or prosecuted, including the dates of the suspected criminal activity.</p>
          <p>(b) This subdivision applies to requests for the following information relating to a potential victim's account:</p>
          <p>(1) the name of the account holder or holders; and</p>
          <p>(2) the last known home address and telephone numbers of the account holder or holders.</p>
          <p>(c) A financial institution may release the information requested under this subdivision that it possesses within a reasonable time after the request. The financial institution may not impose a fee for furnishing the information.</p>
          <p>(d) A financial institution is not liable in a criminal or civil proceeding for releasing information in accordance with this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(e) Release of limited account information to a law enforcement agency under this subdivision is criminal investigative data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.82#stat.13.82.7">13.82, subdivision 7</a>, except that when the investigation becomes inactive the account information remains confidential data on individuals or protected nonpublic data.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.527.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/244/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 244 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/354/#laws.0.3.0">2000 c 354 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/106/#laws.0.1.0">2003 c 106 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.8.9.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 8 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.32.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 32</a>-36; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/293/#laws.0.2.0">2010 c 293 s 2</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/25/#laws.0.1.0">2021 c 25 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.9.3.0">2023 c 52 art 9 s 3</a>,4</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.528">
        <h1 class="shn">609.528 POSSESSION OR SALE OF STOLEN OR COUNTERFEIT CHECK; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.528.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given them in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) "Direct victim" means any person or entity described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.01">611A.01, paragraph (b)</a>, from whom a check is stolen or whose name or other identifying information is contained in a counterfeit check.</p>
          <p>(c) "Indirect victim" means any person or entity described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.01">611A.01, paragraph (b)</a>, other than a direct victim.</p>
          <p>(d) "Loss" means value obtained, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3), and expenses incurred by a direct or indirect victim as a result of a violation of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.528.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who sells, possesses, receives, or transfers a check that is stolen or counterfeit, knowing or having reason to know the check is stolen or counterfeit, is guilty of a crime and may be punished as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.528.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the offense involves a single direct victim and the total, combined loss to the direct victim and any indirect victims is $250 or less, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (5);</p>
          <p>(2) if the offense involves a single direct victim and the total, combined loss to the direct victim and any indirect victims is more than $250 but not more than $500, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (4);</p>
          <p>(3) if the offense involves two or three direct victims or the total, combined loss to the direct and indirect victims is more than $500 but not more than $2,500, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (3); and</p>
          <p>(4) if the offense involves four or more direct victims, or if the total, combined loss to the direct and indirect victims is more than $2,500, the person may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, clause (2).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.528.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/354/#laws.0.4.0">2000 c 354 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.529">
        <h1 class="shn">609.529 MAIL THEFT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.529.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given them in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) "Mail" means a letter, postal card, package, bag, or other sealed article addressed to another.</p>
          <p>(c) "Mail depository" means a mail box, letter box, or mail receptacle; a post office or station of a post office; a mail route; or a postal service vehicle.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.529.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of mail theft and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally and without claim of right removes mail from a mail depository;</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally and without claim of right takes mail from a mail carrier;</p>
          <p>(3) obtains custody of mail by intentionally deceiving a mail carrier, or other person who rightfully possesses or controls the mail, with a false representation which is known to be false, made with intent to deceive and which does deceive a mail carrier or other person who possesses or controls the mail;</p>
          <p>(4) intentionally and without claim of right removes the contents of mail addressed to another;</p>
          <p>(5) intentionally and without claim of right takes mail, or the contents of mail, that has been left for collection on or near a mail depository; or</p>
          <p>(6) receives, possesses, transfers, buys, or conceals mail obtained by acts described in clauses (1) to (5), knowing or having reason to know the mail was obtained illegally.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.529.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted under subdivision 2 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.529.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/627.01">627.01</a>, an offense committed under subdivision 2 may be prosecuted in:</p>
          <p>(1) the county where the offense occurred; or</p>
          <p>(2) the county of residence or place of business of the direct victim or indirect victim.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.529.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/106/#laws.0.4.0">2003 c 106 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.53">
        <h1 class="shn">609.53 RECEIVING STOLEN PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as otherwise provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.526">609.526</a>, any person who receives, possesses, transfers, buys or conceals any stolen property or property obtained by robbery, knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen or obtained by robbery, may be sentenced in accordance with the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.14.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/613/#laws.0.7.0">1982 c 613 s 7</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/613/#laws.0.7.0">1982 c 613 s 7</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.14.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.14.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Civil action; treble damages.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who has been injured by a violation of subdivision 1 or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.526">609.526</a> may bring an action for three times the amount of actual damages sustained by the plaintiff or $1,500, whichever is greater, and the costs of suit and reasonable attorney's fees.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.53.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Value.</span></h2>
          <p>In this section, "value" has the meaning defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.53.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.53; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/669/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 669 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/232/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 232 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/333/#laws.0.14.0">1981 c 333 s 14</a>-17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/613/#laws.0.1.0">1982 c 613 s 1</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/483/#laws.0.2.0">1984 c 483 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/384/#laws.1.46.0">1987 c 384 art 1 s 46</a>,47; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.7.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 7</a>,8</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.531">
        <h1 class="shn">609.531 FORFEITURES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">For the purpose of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a>, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p class="in">(a) "Conveyance device" means a device used for transportation and includes, but is not limited to, a motor vehicle, trailer, snowmobile, airplane, and vessel and any equipment attached to it. The term "conveyance device" does not include property which is, in fact, itself stolen or taken in violation of the law.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Weapon used" means a dangerous weapon as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02#stat.609.02.6">609.02, subdivision 6</a>, that the actor used or had in possession in furtherance of a crime.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "Property" means property as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, clause (1).</p>
          <p class="in">(d) "Contraband" means property which is illegal to possess under Minnesota law.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) "Appropriate agency" means the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, the Department of Commerce Fraud Bureau, the Minnesota Division of Driver and Vehicle Services, the Minnesota State Patrol, a county sheriff's department, the Three Rivers Park District Department of Public Safety, the Department of Natural Resources Division of Enforcement, the University of Minnesota Police Department, the Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit, a city, metropolitan transit, or airport police department; or a multijurisdictional entity established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299A.642">299A.642</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299A.681">299A.681</a>.</p>
          <p class="in">(f) "Designated offense" includes:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) for weapons used: any violation of this chapter, chapter 152 or 624;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) for driver's license or identification card transactions: any violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.22">171.22</a>; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) for all other purposes: a felony violation of, or a felony-level attempt or conspiracy to violate, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325E.17">325E.17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.825">609.825</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.86">609.86</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.88">609.88</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.89">609.89</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.893">609.893</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.895">609.895</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.246">617.246</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.247">617.247</a>; or a gross misdemeanor or felony violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.891">609.891</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.7181">624.7181</a>; or any violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>; or a felony violation of, or a felony-level attempt or conspiracy to violate, Minnesota Statutes 2012, section 609.21.</p>
          <p class="in">(g) "Controlled substance" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.4">152.01, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
          <p>(h) "Prosecuting authority" means the attorney who is responsible for prosecuting an offense that is the basis for a forfeiture under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a>.</p>
          <p>(i) "Asserting person" means a person, other than the driver alleged to have used a vehicle in the transportation or exchange of a controlled substance intended for distribution or sale, claiming an ownership interest in a vehicle that has been seized or restrained under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Construction.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531"> 609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> must be liberally construed to carry out the following remedial purposes:</p>
          <p>(1) to enforce the law;</p>
          <p>(2) to deter crime;</p>
          <p>(3) to reduce the economic incentive to engage in criminal enterprise;</p>
          <p>(4) to increase the pecuniary loss resulting from the detection of criminal activity; and</p>
          <p>(5) to forfeit property unlawfully used or acquired and divert the property to law enforcement purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.17.0">1988 c 665 s 17</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.17.0">1988 c 665 s 17</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Seizure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Property subject to forfeiture under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> may be seized by the appropriate agency upon process issued by any court having jurisdiction over the property. Property may be seized without process if:</p>
          <p>(1) the seizure is incident to a lawful arrest or a lawful search;</p>
          <p>(2) the property subject to seizure has been the subject of a prior judgment in favor of the state in a criminal injunction or forfeiture proceeding under this chapter; or</p>
          <p>(3) the appropriate agency has probable cause to believe that the delay occasioned by the necessity to obtain process would result in the removal or destruction of the property and that:</p>
          <p>(i) the property was used or is intended to be used in commission of a felony; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the property is dangerous to health or safety.</p>
          <p>If property is seized without process under item (i), the prosecuting authority must institute a forfeiture action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5313">609.5313</a> as soon as is reasonably possible.</p>
          <p>(b) When property is seized, the officer must provide a receipt to the person found in possession of the property; or in the absence of any person, the officer must leave a receipt in the place where the property was found, if reasonably possible.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Right to possession vests immediately; custody of seized property.</span></h2>
          <p>All right, title, and interest in property subject to forfeiture under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> vests in the appropriate agency upon commission of the act or omission giving rise to the forfeiture. Any property seized under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> is not subject to replevin, but is deemed to be in the custody of the appropriate agency subject to the orders and decrees of the court having jurisdiction over the forfeiture proceedings. When property is so seized, the appropriate agency shall use reasonable diligence to secure the property and prevent waste and may do any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) place the property under seal;</p>
          <p>(2) remove the property to a place designated by it; and</p>
          <p>(3) in the case of controlled substances, require the state Board of Pharmacy to take custody of the property and remove it to an appropriate location for disposition in accordance with law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Bond by owner for possession.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the owner of property that has been seized under sections<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531"> 609.531</a> to<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318"> 609.5318</a> seeks possession of the property before the forfeiture action is determined, the owner may give security or post bond payable to the appropriate agency in an amount equal to the retail value of the seized property. On posting the security or bond, the seized property must be returned to the owner and the forfeiture action shall proceed against the security as if it were the seized property. This subdivision does not apply to contraband property or property being held for investigatory purposes.</p>
          <p>(b) If the owner of a motor vehicle that has been seized under this section seeks possession of the vehicle before the forfeiture action is determined, the owner may surrender the vehicle's certificate of title in exchange for the vehicle. The motor vehicle must be returned to the owner within 24 hours if the owner surrenders the motor vehicle's certificate of title to the appropriate agency, pending resolution of the forfeiture action. If the certificate is surrendered, the owner may not be ordered to post security or bond as a condition of release of the vehicle. When a certificate of title is surrendered under this provision, the agency shall notify the Department of Public Safety and any secured party noted on the certificate. The agency shall also notify the department and the secured party when it returns a surrendered title to the motor vehicle owner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.17.0">1988 c 665 s 17</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.6a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture a civil procedure; conviction required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An action for forfeiture is a civil in rem action and is independent of any criminal prosecution, except as provided in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) An asset is subject to forfeiture by judicial determination under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5311">609.5311</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> only if:</p>
          <p>(1) a person is convicted of the criminal offense related to the action for forfeiture; or</p>
          <p>(2) a person is not charged with a criminal offense under chapter 152 related to the action for forfeiture based in whole or in part on the person's agreement to provide information regarding the criminal activity of another person.</p>
          <p>For purposes of clause (1), an admission of guilt to an offense chargeable under chapter 152, a sentence under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.152">152.152</a>, a stay of adjudication under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.18">152.18</a>, or a referral to a diversion program for an offense chargeable under chapter 152 is considered a conviction.</p>
          <p>(c) The appropriate agency handling the judicial forfeiture may introduce into evidence in the judicial forfeiture case in civil court the agreement in paragraph (b), clause (2).</p>
          <p>(d) The appropriate agency handling the judicial forfeiture bears the burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence that the property is an instrument or represents the proceeds of the underlying offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Petition for remission or mitigation.</span></h2>
          <p>Prior to the entry of a court order disposing with the forfeiture action, any person who has an interest in forfeited property may file with the prosecuting authority a petition for remission or mitigation of the forfeiture. The prosecuting authority may remit or mitigate the forfeiture upon terms and conditions the prosecuting authority deems reasonable if the prosecuting authority finds that: (1) the forfeiture was incurred without willful negligence or without any intention on the part of the petitioner to violate the law; or (2) extenuating circumstances justify the remission or mitigation of the forfeiture.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture policies; statewide model policy required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) By December 1, 2010, the Peace Officer Standards and Training Board, after consulting with the Minnesota County Attorneys Association, the Minnesota Sheriffs' Association, the Minnesota Chiefs of Police Association, and the Minnesota Police and Peace Officers Association, shall develop a model policy that articulates best practices for forfeiture and is designed to encourage the uniform application of forfeiture laws statewide. At a minimum, the policy shall address the following:</p>
          <p>(1) best practices in pursuing, seizing, and tracking forfeitures;</p>
          <p>(2) type and frequency of training for law enforcement on forfeiture laws; and</p>
          <p>(3) situations in which forfeitures should not be pursued.</p>
          <p>(b) By December 1, 2010, the Minnesota County Attorneys Association, after consulting with the attorney general, the Peace Officer Standards and Training Board, the Minnesota Sheriffs' Association, the Minnesota Chiefs of Police Association, and the Minnesota Police and Peace Officers Association, shall develop a model policy that articulates best practices for forfeiture and is designed to encourage the uniform application of forfeiture laws statewide. At a minimum, the policy shall address the following:</p>
          <p>(1) statutory role of prosecuting authorities in forfeiture procedures;</p>
          <p>(2) best practices for timely and fair resolution of forfeiture cases;</p>
          <p>(3) type and frequency of training for prosecuting authorities on forfeiture laws; and</p>
          <p>(4) situations in which forfeitures should not be pursued.</p>
          <p>(c) By December 1, 2010, the Minnesota County Attorneys Association and the Peace Officer Standards and Training Board shall forward an electronic copy of its respective model policy to the chairs and ranking minority members of the senate and house of representatives committees having jurisdiction over criminal justice and civil law policy.</p>
          <p>(d) By March 1, 2011, the chief law enforcement officer of every state and local law enforcement agency and every prosecution office in the state shall adopt and implement a written policy on forfeiture that is identical or substantially similar to the model policies developed under paragraphs (a) and (b). The written policy shall be made available to the public upon request.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.531.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Transfer of forfeitable property to federal government.</span></h2>
          <p>The appropriate agency shall not directly or indirectly transfer property subject to forfeiture under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> to a federal agency for adoption if the forfeiture would be prohibited under state law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5311">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5311 FORFEITURE OF PROPERTY ASSOCIATED WITH CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5311.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Controlled substances.</span></h2>
          <p>All controlled substances that were manufactured, distributed, dispensed, or acquired in violation of chapter 152 or 342 are subject to forfeiture under this section, except as provided in subdivision 3 and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5316">609.5316</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5311.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Associated property.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) All personal property and real property, other than homestead property exempt from seizure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/510.01">510.01</a>, that is an instrument or represents the proceeds of a controlled substance offense is subject to forfeiture under this section, except as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
          <p>(b) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not seize real property for the purposes of forfeiture under paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) Money is the property of an appropriate agency and may be seized and recovered by the appropriate agency if:</p>
          <p>(1) the money is used by an appropriate agency, or furnished to a person operating on behalf of an appropriate agency, to purchase or attempt to purchase a controlled substance; and</p>
          <p>(2) the appropriate agency records the serial number or otherwise marks the money for identification.</p>
          <p class="bl">As used in this paragraph, "money" means United States currency and coin; the currency and coin of a foreign country; a bank check, cashier's check, or traveler's check; a prepaid credit card; cryptocurrency; or a money order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5311.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Limitations on forfeiture of certain property associated with controlled substances.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A conveyance device is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the retail value of the controlled substance is $100 or more and the conveyance device was used in the transportation or exchange of a controlled substance intended for distribution or sale.</p>
          <p>(b) Real property is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the retail value of the controlled substance or contraband is $2,000 or more.</p>
          <p>(c) Property used by any person as a common carrier in the transaction of business as a common carrier is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the owner of the property is a consenting party to, or is privy to, the use or intended use of the property as described in subdivision 2.</p>
          <p>(d) Property is subject to forfeiture under this section only if its owner was privy to the use or intended use described in subdivision 2, or the unlawful use or intended use of the property otherwise occurred with the owner's knowledge or consent.</p>
          <p>(e) Forfeiture under this section of a conveyance device or real property encumbered by a bona fide security interest is subject to the interest of the secured party unless the secured party had knowledge of or consented to the act or omission upon which the forfeiture is based. A person claiming a security interest bears the burden of establishing that interest by clear and convincing evidence.</p>
          <p>(f) Forfeiture under this section of real property is subject to the interests of a good faith purchaser for value unless the purchaser had knowledge of or consented to the act or omission upon which the forfeiture is based.</p>
          <p>(g) Notwithstanding paragraphs (d), (e), and (f), property is not subject to forfeiture based solely on the owner's or secured party's knowledge of the unlawful use or intended use of the property if: (1) the owner or secured party took reasonable steps to terminate use of the property by the offender; or (2) the property is real property owned by the parent of the offender, unless the parent actively participated in, or knowingly acquiesced to, a violation of chapter 152, or the real property constitutes proceeds derived from or traceable to a use described in subdivision 2.</p>
          <p>(h) Money is subject to forfeiture under this section only if it has a total value of $1,500 or more or there is probable cause to believe that the money was exchanged for the purchase of a controlled substance. As used in this paragraph, "money" means United States currency and coin; the currency and coin of a foreign country; a bank check, cashier's check, or traveler's check; a prepaid credit card; cryptocurrency; or a money order.</p>
          <p>(i) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not seize a conveyance device or real property, for the purposes of forfeiture under paragraphs (a) to (g).</p>
          <p>(j) Nothing in this subdivision prohibits the seizure, with or without warrant, of any property or thing for the purpose of being produced as evidence on any trial or for any other lawful purpose.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5311.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Records; proceeds.</span></h2>
          <p> All books, records, and research products and materials, including formulas, microfilm, tapes, and data that are used, or intended for use in the manner described in subdivision 2 are subject to forfeiture.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5311.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.11.0">1988 c 665 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.3.30.0">1989 c 290 art 3 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/305/#laws.0.5.0">1989 c 305 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/533/#laws.0.2.0">1992 c 533 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/6/#laws.0.5.0">1993 c 6 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.6.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.13.9.0">2005 c 136 art 13 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/391/#laws.0.12.0">2010 c 391 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.5.11.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 5 s 11</a>-13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.45.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5312">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5312 FORFEITURE OF PROPERTY ASSOCIATED WITH DESIGNATED OFFENSES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5312.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Property subject to forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) All personal property is subject to forfeiture if it was used or intended for use to commit or facilitate the commission of a designated offense. All money and other property, real and personal, that represent proceeds of a designated offense, and all contraband property, are subject to forfeiture, except as provided in this section.</p>
          <p>(b) All money used or intended to be used to facilitate the commission of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a> or a violation of a local ordinance substantially similar to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a> is subject to forfeiture.</p>
          <p>(c) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not seize real property for the purposes of forfeiture under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5312.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Computers and related property subject to forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this subdivision, "property" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.87#stat.609.87.6">609.87, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) When a computer or a component part of a computer is used or intended for use to commit or facilitate the commission of a designated offense, the computer and all software, data, and other property contained in the computer are subject to forfeiture unless prohibited by the Privacy Protection Act, United States Code, title 42, sections 2000aa to 2000aa-12, or other state or federal law.</p>
          <p>(c) Regardless of whether a forfeiture action is initiated following the lawful seizure of a computer and related property, if the appropriate agency returns hardware, software, data, or other property to the owner, the agency may charge the owner for the cost of separating contraband from the computer or other property returned, including salary and contract costs. The agency may not charge these costs to an owner of a computer or related property who was not privy to the act or omission upon which the seizure was based, or who did not have knowledge of or consent to the act or omission, if the owner:</p>
          <p>(1) requests from the agency copies of specified legitimate data files and provides sufficient storage media; or</p>
          <p>(2) requests the return of a computer or other property less data storage devices on which contraband resides.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5312.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Limitations on forfeiture of property associated with designated offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Property used by a person as a common carrier in the transaction of business as a common carrier is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the owner of the property is a consenting party to, or is privy to, the commission of a designated offense.</p>
          <p>(b) Property is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the owner was privy to the act or omission upon which the forfeiture is based, or the act or omission occurred with the owner's knowledge or consent.</p>
          <p>(c) Property encumbered by a bona fide security interest is subject to the interest of the secured party unless the party had knowledge of or consented to the act or omission upon which the forfeiture is based. A person claiming a security interest bears the burden of establishing that interest by clear and convincing evidence.</p>
          <p>(d) Notwithstanding paragraphs (b) and (c), property is not subject to forfeiture based solely on the owner's or secured party's knowledge of the act or omission upon which the forfeiture is based if the owner or secured party took reasonable steps to terminate use of the property by the offender.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5312.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Vehicle forfeiture for prostitution offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A motor vehicle is subject to forfeiture under this subdivision if it was used to commit or facilitate, or used during the commission of, a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a> or a violation of a local ordinance substantially similar to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>. A motor vehicle is subject to forfeiture under this subdivision only if the offense is established by proof of a criminal conviction for the offense. Except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, a forfeiture under this subdivision is governed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5312">609.5312</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5313">609.5313</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) When a motor vehicle subject to forfeiture under this subdivision is seized in advance of a judicial forfeiture order, a hearing before a judge or referee must be held within 96 hours of the seizure. Notice of the hearing must be given to the registered owner within 48 hours of the seizure. The prosecuting authority shall certify to the court, at or in advance of the hearing, that it has filed or intends to file charges against the alleged violator for violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a> or a local ordinance substantially similar to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.324">609.324</a>. After conducting the hearing, the court shall order that the motor vehicle be returned to the owner if:</p>
          <p>(1) the prosecuting authority has failed to make the certification required by paragraph (b);</p>
          <p>(2) the owner of the motor vehicle has demonstrated to the court's satisfaction that the owner has a defense to the forfeiture, including but not limited to the defenses contained in subdivision 2; or</p>
          <p>(3) the court determines that seizure of the vehicle creates or would create an undue hardship for members of the owner's family.</p>
          <p>(c) If the defendant is acquitted or prostitution charges against the defendant are dismissed, neither the owner nor the defendant is responsible for paying any costs associated with the seizure or storage of the vehicle.</p>
          <p>(d) A vehicle leased or rented under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.27#stat.168.27.4">168.27, subdivision 4</a>, for a period of 180 days or less is not subject to forfeiture under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(e) For purposes of this subdivision, seizure occurs either:</p>
          <p>(1) at the date at which personal service of process upon the registered owner is made; or</p>
          <p>(2) at the date when the registered owner has been notified by certified mail at the address listed in the Minnesota Department of Public Safety computerized motor vehicle registration records.</p>
          <p>(f) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not participate in paragraphs (a) to (e).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5312.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Vehicle forfeiture for fleeing peace officer.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A motor vehicle is subject to forfeiture under this subdivision if it was used to commit a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a> and endanger life or property. A motor vehicle is subject to forfeiture under this subdivision only if the offense is established by proof of a criminal conviction for the offense. Except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, a forfeiture under this subdivision is governed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5312">609.5312</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5313">609.5313</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315#stat.609.5315.6">609.5315, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) When a motor vehicle subject to forfeiture under this subdivision is seized in advance of a judicial forfeiture order, a hearing before a judge or referee must be held within 96 hours of the seizure. Notice of the hearing must be given to the registered owner within 48 hours of the seizure. The prosecuting authority shall certify to the court, at or in advance of the hearing, that it has filed or intends to file charges against the alleged violator for violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a>. After conducting the hearing, the court shall order that the motor vehicle be returned to the owner if:</p>
          <p>(1) the prosecuting authority has failed to make the certification required by this paragraph;</p>
          <p>(2) the owner of the motor vehicle has demonstrated to the court's satisfaction that the owner has a defense to the forfeiture, including but not limited to the defenses contained in subdivision 2; or</p>
          <p>(3) the court determines that seizure of the vehicle creates or would create an undue hardship for members of the owner's family.</p>
          <p>(c) If the defendant is acquitted or the charges against the defendant are dismissed, neither the owner nor the defendant is responsible for paying any costs associated with the seizure or storage of the vehicle.</p>
          <p>(d) A vehicle leased or rented under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.27#stat.168.27.4">168.27, subdivision 4</a>, for a period of 180 days or less is not subject to forfeiture under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(e) A motor vehicle that is an off-road recreational vehicle as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03#stat.169A.03.16">169A.03, subdivision 16</a>, or a motorboat as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169A.03#stat.169A.03.13">169A.03, subdivision 13</a>, is not subject to paragraph (b).</p>
          <p>(f) For purposes of this subdivision, seizure occurs either:</p>
          <p>(1) at the date at which personal service of process upon the registered owner is made; or</p>
          <p>(2) at the date when the registered owner has been notified by certified mail at the address listed in the Minnesota Department of Public Safety computerized motor vehicle registration records.</p>
          <p>(g) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not seize a motor vehicle for the purposes of forfeiture under paragraphs (a) to (f).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5312.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
