        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.12.0">1988 c 665 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.7.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 7</a>; art 4 s 29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/465/#laws.1.59.0">1994 c 465 art 1 s 59</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.21.0">1995 c 244 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/466/#laws.0.5.0">2000 c 466 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/478/#laws.2.7.0">2000 c 478 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.4.25.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 4 s 25</a>,26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.13.11.0">2005 c 136 art 13 s 11</a>-13; art 17 s 38; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/128/#laws.0.26.0">2012 c 128 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/80/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 80 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5313">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5313 FORFEITURE BY JUDICIAL ACTION; PROCEDURE.</h1>
        <p>(a) The forfeiture of property under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5311">609.5311</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5312">609.5312</a> is governed by this section. A separate complaint must be filed against the property stating the act, omission, or occurrence giving rise to the forfeiture and the date and place of the act or occurrence. Within 60 days from when the seizure occurs, the prosecuting authority shall notify the owner or possessor of the property of the action, if known or readily ascertainable. The action must be captioned in the name of the prosecuting authority or the prosecuting authority's designee as plaintiff and the property as defendant. Upon motion by the prosecuting authority, a court may extend the time period for sending notice for a period not to exceed 90 days for good cause shown.</p>
        <p>(b) If notice is not sent in accordance with paragraph (a), and no time extension is granted or the extension period has expired, the appropriate agency shall return the property to the person from whom the property was seized, if known. An agency's return of property due to lack of proper notice does not restrict the right of the agency to commence a forfeiture proceeding at a later time. The agency shall not be required to return contraband or other property that the person from whom the property was seized may not legally possess.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5313.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.13.0">1988 c 665 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/391/#laws.0.13.0">2010 c 391 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/128/#laws.0.26.0">2012 c 128 s 26</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5314">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5314 ADMINISTRATIVE FORFEITURE OF CERTAIN PROPERTY SEIZED IN CONNECTION WITH A CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES SEIZURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5314.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Property subject to administrative forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The following are subject to administrative forfeiture under this section:</p>
          <p>(1) all money totaling $1,500 or more, precious metals, and precious stones that there is probable cause to believe represent the proceeds of a controlled substance offense;</p>
          <p>(2) all money found in proximity to controlled substances when there is probable cause to believe that the money was exchanged for the purchase of a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(3) all conveyance devices containing controlled substances with a retail value of $100 or more if there is probable cause to believe that the conveyance device was used in the transportation or exchange of a controlled substance intended for distribution or sale; and</p>
          <p>(4) all firearms, ammunition, and firearm accessories found:</p>
          <p>(i) in a conveyance device used or intended for use to commit or facilitate the commission of a felony offense involving a controlled substance;</p>
          <p>(ii) on or in proximity to a person from whom a felony amount of controlled substance is seized; or</p>
          <p>(iii) on the premises where a controlled substance is seized and in proximity to the controlled substance, if possession or sale of the controlled substance would be a felony under chapter 152.</p>
          <p>(b) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not seize items listed in paragraph (a), clauses (3) and (4), for the purposes of forfeiture.</p>
          <p>(c) Money is the property of an appropriate agency and may be seized and recovered by the appropriate agency if:</p>
          <p>(1) the money is used by an appropriate agency, or furnished to a person operating on behalf of an appropriate agency, to purchase or attempt to purchase a controlled substance; and</p>
          <p>(2) the appropriate agency records the serial number or otherwise marks the money for identification.</p>
          <p>(d) As used in this section, "money" means United States currency and coin; the currency and coin of a foreign country; a bank check, cashier's check, or traveler's check; a prepaid credit card; cryptocurrency; or a money order.</p>
          <p>(e) As used in this section, "controlled substance" does not include cannabis flower as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01#stat.342.01.16">342.01, subdivision 16</a>, cannabis products as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/subdivision%2020">subdivision 20</a>, hemp-derived consumer products as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01">342.01, subdivision </a><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/37">37</a>, or lower-potency hemp edibles as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/342.01#stat.342.01.50">342.01, subdivision 50</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5314.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Innocent owner.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any person, other than the defendant driver, alleged to have used a vehicle in the transportation or exchange of a controlled substance intended for distribution or sale, claiming an ownership interest in a vehicle that has been seized or restrained under this section may assert that right by notifying the prosecuting authority in writing and within 60 days of the service of the notice of seizure.</p>
          <p>(b) Upon receipt of notice pursuant to paragraph (a), the prosecuting authority may release the vehicle to the asserting person. If the prosecuting authority proceeds with the forfeiture, the prosecuting authority must, within 30 days, file a separate complaint in the name of the jurisdiction pursuing the forfeiture against the vehicle, describing the vehicle, specifying that the vehicle was used in the transportation or exchange of a controlled substance intended for distribution or sale, and specifying the time and place of the vehicle's unlawful use. The complaint may be filed in district court or conciliation court and the filing fee is waived.</p>
          <p>(c) A complaint filed by the prosecuting authority must be served on the asserting person and on any other registered owners. Service may be made by certified mail at the address listed in the Department of Public Safety's computerized motor vehicle registration records or by any means permitted by court rules.</p>
          <p>(d) The hearing on the complaint shall, to the extent practicable, be held within 30 days of the filing of the petition. The court may consolidate the hearing on the complaint with a hearing on any other complaint involving a claim of an ownership interest in the same vehicle.</p>
          <p>(e) At a hearing held pursuant to this subdivision, the state must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that:</p>
          <p>(1) the seizure was incident to a lawful arrest or a lawful search; and</p>
          <p>(2) the vehicle was used in the transportation or exchange of a controlled substance intended for distribution or sale.</p>
          <p>(f) At a hearing held pursuant to this subdivision, the asserting person must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the asserting person:</p>
          <p>(1) has an actual ownership interest in the vehicle; and</p>
          <p>(2) did not have actual or constructive knowledge that the vehicle would be used or operated in any manner contrary to law or that the asserting person took reasonable steps to prevent use of the vehicle by the alleged offender.</p>
          <p>(g) If the court determines that the state met both burdens under paragraph (e) and the asserting person failed to meet any burden under paragraph (f), the court shall order that the vehicle remains subject to forfeiture under this section.</p>
          <p>(h) The court shall order that the vehicle is not subject to forfeiture under this section and shall order the vehicle returned to the asserting person if it determines that:</p>
          <p>(1) the state failed to meet any burden under paragraph (e);</p>
          <p>(2) the asserting person proved both elements under paragraph (f); or</p>
          <p>(3) clauses (1) and (2) apply.</p>
          <p>(i) If the court determines that the asserting person is an innocent owner and orders the vehicle returned to the innocent owner, an entity in possession of the vehicle is not required to release the vehicle until the innocent owner pays:</p>
          <p>(1) the reasonable costs of the towing, seizure, and storage of the vehicle incurred before the innocent owner provided the notice required under paragraph (a); and</p>
          <p>(2) any reasonable costs of storage of the vehicle incurred more than two weeks after an order issued under paragraph (h).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5314.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Administrative forfeiture procedure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Forfeiture of property described in subdivision 1 that does not exceed $50,000 in value is governed by this subdivision. Within 60 days from when seizure occurs, all persons known to have an ownership, possessory, or security interest in seized property must be notified of the seizure and the intent to forfeit the property. In the case of a motor vehicle required to be registered under chapter 168, notice mailed by certified mail to the address shown in Department of Public Safety records is deemed sufficient notice to the registered owner. The notification to a person known to have a security interest in seized property required under this paragraph applies only to motor vehicles required to be registered under chapter 168 and only if the security interest is listed on the vehicle's title. Upon motion by the appropriate agency or the prosecuting authority, a court may extend the time period for sending notice for a period not to exceed 90 days for good cause shown.</p>
          <p>(b) Notice may otherwise be given in the manner provided by law for service of a summons in a civil action. The notice must be in writing and contain:</p>
          <p>(1) a description of the property seized;</p>
          <p>(2) the date of seizure; and</p>
          <p>(3) notice of the right to obtain judicial review of the forfeiture and of the procedure for obtaining that judicial review, printed in English. This requirement does not preclude the appropriate agency from printing the notice in other languages in addition to English.</p>
          <p>Substantially the following language must appear conspicuously in the notice:</p>
          <p>"WARNING: If you were the person arrested when the property was seized, you will automatically lose the above-described property and the right to be heard in court if you do not file a lawsuit and serve the prosecuting authority within 60 days. You may file your lawsuit in conciliation court if the property is worth $15,000 or less; otherwise, you must file in district court. You do not have to pay a filing fee for your lawsuit.</p>
          <p>WARNING: If you have an ownership interest in the above-described property and were not the person arrested when the property was seized, you will automatically lose the above-described property and the right to be heard in court if you do not notify the prosecuting authority of your interest in writing within 60 days."</p>
          <p>(c) If notice is not sent in accordance with paragraph (a), and no time extension is granted or the extension period has expired, the appropriate agency shall return the property to the person from whom the property was seized, if known. An agency's return of property due to lack of proper notice does not restrict the agency's authority to commence a forfeiture proceeding at a later time. The agency shall not be required to return contraband or other property that the person from whom the property was seized may not legally possess.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5314.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Judicial determination.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Within 60 days following service of a notice of seizure and forfeiture under this section, a claimant may file a demand for a judicial determination of the forfeiture. The demand must be in the form of a civil complaint and must be filed with the court administrator in the county in which the seizure occurred, together with proof of service of a copy of the complaint on the prosecuting authority for that county. The claimant may serve the complaint on the prosecuting authority by certified mail or any means permitted by court rules. If the value of the seized property is $15,000 or less, the claimant may file an action in conciliation court for recovery of the seized property. A copy of the conciliation court statement of claim may be served personally or as permitted by the Rules of Conciliation Court Procedure on the prosecuting authority having jurisdiction over the forfeiture within 60 days following service of the notice of seizure and forfeiture under this subdivision. The claimant does not have to pay the court filing fee. No responsive pleading is required of the prosecuting authority and no court fees may be charged for the prosecuting authority's appearance in the matter. The district court administrator shall schedule the hearing as soon as practicable after, and in any event no later than 90 days following, the conclusion of the criminal prosecution. The proceedings are governed by the Rules of Civil Procedure and, where applicable, by the Rules of Conciliation Court Procedure.</p>
          <p>(b) The complaint must be captioned in the name of the claimant as plaintiff and the seized property as defendant, and must state with specificity the grounds on which the claimant alleges the property was improperly seized and the plaintiff's interest in the property seized. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, an action for the return of property seized under this section may not be maintained by or on behalf of any person who has been served with a notice of seizure and forfeiture unless the person has complied with this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(c) If the claimant makes a timely demand for judicial determination under this subdivision, the appropriate agency must conduct the forfeiture under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a>, subdivision 6a. The limitations and defenses set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5311">609.5311</a>, subdivision 3, apply to the judicial determination.</p>
          <p>(d) If a demand for judicial determination of an administrative forfeiture is filed under this subdivision and the court orders the return of the seized property, the court may order sanctions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/549.211">549.211</a>. If the court orders payment of these costs, they must be paid from forfeited money or proceeds from the sale of forfeited property from the appropriate law enforcement and prosecuting agencies in the same proportion as they would be distributed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315">609.5315</a>, subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5314.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.14.0">1988 c 665 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.3.31.0">1989 c 290 art 3 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/323/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 323 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.8.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/213/#laws.2.5.0">1997 c 213 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/225/#laws.0.3.0">1999 c 225 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.13.14.0">2005 c 136 art 13 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/391/#laws.0.14.0">2010 c 391 s 14</a>,15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/76/#laws.1.67.0">2011 c 76 art 1 s 67</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/128/#laws.0.18.0">2012 c 128 s 18</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/201/#laws.0.2.0">2014 c 201 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.5.14.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 5 s 14</a>-17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.19.40.0">2023 c 52 art 19 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.46.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 46</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5315">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5315 DISPOSITION OF FORFEITED PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Disposition.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Subject to paragraph (b), if the court finds under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5313">609.5313</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5314">609.5314</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> that the property is subject to forfeiture, it shall order the appropriate agency to do one of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) unless a different disposition is provided under clause (3) or (4), either destroy firearms, ammunition, and firearm accessories that the agency decides not to use for law enforcement purposes under clause (8), or sell them to federally licensed firearms dealers, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.7161">624.7161</a>, subdivision 1, and distribute the proceeds under subdivision 5 or 5b;</p>
          <p>(2) sell property that is not required to be destroyed by law and is not harmful to the public and distribute the proceeds under subdivision 5 or 5b;</p>
          <p>(3) sell antique firearms, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.712">624.712</a>, subdivision 3, to the public and distribute the proceeds under subdivision 5 or 5b;</p>
          <p>(4) destroy or use for law enforcement purposes semiautomatic military-style assault weapons, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.712">624.712</a>, subdivision 7;</p>
          <p>(5) take custody of the property and remove it for disposition in accordance with law;</p>
          <p>(6) forward the property to the federal drug enforcement administration;</p>
          <p>(7) disburse money as provided under subdivision 5, 5b, or 5c; or</p>
          <p>(8) keep property other than money for official use by the agency and the prosecuting agency.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), the Hennepin or Ramsey County sheriff may not sell firearms, ammunition, or firearms accessories if the policy is disapproved by the applicable county board.</p>
          <p>(c) If property is sold under paragraph (a), the appropriate agency shall not sell property to: (1) an officer or employee of the agency that seized the property or to a person related to the officer or employee by blood or marriage; or (2) the prosecuting authority or any individual working in the same office or a person related to the authority or individual by blood or marriage.</p>
          <p>(d) Sales of forfeited property under this section must be conducted in a commercially reasonable manner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Disposition of administratively forfeited property.</span></h2>
          <p>If property is forfeited administratively under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5314">609.5314</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a> and no demand for judicial determination is made, the appropriate agency shall provide the prosecuting authority with a copy of the forfeiture or evidence receipt, the notice of seizure and intent to forfeit, a statement of probable cause for forfeiture of the property, and a description of the property and its estimated value. Upon review and certification by the prosecuting authority that (1) the appropriate agency provided a receipt in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a>, subdivision 4, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.16">626.16</a>; (2) the appropriate agency served notice in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5314">609.5314</a>, subdivision 2, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5318">609.5318</a>, subdivision 2; and (3) probable cause for forfeiture exists based on the officer's statement, the appropriate agency may dispose of the property in any of the ways listed in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Use by law enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Property kept under this section may be used only in the performance of official duties of the appropriate agency or prosecuting agency and may not be used for any other purpose. If an appropriate agency keeps a forfeited motor vehicle for official use, it shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that the motor vehicle is available for use and adaptation by the agency's officers who participate in the drug abuse resistance education program.</p>
          <p>(b) Proceeds from the sale of property kept under this subdivision must be disbursed as provided in subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Distribution of proceeds of the offense.</span></h2>
          <p>Property that consists of proceeds derived from or traced to the commission of a designated offense or a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.66#stat.609.66.1e">609.66, subdivision 1e</a>, must be applied first to payment of seizure, storage, forfeiture, and sale expenses, and to satisfy valid liens against the property; and second, to any court-ordered restitution before being disbursed as provided under subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Distribution of money.</span></h2>
          <p>The money or proceeds from the sale of forfeited property, after payment of seizure, storage, forfeiture, and sale expenses, and satisfaction of valid liens against the property, must be distributed as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) 70 percent of the money or proceeds must be forwarded to the appropriate agency for deposit as a supplement to the agency's operating fund or similar fund for use in law enforcement, training, education, crime prevention, equipment, or capital expenses;</p>
          <p>(2) 20 percent of the money or proceeds must be forwarded to the prosecuting authority that handled the forfeiture for deposit as a supplement to its operating fund or similar fund for prosecutorial purposes, training, education, crime prevention, equipment, or capital expenses; and</p>
          <p>(3) the remaining ten percent of the money or proceeds must be forwarded within 60 days after resolution of the forfeiture to the state treasury and credited to the general fund. Any local police relief association organized under chapter 423 which received or was entitled to receive the proceeds of any sale made under this section before the effective date of Laws 1988, chapter 665, sections 1 to 17, shall continue to receive and retain the proceeds of these sales.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Disposition of certain forfeited proceeds; prostitution.</span></h2>
          <p>The proceeds from the sale of motor vehicles forfeited under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5312#stat.609.5312.3">609.5312, subdivision 3</a>, after payment of seizure, storage, forfeiture, and sale expenses, and satisfaction of valid liens against the vehicle, shall be distributed as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) 40 percent of the proceeds must be forwarded to the appropriate agency for deposit as a supplement to the agency's operating fund or similar fund for use in law enforcement;</p>
          <p>(2) 20 percent of the proceeds must be forwarded to the prosecuting authority that handled the forfeiture for deposit as a supplement to its operating fund or similar fund for prosecutorial purposes; and</p>
          <p>(3) the remaining 40 percent of the proceeds must be forwarded to the city treasury for distribution to neighborhood crime prevention programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.5b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Disposition of certain forfeited proceeds; trafficking of persons.</span></h2>
          <p> Except as provided in subdivision 5c, for forfeitures resulting from violations of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.282">609.282</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.283">609.283</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>, the money or proceeds from the sale of forfeited property, after payment of seizure, storage, forfeiture, and sale expenses, and satisfaction of valid liens against the property, must be distributed as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) 40 percent of the proceeds must be forwarded to the appropriate agency for deposit as a supplement to the agency's operating fund or similar fund for use in law enforcement;</p>
          <p>(2) 20 percent of the proceeds must be forwarded to the prosecuting authority that handled the forfeiture for deposit as a supplement to its operating fund or similar fund for prosecutorial purposes; and</p>
          <p>(3) the remaining 40 percent of the proceeds must be forwarded to the commissioner of health and are appropriated to the commissioner for distribution to crime victims services organizations that provide services to victims of trafficking offenses.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.5c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5c.<span class="headnote">Disposition of money; prostitution.</span></h2>
          <p>Money forfeited under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5312#stat.609.5312.1">609.5312, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b), must be distributed as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) 40 percent must be forwarded to the appropriate agency for deposit as a supplement to the agency's operating fund or similar fund for use in law enforcement;</p>
          <p>(2) 20 percent must be forwarded to the prosecuting authority that handled the forfeiture for deposit as a supplement to its operating fund or similar fund for prosecutorial purposes; and</p>
          <p>(3) the remaining 40 percent must be forwarded to the commissioner of health to be deposited in the safe harbor for youth account in the special revenue fund and is appropriated to the commissioner for distribution to crime victims services organizations that provide services to sexually exploited youth, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.31">260C.007, subdivision 31</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reporting requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For each forfeiture occurring in the state regardless of the authority for it and including forfeitures pursued under federal law, the appropriate agency and the prosecuting authority shall provide a written record of the forfeiture incident to the state auditor. The record shall include:</p>
          <p>(1) the amount forfeited;</p>
          <p>(2) the statutory authority for the forfeiture;</p>
          <p>(3) the date of the forfeiture;</p>
          <p>(4) a brief description of the circumstances involved;</p>
          <p>(5) whether the forfeiture was contested;</p>
          <p>(6) whether the defendant was convicted pursuant to a plea agreement or a trial;</p>
          <p>(7) whether there was a forfeiture settlement agreement;</p>
          <p>(8) whether the property was sold, destroyed, or retained by an appropriate agency;</p>
          <p>(9) the gross revenue from the disposition of the forfeited property;</p>
          <p>(10) an estimate of the total costs to the agency to store the property in an impound lot, evidence room, or other location; pay for the time and expenses of an appropriate agency and prosecuting authority to litigate forfeiture cases; and sell or dispose of the forfeited property;</p>
          <p>(11) the net revenue, determined by subtracting the costs identified under clause (10) from the gross revenue identified in clause (9), the appropriate agency received from the disposition of forfeited property;</p>
          <p>(12) if any property was retained by an appropriate agency, the purpose for which it is used;</p>
          <p>(13) for controlled substance and driving while impaired forfeitures, whether the forfeiture was initiated as an administrative or a judicial forfeiture;</p>
          <p>(14) the number of firearms forfeited and the make, model, and serial number of each firearm forfeited; and</p>
          <p>(15) how the property was or is to be disposed of.</p>
          <p>(b) An appropriate agency or the prosecuting authority shall report to the state auditor all instances in which property seized for forfeiture is returned to its owner either because forfeiture is not pursued or for any other reason.</p>
          <p>(c) Each appropriate agency and prosecuting authority shall provide a written record regarding the proceeds of forfeited property, including proceeds received through forfeiture under state and federal law. The record shall include:</p>
          <p>(1) the total amount of money or proceeds from the sale of forfeited property obtained or received by an appropriate agency or prosecuting authority in the previous reporting period;</p>
          <p>(2) the manner in which each appropriate agency and prosecuting authority expended money or proceeds from the sale of forfeited property in the previous reporting period, including the total amount expended in the following categories:</p>
          <p>(i) drug abuse, crime, and gang prevention programs;</p>
          <p>(ii) victim reparations;</p>
          <p>(iii) gifts or grants to crime victim service organizations that provide services to sexually exploited youth;</p>
          <p>(iv) gifts or grants to crime victim service organizations that provide services to victims of trafficking offenses;</p>
          <p>(v) investigation costs, including but not limited to witness protection, informant fees, and controlled buys;</p>
          <p>(vi) court costs and attorney fees;</p>
          <p>(vii) salaries, overtime, and benefits, as permitted by law;</p>
          <p>(viii) professional outside services, including but not limited to auditing, court reporting, expert witness fees, outside attorney fees, and membership fees paid to trade associations;</p>
          <p>(ix) travel, meals, and conferences;</p>
          <p>(x) training and continuing education;</p>
          <p>(xi) other operating expenses, including but not limited to office supplies, postage, and printing;</p>
          <p>(xii) capital expenditures, including but not limited to vehicles, firearms, equipment, computers, and furniture;</p>
          <p>(xiii) gifts or grants to nonprofit or other programs, indicating the recipient of the gift or grant; and</p>
          <p>(xiv) any other expenditure, indicating the type of expenditure and, if applicable, the recipient of any gift or grant;</p>
          <p>(3) the total value of seized and forfeited property held by an appropriate agency and not sold or otherwise disposed of; and</p>
          <p>(4) a statement from the end of each year showing the balance of any designated forfeiture accounts maintained by an appropriate agency or prosecuting authority.</p>
          <p>(d) Reports under paragraphs (a) and (b) shall be made on a quarterly basis in a manner prescribed by the state auditor and reports under paragraph (c) shall be made on an annual basis in a manner prescribed by the state auditor. The state auditor shall report annually to the legislature on the nature and extent of forfeitures, including the information provided by each appropriate agency or prosecuting authority under paragraphs (a) to (c). Summary data on seizures, forfeitures, and expenditures of forfeiture proceeds shall be disaggregated by each appropriate agency and prosecuting authority. The report shall be made public on the state auditor's website.</p>
          <p>(e) For forfeitures resulting from the activities of multijurisdictional law enforcement entities, the entity on its own behalf shall report the information required in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(f) The prosecuting authority is not required to report information required by paragraph (a) or (b) unless the prosecuting authority has been notified by the state auditor that the appropriate agency has not reported it.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5315.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Firearms.</span></h2>
          <p>The agency shall make best efforts for a period of 90 days after the seizure of an abandoned or stolen firearm to protect the firearm from harm and return it to the lawful owner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5315.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.15.0">1988 c 665 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.3.32.0">1989 c 290 art 3 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/335/#laws.4.100.0">1989 c 335 art 4 s 100</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/499/#laws.0.9.0">1990 c 499 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.4.49.0">1992 c 513 art 4 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.10.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 10</a>-12; art 4 s 30; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.3.12.0">1994 c 636 art 3 s 12</a>-15; art 4 s 29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/148/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 148 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.39.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 39</a>,40; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/391/#laws.0.16.0">2010 c 391 s 16</a>-18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/128/#laws.0.20.0">2012 c 128 s 20</a>-23,26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/80/#laws.0.2.0">2013 c 80 s 2</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.137.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 137</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/144/#laws.0.3.0">2018 c 144 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.5.18.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 5 s 18</a>-20</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5316">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5316 SUMMARY FORFEITURES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5316.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Contraband.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, if the property is contraband, the property must be summarily forfeited and either destroyed or used by the appropriate agency for law enforcement purposes. Upon summary forfeiture, weapons used must be destroyed by the appropriate agency unless the agency decides to use the weapons for law enforcement purposes or sell the weapons in a commercially reasonable manner to federally licensed firearms dealers, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.7161">624.7161</a>, subdivision 1. If a weapon is sold under this subdivision, the proceeds must be distributed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315#stat.609.5315.5">609.5315, subdivision 5</a> or 5b.</p>
          <p>(b) If the contraband property is a catalytic converter, the appropriate agency shall sell it to a scrap metal dealer or other business that may lawfully possess it under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325E.21">325E.21</a>. The agency shall make reasonable efforts to determine whether the person from whom it was stolen can be identified. If able to do this, the agency shall forward the proceeds to that person. If unable to do this, the agency may keep 70 percent of the proceeds from the sale and forward the remaining 30 percent to the prosecutorial office that prosecuted the case resulting in the forfeiture. If the catalytic converter is not marked as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325E.21">325E.21</a>, the agency shall mark it in a permanent manner, including but not limited to an engraving or permanent ink, indicating that the converter is recovered contraband.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5316.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Controlled substances.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Controlled substances listed in Schedule I that are possessed, transferred, sold, or offered for sale in violation of chapter 152 or 342, are contraband and must be seized and summarily forfeited. Controlled substances listed in Schedule I that are seized or come into the possession of peace officers, the owners of which are unknown, are contraband and must be summarily forfeited.</p>
          <p>(b) Species of plants from which controlled substances in Schedules I and II may be derived that have been planted or cultivated in violation of chapter 152 or of which the owners or cultivators are unknown, or that are wild growths, may be seized and summarily forfeited to the state. The appropriate agency or its authorized agent may seize the plants if the person in occupancy or in control of land or premises where the plants are growing or being stored fails to produce an appropriate registration or proof that the person is the holder of appropriate registration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5316.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Weapons, telephone cloning paraphernalia, automated sales suppression devices, catalytic converters, and bullet-resistant vests.</span></h2>
          <p>Weapons used are contraband and must be summarily forfeited to the appropriate agency upon conviction of the weapon's owner or possessor for a controlled substance crime; for any offense of this chapter or chapter 624, or for a violation of an order for protection under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/518B.01#stat.518B.01.14">518B.01, subdivision 14</a>. Bullet-resistant vests, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.486">609.486</a>, worn or possessed during the commission or attempted commission of a crime are contraband and must be summarily forfeited to the appropriate agency upon conviction of the owner or possessor for a controlled substance crime or for any offense of this chapter. Telephone cloning paraphernalia used in a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.894">609.894</a>, and automated sales suppression devices, phantom-ware, and other devices containing an automated sales suppression or phantom-ware device or software used in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/289A.63#stat.289A.63.12">289A.63, subdivision 12</a>, are contraband and must be summarily forfeited to the appropriate agency upon a conviction. A catalytic converter possessed in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325E.21">325E.21</a> is contraband and must be summarily forfeited to the appropriate agency upon a conviction.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5316.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/665/#laws.0.16.0">1988 c 665 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/439/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 439 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.3.16.0">1994 c 636 art 3 s 16</a>,17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/331/#laws.0.1.0">1996 c 331 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.4.9.0">1996 c 408 art 4 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/127/#laws.0.1.0">2012 c 127 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/201/#laws.0.3.0">2014 c 201 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/1/#laws.12.4.0">1Sp2017 c 1 art 12 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/15/#laws.0.13.0">2023 c 15 s 13</a>,14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.4.47.0">2023 c 63 art 4 s 47</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.5317"><b>609.5317</b> MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.5.22.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 5 s 22</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5318">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5318 FORFEITURE OF VEHICLES USED IN DRIVE-BY SHOOTINGS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5318.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Motor vehicles subject to forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the prosecuting authority establishes by clear and convincing evidence that a motor vehicle was used in a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.66#stat.609.66.1e">609.66, subdivision 1e</a>, the vehicle is subject to forfeiture under this section upon a conviction for the same offense.</p>
          <p>(b) The Department of Corrections Fugitive Apprehension Unit shall not seize a motor vehicle for the purposes of forfeiture under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5318.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The registered owner of the vehicle must be notified of the seizure and intent to forfeit the vehicle within seven days after the seizure. Notice by certified mail to the address shown in Department of Public Safety records is deemed to be sufficient notice to the registered owner.</p>
          <p>(b) The notice must be in writing and:</p>
          <p>(1) contain a description of the property seized;</p>
          <p>(2) contain the date of seizure; and</p>
          <p>(3) be printed in English. This requirement does not preclude the appropriate agency from printing the notice in other languages in addition to English.</p>
          <p>(c) Substantially, the following language must appear conspicuously in the notice:</p>
          <p>"WARNING: You will automatically lose the above-described property and the right to be heard in court if you do not file a lawsuit and serve the prosecuting authority within 60 days. You may file your lawsuit in conciliation court if the property is worth $15,000 or less; otherwise, you must file in district court. You may not have to pay a filing fee for your lawsuit if you are unable to afford the fee. You do not have to pay a conciliation court fee if your property is worth less than $500."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5318.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Within 60 days following service of a notice of seizure and forfeiture, a claimant may demand a judicial determination of the forfeiture. If a related criminal proceeding is pending, the 60-day period begins to run at the conclusion of those proceedings.</p>
          <p>(b) The demand must be in the form of a civil complaint as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5314#stat.609.5314.3">609.5314, subdivision 3</a>, except as otherwise provided in this section.</p>
          <p>(c) If the claimant makes a timely demand for judicial determination under this subdivision, the appropriate agency must conduct the forfeiture under subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5318.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Procedure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a judicial determination of the forfeiture is requested, a separate complaint must be filed against the vehicle, stating the specific act giving rise to the forfeiture and the date, time, and place of the act. The action must be captioned in the name of the prosecuting authority or the prosecuting authority's designee as plaintiff and the property as defendant.</p>
          <p>(b) If a demand for judicial determination of an administrative forfeiture is filed and the court orders the return of the seized property, the court shall order that filing fees be reimbursed to the person who filed the demand. In addition, the court may order the payment of reasonable costs, expenses, attorney fees, and towing and storage fees. If the court orders payment of these costs, they must be paid from forfeited money or proceeds from the sale of forfeited property from the appropriate law enforcement and prosecuting agencies in the same proportion as they would be distributed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315#stat.609.5315.5">609.5315, subdivision 5</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5318.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Limitations.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A vehicle used by a person as a common carrier in the transaction of business as a common carrier is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the owner is a consenting party to, or is privy to, the commission of the act giving rise to the forfeiture.</p>
          <p>(b) A vehicle is subject to forfeiture under this section only if the registered owner was privy to the act upon which the forfeiture is based, the act occurred with the owner's knowledge or consent, or the act occurred due to the owner's gross negligence in allowing another to use the vehicle.</p>
          <p>(c) A vehicle encumbered by a bona fide security interest is subject to the interest of the secured party unless the party had knowledge of or consented to the act upon which the forfeiture is based. A person claiming a security interest bears the burden of establishing that interest by clear and convincing evidence.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5318.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.13.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/366/#laws.0.9.0">1993 c 366 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.13.16.0">2005 c 136 art 13 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/128/#laws.0.24.0">2012 c 128 s 24-26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/201/#laws.0.4.0">2014 c 201 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5319">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5319 FINANCIAL INSTITUTION SECURED INTEREST.</h1>
        <p>Property that is subject to a bona fide security interest, based upon a loan or other financing arranged by a bank, credit union, or any other financial institution, is subject to the interest of the bank, credit union, or other financial institution in any forfeiture proceeding that is based upon a violation of any provision of this chapter or the commission of any other criminal act. The security interest must be established by clear and convincing evidence.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5319.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.11.7.0">1996 c 408 art 11 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.532">
        <h1 class="shn">609.532 ATTACHMENT OF DEPOSITED FUNDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Attachment.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon application by the prosecuting authority, a court may issue an attachment order directing a financial institution to freeze some or all of the funds or assets deposited with or held by the financial institution by or on behalf of an account holder charged with the commission of a felony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>The application of the prosecuting authority required by this section must contain:</p>
          <p>(1) a copy of a criminal complaint issued by a court of competent jurisdiction that alleges the commission of a felony by the account holder;</p>
          <p>(2) a statement of the actual financial loss caused by the account holder in the commission of the alleged felony, if not already stated in the complaint; and</p>
          <p>(3) identification of the account holder's name and financial institution account number.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Issuance of court order.</span></h2>
          <p>If the court finds that (1) there is probable cause that the account holder was involved in the commission of a felony; (2) the accounts of the account holder are specifically identified; (3) there was a loss of $10,000 or more as a result of the commission of the alleged felony; and (4) it is necessary to freeze the account holder's funds or assets to ensure eventual restitution to victims of the alleged offense, the court may order the financial institution to freeze all or part of the account holder's deposited funds or assets so that the funds or assets may not be withdrawn or disposed of until further order of the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Duty of financial institutions.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon receipt of the order authorized by this section, a financial institution must not permit any funds or assets that were frozen by the order to be withdrawn or disposed of until further order of the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Release of funds.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The account holder may, upon notice and motion, have a hearing to contest the freezing of funds or assets and to seek the release of all or part of them.</p>
          <p>(b) The account holder is entitled to an order releasing the freeze by showing:</p>
          <p>(1) that the account holder has posted a bond or other adequate surety, guaranteeing that, upon conviction, adequate funds or assets will be available to pay complete restitution to victims of the alleged offense;</p>
          <p>(2) that there is no probable cause to believe that the account holder was involved in the alleged offense;</p>
          <p>(3) that the amount of funds or assets frozen is more than is necessary to pay complete restitution to all victims of the alleged offense;</p>
          <p>(4) that a joint account holder who is not involved in the alleged criminal activity has deposited all or part of the funds or assets; or</p>
          <p>(5) that the funds or assets should be returned in the interests of justice.</p>
          <p>(c) It is not grounds for the release of funds or assets that the particular accounts frozen do not contain funds or assets that were proceeds from or used in the commission of the alleged offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Disposition of funds.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the account holder is convicted of a felony or a lesser offense, the funds or assets may be used to pay complete restitution to victims of the offense. The court may order the financial institution to remit all or part of the frozen funds or assets to the court.</p>
          <p>(b) If the account holder is acquitted or the charges are dismissed, the court must issue an order releasing the freeze on the funds or assets.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Time limit.</span></h2>
          <p>The freeze permitted by this section expires 24 months after the date of the court's initial attachment order unless the time limit is extended by the court in writing upon a showing of good cause by the prosecution.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.532.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>Within ten days after a court issues an attachment order under this section, the prosecutor shall send a copy of the order to the account holder's last known address or to the account holder's attorney, if known.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.532.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/217/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 217 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.535">
        <h1 class="shn">609.535 ISSUANCE OF DISHONORED CHECKS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(a) "Check" means a check, draft, order of withdrawal, or similar negotiable or nonnegotiable instrument.</p>
          <p>(b) "Credit" means an arrangement or understanding with the drawee for the payment of a check.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever issues a check which, at the time of issuance, the issuer intends shall not be paid, is guilty of issuing a dishonored check and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2a. In addition, restitution may be ordered by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who is convicted of issuing a dishonored check under subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the value of the dishonored check, or checks aggregated under paragraph (b), is more than $500;</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the value of the dishonored check, or checks aggregated under paragraph (b), is more than $250 but not more than $500; or</p>
          <p>(3) to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both, if the value of the dishonored check, or checks aggregated under paragraph (b), is not more than $250.</p>
          <p>(b) In a prosecution under this subdivision, the value of dishonored checks issued by the defendant in violation of this subdivision within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying this section. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the dishonored checks was issued for all of the offenses aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Proof of intent.</span></h2>
          <p>Any of the following is evidence sufficient to sustain a finding that the person at the time the person issued the check intended it should not be paid:</p>
          <p>(1) proof that, at the time of issuance, the issuer did not have an account with the drawee;</p>
          <p>(2) proof that, at the time of issuance, the issuer did not have sufficient funds or credit with the drawee and that the issuer failed to pay the check within five business days after mailing of notice of nonpayment or dishonor as provided in this subdivision; or</p>
          <p>(3) proof that, when presentment was made within a reasonable time, the issuer did not have sufficient funds or credit with the drawee and that the issuer failed to pay the check within five business days after mailing of notice of nonpayment or dishonor as provided in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>Notice of nonpayment or dishonor that includes a citation to and a description of the penalties in this section shall be sent by the payee or holder of the check to the maker or drawer by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by regular mail, supported by an affidavit of service by mailing, to the address printed on the check. Refusal by the maker or drawer of the check to accept certified mail notice or failure to claim certified or regular mail notice is not a defense that notice was not received.</p>
          <p>The notice may state that unless the check is paid in full within five business days after mailing of the notice of nonpayment or dishonor, the payee or holder of the check will or may refer the matter to proper authorities for prosecution under this section.</p>
          <p>An affidavit of service by mailing shall be retained by the payee or holder of the check.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Proof of lack of funds or credit.</span></h2>
          <p>If the check has been protested, the notice of protest is admissible as proof of presentation, nonpayment, and protest, and is evidence sufficient to sustain a finding that there was a lack of funds or credit with the drawee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to a postdated check or to a check given for a past consideration, except a payroll check or a check issued to a fund for employee benefits.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Release of account information to law enforcement authorities.</span></h2>
          <p>A drawee shall release the information specified below to any state, county, or local law enforcement or prosecuting authority which certifies in writing that it is investigating or prosecuting a complaint against the drawer under this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (3), item (i), and that 15 days have elapsed since the mailing of the notice of dishonor required by subdivisions 3 and 8. This subdivision applies to the following information relating to the drawer's account:</p>
          <p>(1) documents relating to the opening of the account by the drawer and to the closing of the account;</p>
          <p>(2) notices regarding nonsufficient funds, overdrafts, and the dishonor of any check drawn on the account within a period of six months of the date of request;</p>
          <p>(3) periodic statements mailed to the drawer by the drawee for the periods immediately prior to, during, and subsequent to the issuance of any check which is the subject of the investigation or prosecution; or</p>
          <p>(4) the last known home and business addresses and telephone numbers of the drawer.</p>
          <p>The drawee shall release all of the information described in clauses (1) to (4) that it possesses within ten days after receipt of a request conforming to all of the provisions of this subdivision. The drawee may not impose a fee for furnishing this information to law enforcement or prosecuting authorities.</p>
          <p>A drawee is not liable in a criminal or civil proceeding for releasing information in accordance with this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Release of account information to payee or holder.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A drawee shall release the information specified in paragraph (b), clauses (1) to (3) to the payee or holder of a check that has been dishonored who makes a written request for this information and states in writing that the check has been dishonored and that 30 days have elapsed since the mailing of the notice described in subdivision 8 and who accompanies this request with a copy of the dishonored check and a copy of the notice of dishonor.</p>
          <p>The requesting payee or holder shall notify the drawee immediately to cancel this request if payment is made before the drawee has released this information.</p>
          <p>(b) This subdivision applies to the following information relating to the drawer's account:</p>
          <p>(1) whether at the time the check was issued or presented for payment the drawer had sufficient funds or credit with the drawee, and whether at that time the account was open, closed, or restricted for any reason and the date it was closed or restricted;</p>
          <p>(2) the last known home address and telephone number of the drawer. The drawee may not release the address or telephone number of the place of employment of the drawer unless the drawer is a business entity or the place of employment is the home; and</p>
          <p>(3) a statement as to whether the aggregated value of dishonored checks attributable to the drawer within six months before or after the date of the dishonored check exceeds $250; for purposes of this clause, a check is not dishonored if payment was not made pursuant to a stop payment order.</p>
          <p>The drawee shall release all of the information described in clauses (1) to (3) that it possesses within ten days after receipt of a request conforming to all of the provisions of this subdivision. The drawee may require the person requesting the information to pay the reasonable costs, not to exceed 15 cents per page, of reproducing and mailing the requested information.</p>
          <p>(c) A drawee is not liable in a criminal or civil proceeding for releasing information in accordance with this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.535.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>The provisions of subdivisions 6 and 7 are not applicable unless the notice to the maker or drawer required by subdivision 3 states that if the check is not paid in full within five business days after mailing of the notice, the drawee will be authorized to release information relating to the account to the payee or holder of the check and may also release this information to law enforcement or prosecuting authorities.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.535.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.535; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/466/#laws.0.1.0">1967 c 466 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.56.0">1971 c 23 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/106/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 106 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/202/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 202 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/247/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 247 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/225/#laws.0.10.0">1983 c 225 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/436/#laws.0.34.0">1984 c 436 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/140/#laws.0.3.0">1985 c 140 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/527/#laws.0.2.0">1988 c 527 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/256/#laws.0.11.0">1991 c 256 s 11</a>-13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/569/#laws.0.26.0">1992 c 569 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/218/#laws.0.3.0">1999 c 218 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.93.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 93</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.54">
        <h1 class="shn">609.54 EMBEZZLEMENT OF PUBLIC FUNDS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does an act which constitutes embezzlement under the provisions of Minnesota Constitution, article XI, section 13 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) if the value of the funds so embezzled is $2,500, or less, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; or</p>
        <p>(2) if such value is more than $2,500, to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.54.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.54; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/2/#laws.0.172.0">1976 c 2 s 172</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.541">
        <h1 class="shn">609.541 PROTECTION OF LIBRARY PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.541.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Damage to library materials.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally, and without permission from library personnel damages any books, maps, pictures, manuscripts, films, or other property of any public library or library belonging to the state or to any political subdivision is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.541.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Removal of library property.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally, and without permission from library personnel removes any books, maps, pictures, manuscripts, films, or other property of any public library or library belonging to the state or to any political subdivision is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.541.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Detention of library materials.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who detains a book, periodical, pamphlet, film, or other property belonging to any public library, or to a library belonging to the state or any political subdivision, for more than 60 days after notice in writing to return it, given after the expiration of the library's stated loan period for the material, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor. The written notice shall be sent by mail to the last known address of the person detaining the material. The notice shall state the type of material borrowed, the title of the material, the author's name, the library from which the material was borrowed, and the date by which the material was to have been returned to the library. The notice shall include a statement indicating that if the material is not returned within 60 days after the written notice the borrower will be in violation of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.541.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Responsibility for prosecution for regional libraries.</span></h2>
          <p>For regional libraries the county attorney for the county in which the offense occurred shall prosecute violations of subdivisions 1 to 3.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.541.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/280/#laws.0.3.0">1983 c 280 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.545">
        <h1 class="shn">609.545 MISUSING CREDIT CARD TO SECURE SERVICES.</h1>
        <p>Whoever obtains the services of another by the intentional unauthorized use of a credit card issued or purporting to be issued by an organization for use as identification in purchasing services is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.545.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.545; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.57.0">1971 c 23 s 57</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.546">
        <h1 class="shn">609.546 MOTOR VEHICLE TAMPERING.</h1>
        <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor who intentionally:</p>
        <p>(1) rides in or on a motor vehicle knowing that the vehicle was taken and is being driven by another without the owner's permission; or</p>
        <p>(2) tampers with or enters into or on a motor vehicle without the owner's permission.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.546.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.9.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.55"><b>609.55</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.14.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.551">
        <h1 class="shn">609.551 RUSTLING AND LIVESTOCK THEFT; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.551.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined; stealing cattle; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally and without claim of right shoots, kills, takes, uses, transfers, conceals or retains possession of live cattle, swine or sheep or the carcasses thereof belonging to another without the other's consent and with the intent to permanently deprive the owner thereof may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(a) if the value of the animals which are shot, killed, taken, used, transferred, concealed, or retained exceeds $2,500, the defendant may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years, and may be fined up to $20,000;</p>
          <p>(b) if the value of the animals which are shot, killed, taken, used, transferred, concealed, or retained exceeds $300 but is less than $2,500, the defendant may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years, and may be fined up to $10,000;</p>
          <p>(c) if the value of the animals which are shot, killed, taken, used, transferred, concealed, or retained is $300 or less, the defendant may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $300 or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.551.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime defined; selling stolen cattle.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever knowingly buys, sells, transports, or otherwise handles cattle, swine, or sheep illegally acquired under subdivision 1 or knowingly aids or abets another in the violation of subdivision 1 shall be sentenced as in subdivision 1, clauses (a), (b), and (c).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.551.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Aggregation.</span></h2>
          <p>In any prosecution under this section the value of the animals which are shot, killed, taken, used, transferred, concealed, or retained within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.551.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Amount of action.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who has been injured by violation of this section may bring an action for three times the amount of actual damages sustained by the plaintiff, costs of suit and reasonable attorney's fees.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.551.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/314/#laws.0.2.0">1975 c 314 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.8.0">1977 c 355 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.552">
        <h1 class="shn">609.552 UNAUTHORIZED RELEASE OF ANIMALS.</h1>
        <p>A person who intentionally and without permission releases an animal lawfully confined for science, research, commerce, or education is guilty of a misdemeanor. A second or subsequent offense by the same person is a gross misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.552.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/55/#laws.0.2.0">1989 c 55 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.555"><b>609.555</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.10.0">1976 c 124 s 10</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">DAMAGE OR TRESPASS TO PROPERTY</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.556">
        <h1 class="shn">609.556 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.556.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.556">609.556</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.576">609.576</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.611">609.611</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.556.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Property of another.</span></h2>
          <p>"Property of another" means a building or other property, whether real or personal, in which a person other than the accused has an interest which the accused has no authority to defeat or impair even though the accused may also have an interest in the building or property.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.556.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Building.</span></h2>
          <p>"Building" in addition to its ordinary meaning includes any tent, watercraft, structure or vehicle that is customarily used for overnight lodging of a person or persons. If a building consists of two or more units separately secured or occupied, each unit shall be deemed a separate building.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.556.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.3.0">1976 c 124 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/347/#laws.0.63.0">1977 c 347 s 63</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.56"><b>609.56</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.10.0">1976 c 124 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.561">
        <h1 class="shn">609.561 ARSON IN THE FIRST DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.561.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">First degree; dwelling.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever unlawfully by means of fire or explosives, intentionally destroys or damages any building that is used as a dwelling at the time the act is committed, whether the inhabitant is present therein at the time of the act or not, or any building appurtenant to or connected with a dwelling whether the property of the actor or of another, commits arson in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.561.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">First degree; other buildings.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever unlawfully by means of fire or explosives, intentionally destroys or damages any building not included in subdivision 1, whether the property of the actor or another commits arson in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to a fine of not more than $35,000, or both if:</p>
