          <p>(a) another person who is not a participant in the crime is present in the building at the time and the defendant knows that; or</p>
          <p>(b) the circumstances are such as to render the presence of such a person therein a reasonable possibility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.561.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">First degree; flammable material.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever unlawfully by means of fire or explosives, intentionally destroys or damages any building not included in subdivision 1, whether the property of the actor or another, commits arson in the first degree if a flammable material is used to start or accelerate the fire. A person who violates this paragraph may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) As used in this subdivision:</p>
          <p>(1) "combustible liquid" means a liquid having a flash point at or above 100 degrees Fahrenheit;</p>
          <p>(2) "flammable gas" means any material which is a gas at 68 degrees Fahrenheit or less and 14.7 psi of pressure and which: (i) is ignitable when in a mixture of 13 percent or less by volume with air at atmospheric pressure; or (ii) has a flammable range with air at atmospheric pressure of at least 12 percent, regardless of the lower flammable limit;</p>
          <p>(3) "flammable liquid" means any liquid having a flash point below 100 degrees Fahrenheit and having a vapor pressure not exceeding 40 pounds per square inch (absolute) at 100 degrees Fahrenheit, but does not include intoxicating liquor as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.101">340A.101</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) "flammable material" means a flammable or combustible liquid, a flammable gas, or a flammable solid; and</p>
          <p>(5) "flammable solid" means any of the following three types of materials:</p>
          <p>(i) wetted explosives;</p>
          <p>(ii) self-reactive materials that are liable to undergo heat-producing decomposition; or</p>
          <p>(iii) readily combustible solids that may cause a fire through friction or that have a rapid burning rate as determined by specific flammability tests.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.561.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.4.0">1976 c 124 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.42.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/186/#laws.0.100.0">1995 c 186 s 100</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/176/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 176 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.562">
        <h1 class="shn">609.562 ARSON IN THE SECOND DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever unlawfully by means of fire or explosives, intentionally destroys or damages any building not covered by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a>, no matter what its value, or any other real or personal property valued at more than $1,000, whether the property of the actor or another, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.562.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.5.0">1976 c 124 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.16.0">1979 c 258 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/141/#laws.0.2.0">1985 c 141 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.5.7.0">1993 c 326 art 5 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.563">
        <h1 class="shn">609.563 ARSON IN THE THIRD DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.563.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever unlawfully by means of fire or explosives, intentionally destroys or damages any real or personal property may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(a) the property intended by the accused to be damaged or destroyed had a value of more than $300 but less than $1,000; or</p>
          <p>(b) property of the value of $300 or more was unintentionally damaged or destroyed but such damage or destruction could reasonably have been foreseen; or</p>
          <p>(c) the property specified in clauses (a) and (b) in the aggregate had a value of $300 or more.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.563.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 33</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.563.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.6.0">1976 c 124 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.9.0">1977 c 355 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.17.0">1979 c 258 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/141/#laws.0.3.0">1985 c 141 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.5.8.0">1993 c 326 art 5 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5631">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5631 ARSON IN THE FOURTH DEGREE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5631.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Multiple unit residential building" means a building containing two or more apartments.</p>
          <p>(c) "Public building" means a building such as a hotel, hospital, motel, dormitory, sanitarium, nursing home, theater, stadium, gymnasium, amusement park building, school or other building used for educational purposes, museum, restaurant, bar, correctional institution, place of worship, or other building of public assembly.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5631.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime described.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally by means of fire or explosives sets fire to or burns or causes to be burned any personal property in a multiple unit residential building or public building and arson in the first, second, or third degree was not committed is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5631.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.19.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/176/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 176 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5632">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5632 ARSON IN THE FIFTH DEGREE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever intentionally by means of fire or explosives sets fire to or burns or causes to be burned any real or personal property of value is guilty of a misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5632.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.20.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5633">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5633 USE OF IGNITION DEVICES; PETTY MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <p>A student who uses an ignition device, including a butane or disposable lighter or matches, inside an educational building and under circumstances where there is an obvious risk of fire, and arson in the first, second, third, or fourth degree was not committed, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor. This section does not apply if the student uses the device in a manner authorized by the school.</p>
        <p>For the purposes of this section, "student" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/123B.41#stat.123B.41.11">123B.41, subdivision 11</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5633.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/176/#laws.0.3.0">1999 c 176 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.564">
        <h1 class="shn">609.564 EXCLUDED FIRES.</h1>
        <p>A person does not violate section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.562">609.562</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.563">609.563</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5641">609.5641</a> if the person sets a fire pursuant to a validly issued license or permit or with written permission from the fire department of the jurisdiction where the fire occurs.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.564.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/141/#laws.0.4.0">1985 c 141 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/478/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 478 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.5641">
        <h1 class="shn">609.5641 WILDFIRE ARSON.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5641.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Setting wildfires.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally sets a fire to burn out of control on land of another containing timber, underbrush, grass, or other vegetative combustible material is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 1a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5641.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Penalty; felonies.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d), a person who violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 where the fire threatens to damage or damages in excess of five buildings or dwellings, burns 500 acres or more, or damages crops in excess of $100,000, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $15,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates subdivision 1 where the fire threatens to damage or damages in excess of 100 buildings or dwellings, burns 1,500 acres or more, or damages crops in excess of $250,000, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(d) A person who violates subdivision 1 where the fire causes another person to suffer demonstrable bodily harm may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of $15,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(e) For purposes of this section, a building or dwelling is threatened when there is a probability of damage to the building or dwelling requiring evacuation for safety of life.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5641.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Possession of flammables to set wildfires.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who possesses a flammable, explosive, or incendiary device, substance, or material with intent to use the device, substance, or material to violate subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.5641.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote"> Restitution.</span></h2>
          <p> In addition to the sentence otherwise authorized, the court may order a person who is convicted of violating this section to pay fire suppression costs, damages to the owner of the damaged land, costs associated with injuries sustained by a member of a municipal or volunteer fire department in the performance of the member's duties, and any other restitution costs allowed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.04">611A.04</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.5641.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/478/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 478 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/139/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 139 s 1</a>-3</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.565"><b>609.565</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.10.0">1976 c 124 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.57"><b>609.57</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.10.0">1976 c 124 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.575"><b>609.575</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.10.0">1976 c 124 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.576">
        <h1 class="shn">609.576 NEGLIGENT FIRES; DANGEROUS SMOKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.576.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Negligent fire resulting in injury or property damage.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever is grossly negligent in causing a fire to burn or get out of control thereby causing damage or injury to another, and as a result of this:</p>
          <p>(1) a human being is injured and great bodily harm incurred, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) a human being is injured and bodily harm incurred, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(3) property of another is injured, thereby, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(i) to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both, if the value of the property damage is under $300;</p>
          <p>(ii) to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the value of the property damaged is at least $300 but is less than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(iii) to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both, if the value of the property damaged is $2,500 or more.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.576.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Dangerous smoking.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor if the person smokes in the presence of explosives or inflammable materials. If a person violates this subdivision and knows that doing so creates a risk of death or bodily harm or serious property damage, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.576.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.7.0">1976 c 124 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.10.0">1977 c 355 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/107/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 107 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/141/#laws.0.5.0">1985 c 141 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.8.0">1989 c 5 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.20.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.5.9.0">1993 c 326 art 5 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/155/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 155 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/82/#laws.0.1.0">2003 c 82 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.58"><b>609.58</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/321/#laws.0.4.0">1983 c 321 s 4</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.581">
        <h1 class="shn">609.581 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Terms defined.</span></h2>
          <p>For purpose of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582">609.582</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.583">609.583</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Building.</span></h2>
          <p>"Building" means a structure suitable for affording shelter for human beings including any appurtenant or connected structure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Dwelling.</span></h2>
          <p>"Dwelling" means a building used as a permanent or temporary residence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Enters a building without consent.</span></h2>
          <p>"Enters a building without consent" means:</p>
          <p>(a) to enter a building without the consent of the person in lawful possession;</p>
          <p>(b) to enter a building by using artifice, trick, or misrepresentation to obtain consent to enter from the person in lawful possession; or</p>
          <p>(c) to remain within a building without the consent of the person in lawful possession.</p>
          <p>Whoever enters a building while open to the general public does so with consent except when consent was expressly withdrawn before entry.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Government building.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Government building" means a building that is owned, leased, controlled, or operated by a governmental entity for a governmental purpose.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Religious establishment.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Religious establishment" means a building used for worship services by a religious organization and clearly identified as such by a posted sign or other means.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">School building.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"School building" means a public or private preschool, elementary school, middle school, secondary school, or postsecondary school building.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.581.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Historic property.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Historic property" means any property identified as a historic site or historic place by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/138.661">138.661</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/138.664">138.664</a> and clearly identified as such by a posted sign or other means.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.581.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/321/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 321 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.11.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 11</a>-14</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.582">
        <h1 class="shn">609.582 BURGLARY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.582.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Burglary in the first degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever enters a building without consent and with intent to commit a crime, or enters a building without consent and commits a crime while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(a) the building is a dwelling and another person, not an accomplice, is present in it when the burglar enters or at any time while the burglar is in the building;</p>
          <p>(b) the burglar possesses, when entering or at any time while in the building, any of the following: a dangerous weapon, any article used or fashioned in a manner to lead the victim to reasonably believe it to be a dangerous weapon, or an explosive; or</p>
          <p>(c) the burglar assaults a person within the building or on the building's appurtenant property.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.582.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Mandatory minimum sentence for burglary of occupied dwelling.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted of committing burglary of an occupied dwelling, as defined in subdivision 1, clause (a), must be committed to the commissioner of corrections or county workhouse for not less than six months.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.582.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Burglary in the second degree.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Whoever enters a building without consent and with intent to commit a crime, or enters a building without consent and commits a crime while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the building is a dwelling;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the portion of the building entered contains a banking business or other business of receiving securities or other valuable papers for deposit or safekeeping and the entry is with force or threat of force;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the portion of the building entered contains a pharmacy or other lawful business or practice in which controlled substances are routinely held or stored, and the entry is forcible; or</p>
          <p class="in">(4) when entering or while in the building, the burglar possesses a tool to gain access to money or property.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Whoever enters a government building, religious establishment, historic property, or school building without consent and with intent to commit a crime under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595">609.595</a>, or enters a government building, religious establishment, historic property, or school building without consent and commits a crime under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595">609.595</a> while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.582.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Burglary in the third degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in this section, whoever enters a building without consent and with intent to steal or commit any felony or gross misdemeanor while in the building, or enters a building without consent and steals or commits a felony or gross misdemeanor while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever enters a building that is open to the public, other than a building identified in subdivision 2, paragraph (b), with intent to steal while in the building, or enters a building that is open to the public, other than a building identified in subdivision 2, paragraph (b), and steals while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the person enters the building within one year after being told to leave the building and not return; and</p>
          <p>(2) the person has been convicted within the preceding five years for an offense under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.98">256.98</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/268.182">268.182</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.522">609.522</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, or a statute from another state, the United States, or a foreign jurisdiction, in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony sentence for the offense or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow imposition of a felony sentence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.582.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Burglary in the fourth degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever enters a building without consent and with intent to commit a misdemeanor other than to steal, or enters a building without consent and commits a misdemeanor other than to steal while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the fourth degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever enters a building that is open to the public, other than a building identified in subdivision 2, paragraph (b), with intent to steal while in the building, or enters a building that is open to the public, other than a building identified in subdivision 2, paragraph (b), and steals while in the building, either directly or as an accomplice, commits burglary in the fourth degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the person enters the building within one year after being told to leave the building and not return.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.582.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/321/#laws.0.2.0">1983 c 321 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.6.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/470/#laws.0.19.0">1986 c 470 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.9.0">1988 c 712 s 9</a>-12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.13.33.0">1993 c 326 art 13 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.22.0">1995 c 244 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.21.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.15.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.11.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 11</a>,12; art 6 s 16</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.583">
        <h1 class="shn">609.583 SENTENCING; FIRST BURGLARY OF DWELLING.</h1>
        <p>Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1a">609.582, subdivision 1a</a>, in determining an appropriate disposition for a first offense of burglary of a dwelling, the court shall presume that a stay of execution with at least a 90-day period of incarceration as a condition of probation shall be imposed unless the defendant's criminal history score determined according to the Sentencing Guidelines indicates a presumptive executed sentence, in which case the presumptive executed sentence shall be imposed unless the court departs from the Sentencing Guidelines pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/244.10">244.10</a>. A stay of imposition of sentence may be granted only if accompanied by a statement on the record of the reasons for it. The presumptive period of incarceration may be waived in whole or in part by the court if the defendant provides restitution or performs community work service.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.583.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/321/#laws.0.3.0">1983 c 321 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/497/#laws.0.1.0">1984 c 497 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/470/#laws.0.20.0">1986 c 470 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.33.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 33</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.585">
        <h1 class="shn">609.585 DOUBLE JEOPARDY.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction of the crime of burglary is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed on entering or while in the building entered.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.585.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.585; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.31.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.586">
        <h1 class="shn">609.586 POSSESSION OF CODE-GRABBING DEVICES; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.586.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "code-grabbing device" means a device that can receive and record the coded signal sent by the transmitter of a security or other electronic system and can play back the signal to disarm or operate that system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.586.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever possesses a code-grabbing device with intent to use the device to commit an unlawful act may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.586.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.34.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 34</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.59">
        <h1 class="shn">609.59 POSSESSION OF BURGLARY OR THEFT TOOLS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever has in possession any device, explosive, or other instrumentality with intent to use or permit the use of the same to commit burglary or theft may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.59.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.59; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.13.0">1988 c 712 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.591">
        <h1 class="shn">609.591 DAMAGE TO TIMBER OR WOOD PROCESSING AND RELATED EQUIPMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.591.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.592">609.592</a>, "timber" means trees, whether standing or down, that will produce forest products of value including but not limited to logs, posts, poles, bolts, pulpwood, cordwood, lumber, and decorative material.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.591.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, without claim of right or consent of the owner, drives, places, or fastens in timber any device of iron, steel, ceramic, or other substance sufficiently hard to damage saws or wood processing or manufacturing equipment, with the intent to hinder the logging or the processing of timber, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivisions 3 and 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.591.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted of violating subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the violation caused great bodily harm, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) otherwise, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.591.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to any sentence imposed under subdivision 3, the sentencing court may order a person convicted of violating this section, or of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595">609.595</a> by damaging timber or commercial wood processing, manufacturing, or transportation equipment to pay restitution to the owner of the damaged property.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.591.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/180/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 180 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.592">
        <h1 class="shn">609.592 POSSESSION OF TIMBER DAMAGE DEVICES.</h1>
        <p>Whoever commits any of the following acts is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
        <p>(1) possesses a device of iron, steel, ceramic, or other substance sufficiently hard to damage saws, wood processing, manufacturing, or transportation equipment, with the intent to use the device to hinder the logging or the processing of timber; or</p>
        <p>(2) possesses a chemical or biological substance, mechanical equipment, or tool with the intent to use it or permit its use to damage timber processing, manufacturing, or transportation equipment.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.592.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/180/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 180 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.593">
        <h1 class="shn">609.593 DAMAGE OR THEFT TO ENERGY TRANSMISSION OR TELECOMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.593.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever intentionally and without consent from one authorized to give consent causes any damage to or takes, removes, severs, or breaks:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) any line erected or maintained for the purpose of transmitting electricity for light, heat, or power, or any insulator or cross-arm, appurtenance or apparatus connected to the line, or any wire, cable, or current of the line; or any component used in the generation, transmission, or distribution of electricity, including equipment used for grounding, system protection, or personnel protection;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) any pipe or main or hazardous liquid pipeline erected, operated, or maintained for the purpose of transporting, conveying, or distributing gas or other hazardous liquids for light, heat, power, or any other purpose, or any part of the pipe, main, or pipeline, or any valve, meter, holder, compressor, machinery, appurtenance, equipment, or apparatus connected with any main or pipeline; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) any machinery, equipment, or fixtures used in receiving, initiating, amplifying, processing, transmitting, retransmitting, recording, switching, or monitoring telecommunications services, such as computers, transformers, amplifiers, routers, repeaters, multiplexers, and other items performing comparable functions; and machinery, equipment, and fixtures used in the transportation of telecommunications services, radio transmitters and receivers, satellite equipment, microwave equipment, and other transporting media including wire, cable, fiber, poles, and conduit;</p>
          <p class="bl">is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.593.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.593.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.16.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/152/#laws.0.1.0">2016 c 152 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.594">
        <h1 class="shn">609.594 DAMAGE TO PROPERTY OF CRITICAL PUBLIC SERVICE FACILITIES, UTILITIES, AND PIPELINES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.594.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "critical public service facility" includes railroad yards and stations, bus stations, airports, and other mass transit facilities; oil refineries; storage areas or facilities for hazardous materials, hazardous substances, or hazardous wastes; and bridges;</p>
          <p>(2) "pipeline" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.6055#stat.609.6055.1">609.6055, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) "utility" includes: (i) any organization defined as a utility in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216C.06#stat.216C.06.18">216C.06, subdivision 18</a>; (ii) any telecommunications carrier or telephone company regulated under chapter 237; and (iii) any local utility or enterprise formed for the purpose of providing electrical or gas heating and power, telephone, water, sewage, wastewater, or other related utility service, which is owned, controlled, or regulated by a town, a statutory or home rule charter city, a county, a port development authority, the Metropolitan Council, a district heating authority, a regional commission or other regional government unit, or a combination of these governmental units.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.594.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibited conduct; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever causes damage to the physical property of a critical public service facility, utility, or pipeline with the intent to significantly disrupt the operation of or the provision of services by the facility, utility, or pipeline and without the consent of one authorized to give consent, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.594.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Detention authority; immunity.</span></h2>
          <p>An employee or other person designated by a critical public service facility, utility, or pipeline to ensure the provision of services by the critical public service facility or the safe operation of the equipment or facility of the utility or pipeline who has reasonable cause to believe that a person is violating this section may detain the person as provided in this subdivision. The person detained must be promptly informed of the purpose of the detention and may not be subjected to unnecessary or unreasonable force or interrogation. The employee or other designated person must notify a peace officer promptly of the detention and may only detain the person for a reasonable period of time. No employee or other designated person is criminally or civilly liable for any detention that the employee or person reasonably believed was authorized by and conducted in conformity with this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.594.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/401/#laws.1.16.0">2002 c 401 art 1 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.595">
        <h1 class="shn">609.595 DAMAGE TO PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.595.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Criminal damage to property in the first degree.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever intentionally causes damage to physical property of another without the latter's consent may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the damage to the property caused a reasonably foreseeable risk of bodily harm; or</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the property damaged was a public safety motor vehicle, the defendant knew the vehicle was a public safety motor vehicle, and the damage to the vehicle caused a substantial interruption or impairment of public safety service or a reasonably foreseeable risk of bodily harm; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the property damaged belongs to a common carrier and the damage impairs the service to the public rendered by the carrier; or</p>
          <p class="in">(4) the damage reduces the value of the property by more than $1,000 measured by the cost of repair and replacement; or</p>
          <p class="in">(5) the damage reduces the value of the property by more than $500 measured by the cost of repair and replacement and the defendant has been convicted within the preceding three years of an offense under this subdivision or subdivision 2.</p>
          <p class="in">In any prosecution under clause (4), the value of any property damaged by the defendant in violation of that clause within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this section; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.595.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Criminal damage to property in the second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever intentionally causes damage described in subdivision 2, paragraph (a), is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than one year and a day or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the damage:</p>
          <p>(1) was committed in whole or in substantial part because of the property owner's or another's actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) was committed in whole or in substantial part because of the victim's actual or perceived association with another person or group of a certain actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) was motivated in whole or in substantial part by an intent to intimidate or harm an individual or group of individuals because of actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) In any prosecution under paragraph (a), the value of property damaged by the defendant in violation of that paragraph within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying this section. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.595.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Criminal damage to property in the third degree.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 1a, whoever intentionally causes damage to another person's physical property without the other person's consent may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if: (1) the damage reduces the value of the property by more than $500 but not more than $1,000 as measured by the cost of repair and replacement; or (2) the damage was to a public safety motor vehicle and the defendant knew the vehicle was a public safety motor vehicle.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Whoever intentionally causes damage to another person's physical property without the other person's consent may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the damage reduces the value of the property by not more than $500 and:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) was committed in whole or in substantial part because of the property owner's or another's actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) was committed in whole or in substantial part because of the victim's actual or perceived association with another person or group of a certain actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) was motivated in whole or in substantial part by an intent to intimidate or harm an individual or group of individuals because of actual or perceived race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, or disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) In any prosecution under paragraph (a), clause (1), the value of property damaged by the defendant in violation of that paragraph within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying this section. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.595.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Criminal damage to property in the fourth degree.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally causes damage described in subdivision 2 under any other circumstances is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.595.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, "public safety motor vehicle" includes:</p>
          <p>(1) marked vehicles used by law enforcement agencies and specially marked vehicles permitted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.98#stat.169.98.2a">169.98, subdivision 2a</a>, owned or leased by the state or a political subdivision;</p>
          <p>(2) fire apparatuses, including fire-suppression support vehicles, owned or leased by the state or a political subdivision;</p>
          <p>(3) ambulances owned or leased by the state or a political subdivision;</p>
          <p>(4) vehicles owned by ambulance services licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144E.10">144E.10</a> that are equipped and specifically intended for emergency response or providing ambulance services; and</p>
          <p>(5) marked vehicles used by conservation officers of the Division of Enforcement and Field Service of the Department of Natural Resources.</p>
          <p>(b) As used in subdivision 1, clause (2), and subdivision 2, paragraph (a), clause (2), "damage" includes tampering with a public safety motor vehicle and acts that obstruct or interfere with the vehicle's use.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.595.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.595; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.60.0">1971 c 23 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.11.0">1977 c 355 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/258/#laws.0.18.0">1979 c 258 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/421/#laws.0.1.0">1984 c 421 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.11.0">1987 c 329 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/261/#laws.0.2.0">1989 c 261 s 2</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/401/#laws.1.17.0">2002 c 401 art 1 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.17.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 17</a>,18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.3.15.0">2017 c 95 art 3 s 15</a>-17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.13.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 13</a>,14; art 6 s 16</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.596">
        <h1 class="shn">609.596 KILLING OR HARMING PUBLIC SAFETY DOG.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.596.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a felony for any person to intentionally and without justification cause the death of or great or substantial bodily harm to a police dog, a search and rescue dog, or an arson dog when the dog is involved in law enforcement, fire, or correctional investigation or apprehension, search and rescue duties, or the dog is in the custody of or under the control of a peace officer, a trained handler, or an employee of a correctional facility. A person convicted under this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.596.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a gross misdemeanor for any person to intentionally and without justification cause demonstrable bodily harm to a police dog, search and rescue dog, or an arson dog when the dog is involved in law enforcement, fire, or correctional investigation or apprehension, search and rescue duties, or the dog is in the custody of or under the control of a peace officer, a trained handler, or an employee of a correctional facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.596.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a misdemeanor for any person to intentionally and without justification assault a police dog, search and rescue dog, or an arson dog when the dog is involved in law enforcement, fire, or correctional investigation or apprehension, search and rescue duties, or the dog is in the custody of or under the control of a peace officer, a trained handler, or an employee of a correctional facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.596.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Mandatory restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall order a person convicted of violating this section to pay restitution for the costs and expenses resulting from the crime. Costs and expenses include, but are not limited to, the purchase and training of a replacement dog and veterinary services for the injured dog. If the court finds that the convicted person is indigent, the court may reduce the amount of restitution to a reasonable level or order it paid in installments.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.596.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "arson dog" means a dog that has been certified as an arson dog by a state fire or police agency or by an independent testing laboratory;</p>
          <p>(2) "correctional facility" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.021">241.021,</a> subdivision 1i;</p>
          <p>(3) "peace officer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c); and</p>
          <p>(4) "search and rescue dog" means a dog that is trained to locate lost or missing persons, victims of natural or other disasters, and human bodies.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.596.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/167/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 167 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.35.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/77/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 77 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/7/#laws.0.87.0">2001 c 7 s 87</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/9/#laws.0.1.0">2011 c 9 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/85/#laws.0.108.0">2024 c 85 s 108</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.597">
        <h1 class="shn">609.597 ASSAULTING OR HARMING POLICE HORSE; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.597.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "police horse" means a horse that has been trained for crowd control and other law enforcement purposes and is used to assist peace officers or reserve officers in the performance of their official duties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.597.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever assaults or intentionally harms a police horse while the horse is being used or maintained for use by a law enforcement agency, or while under the control of a reserve officer who is operating at the direction of, under the control of, or on behalf of a peace officer or a law enforcement agency, is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.597.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted of violating subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if a peace officer, a reserve officer, or any other person suffers great bodily harm or death as a result of the violation, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the police horse suffers death or great bodily harm as a result of the violation, or if a peace officer or a reserve officer suffers demonstrable bodily harm as a result of the violation, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(3) if the police horse suffers demonstrable bodily harm as a result of the violation, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than one year and one day or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(4) if a peace officer or a reserve officer is involuntarily unseated from the police horse or any person, other than the peace officer or reserve officer, suffers demonstrable bodily harm as a result of the violation, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(5) if a violation other than one described in clauses (1) to (4) occurs, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.597.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/179/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 179 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/85/#laws.0.3.0">2011 c 85 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.599">
        <h1 class="shn">609.599 EXPOSING DOMESTIC ANIMALS TO DISEASE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.599.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who intentionally exposes a domestic animal to an animal disease contrary to reasonable veterinary practice, or intentionally puts a domestic animal at risk of quarantine or destruction by actions contrary to reasonable veterinary practice, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) The provisions of paragraph (a) do not apply to a person performing academic or industry research on domestic animals under protocols approved by an institutional animal care and use committee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.599.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Civil liability.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 is liable in a civil action for damages in an amount three times the value of any domestic animal destroyed because it has the disease, has been exposed to the disease agent, or is at high risk of being exposed to the disease agent because of proximity to diseased animals.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.599.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "domestic animal" means:</p>
          <p>(1) those species of animals that live under the husbandry of humans;</p>
          <p>(2) livestock within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/35.01#stat.35.01.3">35.01, subdivision 3</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) a farm-raised deer, farm-raised game bird, or farm-raised fish; or</p>
          <p>(4) an animal listed as a domestic animal by a rule adopted by the Department of Agriculture.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.599.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/254/#laws.0.45.0">2004 c 254 s 45</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.60"><b>609.60</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.18.0">1989 c 5 s 18</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.605">
        <h1 class="shn">609.605 TRESPASS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.605.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The following terms have the meanings given them for purposes of this section.</p>
          <p>(1) "Premises" means real property and any appurtenant building or structure.</p>
          <p>(2) "Dwelling" means the building or part of a building used by an individual as a place of residence on either a full-time or a part-time basis. A dwelling may be part of a multidwelling or multipurpose building, or a manufactured home as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.16">168.002, subdivision 16</a>.</p>
          <p>(3) "Construction site" means the site of the construction, alteration, painting, or repair of a building or structure.</p>
          <p>(4) "Owner or lawful possessor," as used in paragraph (b), clause (9), means the person on whose behalf a building or dwelling is being constructed, altered, painted, or repaired and the general contractor or subcontractor engaged in that work.</p>
          <p>(5) "Posted," as used:</p>
          <p>(i) in paragraph (b), clause (4), means the placement of a sign at least 8-1/2 inches by 11 inches in a conspicuous place on the exterior of the building, or in a conspicuous place within the property on which the building is located. The sign must carry a general notice warning against trespass;</p>
          <p>(ii) in paragraph (b), clause (9), means the placement of a sign at least 8-1/2 inches by 11 inches in a conspicuous place on the exterior of the building that is under construction, alteration, or repair, or in a conspicuous place within the area being protected. If the area being protected is less than three acres, one additional sign must be conspicuously placed within that area. If the area being protected is three acres but less than ten acres, two additional signs must be conspicuously placed within that area. For each additional full ten acres of area being protected beyond the first ten acres of area, two additional signs must be conspicuously placed within the area being protected. The sign must carry a general notice warning against trespass; and</p>
          <p>(iii) in paragraph (b), clause (10), means the placement of signs that:</p>
          <p>(A) carry a general notice warning against trespass;</p>
          <p>(B) display letters at least two inches high;</p>
          <p>(C) state that Minnesota law prohibits trespassing on the property; and</p>
          <p>(D) are posted in a conspicuous place and at intervals of 500 feet or less.</p>
          <p>(6) "Business licensee," as used in paragraph (b), clause (9), includes a representative of a building trades labor or management organization.</p>
          <p>(7) "Building" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.581#stat.609.581.2">609.581, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a misdemeanor if the person intentionally:</p>
          <p>(1) permits domestic animals or fowls under the actor's control to go on the land of another within a city;</p>
          <p>(2) interferes unlawfully with a monument, sign, or pointer erected or marked to designate a point of a boundary, line or a political subdivision, or of a tract of land;</p>
          <p>(3) trespasses on the premises of another and, without claim of right, refuses to depart from the premises on demand of the lawful possessor;</p>
          <p>(4) occupies or enters the dwelling or locked or posted building of another, without claim of right or consent of the owner or the consent of one who has the right to give consent, except in an emergency situation;</p>
          <p>(5) enters the premises of another with intent to take or injure any fruit, fruit trees, or vegetables growing on the premises, without the permission of the owner or occupant;</p>
          <p>(6) enters or is found on the premises of a public or private cemetery without authorization during hours the cemetery is posted as closed to the public;</p>
          <p>(7) returns to the property of another with the intent to abuse, disturb, or cause distress in or threaten another, after being told to leave the property and not to return, if the actor is without claim of right to the property or consent of one with authority to consent;</p>
          <p>(8) returns to the property of another within one year after being told to leave the property and not to return, if the actor is without claim of right to the property or consent of one with authority to consent;</p>
          <p>(9) enters the locked or posted construction site of another without the consent of the owner or lawful possessor, unless the person is a business licensee;</p>
          <p>(10) enters the locked or posted aggregate mining site of another without the consent of the owner or lawful possessor, unless the person is a business licensee; or</p>
          <p>(11) crosses into or enters any public or private area lawfully cordoned off by or at the direction of a peace officer engaged in the performance of official duties. As used in this clause: (i) an area may be "cordoned off" through the use of tape, barriers, or other means conspicuously placed and identifying the area as being restricted by a peace officer and identifying the responsible authority; and (ii) "peace officer" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>. It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this clause that a peace officer permitted entry into the restricted area.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.605.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever trespasses upon the grounds of a facility providing emergency shelter services for battered women, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.31#stat.611A.31.3">611A.31, subdivision 3</a>, or providing comparable services for sex trafficking victims, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.321#stat.609.321.7b">609.321, subdivision 7b</a>, or of a facility providing transitional housing for battered women and their children or sex trafficking victims and their children, without claim of right or consent of one who has right to give consent, and refuses to depart from the grounds of the facility on demand of one who has right to give consent, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.605.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.34.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.605.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Trespasses on school property.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) It is a misdemeanor for a person to enter or be found in a public or nonpublic elementary, middle, or secondary school building unless the person:</p>
          <p>(1) is an enrolled student in, a parent or guardian of an enrolled student in, or an employee of the school or school district;</p>
          <p>(2) has permission or an invitation from a school official to be in the building;</p>
          <p>(3) is attending a school event, class, or meeting to which the person, the public, or a student's family is invited; or</p>
          <p>(4) has reported the person's presence in the school building in the manner required for visitors to the school.</p>
          <p>(b) It is a misdemeanor for a person to be on the roof of a public or nonpublic elementary, middle, or secondary school building unless the person has permission from a school official to be on the roof of the building.</p>
          <p>(c) It is a gross misdemeanor for a group of three or more persons to enter or be found in a public or nonpublic elementary, middle, or secondary school building unless one of the persons:</p>
          <p>(1) is an enrolled student in, a parent or guardian of an enrolled student in, or an employee of the school or school district;</p>
          <p>(2) has permission or an invitation from a school official to be in the building;</p>
          <p>(3) is attending a school event, class, or meeting to which the person, the public, or a student's family is invited; or</p>
          <p>(4) has reported the person's presence in the school building in the manner required for visitors to the school.</p>
          <p>(d) It is a misdemeanor for a person to enter or be found on school property within one year after being told by the school principal or the principal's designee to leave the property and not to return, unless the principal or the principal's designee has given the person permission to return to the property. As used in this paragraph, "school property" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.14a">152.01, subdivision 14a</a>, clauses (1) and (3).</p>
          <p>(e) A school principal or a school employee designated by the school principal to maintain order on school property, who has reasonable cause to believe that a person is violating this subdivision may detain the person in a reasonable manner for a reasonable period of time pending the arrival of a peace officer. A school principal or designated school employee is not civilly or criminally liable for any action authorized under this paragraph if the person's action is based on reasonable cause.</p>
          <p>(f) A peace officer may arrest a person without a warrant if the officer has probable cause to believe the person violated this subdivision within the preceding four hours. The arrest may be made even though the violation did not occur in the peace officer's presence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.605.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Trespass on a school bus.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this subdivision, "school bus" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/169.011#stat.169.011.71">169.011, subdivision 71</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) As used in this subdivision, "pupils" means persons in grades prekindergarten through grade 12.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who boards a school bus when the bus is on its route or otherwise in operation, or while it has pupils on it, and who refuses to leave the bus on demand of the bus operator, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.605.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Certain trespass on agricultural land.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the person enters the posted premises of another on which cattle, bison, sheep, goats, swine, horses, poultry, farmed Cervidae, farmed Ratitae, aquaculture stock, or other species of domestic animals for commercial production are kept, without the consent of the owner or lawful occupant of the land.</p>
          <p>(b) "Domestic animal," for purposes of this section, has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.599">609.599</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) "Posted," as used in paragraph (a), means the placement of a sign at least 11 inches square in a conspicuous place at each roadway entry to the premises. The sign must provide notice of a biosecurity area and wording such as: "Biosecurity measures are in force. No entrance beyond this point without authorization." The sign may also contain a telephone number or a location for obtaining such authorization.</p>
          <p>(d) The provisions of this subdivision do not apply to employees or agents of the state or county when serving in a regulatory capacity and conducting an inspection on posted premises where domestic animals are kept.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.605.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.605; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.62.0">1971 c 23 s 62</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/123/#laws.5.7.0">1973 c 123 art 5 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/251/#laws.0.1.0">1976 c 251 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/512/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 512 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/365/#laws.0.9.0">1981 c 365 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/408/#laws.0.2.0">1982 c 408 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/159/#laws.0.2.0">1985 c 159 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/307/#laws.0.3.0">1987 c 307 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.9.0">1989 c 5 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/261/#laws.0.5.0">1989 c 261 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/426/#laws.1.54.0">1990 c 426 art 1 s 54</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.14.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 14</a>; art 2 s 13; art 4 s 32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/366/#laws.0.13.0">1993 c 366 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/465/#laws.1.60.0">1994 c 465 art 1 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/226/#laws.3.48.0">1995 c 226 art 3 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/254/#laws.0.46.0">2004 c 254 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.41.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 41</a>,42; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/59/#laws.5.15.0">2009 c 59 art 5 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/123/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 123 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.3.18.0">2017 c 95 art 3 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.2.41.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 2 s 41</a></p>
