      <div class="section" id="stat.609.6055">
        <h1 class="shn">609.6055 TRESPASS ON CRITICAL PUBLIC SERVICE FACILITY; UTILITY; OR PIPELINE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6055.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Critical public service facility" includes buildings and other physical structures, and fenced in or otherwise enclosed property, of railroad yards and stations, bus stations, airports, and other mass transit facilities; oil refineries; and storage areas or facilities for hazardous materials, hazardous substances, or hazardous wastes. The term also includes nonpublic portions of bridges. The term does not include railroad tracks extending beyond a critical public service facility.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "Pipeline" includes an aboveground pipeline, a belowground pipeline housed in an underground structure, and any equipment, facility, or building located in this state that is used to transport natural or synthetic gas, crude petroleum or petroleum fuels or oil or their derivatives, or hazardous liquids, to or within a distribution, refining, manufacturing, or storage facility that is located inside or outside of this state. Pipeline does not include service lines.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) "Utility" includes:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) any organization defined as a utility in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216C.06#stat.216C.06.18">216C.06, subdivision 18</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) any telecommunications carrier or telephone company regulated under chapter 237; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) any local utility or enterprise formed for the purpose of providing electrical or gas heating and power, telephone, water, sewage, wastewater, or other related utility service, which is owned, controlled, or regulated by a town, a statutory or home rule charter city, a county, a port development authority, the Metropolitan Council, a district heating authority, a regional commission or other regional government unit, or a combination of these governmental units.</p>
          <p class="in">The term does not include property located above buried power or telecommunications lines or property located below suspended power or telecommunications lines, unless the property is fenced in or otherwise enclosed.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) "Utility line" includes power, telecommunications, and transmissions lines as well as related equipment owned or controlled by a utility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6055.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibited conduct; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Whoever enters or is found upon property containing a critical public service facility, utility, or pipeline, without claim of right or consent of one who has the right to give consent to be on the property, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor, if:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the person refuses to depart from the property on the demand of one who has the right to give consent;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) within the past six months, the person had been told by one who had the right to give consent to leave the property and not to return, unless a person with the right to give consent has given the person permission to return; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the property is posted.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Whoever enters an underground structure that (1) contains a utility line or pipeline and (2) is not open to the public for pedestrian use, without claim of right or consent of one who has the right to give consent to be in the underground structure, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. The underground structure does not need to be posted for this paragraph to apply.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6055.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Posting.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, a critical public service facility, utility, or pipeline is posted if there are signs that:</p>
          <p>(1) state "no trespassing" or similar terms;</p>
          <p>(2) display letters at least two inches high;</p>
          <p>(3) state that Minnesota law prohibits trespassing on the property; and</p>
          <p>(4) are posted in a conspicuous place and at intervals of 500 feet or less.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6055.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Detention authority; immunity.</span></h2>
          <p>An employee or other person designated by a critical public service facility, utility, or pipeline to ensure the provision of services by the critical public service facility or the safe operation of the equipment or facility of the utility or pipeline who has reasonable cause to believe that a person is violating this section may detain the person as provided in this subdivision. The person detained must be promptly informed of the purpose of the detention and may not be subjected to unnecessary or unreasonable force or interrogation. The employee or other designated person must notify a peace officer promptly of the detention and may only detain the person for a reasonable period of time. No employee or other designated person is criminally or civilly liable for any detention that the employee or person reasonably believed was authorized by and conducted in conformity with this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6055.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Arrest authority.</span></h2>
          <p>A peace officer may arrest a person without a warrant if the officer has probable cause to believe the person violated this section within the preceding four hours. The arrest may be made even though the violation did not occur in the presence of the peace officer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.6055.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/401/#laws.1.18.0">2002 c 401 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/217/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 217 s 1</a>,2</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.6057">
        <h1 class="shn">609.6057 GEOGRAPHIC RESTRICTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6057.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "geographic restriction" means a limitation prohibiting a defendant in a criminal proceeding or a juvenile offender in a delinquency proceeding from entering a designated property or geographic area.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6057.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibited conduct; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who knows of a geographic restriction order issued against the person and intentionally enters or remains in the restricted area is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6057.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A geographic restriction may be issued as a pretrial order before final disposition of the underlying criminal case, as a postconviction probationary order, or both. A geographic restriction order is independent of any condition of pretrial release or probation imposed on the defendant. A geographic restriction order may be issued in addition to a similar restriction imposed as a condition of pretrial release or probation.</p>
          <p>(b) A court may issue a geographic restriction upon a finding that its issuance will serve the interests of protecting public safety or property. In making that determination, a court shall consider the following factors:</p>
          <p>(1) whether a defendant's presence in a restricted area creates a risk to public safety or property;</p>
          <p>(2) a defendant's criminal history;</p>
          <p>(3) the likelihood of future criminal activity within the restricted area; and</p>
          <p>(4) any other factors deemed relevant by the court.</p>
          <p>(c) A court may grant any exceptions to a geographic restriction that it deems necessary in order to avoid the imposition of a significant hardship upon a defendant. In determining whether to grant an exception, a court shall also consider the impact of the exception on the interests of protecting public safety or property.</p>
          <p>(d) A geographic restriction order under this section shall be issued in a proceeding that is separate from but which may be held immediately following a proceeding in which any pretrial release or sentencing issues are decided.</p>
          <p>(e) A court issuing a geographic restriction order under this section shall notify a defendant:</p>
          <p>(1) of the area subject to a geographic restriction; and</p>
          <p>(2) that violation of the geographic restriction order is a crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6057.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Cancellation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A court shall cancel a pretrial geographic restriction order at the final disposition of the underlying criminal case.</p>
          <p>(b) A court shall cancel a postconviction geographic restriction order when an offender completes a period of probationary supervision or is committed to the commissioner of corrections.</p>
          <p>(c) A court may cancel a postconviction geographic restriction order at any time during which an offender is under probationary supervision.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.6057.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/95/#laws.3.19.0">2017 c 95 art 3 s 19</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.606">
        <h1 class="shn">609.606 UNLAWFUL OUSTER OR EXCLUSION.</h1>
        <p>A landlord, agent of the landlord, or person acting under the landlord's direction or control who unlawfully and intentionally removes or excludes a tenant from lands or tenements or intentionally interrupts or causes the interruption of electrical, heat, gas, or water services to the tenant with intent to unlawfully remove or exclude the tenant from lands or tenements is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.606.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/376/#laws.1.16.0">1992 c 376 art 1 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.61"><b>609.61</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.10.0">1976 c 124 s 10</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.611">
        <h1 class="shn">609.611 INSURANCE FRAUD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.611.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Insurance fraud prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever with the intent to defraud for the purpose of depriving another of property or for pecuniary gain, commits, or permits its employees or its agents to commit any of the following acts, is guilty of insurance fraud and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p>(a) presents, causes to be presented, or prepares with knowledge or reason to believe that it will be presented, by or on behalf of an insured, claimant, or applicant to an insurer, insurance professional, or premium finance company in connection with an insurance transaction or premium finance transaction, any information that contains a false representation as to any material fact, or that conceals a material fact concerning any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) an application for, rating of, or renewal of, an insurance policy;</p>
          <p>(2) a claim for payment or benefit under an insurance policy;</p>
          <p>(3) a payment made according to the terms of an insurance policy;</p>
          <p>(4) an application used in a premium finance transaction;</p>
          <p>(b) presents, causes to be presented, or prepares with knowledge or reason to believe that it will be presented, to or by an insurer, insurance professional, or a premium finance company in connection with an insurance transaction or premium finance transaction, any information that contains a false representation as to any material fact, or that conceals a material fact, concerning any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a solicitation for sale of an insurance policy or purported insurance policy;</p>
          <p>(2) an application for certificate of authority;</p>
          <p>(3) the financial condition of an insurer; or</p>
          <p>(4) the acquisition, formation, merger, affiliation, or dissolution of an insurer;</p>
          <p>(c) solicits or accepts new or renewal insurance risks by or for an insolvent insurer;</p>
          <p>(d) removes the assets or any record of assets, transactions, and affairs or any material part thereof, from the home office or other place of business of an insurer, or from the place of safekeeping of an insurer, or destroys or sequesters the same from the Department of Commerce;</p>
          <p>(e) diverts, misappropriates, converts, or embezzles funds of an insurer, insured, claimant, or applicant for insurance in connection with:</p>
          <p>(1) an insurance transaction;</p>
          <p>(2) the conducting of business activities by an insurer or insurance professional; or</p>
          <p>(3) the acquisition, formation, merger, affiliation, or dissolution of any insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.611.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Statute of limitations.</span></h2>
          <p>The applicable statute of limitations provision under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/628.26">628.26</a> shall not begin to run until the insurance company or law enforcement agency is aware of the fraud, but in no event may the prosecution be commenced later than seven years after the act has occurred.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.611.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates this provision may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, based on the greater of (i) the value of property, services, or other benefit wrongfully obtained or attempted to obtain, or (ii) the aggregate economic loss suffered by any person as a result of the violation. A person convicted of a violation of this section must be ordered to pay restitution to persons aggrieved by the violation. Restitution must be ordered in addition to a fine or imprisonment but not in lieu of a fine or imprisonment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.611.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Insurance policy" means the written instrument in which are set forth the terms of any certificate of insurance, binder of coverage, or contract of insurance (including a certificate, binder, or contract issued by a state-assigned risk plan); benefit plan; nonprofit hospital service plan; motor club service plan; or surety bond, cash bond, or any other alternative to insurance authorized by a state's Financial Responsibility Act.</p>
          <p>(b) "Insurance professional" means sales agents, agencies, managing general agents, brokers, producers, claims representatives, adjusters, and third-party administrators.</p>
          <p>(c) "Insurance transaction" means a transaction by, between, or among: (1) an insurer or a person who acts on behalf of an insurer; and (2) an insured, claimant, applicant for insurance, public adjuster, insurance professional, practitioner, or any person who acts on behalf of any of the foregoing, for the purpose of obtaining insurance or reinsurance, calculating insurance premiums, submitting a claim, negotiating or adjusting a claim, or otherwise obtaining insurance, self-insurance, or reinsurance or obtaining the benefits thereof or therefrom.</p>
          <p>(d) "Insurer" means a person purporting to engage in the business of insurance or authorized to do business in the state or subject to regulation by the state, who undertakes to indemnify another against loss, damage, or liability arising from a contingent or unknown event. Insurer includes, but is not limited to, an insurance company; self-insurer; reinsurer; reciprocal exchange; interinsurer; risk retention group; Lloyd's insurer; fraternal benefit society; surety; medical service, dental, optometric, or any other similar health service plan; and any other legal entity engaged or purportedly engaged in the business of insurance, including any person or entity that falls within the definition of insurer found within section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.951#stat.60A.951.5">60A.951, subdivision 5</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) "Premium" means consideration paid or payable for coverage under an insurance policy. Premium includes any payment, whether due within the insurance policy term or otherwise, and any deductible payment, whether advanced by the insurer or insurance professional and subject to reimbursement by the insured or otherwise, any self-insured retention or payment, whether advanced by the insurer or insurance professional and subject to reimbursement by the insured or otherwise, and any collateral or security to be provided to collateralize obligations to pay any of the above.</p>
          <p>(f) "Premium finance company" means a person engaged or purporting to engage in the business of advancing money, directly or indirectly, to an insurer or producer at the request of an insured under the terms of a premium finance agreement, including but not limited to, loan contracts, notes, agreements or obligations, wherein the insured has assigned the unearned premiums, accrued dividends, or loss payments as security for such advancement in payment of premiums on insurance policies only, but does not include the financing of insurance premiums purchased in connection with the financing of goods or services.</p>
          <p>(g) "Premium finance transaction" means a transaction by, between, or among an insured, a producer or other party claiming to act on behalf of an insured and a third-party premium finance company, for the purposes of purportedly or actually advancing money directly or indirectly to an insurer or producer at the request of an insured under the terms of a premium finance agreement, wherein the insured has assigned the unearned premiums, accrued dividends, or loan payments as security for such advancement in payment of premiums on insurance policies only, but does not include the financing of insurance premiums purchased in connection with the financing of goods or services.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.611.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/124/#laws.0.8.0">1976 c 124 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/217/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 217 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.43.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.3.36.0">1996 c 408 art 3 s 36</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.612">
        <h1 class="shn">609.612 EMPLOYMENT OF RUNNERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.612.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Public media" means telephone directories, professional directories, newspapers and other periodicals, radio and television, billboards, and mailed or electronically transmitted written communications that do not involve in-person contact with a specific prospective patient or client.</p>
          <p>(c) "Runner," "capper," or "steerer" means a person who for a pecuniary gain directly procures or solicits prospective patients through telephonic, electronic, or written communication, or in-person contact, at the direction of, or in cooperation with, a health care provider when the person knows or has reason to know that the provider's purpose is to perform or obtain services or benefits under or relating to a contract of motor vehicle insurance. The term runner, capper, or steerer does not include a person who solicits or procures clients either through public media, or consistent with the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65B.54#stat.65B.54.6">65B.54, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.612.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Act constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever employs, uses, or acts as a runner, capper, or steerer is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to a payment of a fine of not more than $6,000, or both. Charges for any services rendered by a health care provider, who violated this section in regard to the person for whom such services were rendered, are noncompensable and unenforceable as a matter of law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.612.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/331/#laws.0.15.0">2002 c 331 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/255/#laws.0.2.0">2012 c 255 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.615">
        <h1 class="shn">609.615 DEFEATING SECURITY ON REALTY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever removes or damages real property which is subject to a mortgage, mechanic's lien, or contract for deed, including during the period of time allowed for redemption, with intent to impair the value of the property, without the consent of the security holder, may be sentenced as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) if the value of the property is impaired by $300 or less, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both; or</p>
        <p>(2) if the value of the property is impaired by more than $300, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.615.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.615; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.63.0">1971 c 23 s 63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/355/#laws.0.12.0">1977 c 355 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/40/#laws.0.10.0">1993 c 40 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.62">
        <h1 class="shn">609.62 DEFEATING SECURITY ON PERSONALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.62.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>In this section "security interest" means an interest in property which secures payment or other performance of an obligation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.62.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $6,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) conceals, removes, or transfers any personal property in which the actor knows that another has a security interest; or</p>
          <p>(2) being an obligor and knowing the location of the property refuses to disclose the same to an obligee entitled to possession thereof.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.62.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.62; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.21.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.621">
        <h1 class="shn">609.621 PROOF OF CONCEALMENT OF PROPERTY BY OBLIGOR OF SECURED PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.621.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined; obligor conceals property.</span></h2>
          <p>When in any prosecution under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.62">609.62</a>, it appears that there is a default in the payment of the debts secured and it further appears that the obligor has failed or refused to reveal the location of the security, this shall be considered sufficient evidence to sustain a finding that the obligor has removed, concealed, or disposed of the property.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.621.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Allegation.</span></h2>
          <p>In any prosecution under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.62">609.62</a>, it is a sufficient allegation and description of the security and the property secured to state generally that such property was duly mortgaged or sold under a conditional sales contract, or as the case may be, giving the date thereof and the names of the obligor and obligee.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.621.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.2.15.0">1963 c 753 art 2 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">FORGERY AND RELATED CRIMES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.625">
        <h1 class="shn">609.625 AGGRAVATED FORGERY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.625.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Making or altering writing or object.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, falsely makes or alters a writing or object of any of the following kinds so that it purports to have been made by another or by the maker or alterer under an assumed or fictitious name, or at another time, or with different provisions, or by authority of one who did not give such authority, is guilty of aggravated forgery and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) a writing or object whereby, when genuine, legal rights, privileges, or obligations are created, terminated, transferred, or evidenced, or any writing normally relied upon as evidence of debt or property rights, other than a check as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a> or a financial transaction card as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) an official seal or the seal of a corporation; or</p>
          <p>(3) a public record or an official authentication or certification of a copy thereof; or</p>
          <p>(4) an official return or certificate entitled to be received as evidence of its contents; or</p>
          <p>(5) a court order, judgment, decree, or process; or</p>
          <p>(6) the records or accounts of a public body, office, or officer; or</p>
          <p>(7) the records or accounts of a bank or person, with whom funds of the state or any of its agencies or subdivisions are deposited or entrusted, relating to such funds.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.625.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Means for false reproduction.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, makes, engraves, possesses or transfers a plate or instrument for the false reproduction of a writing or object mentioned in subdivision 1, a check as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>, or a financial transaction card as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.625.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Uttering or possessing.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, utters or possesses with intent to utter any forged writing or object mentioned in subdivision 1, not including a check as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a> or a financial transaction card as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, knowing it to have been so forged, may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.625.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.625; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/243/#laws.0.9.0">1985 c 243 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.12.0">1987 c 329 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.63">
        <h1 class="shn">609.63 FORGERY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.63.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined; intent to defraud.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to injure or defraud, does any of the following is guilty of forgery and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) uses a false writing, knowing it to be false, for the purpose of identification or recommendation; or</p>
          <p>(2) without consent, places, or possesses with intent to place, upon any merchandise an identifying label or stamp which is or purports to be that of another craftsperson, tradesperson, packer, or manufacturer, or disposes or possesses with intent to dispose of any merchandise so labeled or stamped; or</p>
          <p>(3) falsely makes or alters a membership card purporting to be that of a fraternal, business, professional, or other association, or of any labor union, or possesses any such card knowing it to have been thus falsely made or altered; or</p>
          <p>(4) falsely makes or alters a writing, or possesses a falsely made or altered writing, evidencing a right to transportation on a common carrier; or</p>
          <p>(5) destroys, mutilates, or by alteration, false entry or omission, falsifies any record, account, or other document relating to a private business; or</p>
          <p>(6) without authority of law, destroys, mutilates, or by alteration, false entry, or omission, falsifies any record, account, or other document relating to a person, corporation, or business, or filed in the office of, or deposited with, any public office or officer; or</p>
          <p>(7) destroys a writing or object to prevent it from being produced at a trial, hearing, or other proceeding authorized by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.63.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime defined; forged document at trial.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with knowledge that it is forged, offers in evidence in any trial, hearing or other proceedings authorized by law, as genuine, any forged writing or object may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the writing or object is offered in evidence in the trial of a felony charge, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) in all other cases, to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.63.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.63; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.631">
        <h1 class="shn">609.631 CHECK FORGERY; OFFERING FORGED CHECK.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.631.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The definitions in this subdivision apply to this section.</p>
          <p>(b) "Check" means a check, draft, order of withdrawal, or similar negotiable or nonnegotiable instrument.</p>
          <p>(c) "Property" and "services" have the meanings given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.631.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Check forgery; elements.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of check forgery and may be sentenced under subdivision 4 if the person, with intent to defraud, does any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) falsely makes or alters a check so that it purports to have been made by another or by the maker under an assumed or fictitious name, or at another time, or with different provisions, or by the authority of one who did not give authority; or</p>
          <p>(2) falsely endorses or alters a check so that it purports to have been endorsed by another.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.631.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Offering forged check; elements.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who, with intent to defraud, offers, or possesses with intent to offer, a forged check, whether or not it is accepted, is guilty of offering a forged check and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.631.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Sentencing.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who is convicted under subdivision 2 or 3 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both, if the forged check or checks are used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain, property or services of more than $35,000 or the aggregate amount of the forged check or checks is more than $35,000;</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the forged check or checks are used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain, property or services of more than $2,500 or the aggregate amount of the forged check or checks is more than $2,500;</p>
          <p>(3) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(a) the forged check or checks are used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain, property or services of more than $250 but not more than $2,500, or the aggregate face amount of the forged check or checks is more than $250 but not more than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(b) the forged check or checks are used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain, property or services of no more than $250, or have an aggregate face value of no more than $250, and the person has been convicted within the preceding five years for an offense under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.247">609.247</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a>, 2, or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, or a statute from another state in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence for the offense, or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow imposition of a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence; and</p>
          <p>(4) to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the forged check or checks are used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain, property or services of no more than $250, or the aggregate face amount of the forged check or checks is no more than $250.</p>
          <p>In any prosecution under this subdivision, the value of the checks forged or offered by the defendant in violation of this subdivision within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this section. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the checks was forged or offered for all of the offenses aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.631.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.13.0">1987 c 329 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.14.0">1988 c 712 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.7.10.0">1989 c 290 art 7 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/218/#laws.0.4.0">1999 c 218 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; art 20 s 24</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.632">
        <h1 class="shn">609.632 COUNTERFEITING OF CURRENCY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.632.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Manufacturing; printing. </span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with the intent to defraud, falsely makes, alters, prints, scans, images, or copies any United States postal money order, United States currency, Federal Reserve note, or other obligation or security of the United States so that it purports to be genuine or has different terms or provisions than that of the United States Postal Service or United States Treasury is guilty of counterfeiting and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.632.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Means for false reproduction. </span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, makes, engraves, possesses, or transfers a plate or instrument, computer, printer, camera, software, paper, cloth, fabric, ink, or other material for the false reproduction of any United States postal money order, United States currency, Federal Reserve note, or other obligation or security of the United States is guilty of counterfeiting and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.632.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Uttering or possessing. </span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, with intent to defraud, utters or possesses with intent to utter any counterfeit United States postal money order, United States currency, Federal Reserve note, or other obligation or security of the United States, having reason to know that the money order, currency, note, or obligation or security is forged, counterfeited, falsely made, altered, or printed, is guilty of offering counterfeited currency and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.632.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Penalty. </span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who is convicted of violating subdivision 1 or 2 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who is convicted of violating subdivision 3 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both, if the counterfeited item is used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain property or services having a value of more than $35,000, or the aggregate face value of the counterfeited item is more than $35,000;</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the counterfeited item is used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain property or services having a value of more than $5,000, or the aggregate face value of the counterfeited item is more than $5,000;</p>
          <p>(3) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(i) the counterfeited item is used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain property or services having a value of more than $1,000 or the aggregate face value of the counterfeited item is more than $1,000; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the counterfeited item is used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain property or services having a value of no more than $1,000, or the aggregate face value of the counterfeited item is no more than $1,000, and the person has been convicted within the preceding five years for an offense under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.247">609.247</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582">609.582</a>, subdivision 1, 2, or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.821">609.821</a>, or a statute from another state or the United States in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence for the offense, or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow the imposition of a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence; or</p>
          <p>(4) to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the counterfeited item is used to obtain or in an attempt to obtain property or services having a value of no more than $1,000, or the aggregate face value of the counterfeited item is no more than $1,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.632.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Aggregation; venue. </span></h2>
          <p>In any prosecution under this section, the value of the counterfeited United States postal money orders, United States currency, Federal Reserve notes, or other obligations or securities of the United States, offered by the defendant in violation of this section within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this section. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the counterfeited items was forged, offered, or possessed, for all of the offenses aggregated under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.632.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.27.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; art 20 s 25</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.635">
        <h1 class="shn">609.635 OBTAINING SIGNATURE BY FALSE PRETENSE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, by false pretense, obtains the signature of another to a writing which is a subject of forgery under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625#stat.609.625.1">609.625, subdivision 1</a>, may be punished as therein provided.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.635.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.635</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.64">
        <h1 class="shn">609.64 RECORDING, FILING OF FORGED INSTRUMENT.</h1>
        <p>Whoever intentionally presents for filing, registering, or recording, or files, registers, or records a false or forged instrument relating to or affecting real or personal property in a public office entitled to file, register, or record such instrument when genuine may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.64.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.64; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.645">
        <h1 class="shn">609.645 FRAUDULENT STATEMENTS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, with intent to injure or defraud, does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) circulates or publishes a false statement, oral or written, relating to a corporation, association, or individual, intending thereby to give a false apparent value to securities issued or to be issued by, or to the property of, such corporation, association, or individual; or</p>
        <p>(2) makes a false ship's or airplane's manifest, invoice, register, or protest.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.645.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.645; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.65">
        <h1 class="shn">609.65 FALSE CERTIFICATION BY NOTARY PUBLIC.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, when acting or purporting to act as a notary public or other public officer, certifies falsely that an instrument has been acknowledged or that any other act was performed by a party appearing before the actor or that as such notary public or other public officer the actor performed any other official act may be sentenced as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) if the actor so certifies with intent to injure or defraud, to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both; or</p>
        <p>(2) in any other case, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.65.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.65; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.64.0">1971 c 23 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.651">
        <h1 class="shn">609.651 STATE LOTTERY FRAUD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.651.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced under subdivision 4 if the person does any of the following with intent to defraud the State Lottery:</p>
          <p>(1) alters or counterfeits a State Lottery ticket;</p>
          <p>(2) knowingly presents an altered or counterfeited State Lottery ticket for payment;</p>
          <p>(3) knowingly transfers an altered or counterfeited State Lottery ticket to another person; or</p>
          <p>(4) otherwise claims a lottery prize by means of fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.651.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Computer access.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced under subdivision 4 if the person:</p>
          <p>(1) obtains access to a computer database maintained by the director without the specific authorization of the director;</p>
          <p>(2) obtains access to a computer database maintained by a person under contract with the director to maintain the database without the specific authorization of the director and the person maintaining the database.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.651.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">False statements.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced under subdivision 4 if the person:</p>
          <p>(1) makes a materially false or misleading statement, or a material omission, in a record required to be submitted under chapter 349A; or</p>
          <p>(2) makes a materially false or misleading statement, or a material omission, in information submitted to the director of the State Lottery in a lottery retailer's application or a document related to a bid.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.651.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who violates subdivision 1 or 2 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 or 2 and defrauds the State Lottery of $35,000 or more may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates subdivision 3 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.651.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/334/#laws.3.16.0">1989 c 334 art 3 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/356/#laws.0.36.0">1989 c 356 s 36</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.652">
        <h1 class="shn">609.652 FRAUDULENT DRIVERS' LICENSES AND IDENTIFICATION CARDS; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.652.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "driver's license or identification card" means a driver's license or identification card issued by the Driver and Vehicle Services Division of the Department of Public Safety or receipts issued by its authorized agents or those of any state as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.01">171.01</a> that issues licenses recognized in this state for the operation of a motor vehicle or that issues identification cards recognized in this state for the purpose of indicating a person's legal name and age;</p>
          <p>(2) "fraudulent driver's license or identification card" means a document purporting to be a driver's license or identification card, but that is not authentic; and</p>
          <p>(3) "sell" means to sell, barter, deliver, exchange, distribute, or dispose of to another.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.652.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Criminal acts.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who does any of the following for consideration and with intent to manufacture, sell, issue, publish, or pass more than one fraudulent driver's license or identification card or to cause or permit any of the items listed in clauses (1) to (5) to be used in forging or making more than one false or counterfeit driver's license or identification card is guilty of a crime:</p>
          <p>(1) has in control, custody, or possession any plate, block, press, stone, digital image, computer software program, encoding equipment, computer optical scanning equipment, or digital photo printer, or other implement, or any part of such an item, designed to assist in making a fraudulent driver's license or identification card;</p>
          <p>(2) engraves, makes, or amends, or begins to engrave, make, or amend, any plate, block, press, stone, or other implement for the purpose of producing a fraudulent driver's license or identification card;</p>
          <p>(3) uses a photocopier, digital camera, photographic image, or computer software to generate a fraudulent driver's license or identification card;</p>
          <p>(4) has in control, custody, or possession or makes or provides paper or other material adapted and designed for the making of a fraudulent driver's license or identification card; or</p>
          <p>(5) prints, photographs, or in any manner makes or executes an engraved photograph, print, or impression purporting to be a driver's license or identification card.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/171.22">171.22</a>, a person who manufactures or possesses more than one fraudulent driver's license or identification card with intent to sell is guilty of a crime.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.652.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who commits any act described in subdivision 2 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. A person convicted of a second or subsequent offense of this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.652.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/8/#laws.8.27.0">1Sp2001 c 8 art 8 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/212/#laws.1.19.0">2006 c 212 art 1 s 19</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.655"><b>609.655</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/112/#laws.0.2.0">1976 c 112 s 2</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST PUBLIC SAFETY AND HEALTH</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.66">
        <h1 class="shn">609.66 DANGEROUS WEAPONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor crimes.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in paragraph (b):</p>
          <p>(1) recklessly handles or uses a gun or other dangerous weapon or explosive so as to endanger the safety of another; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally points a gun of any kind, capable of injuring or killing a human being and whether loaded or unloaded, at or toward another; or</p>
          <p>(3) manufactures or sells for any unlawful purpose any weapon known as a slungshot or sand club; or</p>
          <p>(4) manufactures, transfers, or possesses metal knuckles or a switch blade knife opening automatically; or</p>
          <p>(5) possesses any other dangerous article or substance for the purpose of being used unlawfully as a weapon against another; or</p>
          <p>(6) outside of a municipality and without the parent's or guardian's consent, furnishes a child under 14 years of age, or as a parent or guardian permits the child to handle or use, outside of the parent's or guardian's presence, a firearm or airgun of any kind, or any ammunition or explosive.</p>
          <p>Possession of written evidence of prior consent signed by the minor's parent or guardian is a complete defense to a charge under clause (6).</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted under paragraph (a) may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the act was committed in a public housing zone, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.19">152.01, subdivision 19</a>, a school zone, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.14a">152.01, subdivision 14a</a>, or a park zone, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.12a">152.01, subdivision 12a</a>, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) otherwise, including where the act was committed on residential premises within a zone described in clause (1) if the offender was at the time an owner, tenant, or invitee for a lawful purpose with respect to those residential premises, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Felony crimes; suppressors; reckless discharge.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced as provided in paragraph (b):</p>
          <p>(1) sells or has in possession a suppressor that is not lawfully possessed under federal law;</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally discharges a firearm under circumstances that endanger the safety of another; or</p>
          <p>(3) recklessly discharges a firearm within a municipality.</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted under paragraph (a) may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the act was a violation of paragraph (a), clause (2), or if the act was a violation of paragraph (a), clause (1) or (3), and was committed in a public housing zone, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.19">152.01, subdivision 19</a>, a school zone, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.14a">152.01, subdivision 14a</a>, or a park zone, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.12a">152.01, subdivision 12a</a>, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(2) otherwise, to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) As used in this subdivision, "suppressor" means any device for silencing, muffling, or diminishing the report of a portable firearm, including any combination of parts, designed or redesigned, and intended for use in assembling or fabricating a firearm silencer or firearm muffler, and any part intended only for use in such assembly or fabrication.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Felony; furnishing to minors.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever, in any municipality of this state, furnishes a minor under 18 years of age with a firearm, airgun, ammunition, or explosive without the prior consent of the minor's parent or guardian or of the police department of the municipality is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both. Possession of written evidence of prior consent signed by the minor's parent or guardian is a complete defense to a charge under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Felony; furnishing dangerous weapon.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever recklessly furnishes a person with a dangerous weapon in conscious disregard of a known substantial risk that the object will be possessed or used in furtherance of a felony crime of violence is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1d.<span class="headnote">Possession on school property; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided under paragraphs (d) and (f), whoever possesses, stores, or keeps a dangerous weapon while knowingly on school property is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever uses or brandishes a replica firearm or a BB gun while knowingly on school property is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) Whoever possesses, stores, or keeps a replica firearm or a BB gun while knowingly on school property is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(d) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), (b), or (c), it is a misdemeanor for a person authorized to carry a firearm under the provisions of a permit or otherwise to carry a firearm on or about the person's clothes or person in a location the person knows is school property. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a>, a firearm carried in violation of this paragraph is not subject to forfeiture.</p>
          <p>(e) As used in this subdivision:</p>
          <p>(1) "BB gun" means a device that fires or ejects a shot measuring .18 of an inch or less in diameter;</p>
          <p>(2) "dangerous weapon" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.02#stat.609.02.6">609.02, subdivision 6</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) "replica firearm" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) "school property" means:</p>
          <p>(i) a public or private elementary, middle, or secondary school building and its improved grounds, whether leased or owned by the school;</p>
          <p>(ii) a child care center licensed under chapter 142B during the period children are present and participating in a child care program;</p>
          <p>(iii) the area within a school bus when that bus is being used by a school to transport one or more elementary, middle, or secondary school students to and from school-related activities, including curricular, cocurricular, noncurricular, extracurricular, and supplementary activities; and</p>
          <p>(iv) that portion of a building or facility under the temporary, exclusive control of a public or private school, a school district, or an association of such entities where conspicuous signs are prominently posted at each entrance that give actual notice to persons of the school-related use.</p>
          <p>(f) This subdivision does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) active licensed peace officers;</p>
          <p>(2) military personnel or students participating in military training, who are on-duty, performing official duties;</p>
          <p>(3) persons authorized to carry a pistol under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.714">624.714</a> while in a motor vehicle or outside of a motor vehicle to directly place a firearm in, or retrieve it from, the trunk or rear area of the vehicle;</p>
          <p>(4) persons who keep or store in a motor vehicle pistols in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.714">624.714</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.715">624.715</a> or other firearms in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/97B.045">97B.045</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) firearm safety or marksmanship courses or activities conducted on school property;</p>
          <p>(6) possession of dangerous weapons, BB guns, or replica firearms by a ceremonial color guard;</p>
          <p>(7) a gun or knife show held on school property;</p>
          <p>(8) possession of dangerous weapons, BB guns, or replica firearms with written permission of the principal or other person having general control and supervision of the school or the director of a child care center; or</p>
          <p>(9) persons who are on unimproved property owned or leased by a child care center, school, or school district unless the person knows that a student is currently present on the land for a school-related activity.</p>
          <p>(g) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/471.634">471.634</a>, a school district or other entity composed exclusively of school districts may not regulate firearms, ammunition, or their respective components, when possessed or carried by nonstudents or nonemployees, in a manner that is inconsistent with this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1e">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1e.<span class="headnote">Felony; drive-by shooting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony who, while in or having just exited from a motor vehicle, recklessly discharges a firearm at or toward:</p>
          <p>(1) an unoccupied motor vehicle or building;</p>
          <p>(2) an occupied motor vehicle or building; or</p>
          <p>(3) a person.</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted under paragraph (a), clause (1), may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $6,000, or both. A person convicted under paragraph (a), clause (2) or (3), may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this subdivision, "motor vehicle" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, and "building" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.581#stat.609.581.2">609.581, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1f">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1f.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor; transferring firearm without background check.</span></h2>
          <p>A person, other than a federally licensed firearms dealer, who transfers a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to another without complying with the transfer requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.7132">624.7132</a>, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the transferee possesses or uses the weapon within one year after the transfer in furtherance of a felony crime of violence, and if:</p>
          <p>(1) the transferee was prohibited from possessing the weapon under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713">624.713</a> at the time of the transfer; or</p>
          <p>(2) it was reasonably foreseeable at the time of the transfer that the transferee was likely to use or possess the weapon in furtherance of a felony crime of violence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1g">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1g.<span class="headnote">Felony; possession in courthouse or certain state buildings.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who commits either of the following acts is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) possesses a dangerous weapon, ammunition, or explosives within any courthouse complex; or</p>
          <p>(2) possesses a dangerous weapon, ammunition, or explosives in any state building within the Capitol Area described in chapter 15B, other than the National Guard Armory.</p>
          <p>(b) Unless a person is otherwise prohibited or restricted by other law to possess a dangerous weapon, this subdivision does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) licensed peace officers or military personnel who are performing official duties;</p>
          <p>(2) persons who carry pistols according to the terms of a permit issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.714">624.714</a> and who so notify the sheriff or the commissioner of public safety, as appropriate;</p>
          <p>(3) persons who possess dangerous weapons for the purpose of display as demonstrative evidence during testimony at a trial or hearing or exhibition in compliance with advance notice and safety guidelines set by the sheriff or the commissioner of public safety; or</p>
          <p>(4) persons who possess dangerous weapons in a courthouse complex with the express consent of the county sheriff or who possess dangerous weapons in a state building with the express consent of the commissioner of public safety.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this subdivision, the issuance of a permit to carry under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.714">624.714</a> constitutes notification of the commissioner of public safety as required under paragraph (b), clause (2).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.1h">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1h.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.3.38.0">2015 c 65 art 3 s 38</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.66.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in this section prohibits the possession of the articles mentioned by museums or collectors of art or for other lawful purposes of public exhibition.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.661">
        <h1 class="shn">609.661 PENALTY FOR SET GUNS; SWIVEL GUNS.</h1>
        <p>A person who violates a provision relating to set guns or swivel guns is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.661.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/386/#laws.4.31.0">1986 c 386 art 4 s 31</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.662">
        <h1 class="shn">609.662 SHOOTING VICTIM; DUTY TO RENDER AID.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.662.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "reasonable assistance" means aid appropriate to the circumstances, and includes obtaining or attempting to obtain assistance from a conservation or law enforcement officer, or from medical personnel.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.662.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duty to render aid.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who discharges a firearm and knows or has reason to know that the discharge has caused bodily harm to another person, shall:</p>
          <p>(1) immediately investigate the extent of the person's injuries; and</p>
          <p>(2) render immediate reasonable assistance to the injured person.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates this subdivision is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the injured person suffered death or great bodily harm as a result of the discharge, to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the injured person suffered substantial bodily harm as a result of the discharge, to imprisonment for not more than one year and one day or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(3) otherwise, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.035">609.035</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction under this subdivision is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.662.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Duty of witness.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who witnesses the discharge of a firearm and knows or has reason to know that the discharge caused bodily harm to a person shall:</p>
          <p>(1) immediately investigate the extent of the injuries; and</p>
          <p>(2) render immediate reasonable assistance to the injured person.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates this subdivision is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the defendant was a companion of the person who discharged the firearm at the time of the discharge, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) otherwise, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.662.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant failed to investigate or render assistance as required under this section because the defendant reasonably perceived that these actions could not be taken without a significant risk of bodily harm to the defendant or others.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.662.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/623/#laws.5.3.0">1994 c 623 art 5 s 3</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.662.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/243/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 243 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.663">
        <h1 class="shn">609.663 DISPLAY OF HANDGUN AMMUNITION.</h1>
        <p>It is a petty misdemeanor to display centerfire metallic-case handgun ammunition for sale to the public in a manner that makes the ammunition directly accessible to persons under the age of 18 years, other than employees or agents of the seller, unless the display is under observation of the seller or the seller's employee or agent, or the seller takes reasonable steps to exclude underage persons from the immediate vicinity of the display. Ammunition displayed in an enclosed display case or behind a counter is not directly accessible. This section does not apply to ammunition suitable for big game hunting.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.663.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/251/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 251 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.665">
        <h1 class="shn">609.665 SPRING GUNS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever sets a spring gun, pitfall, deadfall, snare, or other like dangerous weapon or device may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than six months or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.665.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.665; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.666">
        <h1 class="shn">609.666 NEGLIGENT STORAGE OF FIREARMS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.666.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, the following words have the meanings given.</p>
