          <p>(a) "Firearm" means a device designed to be used as a weapon, from which is expelled a projectile by the force of any explosion or force of combustion.</p>
          <p>(b) "Child" means a person under the age of 18 years.</p>
          <p>(c) "Loaded" means the firearm has ammunition in the chamber or magazine, if the magazine is in the firearm, unless the firearm is incapable of being fired by a child who is likely to gain access to the firearm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.666.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Access to firearms.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who negligently stores or leaves a loaded firearm in a location where the person knows, or reasonably should know, that a child is likely to gain access, unless reasonable action is taken to secure the firearm against access by the child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.666.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Limitations.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivision 2 does not apply to a child's access to firearms that was obtained as a result of an unlawful entry.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.666.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.18.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.4.11.0">1996 c 408 art 4 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.667">
        <h1 class="shn">609.667 FIREARMS; REMOVAL OR ALTERATION OF SERIAL NUMBER.</h1>
        <p>Whoever commits any of the following acts may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) obliterates, removes, changes, or alters the serial number or other identification of a firearm;</p>
        <p>(2) receives or possesses a firearm, the serial number or other identification of which has been obliterated, removed, changed, or altered; or</p>
        <p>(3) receives or possesses a firearm that is not identified by a serial number.</p>
        <p>As used in this section, "serial number or other identification" means the serial number and other information required under United States Code, title 26, section 5842, for the identification of firearms.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.667.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.3.22.0">1994 c 636 art 3 s 22</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.668">
        <h1 class="shn">609.668 EXPLOSIVE AND INCENDIARY DEVICES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(a) "Explosive device" means a device so articulated that an ignition by fire, friction, concussion, chemical reaction, or detonation of any part of the device may cause such sudden generation of highly heated gases that the resultant gaseous pressures are capable of producing destructive effects. Explosive devices include, but are not limited to, bombs, grenades, rockets having a propellant charge of more than four ounces, mines, and fireworks modified for other than their intended purpose. The term includes devices that produce a chemical reaction that produces gas capable of bursting its container and producing destructive effects. The term does not include firearms ammunition.</p>
          <p>(b) "Incendiary device" means a device so articulated that an ignition by fire, friction, concussion, detonation, or other method may produce destructive effects primarily through combustion rather than explosion. The term does not include a manufactured device or article in common use by the general public that is designed to produce combustion for a lawful purpose, including but not limited to matches, lighters, flares, or devices commercially manufactured primarily for the purpose of illumination, heating, or cooking. The term does not include firearms ammunition.</p>
          <p>(c) "Crime of violence" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.712#stat.624.712.5">624.712, subdivision 5</a>, and also includes a domestic assault conviction when committed within the last three years or while an order for protection is active against the person, whichever period is longer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Possession by certain persons prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>The following persons are prohibited from possessing or reporting an explosive device or incendiary device:</p>
          <p>(a) a person under the age of 18 years;</p>
          <p>(b) a person who has been convicted in this state or elsewhere of a crime of violence unless ten years have elapsed since the person's civil rights have been restored or the sentence has expired, whichever occurs first, and during that time the person has not been convicted of any other crime of violence. For purposes of this section, crime of violence includes crimes in other states or jurisdictions that would have been crimes of violence if they had been committed in this state;</p>
          <p>(c) a person who is or has ever been confined or committed in Minnesota or elsewhere as a person who is mentally ill, developmentally disabled, or mentally ill and dangerous to the public, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.02">253B.02</a>, to a treatment facility, unless the person possesses a certificate of a medical doctor or psychiatrist licensed in Minnesota, or other satisfactory proof, that the person is no longer suffering from this disability;</p>
          <p>(d) a person who has been convicted in Minnesota or elsewhere for the unlawful use, possession, or sale of a controlled substance other than conviction for possession of a small amount of marijuana, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01#stat.152.01.16">152.01, subdivision 16</a>, or who is or has ever been hospitalized or committed for treatment for the habitual use of a controlled substance or marijuana, as defined in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.01">152.01</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.02">152.02</a>, unless the person possesses a certificate of a medical doctor or psychiatrist licensed in Minnesota, or other satisfactory proof, that the person has not abused a controlled substance or marijuana during the previous two years;</p>
          <p>(e) a person who has been confined or committed to a treatment facility in Minnesota or elsewhere as chemically dependent, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.02">253B.02</a>, unless the person has completed treatment; and</p>
          <p>(f) a peace officer who is informally admitted to a treatment facility under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/253B.04">253B.04</a> for chemical dependency, unless the officer possesses a certificate from the head of the treatment facility discharging or provisionally discharging the officer from the treatment facility.</p>
          <p>A person who in good faith issues a certificate to a person described in this subdivision to possess or use an incendiary or explosive device is not liable for damages resulting or arising from the actions or misconduct with an explosive or incendiary device committed by the individual who is the subject of the certificate.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Uses permitted.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The following persons may own or possess an explosive device or incendiary device provided that subdivision 4 is complied with:</p>
          <p>(1) law enforcement officers for use in the course of their duties;</p>
          <p>(2) fire department personnel for use in the course of their duties;</p>
          <p>(3) corrections officers and other personnel at correctional facilities or institutions when used for the retention of persons convicted or accused of crime;</p>
          <p>(4) persons possessing explosive devices or incendiary devices that although designed as devices have been determined by the commissioner of public safety or the commissioner's delegate, by reason of the date of manufacture, value, design, or other characteristics, to be a collector's item, relic, museum piece, or specifically used in a particular vocation or employment, such as the entertainment industry; and</p>
          <p>(5) dealers and manufacturers who are federally licensed or registered.</p>
          <p>(b) Persons listed in paragraph (a) shall also comply with the federal requirements for the registration and licensing of destructive devices.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Report required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Before owning or possessing an explosive device or incendiary device as authorized by subdivision 3, a person shall file a written report with the Department of Public Safety showing the person's name and address; the person's title, position, and type of employment; a description of the explosive device or incendiary device sufficient to enable identification of the device; the purpose for which the device will be owned or possessed; the federal license or registration number, if appropriate; and other information as the department may require.</p>
          <p>(b) Before owning or possessing an explosive device or incendiary device, a dealer or manufacturer shall file a written report with the Department of Public Safety showing the name and address of the dealer or manufacturer; the federal license or registration number, if appropriate; the general type and disposition of the device; and other information as the department may require.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) members of the armed forces of either the United States or the state of Minnesota when for use in the course of duties;</p>
          <p>(2) educational institutions when the devices are manufactured or used in conjunction with an official education course or program;</p>
          <p>(3) propellant-actuated devices, or propellant-actuated industrial tools manufactured, imported, or distributed for their intended purpose;</p>
          <p>(4) items that are neither designed or redesigned for use as explosive devices or incendiary devices;</p>
          <p>(5) governmental organizations using explosive devices or incendiary devices for agricultural purposes or control of wildlife;</p>
          <p>(6) governmental organizations using explosive devices or incendiary devices for official training purposes or as items retained as evidence; or</p>
          <p>(7) arsenals, navy yards, depots, or other establishments owned by, or operated by or on behalf of, the United States.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Acts prohibited; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in this section, whoever possesses, manufactures, transports, or stores an explosive device or incendiary device in violation of this section may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever legally possesses, manufactures, transports, or stores an explosive device or incendiary device, with intent to use the device to damage property or cause injury, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) Whoever, acting with gross disregard for human life or property, negligently causes an explosive device or incendiary device to be discharged, may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.668.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/2/#laws.1.45.0">2003 c 2 art 1 s 45</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.668.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.5.15.0">1994 c 636 art 5 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/221/#laws.0.47.0">2002 c 221 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.669">
        <h1 class="shn">609.669 CIVIL DISORDER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.669.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Prohibited acts.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who:</p>
          <p>(1) teaches or demonstrates to any other person how to use or make any firearm, or explosive or incendiary device capable of causing injury or death, knowing or having reason to know that it will be unlawfully employed for use in, or in furtherance of, a civil disorder; or</p>
          <p>(2) assembles with one or more persons for the purpose of training with, practicing with, or being instructed in the use of any firearm, or explosive or incendiary device capable of causing injury or death, with the intent that it be unlawfully employed for use in, or in furtherance of, a civil disorder.</p>
          <p>(b) This section does not apply to law enforcement officers engaged in the lawful performance of the officer's official duties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.669.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them:</p>
          <p>(1) "civil disorder" means any public disturbance involving acts of violence by assemblages of three or more persons, which causes an immediate danger of or results in damage or injury to the property or person of any other individual;</p>
          <p>(2) "firearm" means any weapon which is designed to or may readily be converted to expel any projectile by the action of an explosive; or the frame or receiver of any such weapon;</p>
          <p>(3) "explosive or incendiary device" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.668#stat.609.668.1">609.668, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) "law enforcement officer" means any officer or employee of the United States, the state, or any political subdivision of the state, and specifically includes members of the National Guard and members of the armed forces of the United States.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.669.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/244/#laws.0.23.0">1995 c 244 s 23</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.67">
        <h1 class="shn">609.67 MACHINE GUNS AND SHORT-BARRELED SHOTGUNS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.67.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Machine gun" means any firearm designed to discharge, or capable of discharging automatically more than once by a single function of the trigger.</p>
          <p>(b) "Shotgun" means a weapon designed, redesigned, made or remade which is intended to be fired from the shoulder and uses the energy of the explosive in a fixed shotgun shell to fire through a smooth bore either a number of ball shot or a single projectile for each single pull of the trigger.</p>
          <p>(c) "Short-barreled shotgun" means a shotgun having one or more barrels less than 18 inches in length and any weapon made from a shotgun if such weapon as modified has an overall length less than 26 inches.</p>
          <p>(d) "Trigger activator" means:</p>
          <p>(1) a removable manual or power driven trigger activating device constructed and designed so that, when attached to a firearm, the rate at which the trigger may be pulled increases and the rate of fire of the firearm increases to that of a machine gun;</p>
          <p>(2) a device that allows a semiautomatic firearm to shoot more than one shot with a single pull of the trigger or by harnessing the recoil of energy of the semiautomatic firearm to which it is affixed so that the trigger resets and continues firing without additional physical manipulation of the trigger; or</p>
          <p>(3) a device that allows a firearm to shoot one shot on the pull of the trigger and a second shot on the release of the trigger without requiring a subsequent pull of the trigger.</p>
          <p>(e) "Machine gun conversion kit" means any part or combination of parts designed and intended for use in converting a weapon into a machine gun, and any combination of parts from which a machine gun can be assembled, but does not include a spare or replacement part for a machine gun that is possessed lawfully under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.67#stat.609.67.3">609.67, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.67.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided herein, whoever owns, possesses, or operates a machine gun, or any trigger activator or machine gun conversion kit may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Except as otherwise provided herein, whoever owns, possesses, or operates a short-barreled shotgun may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.67.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Uses permitted.</span></h2>
          <p>The following persons may own or possess a machine gun or short-barreled shotgun provided the provisions of subdivision 4 are complied with:</p>
          <p>(1) law enforcement officers for use in the course of their duties;</p>
          <p>(2) chief executive officers of correctional facilities and other personnel thereof authorized by them and persons in charge of other institutions for the retention of persons convicted or accused of crime, for use in the course of their duties;</p>
          <p>(3) persons possessing machine guns or short-barreled shotguns which, although designed as weapons, have been determined by the superintendent of the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension or the superintendent's delegate by reason of the date of manufacture, value, design or other characteristics to be primarily collector's items, relics, museum pieces or objects of curiosity, ornaments or keepsakes, and are not likely to be used as weapons;</p>
          <p>(4) manufacturers of ammunition who possess and use machine guns for the sole purpose of testing ammunition manufactured for sale to federal and state agencies or political subdivisions;</p>
          <p>(5) dealers and manufacturers who are federally licensed to buy and sell, or manufacture machine guns or short-barreled shotguns and who either use the machine guns or short-barreled shotguns in peace officer training under courses approved by the Board of Peace Officer Standards and Training, or are engaged in the sale of machine guns or short-barreled shotguns to federal and state agencies or political subdivisions; and</p>
          <p>(6) persons employed by the Minnesota National Guard as security guards, for use in accordance with applicable federal military regulations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.67.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Report required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person owning or possessing a machine gun or short-barreled shotgun as authorized by subdivision 3, clause (1), (2), (3), or (4) shall, within ten days after acquiring such ownership or possession, file a written report with the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, showing the person's name and address; the person's official title and position, if any; a description of the machine gun or short-barreled shotgun sufficient to enable identification thereof; the purpose for which it is owned or possessed; and such further information as the bureau may reasonably require.</p>
          <p>(b) A dealer or manufacturer owning or having a machine gun or short-barreled shotgun as authorized by subdivision 3, clause (5) shall, by the tenth day of each month, file a written report with the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension showing the name and address of the dealer or manufacturer and the serial number of each machine gun or short-barreled shotgun acquired or manufactured during the previous month.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.67.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to members of the armed services of either the United States or the state of Minnesota for use in the course of their duties or to security guards employed by the Minnesota National Guard for use in accordance with applicable federal military regulations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.67.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Preemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Laws 1977, chapter 255, supersedes all local ordinances, rules, and regulations.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.67.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.67; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/255/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 255 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/102/#laws.0.13.0">1979 c 102 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/93/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 93 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/439/#laws.0.5.0">1990 c 439 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.19.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 19</a>,20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/366/#laws.0.10.0">1993 c 366 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/273/#laws.0.11.0">2006 c 273 s 11</a>,12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.15.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 15</a>,16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.36.2.0">2024 c 127 art 36 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.671">
        <h1 class="shn">609.671 ENVIRONMENT; CRIMINAL PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The definitions in this subdivision apply to this section.</p>
          <p>(b) "Agency" means the Pollution Control Agency.</p>
          <p>(c) "Deliver" or "delivery" means the transfer of possession of hazardous waste, with or without consideration.</p>
          <p>(d) "Dispose" or "disposal" has the meaning given it in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115A.03#stat.115A.03.9">115A.03, subdivision 9</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) "Hazardous air pollutant" means an air pollutant listed under United States Code, title 42, section 7412(b).</p>
          <p>(f) "Hazardous waste" means any waste identified as hazardous under the authority of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.07#stat.116.07.4">116.07, subdivision 4</a>, except for those wastes exempted under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/7045.0120">7045.0120</a>, wastes generated under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/7045.0213">7045.0213</a>, and household appliances.</p>
          <p>(g) "Permit" means a permit issued by the Pollution Control Agency under chapter 115 or 116 or the rules promulgated under those chapters including interim status for hazardous waste facilities.</p>
          <p>(h) "Solid waste" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.06#stat.116.06.22">116.06, subdivision 22</a>.</p>
          <p>(i) "Toxic pollutant" means a toxic pollutant on the list established under United States Code, title 33, section 1317.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definition of knowing.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, an act is committed knowingly if it is done voluntarily and is not the result of negligence, mistake, accident, or circumstances that are beyond the control of the defendant. Whether an act was knowing may be inferred from the person's conduct, from the person's familiarity with the subject matter in question, or from all of the facts and circumstances connected with the case. Knowledge may also be established by evidence that the person took affirmative steps to shield the person from relevant information. Proof of knowledge does not require that a person knew a particular act or failure to act was a violation of law or that the person had specific knowledge of the regulatory limits or testing procedures involved in a case.</p>
          <p>(b) Knowledge of a corporate official may be established under paragraph (a) or by proof that the person is a responsible corporate official. To prove that a person is a responsible corporate official, it must be shown that:</p>
          <p>(1) the person is an official of the corporation, not merely an employee;</p>
          <p>(2) the person has direct control of or supervisory responsibility for the activities related to the alleged violation, but not solely that the person held a certain job or position in a corporation; and</p>
          <p>(3) the person had information regarding the offense for which the defendant is charged that would lead a reasonable and prudent person in the defendant's position to learn the actual facts.</p>
          <p>(c) Knowledge of a corporation may be established by showing that an illegal act was performed by an agent acting on behalf of the corporation within the scope of employment and in furtherance of the corporation's business interest, unless a high managerial person with direct supervisory authority over the agent demonstrated due diligence to prevent the crime's commission.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Knowing endangerment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony if the person:</p>
          <p>(1) commits an act described in subdivision 4, 5, 8, paragraph (a), or 12; and</p>
          <p>(2) at the time of the violation knowingly places another person in imminent danger of death, great bodily harm, or substantial bodily harm.</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted under this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both, except that a defendant that is an organization may be sentenced to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Hazardous waste; unlawful disposal or abandonment.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who knowingly disposes of or abandons hazardous waste or arranges for the disposal of hazardous waste at a location other than one authorized by the Pollution Control Agency or the United States Environmental Protection Agency, or in violation of any material term or condition of a hazardous waste facility permit, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Hazardous waste; unlawful treatment, storage, transportation, or delivery.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony who knowingly does any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) delivers hazardous waste to any person other than a person who is authorized to receive the waste under rules adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.07#stat.116.07.4">116.07, subdivision 4</a>, or under United States Code, title 42, sections 6921 to 6938;</p>
          <p>(2) treats or stores hazardous waste without a permit if a permit is required, or in violation of a material term or condition of a permit held by the person, unless:</p>
          <p>(i) the person notifies the agency prior to the time a permit would be required that the person will be treating or storing waste without a permit; or</p>
          <p>(ii) for a violation of a material term or condition of a permit, the person immediately notifies the agency issuing the permit of the circumstances of the violation as soon as the person becomes aware of the violation;</p>
          <p>(3) transports hazardous waste to any location other than a facility that is authorized to receive, treat, store, or dispose of the hazardous waste under rules adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.07#stat.116.07.4">116.07, subdivision 4</a>, or under United States Code, title 42, sections 6921 to 6938;</p>
          <p>(4) transports hazardous waste without a manifest as required by the rules under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.07#stat.116.07.4">116.07, subdivision 4</a>; or</p>
          <p>(5) transports hazardous waste without a license required for the transportation of hazardous waste by chapter 221.</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted under this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both. A person convicted for a second or subsequent offense may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Negligent violation as gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who commits any of the acts set forth in subdivision 4, 5, or 12 as a result of the person's gross negligence is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days, or to payment of a fine of not more than $15,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>When two or more offenses in violation of this section are committed by the same person in two or more counties within a two-year period, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Water pollution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony who knowingly:</p>
          <p>(1) causes the violation of an effluent standard or limitation for a toxic pollutant in a national pollutant discharge elimination system permit or state disposal system permit;</p>
          <p>(2) introduces into a sewer system or into a publicly owned treatment works a hazardous substance that the person knew or reasonably should have known is likely to cause personal injury or property damage; or</p>
          <p>(3) except in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements and permits, introduces into a sewer system or into a publicly owned treatment works a hazardous substance that causes the treatment works to violate an effluent limitation or condition of the treatment works' national pollutant discharge elimination system permit.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of paragraph (a), "hazardous substance" means a substance on the list established under United States Code, title 33, section 1321(b).</p>
          <p>(c) A person convicted under paragraph (a) may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000 per day of violation, or both.</p>
          <p>(d) A person is guilty of a crime who knowingly:</p>
          <p>(1) violates any effluent standard or limitation, or any water quality standard adopted by the agency;</p>
          <p>(2) violates any material term or condition of a national pollutant discharge elimination system permit or state disposal system permit;</p>
          <p>(3) fails to carry out any recording, reporting, monitoring, sampling, or information gathering requirement provided for under chapter 115 or 116; or</p>
          <p>(4) fails to file a discharge monitoring report or other document required for compliance with a national pollutant discharge elimination system or state disposal system permit.</p>
          <p>(e) A person convicted under paragraph (d) may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days, or to payment of a fine of not less than $2,500 and not more than $25,000 per day of violation, or both. A person convicted for a second or subsequent offense may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000 per day of violation, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">False statements; tampering.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony who knowingly:</p>
          <p>(1) makes any false material statement, representation, or certification in; omits material information from; or alters, conceals, or fails to file or maintain a notice, application, record, report, plan, manifest, permit, license, or other document required under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103F.701">103F.701</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103F.755">103F.755</a>; chapter 115 or 116; the hazardous waste transportation requirements of chapter 221; or rules adopted under these laws; or</p>
          <p>(2) falsifies, tampers with, renders inaccurate, or fails to install any monitoring device or method required to be maintained or followed for the purpose of compliance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103F.701">103F.701</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103F.755">103F.755</a>, chapter 115 or 116, or rules adopted under these laws.</p>
          <p>(b) Except as provided in paragraph (c), a person convicted under this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) A person convicted under this subdivision for a violation related to a notice or report required by an air permit issued by the agency as provided in United States Code, title 42, section 7661a(a), as amended through January 1, 1991, may be sentenced to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000 per day of violation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Failure to report release of hazardous substance or extremely hazardous substance.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is, upon conviction, subject to a fine of up to $25,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, who:</p>
          <p>(1) is required to report the release of a hazardous substance under United States Code, title 42, section 9603, or the release of an extremely hazardous substance under United States Code, title 42, section 11004;</p>
          <p>(2) knows that a hazardous substance or an extremely hazardous substance has been released; and</p>
          <p>(3) fails to provide immediate notification of the release of a reportable quantity of a hazardous substance or an extremely hazardous substance to the state emergency response center and, if directed by the center, to notify a local 911 emergency dispatch center.</p>
          <p>For purposes of clause (3), the state emergency response center shall direct a caller to notify a local 911 emergency dispatch center if the situation requires an immediate response or the area is unknown to the center. In all other cases, the state emergency response center must notify a local firefighting or law enforcement organization of the situation within 24 hours of receiving the notification.</p>
          <p>(b) For a second or subsequent conviction under this subdivision, the violator is subject to a fine of up to $50,000 or imprisonment for not more than five years, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this subdivision, a "hazardous substance" means a substance on the list established under United States Code, title 42, section 9602.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this subdivision, an "extremely hazardous substance" means a substance on the list established under United States Code, title 42, section 11002.</p>
          <p>(e) For purposes of this subdivision, a "reportable quantity" means a quantity that must be reported under United States Code, title 42, section 9602 or 11002.</p>
          <p>(f) The penalties in paragraphs (a) and (b) do not apply to an employee of a state emergency response center to the extent that the employee is acting in the scope of that employee's official duties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Infectious waste.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who knowingly disposes of or arranges for the disposal of infectious waste as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.76">116.76</a> at a location or in a manner that is prohibited by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/116.78">116.78</a> is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days, or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both. A person convicted a second or subsequent time under this subdivision is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Air pollution.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a felony who knowingly:</p>
          <p>(1) causes a violation of a national emission standard for a hazardous air pollutant adopted under United States Code, title 42, section 7412; or</p>
          <p>(2) causes a violation of an emission standard, limitation, or operational limitation for a hazardous air pollutant established in a permit issued by the Pollution Control Agency.</p>
          <p>A person convicted under this paragraph may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years, or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000 per day of violation, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a misdemeanor who knowingly violates:</p>
          <p>(1) a requirement of chapter 116, or a rule adopted under that chapter, that is an applicable requirement of the federal Clean Air Act, as defined in Federal Register, volume 57, page 32295;</p>
          <p>(2) a condition of an air emission permit issued by the agency under chapter 116 or a rule adopted under that chapter; or</p>
          <p>(3) a requirement to pay a fee based on air emissions under chapter 116 or a rule adopted under that chapter.</p>
          <p>A person convicted under this paragraph may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000 per day of violation, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Solid waste disposal.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who:</p>
          <p>(1) knowingly disposes of solid waste at, transports solid waste to, or arranges for disposal of solid waste at a location that does not have a required permit for the disposal of solid waste; and</p>
          <p>(2) does so in exchange for or in expectation of money or other consideration.</p>
          <p>(b) A person convicted under this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days, or to payment of a fine of not more than $15,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.671.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>Except for intentional violations, a person is not guilty of a crime for air quality violations under subdivision 6 or 12, or for water quality violations under subdivision 8, if the person notified the Pollution Control Agency of the violation as soon as the person discovered the violation and took steps to promptly remedy the violation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.671.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/267/#laws.0.3.0">1987 c 267 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/553/#laws.0.2.0">1988 c 553 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/315/#laws.0.11.0">1989 c 315 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/337/#laws.0.12.0">1989 c 337 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/391/#laws.10.3.0">1990 c 391 art 10 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/347/#laws.3.4.0">1991 c 347 art 3 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/365/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 365 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/238/#laws.2.77.0">1999 c 238 art 2 s 77</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/212/#laws.3.40.0">2006 c 212 art 3 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/107/#laws.0.107.0">2011 c 107 s 107</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/92/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 92 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.672">
        <h1 class="shn">609.672 PERMISSIVE INFERENCE; FIREARMS IN AUTOMOBILES.</h1>
        <p>The presence of a firearm in a passenger automobile permits the fact finder to infer knowing possession of the firearm by the driver or person in control of the automobile when the firearm was in the automobile. The inference does not apply:</p>
        <p>(1) to a licensed operator of an automobile who is at the time operating it for hire in the lawful and proper pursuit of the operator's trade;</p>
        <p>(2) to any person in the automobile if one of them legally possesses a firearm; or</p>
        <p>(3) when the firearm is concealed on the person of one of the occupants.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.672.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.1.21.0">1993 c 326 art 1 s 21</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.675">
        <h1 class="shn">609.675 EXPOSURE OF UNUSED REFRIGERATOR OR CONTAINER TO CHILDREN.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, being the owner or in possession or control, permits an unused refrigerator or other container, sufficiently large to retain any child and with doors which fasten automatically when closed, to be exposed and accessible to children, without removing the doors, lids, hinges, or latches, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.675.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.675; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.67.0">1971 c 23 s 67</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.68">
        <h1 class="shn">609.68 UNLAWFUL DEPOSIT OF GARBAGE, LITTER, OR LIKE.</h1>
        <p>Whoever unlawfully deposits garbage, rubbish, cigarette filters, debris from fireworks, offal, or the body of a dead animal, or other litter in or upon any public highway, public waters or the ice thereon, shoreland areas adjacent to rivers or streams as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103F.205">103F.205</a>, public lands, or, without the consent of the owner, private lands or water or ice thereon, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.68.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.68; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.68.0">1971 c 23 s 68</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/685/#laws.0.36.0">1988 c 685 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/391/#laws.8.56.0">1990 c 391 art 8 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/28/#laws.1.19.0">2003 c 28 art 1 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.8.12.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 8 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.681">
        <h1 class="shn">609.681 UNLAWFUL SMOKING.</h1>
        <p>A person is guilty of a petty misdemeanor if the person intentionally smokes in a building, area, or common carrier in which "no smoking" notices have been prominently posted, or when requested not to by the operator of the common carrier.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.681.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.10.0">1989 c 5 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.8.13.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 8 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.684">
        <h1 class="shn">609.684 ABUSE OF TOXIC SUBSTANCES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.684.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Toxic substances.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "toxic substance" means:</p>
          <p>(1) glue, cement, or aerosol paint containing toluene, benzene, xylene, amyl nitrate, butyl nitrate, nitrous oxide, or containing other aromatic hydrocarbon solvents, but does not include glue, cement, or paint contained in a packaged kit for the construction of a model automobile, airplane, or similar item;</p>
          <p>(2) butane or a butane lighter; or</p>
          <p>(3) any similar substance declared to be toxic to the central nervous system and to have a potential for abuse, by a rule adopted by the commissioner of health under chapter 14.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.684.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.25.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.684.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Use for intoxication prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor who uses or possesses any toxic substance with the intent of inducing intoxication, excitement, or stupefaction of the central nervous system, except under the direction and supervision of a medical doctor. A person is guilty of a misdemeanor who intentionally aids another in violation of this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.684.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notice required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A business establishment that offers for sale at retail any toxic substance must display a conspicuous sign that contains the following, or substantially similar, language:</p>
          <p class="ce">"NOTICE</p>
          <p class="bl">It is a misdemeanor for a person to use or possess glue, cement, aerosol paint, with the intent of inducing intoxication, excitement, or stupefaction of the central nervous system. This use can be harmful or fatal."</p>
          <p>(b) A business establishment may omit from the required notice references to any toxic substance that is not offered for sale by that business establishment.</p>
          <p>(c) A business establishment that does not sell any toxic substance listed in subdivision 1 other than butane or butane lighters is not required to post a notice under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.684.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/485/#laws.0.2.0">1992 c 485 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.18.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 18</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.685">
        <h1 class="shn">609.685 SALE OF TOBACCO TO PERSONS UNDER AGE 21.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, the following terms shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them in this section.</p>
          <p>(a) "Tobacco" means cigarettes and any product containing, made, or derived from tobacco that is intended for human consumption, whether chewed, smoked, absorbed, dissolved, inhaled, snorted, sniffed, or ingested by any other means, or any component, part, or accessory of a tobacco product including but not limited to cigars; cheroots; stogies; perique; granulated, plug cut, crimp cut, ready rubbed, and other smoking tobacco; snuff; snuff flour; cavendish; plug and twist tobacco; fine cut and other chewing tobaccos; shorts; refuse scraps, clippings, cuttings and sweepings of tobacco; and other kinds and forms of tobacco. Tobacco excludes any drugs, devices, or combination products, as those terms are defined in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, that are authorized for sale by the United States Food and Drug Administration.</p>
          <p>(b) "Tobacco-related devices" means cigarette papers or pipes for smoking or other devices intentionally designed or intended to be used in a manner which enables the chewing, sniffing, smoking, or inhalation of aerosol or vapor of tobacco or tobacco products. Tobacco-related devices include components of tobacco-related devices which may be marketed or sold separately.</p>
          <p>(c) "Electronic delivery device" means any product containing or delivering nicotine, lobelia, or any other substance, whether natural or synthetic, intended for human consumption through inhalation of aerosol or vapor from the product. Electronic delivery device includes but is not limited to devices manufactured, marketed, or sold as electronic cigarettes, electronic cigars, electronic pipe, vape pens, modes, tank systems, or under any other product name or descriptor. Electronic delivery device includes any component part of a product, whether or not marketed or sold separately. Electronic delivery device excludes drugs, devices, or combination products, as those terms are defined in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, that are authorized for sale by the United States Food and Drug Administration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Penalty to sell or furnish.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any person 21 years of age or older who sells, gives, or otherwise furnishes tobacco, tobacco-related devices, or electronic delivery devices to a person under the age of 21 years is guilty of a petty misdemeanor for the first violation. Whoever violates this subdivision a subsequent time within five years of a previous conviction under this subdivision is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this subdivision if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant reasonably and in good faith relied on proof of age as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.503#stat.340A.503.6">340A.503, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of false identification.</span></h2>
          <p> A person under the age of 21 years who purchases or attempts to purchase tobacco, tobacco-related devices, or electronic delivery devices and who uses a driver's license, permit, Minnesota identification card, or any type of false identification to misrepresent the person's age, shall only be subject to an alternative civil penalty, in accordance with subdivision 2a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Alternative penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Law enforcement and court system representatives shall consult, as applicable, with interested persons, including but not limited to parents, guardians, educators, and persons under the age of 21 years, to develop alternative civil penalties for persons under the age of 21 years who violate this section. Consulting participants shall consider a variety of alternative civil penalties including but not limited to tobacco-free education programs, community service, court diversion programs, and tobacco cessation programs, and for persons under the age of 18 years, notice to schools and to parents or guardians. Alternative civil penalties developed under this subdivision shall not include fines or monetary penalties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/88/#laws.0.11.0">2020 c 88 s 11</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Effect on local ordinances.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in subdivisions 1 to 2a shall supersede or preclude the continuation or adoption of any local ordinance which provides for more stringent regulation of the subject matter in subdivisions 1 to 2a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding subdivision 1a, an Indian may furnish tobacco to an Indian under the age of 21 years if the tobacco is furnished as part of a traditional Indian spiritual or cultural ceremony. For purposes of this paragraph, an Indian is a person who is a member of an Indian tribe as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260.755#stat.260.755.12">260.755, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The penalties in this section do not apply to a person under the age of 21 years who purchases or attempts to purchase tobacco, tobacco-related devices, or electronic delivery devices while under the direct supervision of a responsible adult for training, education, research, or enforcement purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.685.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Seizure of false identification.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee may seize a form of identification listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.503#stat.340A.503.6">340A.503, subdivision 6</a>, if the licensee has reasonable grounds to believe that the form of identification has been altered or falsified or is being used to violate any law. A licensee that seizes a form of identification as authorized under this subdivision shall deliver it to a law enforcement agency within 24 hours of seizing it.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.685.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.685; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/218/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 218 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/352/#laws.0.4.0">1986 c 352 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.3.33.0">1989 c 290 art 3 s 33</a>,34; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/588/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 588 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/224/#laws.9.44.0">1993 c 224 art 9 s 44</a>,45; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.44.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/139/#laws.4.2.0">1999 c 139 art 4 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/472/#laws.0.5.0">2000 c 472 s 5</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/305/#laws.0.11.0">2010 c 305 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.33.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/88/#laws.0.11.0">2020 c 88 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.6855">
        <h1 class="shn">609.6855 SALE OF NICOTINE DELIVERY PRODUCTS TO PERSONS UNDER AGE 21.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6855.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Penalty to sell or furnish.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any person 21 years of age or older who sells, gives, or otherwise furnishes to a person under the age of 21 years a product containing or delivering nicotine or lobelia, whether natural or synthetic, intended for human consumption, or any part of such a product, that is not tobacco or an electronic delivery device as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685">609.685</a>, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor for the first violation. Whoever violates this subdivision a subsequent time within five years of a previous conviction under this subdivision is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this subdivision if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant reasonably and in good faith relied on proof of age as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.503#stat.340A.503.6">340A.503, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a product containing or delivering nicotine or lobelia intended for human consumption, whether natural or synthetic, or any part of such a product, that is not tobacco or an electronic delivery device as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685">609.685</a>, may be sold to persons under the age of 21 if the product is a drug, device, or combination product, as those terms are defined in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, that is authorized for sale by the United States Food and Drug Administration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6855.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of false identification.</span></h2>
          <p>A person under the age of 21 years who purchases or attempts to purchase a product containing or delivering nicotine or lobelia intended for human consumption, or any part of such a product, that is not tobacco or an electronic delivery device as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685">609.685</a>, and who uses a driver's license, permit, Minnesota identification card, or any type of false identification to misrepresent the person's age, shall only be subject to an alternative civil penalty in accordance with subdivision 3. No penalty shall apply to a person under the age of 21 years who purchases or attempts to purchase these products while under the direct supervision of a responsible adult for training, education, research, or enforcement purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.6855.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Alternative penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Law enforcement and court system representatives shall consult, as applicable, with interested persons, including but not limited to parents, guardians, educators, and persons under the age of 21 years, to develop alternative civil penalties for persons under the age of 21 years who violate this section. Consulting participants shall consider a variety of alternative civil penalties including but not limited to tobacco-free education programs, community service, court diversion programs, and tobacco cessation programs, and for persons under the age of 18 years, notice to schools and to parents or guardians. Alternative civil penalties developed under this subdivision shall not include fines or monetary penalties.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.6855.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/305/#laws.0.12.0">2010 c 305 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.34.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/88/#laws.0.12.0">2020 c 88 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.686">
        <h1 class="shn">609.686 FALSE FIRE ALARMS; TAMPERING WITH OR INJURING FIRE ALARM SYSTEM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.686.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally gives a false alarm of fire, or unlawfully tampers or interferes with any fire alarm system, fire protection device, or the station or signal box of any fire alarm system or any auxiliary fire appliance, or unlawfully breaks, injures, defaces, or removes any such system, device, box or station, or unlawfully breaks, injures, destroys, disables, renders inoperable, or disturbs any of the wires, poles, or other supports and appliances connected with or forming a part of any fire alarm system or fire protection device or any auxiliary fire appliance is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.686.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 1 by tampering and knows or has reason to know that the tampering creates the potential for bodily harm or the tampering results in bodily harm is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.686.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Tampering.</span></h2>
          <p>For purpose of this section, tampering means to intentionally disable, alter, or change the fire alarm system, fire protective device, or the station or signal box of any fire alarm system of any auxiliary fire appliance, with knowledge that it will be disabled or rendered inoperable.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.686.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/77/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 77 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.5.10.0">1993 c 326 art 5 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">PUBLIC MISCONDUCT OR NUISANCE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.687">
        <h1 class="shn">609.687 ADULTERATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.687.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Adulteration" is the intentional adding of any substance, which has the capacity to cause death, bodily harm or illness by ingestion, injection, inhalation or absorption, to a substance having a customary or reasonably foreseeable human use.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.687.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever, knowing or having reason to know that the adulteration will cause or is capable of causing death, bodily harm or illness, adulterates any substance with the intent to cause death, bodily harm or illness is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3; or</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever, knowing or having reason to know that a substance has been adulterated as defined in subdivision 1, distributes, disseminates, gives, sells, or otherwise transfers an adulterated substance with the intent to cause death, bodily harm or illness is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.687.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the adulteration causes death, to imprisonment for not more than 40 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the adulteration causes any illness, pain, or other bodily harm, to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(3) otherwise, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.687.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Charging discretion.</span></h2>
          <p>Criminal proceedings may be instituted under this section, notwithstanding the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/29.24">29.24</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/31.02">31.02</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/31.601">31.601</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/34.01">34.01</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/151.34">151.34</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.508#stat.340A.508.2">340A.508, subdivision 2</a>, or other law proscribing adulteration of substances intended for use by persons.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.687.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/8/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 8 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/384/#laws.2.110.0">1987 c 384 art 2 s 110</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/64/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 64 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/2/#laws.0.148.0">1Sp2001 c 2 s 148</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.688">
        <h1 class="shn">609.688 ADULTERATION BY BODILY FLUID.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.688.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Adulterates" is the intentional adding of a bodily fluid to a substance.</p>
          <p>(c) "Bodily fluid" means the blood, seminal fluid, vaginal fluid, urine, or feces of a human.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.688.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever adulterates any substance that the person knows or should know is intended for human consumption is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever violates paragraph (a) and another person ingests the adulterated substance without knowledge of the adulteration is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.688.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/65/#laws.6.17.0">2015 c 65 art 6 s 17</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.705">
        <h1 class="shn">609.705 UNLAWFUL ASSEMBLY.</h1>
        <p>When three or more persons assemble, each participant is guilty of unlawful assembly, which is a misdemeanor, if the assembly is:</p>
        <p>(1) with intent to commit any unlawful act by force; or</p>
        <p>(2) with intent to carry out any purpose in such manner as will disturb or threaten the public peace; or</p>
        <p>(3) without unlawful purpose, but the participants so conduct themselves in a disorderly manner as to disturb or threaten the public peace.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.705.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.705; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.69.0">1971 c 23 s 69</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.71">
        <h1 class="shn">609.71 RIOT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.71.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Riot first degree.</span></h2>
          <p>When three or more persons assembled disturb the public peace by an intentional act or threat of unlawful force or violence to person or property and a death results, and one of the persons is armed with a dangerous weapon, that person is guilty of riot first degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $35,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.71.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Riot second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>When three or more persons assembled disturb the public peace by an intentional act or threat of unlawful force or violence to person or property, each participant who is armed with a dangerous weapon or knows that any other participant is armed with a dangerous weapon is guilty of riot second degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.71.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Riot third degree.</span></h2>
          <p>When three or more persons assembled disturb the public peace by an intentional act or threat of unlawful force or violence to person or property, each participant therein is guilty of riot third degree and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.71.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.71; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.33.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.712">
        <h1 class="shn">609.712 REAL AND SIMULATED WEAPONS OF MASS DESTRUCTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.712.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Biological agent" means any microorganism, virus, infectious substance, or biological product that may be engineered as a result of biotechnology, or any naturally occurring or bioengineered component of a microorganism, virus, infectious substance, or biological product, that is capable of causing:</p>
          <p>(1) death, disease, or other biological malfunction in a human, an animal, a plant, or another living organism;</p>
          <p>(2) deterioration of food, water, equipment, supplies, or material of any kind; or</p>
          <p>(3) deleterious alteration of the environment.</p>
          <p>(c) "Simulated weapon of mass destruction" means any device, substance, or object that by its design, construction, content, or characteristics, appears to be or to contain, or is represented to be, constitute, or contain, a weapon of mass destruction, but that is, in fact, an inoperative facsimile, imitation, counterfeit, or representation of a weapon of mass destruction that does not meet the definition of a weapon of mass destruction or that does not actually contain or constitute a weapon, biological agent, toxin, vector, or delivery system prohibited by this section.</p>
          <p>(d) "Toxin" means the toxic material of plants, animals, microorganisms, viruses, fungi, or infectious substances, or a recombinant molecule, whatever its origin or method of production, including:</p>
          <p>(1) any poisonous substance or biological product that may be engineered as a result of biotechnology or produced by a living organism; or</p>
          <p>(2) any poisonous isomer or biological product, homolog, or derivative of such a substance.</p>
          <p>(e) "Vector" means a living organism or molecule, including a recombinant molecule or biological product that may be engineered as a result of biotechnology, capable of carrying a biological agent or toxin to a host.</p>
          <p>(f) "Weapon of mass destruction" includes weapons, substances, devices, vectors, or delivery systems that:</p>
          <p>(1) are designed or have the capacity to cause death or great bodily harm to a considerable number of people through the release, dissemination, or impact of toxic or poisonous chemicals, or their precursors, disease organisms, biological agents, or toxins; or</p>
          <p>(2) are designed to release radiation or radioactivity at a level dangerous to human life.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.712.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Weapons of mass destruction.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever manufactures, acquires, possesses, or makes readily accessible to another a weapon of mass destruction with the intent to cause injury to another is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) It is an affirmative defense to criminal liability under this subdivision if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the conduct engaged in:</p>
          <p>(1) was specifically authorized under state or federal law and conducted in accordance with that law; or</p>
          <p>(2) was part of a legitimate scientific or medical research project, or constituted legitimate medical treatment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.712.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prohibited substances.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever knowingly manufactures, acquires, possesses, or makes readily accessible to another the following, or substances that are substantially similar in chemical makeup to the following, in levels dangerous to human life, is guilty of a crime:</p>
          <p>(1) variola major (smallpox);</p>
          <p>(2) <i>bacillus anthracis</i> (anthrax);</p>
          <p>(3) <i>yersinia pestis</i> (plague);</p>
          <p>(4) botulinum toxin (botulism);</p>
          <p>(5) <i>francisella tularensis</i> (tularemia);</p>
          <p>(6) viral hemorrhagic fevers;</p>
          <p>(7) a mustard agent;</p>
          <p>(8) lewisite;</p>
          <p>(9) hydrogen cyanide;</p>
          <p>(10) GA (Tabun);</p>
          <p>(11) GB (Sarin);</p>
          <p>(12) GD (Soman);</p>
          <p>(13) GF (cyclohexymethyl phosphonofluoridate);</p>
          <p>(14) VX (0-ethyl, supdiisopropylaminomethyl methylphosphonothiolate);</p>
          <p>(15) radioactive materials; or</p>
          <p>(16) any combination of the above.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates this subdivision may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(c) This subdivision does not apply to conduct:</p>
          <p>(1) specifically authorized under state or federal law and conducted in accordance with that law;</p>
          <p>(2) that is part of a legitimate scientific or medical research project; or</p>
          <p>(3) that constitutes legitimate medical treatment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.712.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Simulated weapons of mass destruction; penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever manufactures, acquires, possesses, or makes readily accessible to another a simulated weapon of mass destruction with the intent of terrorizing another may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.712.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Threats involving real or simulated weapons of mass destruction.</span></h2>
