      <div class="section" id="stat.609.7495">
        <h1 class="shn">609.7495 PHYSICAL INTERFERENCE WITH SAFE ACCESS TO HEALTH CARE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.7495.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(a) "Facility" means any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a hospital or other health institution licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a medical facility as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.561">144.561</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) an agency, clinic, or office operated under the direction of or under contract with the commissioner of health or a community health board, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02">145A.02</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) a facility providing counseling regarding options for medical services or recovery from an addiction;</p>
          <p>(5) a facility providing emergency shelter services for battered women, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.31#stat.611A.31.3">611A.31, subdivision 3</a>, or a facility providing transitional housing for battered women and their children;</p>
          <p>(6) a facility as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.03">260E.03</a>, subdivision 6;</p>
          <p>(7) a facility as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572#stat.626.5572.6">626.5572, subdivision 6</a>, where the services described in that paragraph are provided;</p>
          <p>(8) a place to or from which ambulance service, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144E.001">144E.001</a>, is provided or sought to be provided; and</p>
          <p>(9) a hospice provider licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.753">144A.753</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) "Aggrieved party" means a person whose access to or egress from a facility is obstructed in violation of subdivision 2, or the facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.7495.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Obstructing access prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor who intentionally and physically obstructs any individual's access to or egress from a facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.7495.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Not applicable.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in this section shall be construed to impair the right of any individual or group to engage in speech protected by the United States Constitution, the Minnesota Constitution, or federal or state law, including but not limited to peaceful and lawful handbilling and picketing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.7495.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Civil remedies.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A party who is aggrieved by an act prohibited by this section, or by an attempt or conspiracy to commit an act prohibited by this section, may bring an action for damages, injunctive or declaratory relief, as appropriate, in district court against any person or entity who has violated or has conspired to violate this section.</p>
          <p>(b) A party who prevails in a civil action under this subdivision is entitled to recover from the violator damages, costs, attorney fees, and other relief as determined by the court. In addition to all other damages, the court may award to the aggrieved party a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for each violation. If the aggrieved party is a facility and the political subdivision where the violation occurred incurred law enforcement or prosecution expenses in connection with the same violation, the court shall award any civil penalty it imposes to the political subdivision instead of to the facility.</p>
          <p>(c) The remedies provided by this subdivision are in addition to any other legal or equitable remedies the aggrieved party may have and are not intended to diminish or substitute for those remedies or to be exclusive.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.7495.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/284/#laws.0.2.0">1993 c 284 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.4.19.0">1995 c 229 art 4 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/199/#laws.0.14.0">1997 c 199 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.1.102.0">1998 c 254 art 1 s 102</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/252/#laws.0.22.0">2002 c 252 s 22</a>,24; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.1.126.0">2015 c 71 art 1 s 126</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.141.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 141</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">GAMBLING</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.75">
        <h1 class="shn">609.75 GAMBLING; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Lottery.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A lottery is a plan which provides for the distribution of money, property or other reward or benefit to persons selected by chance from among participants some or all of whom have given a consideration for the chance of being selected. A participant's payment for use of a 900 telephone number or another means of communication that results in payment to the sponsor of the plan constitutes consideration under this paragraph.</p>
          <p>(b) An in-package chance promotion is not a lottery if all of the following are met:</p>
          <p>(1) participation is available, free and without purchase of the package, from the retailer or by mail or toll-free telephone request to the sponsor for entry or for a game piece;</p>
          <p>(2) the label of the promotional package and any related advertising clearly states any method of participation and the scheduled termination date of the promotion;</p>
          <p>(3) the sponsor on request provides a retailer with a supply of entry forms or game pieces adequate to permit free participation in the promotion by the retailer's customers;</p>
          <p>(4) the sponsor does not misrepresent a participant's chances of winning any prize;</p>
          <p>(5) the sponsor randomly distributes all game pieces and maintains records of random distribution for at least one year after the termination date of the promotion;</p>
          <p>(6) all prizes are randomly awarded if game pieces are not used in the promotion; and</p>
          <p>(7) the sponsor provides on request of a state agency a record of the names and addresses of all winners of prizes valued at $100 or more, if the request is made within one year after the termination date of the promotion.</p>
          <p>(c) Except as provided by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299L.07">299L.07</a>, acts in this state in furtherance of a lottery conducted outside of this state are included notwithstanding its validity where conducted.</p>
          <p>(d) The distribution of property, or other reward or benefit by an employer to persons selected by chance from among participants, all of whom:</p>
          <p>(1) have made a contribution through a payroll or pension deduction campaign to a registered combined charitable organization, within the meaning of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/43A.50">43A.50</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) have paid other consideration to the employer entirely for the benefit of such a registered combined charitable organization, as a precondition to the chance of being selected, is not a lottery if:</p>
          <p>(i) all of the persons eligible to be selected are employed by or retirees of the employer; and</p>
          <p>(ii) the cost of the property or other reward or benefit distributed and all costs associated with the distribution are borne by the employer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Bet.</span></h2>
          <p>A bet is a bargain whereby the parties mutually agree to a gain or loss by one to the other of specified money, property or benefit dependent upon chance although the chance is accompanied by some element of skill.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">What are not bets.</span></h2>
          <p>The following are not bets:</p>
          <p>(1) a contract to insure, indemnify, guarantee or otherwise compensate another for a harm or loss sustained, even though the loss depends upon chance;</p>
          <p>(2) a contract for the purchase or sale at a future date of securities or other commodities;</p>
          <p>(3) offers of purses, prizes or premiums to the actual contestants in any bona fide contest for the determination of skill, speed, strength, endurance, or quality or to the bona fide owners of animals or other property entered in such a contest;</p>
          <p>(4) the game of bingo when conducted in compliance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.11">349.11</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.23">349.23</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) a private social bet not part of or incidental to organized, commercialized, or systematic gambling;</p>
          <p>(6) the operation of equipment or the conduct of a raffle under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.11">349.11</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.22">349.22</a>, by an organization licensed by the Gambling Control Board or an organization exempt from licensing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.166">349.166</a>;</p>
          <p>(7) pari-mutuel betting on horse racing when the betting is conducted under chapter 240; and</p>
          <p>(8) the purchase and sale of State Lottery tickets under chapter 349A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Gambling device.</span></h2>
          <p>A gambling device is a contrivance the purpose of which is that for a consideration a player is afforded an opportunity to obtain something of value, other than free plays, automatically from the machine or otherwise, the award of which is determined principally by chance, whether or not the contrivance is actually played. "Gambling device" also includes a video game of chance, as defined in subdivision 8.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Associated equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>Associated equipment means any equipment used in connection with gambling that would not be classified as a gambling device, including but not limited to: cards, dice, computerized systems of betting at a race book or sports pool, computerized systems for monitoring slot machines or games of chance, devices for weighing or counting money, and links which connect progressive slot machines.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Gambling place.</span></h2>
          <p>A gambling place is a location or structure, stationary or movable, or any part thereof, wherein, as one of its uses, betting is permitted or promoted, a lottery is conducted or assisted or a gambling device is operated.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Bucket shop.</span></h2>
          <p>A bucket shop is a place wherein the operator is engaged in making bets in the form of purchases or sales on public exchanges of securities, commodities or other personal property for future delivery to be settled at prices dependent on the chance of those prevailing at the public exchanges without a bona fide purchase or sale being in fact made on a board of trade or exchange.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Sports bookmaking.</span></h2>
          <p>Sports bookmaking is the activity of intentionally receiving, recording or forwarding within any 30-day period more than five bets, or offers to bet, that total more than $2,500 on any one or more sporting events.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Video game of chance.</span></h2>
          <p>A video game of chance is a game or device that simulates one or more games commonly referred to as poker, blackjack, craps, hi-lo, roulette, or other common gambling forms, though not offering any type of pecuniary award or gain to players. The term also includes any video game having one or more of the following characteristics:</p>
          <p>(1) it is primarily a game of chance, and has no substantial elements of skill involved;</p>
          <p>(2) it awards game credits or replays and contains a meter or device that records unplayed credits or replays. A video game that simulates horse racing that does not involve a prize payout is not a video game of chance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">900 telephone number.</span></h2>
          <p>A 900 telephone number is a ten-digit number, the first three numbers of which are from 900 to 999.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Game.</span></h2>
          <p>A game means any game played with cards, dice, equipment, or any mechanical or electronic device or machine for money or other value, whether or not approved by law, and includes, but is not limited to: card and dice games of chance, slot machines, banking or percentage games, video games of chance, sports pools, pari-mutuel betting, and race book. "Game" does not include any private social bet.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Authorized gambling activity.</span></h2>
          <p>An authorized gambling activity means any form of gambling authorized by and operated in conformance with law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Authorized gambling establishment.</span></h2>
          <p>An authorized gambling establishment means any premises where gambling authorized by law is occurring.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/29/#laws.0.9.0">2015 c 29 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Savings promotion raffle.</span></h2>
          <p>A "savings promotion raffle" means a contest or promotion in which a chance of winning designated prizes is obtained by the deposit of a specified amount of money in a savings account, share account, savings association, share certificate, or other savings program offered by a state or federally chartered credit union or bank.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Qualifying account.</span></h2>
          <p>"Qualifying account" means a savings account, share account, savings association, share certificate, or other savings program through which depositors may obtain chances to win prizes in a savings promotion raffle by depositing specified sums of money.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Nonqualifying account.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nonqualifying account" means a savings account, share account, savings association, share certificate, or other savings program that is not a qualifying account.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.75.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Applicability of definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.75">609.75</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.762">609.762</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.75.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.75; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/947/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 947 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/2/#laws.0.152.0">1976 c 2 s 152</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/239/#laws.0.126.0">1976 c 239 s 126</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/261/#laws.0.14.0">1976 c 261 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/336/#laws.0.5.0">2000 c 336 s 5</a>-9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/5/#laws.20.18.0">1Sp2001 c 5 art 20 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/166/#laws.1.37.0">2005 c 166 art 1 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/86/#laws.1.82.0">2009 c 86 art 1 s 82</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/29/#laws.0.4.0">2015 c 29 s 4</a>-7</p>

      <div class="section" id="stat.609.755">
        <h1 class="shn">609.755 GAMBLING; MISDEMEANOR.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
        <p>(1) makes a bet;</p>
        <p>(2) sells or transfers a chance to participate in a lottery;</p>
        <p>(3) disseminates information about a lottery, except a lottery conducted by an adjoining state, with intent to encourage participation therein;</p>
        <p>(4) permits a structure or location owned or occupied by the actor or under the actor's control to be used as a gambling place; or</p>
        <p>(5) except where authorized by statute, possesses a gambling device.</p>
        <p>Clause (5) does not prohibit possession of a gambling device in a person's dwelling for amusement purposes in a manner that does not afford players an opportunity to obtain anything of value.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.755.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609.755</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.76.0">1971 c 23 s 76</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/336/#laws.2.47.0">1991 c 336 art 2 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/633/#laws.4.10.0">1994 c 633 art 4 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.76">
        <h1 class="shn">609.76 GAMBLING; GROSS MISDEMEANOR; FELONY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanors.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) maintains or operates a gambling place or operates a bucket shop;</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally participates in the income of a gambling place or bucket shop;</p>
          <p>(3) conducts a lottery, or, with intent to conduct a lottery, possesses facilities for doing so;</p>
          <p>(4) sets up for use for the purpose of gambling, or collects the proceeds of, any gambling device or bucket shop;</p>
          <p>(5) except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299L.07">299L.07</a>, manufactures, sells, offers for sale, or otherwise provides, in whole or any part thereof, any gambling device including those defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.30#stat.349.30.2">349.30, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(6) with intent that it be so used, manufactures, sells, or offers for sale any facility for conducting a lottery, except as provided by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299L.07">299L.07</a>; or</p>
          <p>(7) receives, records, or forwards bets or offers to bet or, with intent to receive, record, or forward bets or offers to bet, possesses facilities to do so.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sports bookmaking.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever engages in sports bookmaking is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Cheating.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever cheats in a game, as described in this subdivision, is subject to the following penalties:</p>
          <p>(i) if the person holds a license related to gambling or is an employee of the licensee, the person is guilty of a felony; and</p>
          <p>(ii) any other person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. Any person who is a repeat offender is guilty of a felony.</p>
          <p>A person cheats in a game by intentionally:</p>
          <p>(1) altering or misrepresenting the outcome of a game or event on which wagers have been made, after the outcome is determined, but before the outcome is revealed to the players;</p>
          <p>(2) placing, canceling, increasing, or decreasing a bet after acquiring knowledge, not available to other players, of the outcome of the game or subject of the bet, or of events affecting the outcome of the game or subject of the bet;</p>
          <p>(3) claiming or collecting money or anything of value from a game or authorized gambling establishment not won or earned from the game or authorized gambling establishment;</p>
          <p>(4) manipulating a gambling device or associated equipment to affect the outcome of the game or the number of plays or credits available on the game; or</p>
          <p>(5) otherwise altering the elements of chance or methods of selection or criteria which determine the result of the game or amount or frequency of payment of the game.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Certain devices prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever uses or possesses a probability-calculating or outcome-affecting device at an authorized gambling establishment is guilty of a felony. For purposes of this subdivision, a "probability-calculating" or "outcome-affecting" device is any device to assist in:</p>
          <p>(1) projecting the outcome of a game other than pari-mutuel betting authorized by chapter 240;</p>
          <p>(2) keeping track of or counting cards used in a game;</p>
          <p>(3) analyzing the probability of the occurrence of an event relating to a game other than pari-mutuel betting authorized by chapter 240; or</p>
          <p>(4) analyzing the strategy for playing or betting in a game other than pari-mutuel betting authorized by chapter 240.</p>
          <p>For purposes of this section, a book, graph, periodical, chart, or pamphlet is not a "probability-calculating" or "outcome-affecting" device.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever uses, or possesses with intent to use, a key or other instrument for the purpose of opening, entering, and affecting the operation of any game or gambling device or for removing money, chips, tokens, or other contents from therein, is guilty of a felony. This paragraph does not apply to an agent or employee of an authorized gambling establishment acting within the scope of employment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Counterfeit chips prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally uses counterfeit chips or tokens to play a game at an authorized gambling establishment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.75#stat.609.75.5">609.75, subdivision 5</a>, designed to be played with or operated by chips or tokens is guilty of a felony. For purposes of this subdivision, counterfeit chips or tokens are chips or tokens not approved by the government regulatory agency for use in an authorized gambling activity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Manufacture, sale, and modification prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever manufactures, sells, distributes, or otherwise provides cards, chips, tokens, dice, or other equipment or devices intended to be used to violate this section, is guilty of a felony.</p>
          <p>(b) Whoever intentionally marks, alters, or otherwise modifies lawful associated equipment or gambling devices for the purpose of violating this section is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Instruction.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever instructs another person to violate the provisions of this section, with the intent that the information or knowledge conveyed be used to violate this section, is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.76.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Value of chips or tokens.</span></h2>
          <p>The value of chips or tokens approved for use in a game designed to be played with or operated by chips or tokens, as the term "value" is used in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>, is the amount or denomination shown on the face of the chip or token representing United States currency. Chips used in tournament play at a card club at a class A facility have no United States currency value.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.76.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.76; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/126/#laws.0.4.0">1981 c 126 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/214/#laws.0.37.0">1983 c 214 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/334/#laws.6.9.0">1989 c 334 art 6 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/590/#laws.2.17.0">1990 c 590 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/336/#laws.2.48.0">1991 c 336 art 2 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/336/#laws.0.10.0">2000 c 336 s 10</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/86/#laws.1.83.0">2009 c 86 art 1 s 83</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.761">
        <h1 class="shn">609.761 OPERATIONS PERMITTED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.761.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Lawful gambling.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.755">609.755</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.76">609.76</a>, an organization may conduct lawful gambling as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.12">349.12</a>, if authorized under chapter 349, and a person may manufacture, sell, or offer for sale a gambling device to an organization authorized under chapter 349 to conduct lawful gambling, and pari-mutuel betting on horse racing may be conducted under chapter 240.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.761.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">State Lottery.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.755">609.755</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.76">609.76</a> do not prohibit the operation of the State Lottery or the sale, possession, or purchase of tickets for the State Lottery under chapter 349A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.761.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Social skill game.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.755">609.755</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.76">609.76</a> do not prohibit tournaments or contests that satisfy all of the following requirements:</p>
          <p>(1) the tournament or contest consists of the card games of chance commonly known as cribbage, skat, sheepshead, bridge, euchre, pinochle, gin, 500, smear, Texas hold'em, or whist;</p>
          <p>(2) the tournament or contest does not provide any direct financial benefit to the promoter or organizer;</p>
          <p>(3) the value of all prizes awarded for each tournament or contest does not exceed $200; and</p>
          <p>(4) for a tournament or contest involving Texas hold'em:</p>
          <p>(i) no person under 18 years of age may participate;</p>
          <p>(ii) the payment of an entry fee or other consideration for participating is prohibited;</p>
          <p>(iii) the value of all prizes awarded to an individual winner of a tournament or contest at a single location may not exceed $200 each day; and</p>
          <p>(iv) the organizer or promoter must ensure that reasonable accommodations are made for players with disabilities. Accommodations to the table and the cards shall include the announcement of the cards visible to the entire table and the use of Braille cards for players who are blind.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.761.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Social dice games.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.755">609.755</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.76">609.76</a> do not prohibit dice games conducted on the premises and adjoining rooms of a retail establishment licensed to sell alcoholic beverages if the following requirements are satisfied:</p>
          <p>(1) the games consist of board games played with dice or commonly known dice games such as "shake-a-day," "3-2-1," "who buys," "last chance," "liar's poker," "6-5-4," "horse," and "aces";</p>
          <p>(2) wagers or prizes for the games are limited to food or beverages; and</p>
          <p>(3) the retail establishment does not organize or participate financially in the games.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.761.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">High school raffles.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.755">609.755</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.76">609.76</a> do not prohibit a raffle, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.12#stat.349.12.33">349.12, subdivision 33</a>, conducted by a school district or a nonprofit organization organized primarily to support programs of a school district, if the following conditions are complied with:</p>
          <p>(1) tickets for the raffle may only be sold and the drawing conducted at a high school event sponsored by a school district. All tickets must be sold for the same price;</p>
          <p>(2) tickets may only be sold to persons 18 years of age or older attending the event;</p>
          <p>(3) the drawing must be held during or immediately after the conclusion of the event;</p>
          <p>(4) one-half of the gross receipts from the sale of tickets must be awarded as prizes for the raffle, and the remaining one-half may only be expended to defray the school district's costs of sending event participants to high school activities held at other locations; and</p>
          <p>(5) if a school district's or nonprofit organization's gross receipts from the conduct of raffles exceeds $12,000 in a calendar year or $5,000 in a single raffle, the school district or organization must report the following information to the Gambling Control Board annually: the total amount of gross receipts received, the total expenses for the raffles, the total prizes awarded, and an accounting of the expenditures from the gross receipts of the raffles.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.761.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Savings promotion raffles.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.755">609.755</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.76">609.76</a> do not prohibit the conduct of or participation in a savings promotion raffle, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.75">609.75</a>, subdivision 14, if the following conditions are complied with:</p>
          <p>(1) participants in a savings promotion raffle shall not be required to provide any consideration, other than the deposit of a sum of money in a qualifying account, to obtain chances to win prizes in a savings promotion raffle. For purposes of this clause, participants shall not be deemed to have provided such consideration merely because the interest rate, if any, associated with a qualifying account is lower than the interest rate associated with comparable nonqualifying accounts. Participants shall not be deemed to have given consideration as a consequence of paying any fees associated with a qualifying account, so long as such fees are approximately of a kind and in an amount charged in connection with comparable nonqualifying accounts, if any, offered by the savings promotion raffle sponsor;</p>
          <p>(2) a savings promotion raffle shall be conducted so that each entry in the savings promotion raffle has an equal chance of being drawn; and</p>
          <p>(3) participants in a savings promotion raffle shall not be required to be present at a prize drawing in order to win.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.761.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/507/#laws.0.6.0">1978 c 507 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/214/#laws.0.38.0">1983 c 214 s 38</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/502/#laws.12.23.0">1984 c 502 art 12 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/467/#laws.0.30.0">1986 c 467 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/334/#laws.6.10.0">1989 c 334 art 6 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/155/#laws.0.10.0">1997 c 155 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/187/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 187 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/378/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 378 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/110/#laws.0.43.0">2003 c 110 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/166/#laws.4.1.0">2005 c 166 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/29/#laws.0.8.0">2015 c 29 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.762">
        <h1 class="shn">609.762 FORFEITURE OF GAMBLING DEVICES, PRIZES AND PROCEEDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.762.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>The following are subject to forfeiture:</p>
          <p>(1) devices used or intended for use, including those defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.30#stat.349.30.2">349.30, subdivision 2</a>, as a gambling device, except as authorized in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299L.07">299L.07</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.11">349.11</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/349.23">349.23</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) all moneys, materials, and other property used or intended for use as payment to participate in gambling or a prize or receipt for gambling;</p>
          <p>(3) books, records, and research products and materials, including formulas, microfilm, tapes, and data used or intended for use in gambling; and</p>
          <p>(4) property used or intended to be used to illegally influence the outcome of a horse race.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.762.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Seizure.</span></h2>
          <p>Property subject to forfeiture under subdivision 1 may be seized by any law enforcement agency upon process issued by any court having jurisdiction over the property. Seizure without process may be made if:</p>
          <p>(1) the seizure is incident to an arrest or a search under a search warrant;</p>
          <p>(2) the property subject to seizure has been the subject of a prior judgment in favor of the state in a criminal injunction or forfeiture proceeding; or</p>
          <p>(3) the law enforcement agency has probable cause to believe that the property was used or is intended to be used in a gambling violation and the delay occasioned by the necessity to obtain process would result in the removal, loss, or destruction of the property.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.762.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Not subject to replevin.</span></h2>
          <p>Property taken or detained under subdivision 2 is not subject to a replevin action, but is considered to be in the custody of the law enforcement agency subject only to the orders and decrees of the court having jurisdiction over the forfeiture proceedings.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.762.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>Property must be forfeited after a conviction for a gambling violation according to the following procedure:</p>
          <p>(1) a separate complaint must be filed against the property describing it, charging its use in the specified violation, and specifying the time and place of its unlawful use;</p>
          <p>(2) if the person charged with a gambling offense is acquitted, the court shall dismiss the complaint and order the property returned to the persons legally entitled to it; and</p>
          <p>(3) if after conviction the court finds the property, or any part of it, was used in violation as specified in the complaint, it shall order that the property be sold or retained by the law enforcement agency for official use. Proceeds from the sale of forfeited property may be retained for official use and shared equally between the law enforcement agency investigating the offense involved in the forfeiture and the prosecuting agency that prosecuted the offense involved in the forfeiture and handled the forfeiture proceedings.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.762.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exception.</span></h2>
          <p>Property may not be seized or forfeited under this section if the owner shows to the satisfaction of the court that the owner had no notice or knowledge or reason to believe that the property was used or intended to be used in violation of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.762.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>The law enforcement and prosecuting agencies shall report on forfeitures occurring under this section as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315">609.5315</a>, subdivision 6.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.762.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/214/#laws.0.39.0">1983 c 214 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/86/#laws.1.84.0">2009 c 86 art 1 s 84</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/391/#laws.0.19.0">2010 c 391 s 19</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.763">
        <h1 class="shn">609.763 LAWFUL GAMBLING FRAUD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.763.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2 if the person does any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) knowingly claims a lawful gambling prize using altered or counterfeited gambling equipment;</p>
          <p>(2) knowingly claims a lawful gambling prize by means of fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation;</p>
          <p>(3) manipulates any form of lawful gambling or tampers with any gambling equipment with intent to influence the outcome of a game or the receipt of a prize;</p>
          <p>(4) knowingly tampers with or attempts to alter any component or device used in the conduct or play of electronic pull-tabs or electronic linked bingo as authorized under chapter 349 or attempts to convert legal gambling into illegal gambling at an establishment licensed under chapter 340A;</p>
          <p>(5) has unauthorized possession of an electronic pull-tab device, an electronic linked bingo device, or other component used in the conduct of electronic pull-tabs or electronic linked bingo as authorized under chapter 349; or</p>
          <p>(6) knowingly places or uses false information on a prize receipt or on any other form approved for use by the Gambling Control Board or the Alcohol and Gambling Enforcement Division of the Department of Public Safety.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.763.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the dollar amount involved is $500 or less, the person is guilty of a misdemeanor;</p>
          <p>(2) if the dollar amount involved is more than $500 but not more than $2,500, the person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor; and</p>
          <p>(3) if the dollar amount involved is more than $2,500, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $6,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.763.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Aggregation; jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>In a prosecution under this section, the dollar amounts involved in violation of subdivision 1 within any 12-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the defendant may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed for all of the offenses aggregated under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.763.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/318/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 318 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.47.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/240/#laws.0.20.0">2014 c 240 s 20</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST REPUTATION</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.765">
        <h1 class="shn">609.765 CRIMINAL DEFAMATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.765.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>Defamatory matter is anything which exposes a person or a group, class or association to hatred, contempt, ridicule, degradation or disgrace in society, or injury to business or occupation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.765.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever with knowledge of its false and defamatory character orally, in writing or by any other means, communicates any false and defamatory matter to a third person without the consent of the person defamed is guilty of criminal defamation and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.765.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Justification.</span></h2>
          <p>Violation of subdivision 2 is justified if:</p>
          <p>(1) the communication is absolutely privileged; or</p>
          <p>(2) the communication consists of fair comment made in good faith with respect to persons participating in matters of public concern; or</p>
          <p>(3) the communication consists of a fair and true report or a fair summary of any judicial, legislative or other public or official proceedings; or</p>
          <p>(4) the communication is between persons each having an interest or duty with respect to the subject matter of the communication and is made with intent to further such interest or duty.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.765.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Testimony required.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall be convicted on the basis of an oral communication of defamatory matter except upon the testimony of at least two other persons that they heard and understood the oral statement as defamatory or upon a plea of guilty.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.765.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.765; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/126/#laws.0.8.0">2016 c 126 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.77">
        <h1 class="shn">609.77 FALSE INFORMATION TO NEWS MEDIA.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, with intent that it be published or disseminated and that it defame another person, communicates to any newspaper, magazine or other news media, any statement, knowing it to be false, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.77.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.77; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.77.0">1971 c 23 s 77</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.771">
        <h1 class="shn">609.771 USE OF DEEP FAKE TECHNOLOGY TO INFLUENCE ELECTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.771.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Candidate" means an individual who seeks nomination or election to a federal, statewide, legislative, judicial, or local office including special districts, school districts, towns, home rule charter and statutory cities, and counties.</p>
          <p>(c) "Deep fake" means any video recording, motion-picture film, sound recording, electronic image, or photograph, or any technological representation of speech or conduct substantially derivative thereof:</p>
          <p>(1) that is so realistic that a reasonable person would believe it depicts speech or conduct of an individual who did not in fact engage in such speech or conduct; and</p>
          <p>(2) the production of which was substantially dependent upon technical means, rather than the ability of another individual to physically or verbally impersonate such individual.</p>
          <p>(d) "Depicted individual" means an individual in a deep fake who appears to be engaging in speech or conduct in which the individual did not engage.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.771.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Violation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who disseminates a deep fake or enters into a contract or other agreement to disseminate a deep fake is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3 if the person knows or acts with reckless disregard about whether the item being disseminated is a deep fake and dissemination:</p>
          <p>(1) is made without the consent of the depicted individual;</p>
          <p>(2) is made with the intent to injure a candidate or influence the result of an election; and</p>
          <p>(3) takes place either:</p>
          <p>(i) within 90 days before a political party nominating convention; or</p>
          <p>(ii) after the start of the absentee voting period prior to a presidential nomination primary, or a regular or special state or local primary or general election.</p>
          <p>(b) This subdivision does not apply to a broadcaster or cable television system that disseminates a deep fake produced by a candidate if the broadcaster's or cable television system's dissemination is required by federal law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.771.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person convicted of violating subdivision 2 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) if the person commits the violation within five years of one or more prior convictions under this section, to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both;</p>
          <p>(2) if the person commits the violation with the intent to cause violence or bodily harm, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(3) in other cases, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) In the case of a candidate for state or local office convicted of violating subdivision 2, the court must enter a supplemental judgment declaring that the candidate has forfeited the nomination or office in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/211B.17">211B.17</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) A candidate for state or local office or other individual convicted of violating subdivision 2 is disqualified from being appointed to that office or any other office for which the legislature may establish qualifications under the Minnesota Constitution, article XII, section 3, in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/211B.18">211B.18</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.771.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Relief.</span></h2>
          <p>A cause of action for injunctive or equitable relief may be maintained against any person who is reasonably believed to be about to violate or who is in the course of violating this section by:</p>
          <p>(1) the attorney general;</p>
          <p>(2) a county attorney or city attorney;</p>
          <p>(3) the depicted individual; or</p>
          <p>(4) a candidate for nomination or election to a public office who is injured or likely to be injured by dissemination.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.771.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; c 58 s 2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/112/#laws.2.76.0">2024 c 112 art 2 s 76</a>-78</p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES RELATING TO COMMUNICATIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.774">
        <h1 class="shn">609.774 EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS; KIDNAPPINGS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.774.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, "supervising peace officer" means a person licensed pursuant to chapter 626, who has probable cause to believe that a person is being unlawfully confined, and who has lawful jurisdiction in the geographical area where the violation is believed to be occurring.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.774.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>A supervising peace officer may order a telephone company to cut, reroute, or divert telephone lines for the purpose of establishing and controlling communications with a violator.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.774.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Designation.</span></h2>
          <p>Each telephone company shall designate an employee to serve as a security official and to provide assistance as required by the supervising peace officer to carry out the purposes of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.774.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Unauthorized communication prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever initiates telephone communications with a violator with knowledge of an order issued pursuant to subdivision 2 and without prior police authorization, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.774.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>Good faith reliance by telephone employees on an order issued pursuant to subdivision 2 shall constitute a complete defense to any legal action brought for an interruption of telephone communications occurring by reason of this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.774.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/63/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 63 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/289/#laws.0.2.0">1979 c 289 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.775">
        <h1 class="shn">609.775 DIVULGING TELEPHONE OR TELEGRAPH MESSAGE; NONDELIVERY.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
        <p>(1) being entrusted as an employee of a telephone or telegraph company with the transmission or delivery of a telephonic or telegraphic message, intentionally or through culpable negligence discloses the contents or meaning thereof to a person other than the intended receiver; or</p>
        <p>(2) having knowledge of not being the intended receiver, obtains such disclosure from such employee; or</p>
        <p>(3) being such employee, intentionally or negligently fails duly to deliver such message.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.775.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.775; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.78.0">1971 c 23 s 78</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.776">
        <h1 class="shn">609.776 INTERFERENCE WITH EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS.</h1>
        <p>Whoever, without prior authorization, broadcasts or transmits on, interferes with, blocks, or cross-patches another frequency onto a law enforcement, firefighting, emergency medical services, emergency radio frequency or channel, any assigned or alternate emergency frequency or channel, or an official cellular telephone communication of a law enforcement agency, a fire department, or emergency medical services provider, knowing, or having reason to know that the act creates a risk of obstructing, preventing, or misdirecting official law enforcement, firefighting, or emergency medical services communications, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.776.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/2/#laws.4.27.0">1Sp2003 c 2 art 4 s 27</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.78">
        <h1 class="shn">609.78 EMERGENCY TELEPHONE CALLS AND COMMUNICATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.78.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) refuses to relinquish immediately a coin-operated telephone or a telephone line consisting of two or more stations when informed that the line is needed to make an emergency call;</p>
          <p>(2) secures a relinquishment of a coin-operated telephone or a telephone line consisting of two or more stations by falsely stating that the line is needed for an emergency;</p>
          <p>(3) publishes telephone directories to be used for telephones or telephone lines and the directories do not contain a copy of this section;</p>
          <p>(4) makes a call for emergency police, fire, medical, or ambulance service, knowing that no police, fire, or medical emergency exists;</p>
          <p>(5) interrupts, disrupts, impedes, or otherwise interferes with the transmission of a citizen's band radio channel communication the purpose of which is to inform or inquire about a medical emergency or an emergency in which property is or is reasonably believed to be in imminent danger of damage or destruction; or</p>
          <p>(6) makes or initiates an emergency call, knowing that no emergency exists, and with the intent to disrupt, interfere with, or reduce the provision of emergency services or the emergency call center's resources, remains silent, or makes abusive or harassing statements to the call recipient.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.78.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does the following is guilty of a gross misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally interrupts, disrupts, impedes, or interferes with an emergency call or who intentionally prevents or hinders another from placing an emergency call, and whose conduct does not result in a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.498">609.498</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) places an emergency call and reports a fictitious emergency with the intent of prompting an emergency response by law enforcement, fire, or emergency medical services personnel; or</p>
          <p>(3) violates subdivision 1, clause (6), after having been previously convicted or adjudicated delinquent for violating that clause.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.78.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Felony offense; reporting fictitious emergency resulting in serious injury.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 2, clause (2), is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the call triggers an emergency response and, as a result of the response, someone suffers great bodily harm or death; or</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment of not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the call triggers an emergency response and as a result of the response, someone suffers substantial bodily harm.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.78.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Other felony offenses.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does the following is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) violates subdivision 1, clause (6), after having been previously convicted or adjudicated delinquent for violating that clause on more than one occasion; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally uses multiple communications devices or electronic means to block, interfere with, overload, or otherwise prevent the emergency call center's system from functioning properly, and these actions make the system unavailable to someone needing emergency assistance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.78.2c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2c.<span class="headnote">Felony offense; reporting fictitious emergency resulting in response to the home of certain officials.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 2, clause (2), is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than one year or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both, if the person places the call with the intent of prompting an emergency response to the home of:</p>
          <p>(1) an elected official;</p>
          <p>(2) a judge as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221#stat.609.221.6">609.221, subdivision 6</a>, clause (5);</p>
          <p>(3) a prosecuting attorney as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221#stat.609.221.6">609.221, subdivision 6</a>, clause (4);</p>
          <p>(4) an employee of a correctional facility as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.021#stat.241.021.1i">241.021, subdivision 1i</a>; or</p>
          <p>(5) a peace officer as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.78.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), for purposes of this section, "emergency call" means:</p>
          <p>(1) a 911 call;</p>
          <p>(2) any call for emergency medical or ambulance service; or</p>
          <p>(3) any call for assistance from a police or fire department or for other assistance needed in an emergency to avoid serious harm to person or property, and an emergency exists.</p>
          <p>(b) As used in subdivisions 1, clause (6); 2, clause (2); 2a; and 2c:</p>
          <p>(1) "call" includes the use of any method of communication including, but not limited to: telephones, facsimiles, Voice over Internet Protocols, email messages, text messages, and electronic transmissions of an image or video; and</p>
          <p>(2) "emergency call" has the meaning given in paragraph (a) but does not require the existence of an emergency.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.78.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.78; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.79.0">1971 c 23 s 79</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/140/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 140 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/630/#laws.0.1.0">1984 c 630 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.19.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/24/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 24 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/270/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 270 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/20/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 20 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.4.19.0">2023 c 52 art 4 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.17.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 17</a>,18</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.785"><b>609.785</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/494/#laws.0.7.0">1990 c 494 s 7</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.79">
        <h1 class="shn">609.79 OBSCENE OR HARASSING TELEPHONE CALLS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.79.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime defined; obscene call.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever,</p>
          <p>(1) by means of a telephone,</p>
          <p>(i) makes any comment, request, suggestion or proposal which is obscene, lewd, or lascivious,</p>
          <p>(ii) with the intent to harass or intimidate another person, repeatedly makes telephone calls, whether or not conversation ensues, and thereby places the other person in reasonable fear of substantial bodily harm; places the person in reasonable fear that the person's family or household members will be subject to substantial bodily harm; or causes or would reasonably be expected to cause substantial emotional distress to the other person, or</p>
          <p>(iii) with the intent to harass or intimidate any person at the called or notified number, makes or causes the telephone of another to repeatedly or continuously ring or receive electronic notifications and thereby places the other person in reasonable fear of substantial bodily harm; places the person in reasonable fear that the person's family or household members will be subject to substantial bodily harm; or causes or would reasonably be expected to cause substantial emotional distress as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749#stat.609.749.2">609.749, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (4), to the other person, or</p>
          <p>(2) having control of a telephone, knowingly permits it to be used for any purpose prohibited by this section,</p>
          <p class="bl">shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.79.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.34.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.79.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>The offense may be prosecuted either at the place where the call is made or where it is received or, additionally in the case of wireless or electronic communication, where the sender or receiver resides.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.79.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.79; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/174/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 174 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/307/#laws.0.5.0">1987 c 307 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/261/#laws.0.7.0">1989 c 261 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.23.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.48.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/96/#laws.0.4.0">2020 c 96 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.795">
        <h1 class="shn">609.795 LETTER, TELEGRAM, OR PACKAGE; OPENING; HARASSMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.795.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanors.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) knowing that the actor does not have the consent of either the sender or the addressee, intentionally opens any sealed letter, telegram, or package addressed to another; or</p>
          <p>(2) knowing that a sealed letter, telegram, or package has been opened without the consent of either the sender or addressee, intentionally publishes any of the contents thereof; or</p>
          <p>(3) with the intent to harass or intimidate another person, repeatedly mails or delivers or causes the delivery by any means, including electronically, of letters, telegrams, or packages and thereby places the other person in reasonable fear of substantial bodily harm; places the person in reasonable fear that the person's family or household members will be subject to substantial bodily harm; or causes or would reasonably be expected to cause substantial emotional distress as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.749">609.749, subdivision </a>2, paragraph (a), clause (4), to the other person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.795.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.34.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.795.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Venue.</span></h2>
          <p>The offense may be prosecuted either at the place where the letter, telegram, or package is sent or received or, alternatively in the case of wireless electronic communication, where the sender or receiver resides.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.795.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.795; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.81.0">1971 c 23 s 81</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/307/#laws.0.6.0">1987 c 307 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/261/#laws.0.8.0">1989 c 261 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.2.24.0">1993 c 326 art 2 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/311/#laws.4.7.0">2000 c 311 art 4 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.49.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/96/#laws.0.5.0">2020 c 96 s 5</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.80">
        <h1 class="shn">609.80 INTERFERING WITH CABLE COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.80.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally and with the purpose of making or aiding in an unauthorized connection as prohibited by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (12), to a licensed cable communications system as defined in chapter 238 lends, offers, or gives to another any instrument, apparatus, equipment, or device designed to make an unauthorized connection, or plan, specification or instruction for making an unauthorized connection, without receiving or seeking to receive money or any other thing of value in exchange; or</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally tampers with, removes or injures any cable, wire, or other component of a licensed cable communications system as defined in chapter 238; or</p>
          <p>(3) intentionally and without claim of right interrupts a service of a licensed cable communications system as defined in chapter 238.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.80.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commercial activity; felony.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever sells or rents, or offers or advertises for sale or rental, any instrument, apparatus, equipment, or device designed to make an unauthorized connection as prohibited by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (12), to a licensed cable communications system as defined in chapter 238, or a plan, specification, or instructions for making an unauthorized connection, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to not more than three years of imprisonment or a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.80.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/396/#laws.0.2.0">1977 c 396 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/410/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 410 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.94.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 94</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.805"><b>609.805</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/47/#laws.0.1.0">2007 c 47 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/54/#laws.2.19.0">2007 c 54 art 2 s 19</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES RELATING TO BUSINESS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.806">
        <h1 class="shn">609.806 INTERFERING WITH INTERNET TICKET SALES.</h1>
        <p class="in">(a) A person who intentionally uses or sells software to circumvent on a ticket seller's website a security measure, an access control system, or a control or measure that is used to ensure an equitable ticket buying process, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) For the purposes of this section, "software" means computer programs that are primarily designed or produced for the purpose of interfering with the operation of any person or entity that sells, over the Internet, tickets of admission to a sporting event, theater, musical performance, or place of public entertainment or amusement of any kind.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.806.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/245/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 245 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.807">
        <h1 class="shn">609.807 EVENT TICKETS; PROHIBITED ACTS.</h1>
        <p>(a) As used in this section: (1) "initial seller" means a person or entity with whom a provider of an event or venue has contracted for the sale of tickets for the purpose of the initial sale of those tickets to the general public; and (2) "ticket" means a ticket of admission to a sporting event, theater, musical performance, or place of public entertainment or amusement of any kind.</p>
        <p>(b) The initial seller of tickets shall make available for sale all tickets under control of the initial seller in the manner and under terms directed by the provider of the event or venue. The initial seller shall not, unless authorized by the provider of the event or venue, divert tickets from the initial sale to the general public to be sold in any other manner or under any other terms.</p>
        <p>(c) No person or entity, with intent to defraud, may sell or offer for sale a ticket that is invalid, counterfeit, altered, or otherwise not genuine.</p>
        <p>(d) A violation of this section is a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.807.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/61/#laws.0.1.0">2009 c 61 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.609.81"><b>609.81</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/404/#laws.0.18.0">1996 c 404 s 18</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.815">
        <h1 class="shn">609.815 MISCONDUCT OF JUNK OR SECONDHAND DEALER.</h1>
        <p>Whoever is a junk dealer or secondhand dealer and does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
        <p>(1) has stolen goods in possession and refuses to permit a law enforcement officer to examine them during usual business hours; or</p>
        <p>(2) purchases property from a person under lawful age, without the written consent of the person's parent or guardian.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.815.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.815; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.84.0">1971 c 23 s 84</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.816">
        <h1 class="shn">609.816 WRONGFUL EMPLOYMENT AT A CHILD CARE CENTER.</h1>
        <p>A person is guilty of a crime and may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>, subdivision 3, clauses (1) to (5), if the person:</p>
        <p>(1) is a child care center owner, director, manager, license holder, or other controlling individual or agent of a child care center;</p>
        <p>(2) engages in the recruitment or screening of potential employees or applicants or instructs other persons engaged in the recruitment or screening of potential employees or applicants; and</p>
        <p>(3) requires, as a condition of obtaining or continuing employment at the child care center, in order to obtain child care assistance program funds, that the applicant, potential employee, or employee has one or more children who are eligible for or receive child care assistance.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.816.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
