          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.4.59.0">2015 c 78 art 4 s 59</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.82">
        <h1 class="shn">609.82 FRAUD IN OBTAINING CREDIT.</h1>
        <p>A person who, with intent to defraud, obtains personal credit or credit for another from a bank, trust company, savings association, or credit union, by means of a present or past false representation as to the person's or another's financial ability may be sentenced as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) if no money or property is obtained by the defendant by means of such credit, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $300, or both; or</p>
        <p>(2) if money or property is so obtained, the value thereof shall be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.1">609.52, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3) and the person obtaining the credit may be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.82.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.82; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/23/#laws.0.85.0">1971 c 23 s 85</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/202/#laws.1.25.0">1995 c 202 art 1 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.821">
        <h1 class="shn">609.821 FINANCIAL TRANSACTION CARD FRAUD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.821.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them:</p>
          <p>(a) "Financial transaction card" means any instrument or device, whether known as a credit card, credit plate, charge plate, courtesy card, bank services card, banking card, check guarantee card, debit card, electronic benefit system (EBS) card, electronic benefit transfer (EBT) card, assistance transaction card, or by any other name, issued with or without fee by an issuer for the use of the cardholder in obtaining credit, money, goods, services, public assistance benefits, or anything else of value, and includes the account or identification number or symbol of a financial transaction card.</p>
          <p>(b) "Cardholder" means a person in whose name a card is issued.</p>
          <p>(c) "Issuer" means a person, firm, or governmental agency, or a duly authorized agent or designee, that issues a financial transaction card.</p>
          <p>(d) "Property" includes money, goods, services, public assistance benefit, or anything else of value.</p>
          <p>(e) "Public assistance benefit" means any money, goods or services, or anything else of value, issued under chapters 256, 256B, 256D, or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/393.07#stat.393.07.10">393.07, subdivision 10</a>.</p>
          <p>(f) "Trafficking of SNAP benefits" means:</p>
          <p>(1) the buying, selling, stealing, or otherwise effecting an exchange of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits issued and accessed via an electronic benefit transfer (EBT) card, card number and personal identification number (PIN), or manual voucher and signature, for cash or consideration other than eligible food, either directly, indirectly, in complicity or collusion with others, or acting alone;</p>
          <p>(2) the exchange of one of the following for SNAP benefits: firearms, ammunition, explosives, or controlled substances as defined in United States Code, title 21, section 802;</p>
          <p>(3) purchasing a product with SNAP benefits that has a container requiring a return deposit with the intent of obtaining cash by discarding the product and returning the container for the deposit amount, intentionally discarding the product, and intentionally returning the container for the deposit amount;</p>
          <p>(4) purchasing a product with SNAP benefits with the intent of obtaining cash or consideration other than eligible food by reselling the product, and intentionally reselling the product purchased with SNAP benefits in exchange for cash or consideration other than eligible food;</p>
          <p>(5) intentionally purchasing products originally purchased with SNAP benefits in exchange for cash or consideration other than eligible food; or</p>
          <p>(6) attempting to buy, sell, steal, or otherwise effect an exchange of SNAP benefits issued and accessed via an EBT card, card number and PIN number, or manual voucher and signature, for cash or consideration other than eligible food, either directly, indirectly, in complicity or collusion with others, or acting alone.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.821.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Violations; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who does any of the following commits financial transaction card fraud:</p>
          <p>(1) without the consent of the cardholder, and knowing that the cardholder has not given consent, uses or attempts to use a card to obtain the property of another, or a public assistance benefit issued for the use of another;</p>
          <p>(2) uses or attempts to use a card knowing it to be forged, false, fictitious, or obtained in violation of clause (6);</p>
          <p>(3) sells or transfers a card knowing that the cardholder and issuer have not authorized the person to whom the card is sold or transferred to use the card, or that the card is forged, false, fictitious, or was obtained in violation of clause (6);</p>
          <p>(4) without a legitimate business purpose, and without the consent of the cardholders, receives or possesses, with intent to use, or with intent to sell or transfer in violation of clause (3), two or more cards issued in the name of another, or two or more cards knowing the cards to be forged, false, fictitious, or obtained in violation of clause (6);</p>
          <p>(5) being authorized by an issuer to furnish money, goods, services, or anything else of value, knowingly and with an intent to defraud the issuer or the cardholder:</p>
          <p>(i) furnishes money, goods, services, or anything else of value upon presentation of a financial transaction card knowing it to be forged, expired, or revoked, or knowing that it is presented by a person without authority to use the card; or</p>
          <p>(ii) represents in writing to the issuer that the person has furnished money, goods, services, or anything else of value which has not in fact been furnished;</p>
          <p>(6) upon applying for a financial transaction card to an issuer, or for a public assistance benefit which is distributed by means of a financial transaction card:</p>
          <p>(i) knowingly gives a false name or occupation;</p>
          <p>(ii) knowingly and substantially overvalues assets or substantially undervalues indebtedness for the purpose of inducing the issuer to issue a financial transaction card; or</p>
          <p>(iii) knowingly makes a false statement or representation for the purpose of inducing an issuer to issue a financial transaction card used to obtain a public assistance benefit;</p>
          <p>(7) with intent to defraud, falsely notifies the issuer or any other person of a theft, loss, disappearance, or nonreceipt of a financial transaction card;</p>
          <p>(8) without the consent of the cardholder and knowing that the cardholder has not given consent, falsely alters, makes, or signs any written document pertaining to a card transaction to obtain or attempt to obtain the property of another; or</p>
          <p>(9) engages in trafficking of SNAP benefits.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.821.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who commits financial transaction card fraud may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) for a violation of subdivision 2, clause (1), (2), (5), (8), or (9):</p>
          <p>(i) to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both, if the value of the property the person obtained or attempted to obtain was more than $35,000, or the aggregate amount of the transactions under this subdivision was more than $35,000; or</p>
          <p>(ii) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the value of the property the person obtained or attempted to obtain was more than $2,500, or the aggregate amount of the transactions under this subdivision was more than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(iii) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the value of the property the person obtained or attempted to obtain was more than $250 but not more than $2,500, or the aggregate amount of the transactions under this subdivision was more than $250 but not more than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(iv) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the value of the property the person obtained or attempted to obtain was not more than $250, or the aggregate amount of the transactions under this subdivision was not more than $250, and the person has previously been convicted within the preceding five years for an offense under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.24">609.24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.247">609.247</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52">609.52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a>, 2, or 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.625">609.625</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.63">609.63</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.631">609.631</a>, or a statute from another state in conformity with any of those sections, and the person received a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence for the offense, or a sentence that was stayed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.135">609.135</a> if the offense to which a plea was entered would allow imposition of a felony or gross misdemeanor sentence; or</p>
          <p>(v) to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the value of the property the person obtained or attempted to obtain was not more than $250, or the aggregate amount of the transactions under this subdivision was not more than $250;</p>
          <p>(2) for a violation of subdivision 2, clause (3) or (4), to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(3) for a violation of subdivision 2, clause (6) or (7):</p>
          <p>(i) if no property, other than a financial transaction card, has been obtained by the defendant by means of the false statement or false report, to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both; or</p>
          <p>(ii) if property, other than a financial transaction card, is so obtained, in the manner provided in clause (1).</p>
          <p>(b) In any prosecution under paragraph (a), clause (1), the value of the transactions made or attempted within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this section. When two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the card transactions occurred for all of the transactions aggregated under this paragraph.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.821.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/243/#laws.0.10.0">1985 c 243 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/329/#laws.0.14.0">1987 c 329 s 14</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/712/#laws.0.16.0">1988 c 712 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/1/#laws.6.53.0">1Sp1993 c 1 art 6 s 53</a>,54; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/218/#laws.0.5.0">1999 c 218 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.4.60.0">2015 c 78 art 4 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a>; art 20 s 26</p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">RESIDENTIAL MORTGAGE FRAUD</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.822">
        <h1 class="shn">609.822 RESIDENTIAL MORTGAGE FRAUD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.822.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Mortgage lending process" means the process through which a person seeks or obtains a residential mortgage loan including, but not limited to, solicitation, application, or origination, negotiation of terms, third-party provider services, underwriting, signing and closing, and funding of the loan. Documents involved in the mortgage lending process include, but are not limited to, uniform residential loan applications or other loan applications; appraisal reports; HUD-1 settlement statements; supporting personal documentation for loan applications such as W-2 forms, verifications of income and employment, bank statements, tax returns, and payroll stubs; and any required disclosures.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "Residential mortgage loan" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/58.02#stat.58.02.18">58.02, subdivision 18</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.822.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Residential mortgage fraud prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever does any of the following commits residential mortgage fraud and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) knowingly makes or causes to be made any deliberate and material misstatement, misrepresentation, or omission during the mortgage lending process with the intention that it be relied on by a mortgage lender, borrower, or any other party to the mortgage lending process;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) knowingly uses or facilitates the use of any deliberate and material misstatement, misrepresentation, or omission, knowing the same to contain a material misstatement, misrepresentation, or omission, during the mortgage lending process with the intention that it be relied on by a mortgage lender, borrower, or any other party to the mortgage lending process; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) conspires to violate clause (1) or (2).</p>
          <p class="in">An offense of residential mortgage fraud must not be predicated solely upon information lawfully disclosed under federal disclosure laws, regulations, and interpretations related to the mortgage lending process.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.822.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever violates this section shall be sentenced as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.3">609.52, subdivision 3</a>, based on the aggregate economic loss suffered by any person as a result of the violation. However, the maximum sentence of imprisonment for the offense may not exceed two years. A person convicted of a violation of this section shall be ordered to pay restitution to persons aggrieved by the violation. Restitution shall be ordered in addition to a fine or imprisonment but not in lieu of a fine or imprisonment. Nothing in this section limits the power of the state to punish any person for conduct which constitutes a crime under any other statute.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.822.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Vulnerable victim.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">If the person who violates subdivision 2 knew or had reason to know that the victim was vulnerable due to age, infirmity, or reduced physical or mental capacity, the court may order an aggravated departure under the sentencing guidelines.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.822.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/74/#laws.0.7.0">2007 c 74 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/215/#laws.0.2.0">2008 c 215 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MISCELLANEOUS CRIMES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.825">
        <h1 class="shn">609.825 BRIBERY OF PARTICIPANT OR OFFICIAL IN CONTEST.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.825.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section, "official" means one who umpires, referees, judges, officiates or is otherwise designated to render decisions concerning the conduct or outcome of any contest included herein.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.825.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
          <p>(1) offers, gives, or agrees to give, directly or indirectly, any benefit, reward or consideration to a participant, manager, director, or other official, or to one who intends to become such participant or official, in any sporting event, race or other contest of any kind whatsoever with intent thereby to influence such participant not to use the participant's best effort to win or enable the participant's team to win or to attain a maximum score or margin of victory, or to influence such official in decisions with respect to such contest; or</p>
          <p>(2) requests, receives, or agrees to receive, directly or indirectly, any benefit, reward or consideration upon the understanding that the actor will be so influenced as such participant or official.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.825.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Duty to report.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever is offered or promised such benefit, reward or consideration upon the understanding to be so influenced as such participant or official and fails promptly to report the same to the offeree's or promisee's employer, manager, coach, or director, or to a county attorney may be punished by imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.825.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.825; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.83">
        <h1 class="shn">609.83 FALSELY IMPERSONATING ANOTHER.</h1>
        <p>Whoever does either of the following may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:</p>
        <p>(1) assumes to enter into a marriage relationship with another by falsely impersonating a third person; or</p>
        <p>(2) by falsely impersonating another with intent to defraud the other or a third person, appears, participates, or executes an instrument to be used in a judicial proceeding.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.83.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1963/0/753/#laws.1.609.0">1963 c 753 art 1 s 609</a>.83; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.833">
        <h1 class="shn">609.833 MISREPRESENTATION OF SERVICE ANIMAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.833.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in this section:</p>
          <p>(1) "place of public accommodation" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/363A.03">363A.03</a>, subdivision 34; and</p>
          <p>(2) "service animal" has the meaning given in Code of Federal Regulations, title 28, section 36.104, as amended through March 1, 2018.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.833.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibited conduct.</span></h2>
          <p>A person may not, directly or indirectly through statements or conduct, intentionally misrepresent an animal in that person's possession as a service animal in any place of public accommodation to obtain any rights or privileges available to a person who qualifies for a service animal under state or federal law knowing that the person is not entitled to those rights or privileges.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.833.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), a person who violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 2 a second or subsequent time is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.833.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A conspicuous sign may be posted in a location accessible to public view in a place of public accommodation that contains the following, or substantially similar, language:</p>
          <p class="ce">"NOTICE</p>
          <p>Service Animals Welcome. It is illegal for a person to misrepresent an animal in that person's possession as a service animal."</p>
          <p>(b) The Council on Disability may prepare and make available to businesses a brochure detailing permissible questions a business owner may ask to determine whether an animal is a service animal, proper answers to those questions, and guidelines defining unacceptable behavior.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.833.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/106/#laws.0.2.0">2018 c 106 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.84">
        <h1 class="shn">609.84 SALE OF HUMAN REMAINS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.84.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Human remains" means any part of a dead human body, the cremated remains of a dead human body, or the hydrolyzed remains of a dead human body.</p>
          <p>(c) "Law enforcement agency" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (f).</p>
          <p>(d) "Local organization for emergency management" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/12.03#stat.12.03.6">12.03, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) "Search and rescue unit" means an organization, team, or individual authorized by the state or federal government, a Tribal government, or by a county, city, town, or a metropolitan airports commission organized and existing under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.601">473.601</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.679">473.679 </a>whose mission is to locate lost, missing, or trapped persons, victims of natural or other disasters, and human bodies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.84.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sale of human remains prohibited; donation and reimbursement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), a person is prohibited from selling human remains or offering human remains for sale.</p>
          <p>(b) Paragraph (a) shall not be construed to limit the donation of human remains:</p>
          <p>(1) to a licensed health care provider, an individual employed by or under contract with a licensed health care provider, a public or private postsecondary educational institution, or an individual employed by or under contract with a public or private postsecondary educational institution, for legitimate medical or scientific purposes or for educational purposes;</p>
          <p>(2) to a company registered with the United States Food and Drug Administration or an individual, company, or entity employed by or under contract with a company registered with the United States Food and Drug Administration for legitimate medical or scientific purposes, including but not limited to the development, manufacturing, and research of medical products; or</p>
          <p>(3) to a law enforcement agency, search and rescue unit, or local organization for emergency management to conduct search and rescue training or to entities that train dogs to locate dead human bodies.</p>
          <p>(c) Paragraph (a) does not apply to the sale or offer for sale of human remains that is incidental to the sale of real property, including undisturbed burial plots, cemeteries, crypts, or other burial features.</p>
          <p>(d) Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit a person from recovering reasonable expenses for the processing, preservation, quality control, storage, transportation, or final disposition of human remains for the legitimate purposes as described in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.84.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates this section is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.84.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/123/#laws.6.19.0">2024 c 123 art 6 s 19</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.849">
        <h1 class="shn">609.849 RAILROAD THAT OBSTRUCTS TREATMENT OF INJURED WORKER.</h1>
        <p>(a) It shall be unlawful for a railroad or person employed by a railroad to intentionally:</p>
        <p>(1) deny, delay, or interfere with medical treatment or first aid treatment to an employee of a railroad who has been injured during employment; or</p>
        <p>(2) discipline, harass, or intimidate an employee to discourage the employee from receiving medical attention or threaten to discipline an employee who has been injured during employment for requesting medical treatment or first aid treatment.</p>
        <p>(b) Nothing in this section shall deny a railroad company or railroad employee from making a reasonable inquiry of an injured employee about the circumstance of an injury in order to gather information necessary to identify a safety hazard.</p>
        <p>(c) It is not a violation under this section for a railroad company or railroad employee to enforce safety regulations.</p>
        <p>(d) A railroad or a person convicted of a violation of paragraph (a), clause (1) or (2), is guilty of a misdemeanor and may be fined not more than $1,000 but is not subject to an incarcerative sanction.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.849.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.50.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/1/#laws.4.116.0">1Sp2005 c 1 art 4 s 116</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>Paragraph (a), clause (1), was found preempted by the federal Railroad Safety Act in <i>BNSF Railway Co. v. Swanson</i>, 533 F.3d 618 (8th Cir. 2008).</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.85">
        <h1 class="shn">609.85 CRIMES AGAINST RAILROAD EMPLOYEES AND PROPERTY; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.85.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Intent to cause derailment.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever throws or deposits any type of debris, waste material, or other obstruction on any railroad track or whoever causes damage or causes another person to damage, tamper, change or destroy any railroad track, switch, bridge, trestle, tunnel, signal or moving equipment used in providing rail services, with intention to cause injury, accident or derailment, is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.85.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Foreseeable risk.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally throws or deposits any type of debris, waste material, or other obstruction on any railroad track or whoever intentionally causes damage or causes another person to damage, tamper, change or destroy any railroad track, switch, bridge, trestle, tunnel, signal or moving equipment used in providing rail services, which creates a reasonably foreseeable risk of any injury, accident or derailment, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.85.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Shooting at train.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally shoots a firearm at any portion of a railroad train, car, caboose, engine or moving equipment so as to endanger the safety of another is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.85.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Throwing objects at train.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally throws, shoots or propels any stone, brick or other missile at any railroad train, car, caboose, engine or moving equipment, so as to endanger the safety of another is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.85.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Placing obstruction on track.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever places an obstruction on a railroad track is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.85.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Trespass; allowing animals on track; exception.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Whoever intentionally trespasses, or who permits animals under the person's control to trespass on a railroad track, yard, or bridge is guilty of a misdemeanor. This subdivision does not apply to an elected union official's access to those facilities when acting in an official capacity, to an employee acting within the scope of employment, or to a person with written permission from the railroad company to enter upon the railroad facility.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.85.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/179/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 179 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.11.0">1989 c 5 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/350/#laws.2.3.0">2008 c 350 art 2 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.851">
        <h1 class="shn">609.851 FALSE TRAFFIC SIGNAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.851.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of a misdemeanor if the person exhibits a false light or signal or interferes with a light, signal, or sign controlling or guiding traffic on a highway, railroad track, navigable waters, or in the air.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.851.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 and knows that doing so creates a risk of death or bodily harm or serious property damage is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.851.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.12.0">1989 c 5 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.855">
        <h1 class="shn">609.855 CRIMES INVOLVING TRANSIT; SHOOTING AT TRANSIT VEHICLE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Unlawfully obtaining services; petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person is guilty of a petty misdemeanor who intentionally obtains or attempts to obtain service for himself, herself, or another person from a provider of public transit or from a public conveyance by doing any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) occupies or rides in any public transit vehicle without paying the applicable fare or otherwise obtaining the consent of the transit provider including:</p>
          <p>(i) the use of a reduced fare when a person is not eligible for the fare; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the use of a fare medium issued solely for the use of a particular individual by another individual;</p>
          <p>(2) presents a falsified, counterfeit, photocopied, or other deceptively manipulated fare medium as fare payment or proof of fare payment;</p>
          <p>(3) sells, provides, copies, reproduces, or creates any version of any fare medium without the consent of the transit provider; or</p>
          <p>(4) puts or attempts to put any of the following into any fare box, pass reader, ticket vending machine, or other fare collection equipment of a transit provider:</p>
          <p>(i) papers, articles, instruments, or items other than fare media or currency; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a fare medium that is not valid for the place or time at, or the manner in, which it is used.</p>
          <p>(b) Where self-service barrier-free fare collection is utilized by a public transit provider, it is a violation of this subdivision to intentionally fail to exhibit proof of fare payment upon the request of an authorized transit representative when entering, riding upon, or leaving a transit vehicle or when present in a designated paid fare zone located in a transit facility.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates this subdivision must pay a fine of no more than $10.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Unlawful interference with transit operator.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever intentionally commits an act that interferes with or obstructs, or tends to interfere with or obstruct, the operation of a transit vehicle is guilty of unlawful interference with a transit operator and may be sentenced as provided in paragraph (c).</p>
          <p>(b) An act that is committed on a transit vehicle that distracts the driver from the safe operation of the vehicle or that endangers passengers is a violation of this subdivision if an authorized transit representative has clearly warned the person once to stop the act.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates this subdivision may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both, if the violation was accompanied by force or violence or a communication of a threat of force or violence; or</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both, if the violation was not accompanied by force or violence or a communication of a threat of force or violence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prohibited activities; petty misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who throws or deposits litter while riding in a vehicle providing public transit service is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(b) A person is guilty of a violation of this subdivision only if the person continues to act in violation of this subdivision after being warned once by an authorized transit representative to stop the conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Prohibited activities; misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who performs any of the following while in a transit vehicle or at a transit facility is guilty of a misdemeanor:</p>
          <p>(1) smokes, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.413#stat.144.413.4">144.413, subdivision 4</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) urinates or defecates;</p>
          <p>(3) consumes an alcoholic beverage, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/340A.101#stat.340A.101.2">340A.101, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) damages a transit vehicle or transit facility in a manner that meets the requirements for criminal damage to property in the fourth degree under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595#stat.609.595.3">609.595, subdivision 3</a>, and is not otherwise a violation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.595#stat.609.595.1">609.595, subdivision 1</a>, 1a, or 2;</p>
          <p>(5) performs vandalism, defacement, or placement of graffiti, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/617.90#stat.617.90.1">617.90, subdivision 1</a>; or</p>
          <p>(6) engages in disorderly conduct as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.72#stat.609.72.1">609.72, subdivision 1</a>, clause (3).</p>
          <p>(b) A peace officer, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (c), may order a person to depart a transit vehicle or transit facility for a violation under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.69.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 69</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Shooting at or in public transit vehicle or facility.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever recklessly discharges a firearm at or in any portion of a public transit vehicle or facility is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $6,000, or both. If the transit vehicle or facility is occupied by any person other than the offender, the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Restraining orders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) At the sentencing on a violation of this section, the district court shall consider the extent to which the person's conduct has negatively disrupted the delivery of transit services or has affected the utilization of public transit services by others. The district court may, in its discretion, include as part of any sentence for a violation of this section, an order restraining the person from using public transit vehicles and facilities for a fixed period, not to exceed two years or any term of probation, whichever is longer.</p>
          <p>(b) The district court administrator shall forward copies of any orders, and any subsequent orders of the court rescinding or modifying the original order, promptly to the operator of the transit system on which the offense took place.</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates an order issued under this subdivision is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.855.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The definitions in this subdivision apply in this section.</p>
          <p>(b) "Public transportation" or "transit" has the meaning given to "public transportation" in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/174.22#stat.174.22.7">174.22, subdivision 7</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) "Public transit vehicle" or "transit vehicle" means any vehicle used for the purpose of providing public transit, whether or not the vehicle is owned or operated by a public entity.</p>
          <p>(d) "Public transit facilities" or "transit facilities" means any vehicles, equipment, property, structures, stations, improvements, plants, parking or other facilities, or rights that are owned, leased, held, or used for the purpose of providing public transit, whether or not the facility is owned or operated by a public entity.</p>
          <p>(e) "Fare medium" means a ticket, smart card, pass, coupon, token, transfer, or other medium sold or distributed by a public transit provider, or its authorized agents, for use in gaining entry to or use of the public transit facilities or vehicles of the provider.</p>
          <p>(f) "Proof of fare payment" means a fare medium valid for the place or time at, or the manner in, which it is used. If using a reduced-fare medium, proof of fare payment also includes proper identification demonstrating a person's eligibility for the reduced fare. If using a fare medium issued solely for the use of a particular individual, proof of fare payment also includes an identification document bearing a photographic likeness of the individual and demonstrating that the individual is the person to whom the fare medium is issued.</p>
          <p>(g) "Authorized transit representative" means the person authorized by the transit provider to operate the transit vehicle, a peace officer, a transit official under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.4075">473.4075</a>, subdivision 1, or any other person designated by the transit provider as an authorized transit representative under this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.855.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/189/#laws.0.1.0">1983 c 189 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.3.139.0">1984 c 654 art 3 s 139</a>,140; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/271/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 271 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/5/#laws.0.13.0">1989 c 5 s 13</a>,14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.49.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.4.13.0">1996 c 408 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/245/#laws.0.3.0">2004 c 245 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/68/#laws.4.99.0">2023 c 68 art 4 s 99</a>-102; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/104/#laws.2.14.0">2024 c 104 art 2 s 14</a>,15</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.856">
        <h1 class="shn">609.856 USE OF POLICE RADIOS DURING COMMISSION OF CRIME; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.856.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever has in possession or uses a radio or device capable of receiving or transmitting a police radio signal, message, or transmission of information used for law enforcement purposes, while in the commission of a felony or violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a> or the attempt to commit a felony or violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a>, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.04">609.04</a>, a prosecution for or conviction under this section is not a bar to conviction of or punishment for any other crime committed by the defendant as part of the same conduct.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.856.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>A radio or device defined in subdivision 1 that is used in the commission of a felony or violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a> or attempt to commit a felony or violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.487">609.487</a> is contraband property and subject to the forfeiture provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.856.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/111/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 111 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.4.35.0">1993 c 326 art 4 s 35</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.857">
        <h1 class="shn">609.857 DISCHARGING A LASER AT AN AIRCRAFT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.857.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Aircraft" means any contrivance now known or hereafter invented, used, or designed for navigation of or flight in the air, but excluding parachutes.</p>
          <p>(c) "Laser" means both of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) any device that utilizes the natural oscillations of atoms or molecules between energy levels for generating coherent electromagnetic radiation in the ultraviolet, visible, or infrared region of the spectrum and when discharged exceeds one milliwatt continuous wave;</p>
          <p>(2) any device designed or used to amplify electromagnetic radiation by simulated emission that is visible to the human eye.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.857.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever knowingly aims and discharges a laser or other device that creates visible light into the cockpit of an aircraft that is in the process of taking off or landing or is in flight is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.857.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to the following individuals who aim and discharge a laser or other device at an aircraft:</p>
          <p>(1) an authorized individual in the conduct of research and development or flight test operations conducted by an aircraft manufacturer, the Federal Aviation Administration, or any other person authorized by the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct such research and development or flight test operations; or</p>
          <p>(2) members or elements of the Department of Defense or Department of Homeland Security acting in an official capacity for the purpose of research, development, operations, testing, or training.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.857.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Defense.</span></h2>
          <p>It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section if the defendant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant intended to send an emergency distress signal.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.857.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/73/#laws.0.1.0">2009 c 73 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CRIMES AGAINST COMMERCE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.86">
        <h1 class="shn">609.86 COMMERCIAL BRIBERY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.86.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Corruptly" means that the actor intends the action to injure or defraud:</p>
          <p>(1) the actor's employer or principal; or</p>
          <p>(2) the employer or principal of the person to whom the actor offers, gives or agrees to give the bribe or from whom the actor requests, receives or agrees to receive the bribe.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.86.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Acts constituting.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following, when not consistent with usually accepted business practices, is guilty of commercial bribery and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3:</p>
          <p>(1) corruptly offers, gives, or agrees to give, directly or indirectly, any benefit, consideration, compensation, or reward to any employee, agent or fiduciary of a person with the intent to influence the person's performance of duties as an employee, agent, or fiduciary in relation to the person's employer's or principal's business; or</p>
          <p>(2) being an employee, agent or fiduciary of a person, corruptly requests, receives or agrees to receive, directly or indirectly, from another person any benefit, consideration, compensation, or reward with the understanding or agreement to be influenced in the performance of duties as an employee, agent, or fiduciary in relation to the employer's or principal's business.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.86.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sentence.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever commits commercial bribery may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the value of the benefit, consideration, compensation or reward is greater than $500;</p>
          <p>(2) in all other cases where the value of the benefit, consideration, compensation or reward is $500 or less, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000; provided, however, in any prosecution of the value of the benefit, consideration, compensation or reward received by the defendant within any six-month period may be aggregated and the defendant charged accordingly in applying the provisions of this subdivision; provided that when two or more offenses are committed by the same person in two or more counties, the accused may be prosecuted in any county in which one of the offenses was committed, or all of the offenses aggregated under this clause.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.86.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/442/#laws.0.1.0">1982 c 442 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/290/#laws.6.22.0">1989 c 290 art 6 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.87">
        <h1 class="shn">609.87 COMPUTER CRIME; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.87">609.87</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.891"> 609.891</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.8912">609.8912</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.8913">609.8913</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Access.</span></h2>
          <p>"Access" means to instruct, communicate with, store data in, or retrieve data from a computer, computer system, or computer network.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Authorization.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Authorization" means:</p>
          <p>(1) with the permission of the owner of the computer, computer system, computer network, computer software, or other property;</p>
          <p>(2) access by employees of the Department of Commerce acting under the authority and powers granted to the director of the Weights and Measures Division in chapter 239 at any time the device is commercially available for use;</p>
          <p>(3) access by registrants in the voluntary placing in service program and registered liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) meter inspectors acting under the authority and powers granted in Minnesota Rules, chapter 7601, but only at times specified by the device owner or operator or the device owner's or operator's designated representative; or</p>
          <p>(4) access by other people who have the express permission of the device owner or operator or the device owner's or operator's designated representative but only at times as approved by the device owner or operator and only for purposes approved by the device owner or operator.</p>
          <p>(b) Authorization may be limited by the owner by:</p>
          <p>(1) giving the user actual notice orally or in writing;</p>
          <p>(2) posting a written notice in a prominent location adjacent to the computer being used; or</p>
          <p>(3) using a notice displayed on or announced by the computer being used.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Computer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Computer" means an electronic device which performs logical, arithmetic or memory functions by the manipulations of signals, including but not limited to electronic or magnetic impulses.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Computer system.</span></h2>
          <p>"Computer system" means related, connected or unconnected, computers and peripheral equipment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Computer network.</span></h2>
          <p>"Computer network" means the interconnection of a communication system with a computer through a remote terminal, or with two or more interconnected computers or computer systems, and includes private and public telecommunications networks.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Property.</span></h2>
          <p>"Property" includes, but is not limited to, electronically processed or produced data and information contained in a computer or computer software in either machine or human readable form.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Services.</span></h2>
          <p>"Services" includes but is not limited to, computer time, data processing, and storage functions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Computer program.</span></h2>
          <p>"Computer program" means an instruction or statement or a series of instructions or statements, in a form acceptable to a computer, which directs the functioning of a computer system in a manner designed to provide appropriate products from the computer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Computer software.</span></h2>
          <p>"Computer software" means a computer program or procedures, or associated documentation concerned with the operation of a computer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Loss.</span></h2>
          <p>"Loss" means the greatest of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the retail market value of the property or services involved;</p>
          <p>(2) the reasonable repair or replacement cost, whichever is less; or</p>
          <p>(3) the reasonable value of the damage created by the unavailability or lack of utility of the property or services involved until repair or replacement can be effected.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Computer security system.</span></h2>
          <p>"Computer security system" means a software program or computer device that is intended to protect the confidentiality and secrecy of data and information stored in or accessible through the computer system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Destructive computer program.</span></h2>
          <p>"Destructive computer program" means a computer program that performs a destructive function or produces a destructive product. A program performs a destructive function if it degrades performance of the affected computer, associated peripherals or a computer program; disables the computer, associated peripherals or a computer program; or destroys or alters computer programs or data. A program produces a destructive product if it produces unauthorized data, including data that make computer memory space unavailable; results in the unauthorized alteration of data or computer programs; or produces a destructive computer program, including a self-replicating computer program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Encryption.</span></h2>
          <p>"Encryption" means any protective or disruptive measure, including but not limited to, cryptography, enciphering, or encoding that:</p>
          <p>(1) causes or makes any data, information, image, program, signal, or sound unintelligible or unusable; or</p>
          <p>(2) prevents, impedes, delays, or disrupts access to any data, information, image, program, signal, or sound.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Personal data.</span></h2>
          <p>"Personal data" means any computer property or computer program which contains records of the employment, salary, credit, or other financial or personal information relating to another person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Electronic terminal.</span></h2>
          <p>"Electronic terminal" means an electronic device, other than a telephone operated by a consumer, through which an individual or company may initiate an electronic fund transfer. The term includes, but is not limited to, point-of-sale terminals, automated teller machines, cash dispensing machines, and gas pump dispensers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Access device.</span></h2>
          <p>"Access device" means a card that is used by an individual or company to initiate transactions and is:</p>
          <p>(1) a means of access to an individual's or company's account;</p>
          <p>(2) issued on a prepaid basis to the individual or company in a specific amount; or</p>
          <p>(3) used by the individual or company to access government benefits.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.87.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Electronic data.</span></h2>
          <p>"Electronic data" means records or information in digital form on a computer, computer network, computer system, or in computer software that can be stored, transmitted, or processed.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.87.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/534/#laws.0.1.0">1982 c 534 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/95/#laws.0.2.0">1989 c 95 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/159/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 159 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/494/#laws.0.3.0">1990 c 494 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.50.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.30.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 30</a>-33; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/123/#laws.0.1.0">2018 c 123 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.5.47.0">2023 c 52 art 5 s 47</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.88">
        <h1 class="shn">609.88 COMPUTER DAMAGE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.88.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of computer damage and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2:</p>
          <p>(a) intentionally and without authorization damages or destroys any computer, computer system, computer network, computer software, or any other property specifically defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.87#stat.609.87.6">609.87, subdivision 6</a>;</p>
          <p>(b) intentionally and without authorization or with intent to injure or defraud alters any computer, computer system, computer network, computer software, or any other property specifically defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.87#stat.609.87.6">609.87, subdivision 6</a>; or</p>
          <p>(c) distributes a destructive computer program, without authorization and with intent to damage or destroy any computer, computer system, computer network, computer software, or any other property specifically defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.87#stat.609.87.6">609.87, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.88.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever commits computer damage may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(a) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both, if the damage, destruction or alteration results in a loss in excess of $2,500, to the owner, or the owner's agent, or lessee;</p>
          <p>(b) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the damage, destruction or alteration results in a loss of more than $500, but not more than $2,500 to the owner, or the owner's agent or lessee; or</p>
          <p>(c) in all other cases to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.88.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/534/#laws.0.2.0">1982 c 534 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/159/#laws.0.2.0">1989 c 159 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.51.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.89">
        <h1 class="shn">609.89 COMPUTER OR ELECTRONIC DATA THEFT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.89.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acts.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever does any of the following is guilty of computer or electronic data theft and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally and without authorization or claim of right accesses or causes to be accessed any computer, computer system, computer network or any part thereof for the purpose of obtaining services or property;</p>
          <p>(2) intentionally and without claim of right, and with intent to deprive the owner of use or possession, takes, transfers, conceals or retains possession of any computer, computer system, or any computer software or data contained in a computer, computer system, or computer network;</p>
          <p>(3) intentionally and without authorization or claim of right accesses or copies any computer software or electronic data and uses, alters, transfers, retains, or publishes the computer software or electronic data; or</p>
          <p>(4) intentionally retains copies of any computer software or electronic data beyond the individual's authority.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.89.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Anyone who commits computer or electronic data theft may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both, if the loss to the owner, or the owner's agent, or lessee is in excess of $2,500;</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the loss to the owner, or the owner's agent, or lessee is more than $500 but not more than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(3) in all other cases to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.89.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/534/#laws.0.3.0">1982 c 534 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.52.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.5.48.0">2023 c 52 art 5 s 48</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.891">
        <h1 class="shn">609.891 UNAUTHORIZED COMPUTER ACCESS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.891.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of unauthorized computer access if the person intentionally and without authorization attempts to or does penetrate a computer security system or electronic terminal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.891.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Felony.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who violates subdivision 1 in a manner that creates a grave risk of causing the death of a person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who is convicted of a second or subsequent gross misdemeanor violation of subdivision 1 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced under paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates subdivision 1 by accessing, or attempting to access, an electronic terminal through opening any panel or access door without authorization and placing or attaching, or attempting to place or attach, an electronic device to capture, store, or communicate access device information is guilty of a felony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.891.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who violates subdivision 1 in a manner that creates a risk to public health and safety is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 in a manner that compromises the security of data that are protected under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (8), or are not public data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.8a">13.02, subdivision 8a</a>, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced under paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) A person who violates subdivision 1 and gains access to personal data is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced under paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(d) A person who is convicted of a second or subsequent misdemeanor violation of subdivision 1 within five years is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced under paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(e) A person who violates subdivision 1 by accessing, or attempting to access, an electronic terminal through opening, or attempting to open, any panel or access door without authorization is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.891.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.891.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/95/#laws.0.4.0">1989 c 95 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.13.34.0">1993 c 326 art 13 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.34.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 34</a>,35; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/123/#laws.0.4.0">2018 c 123 s 4</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.95.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 95</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.8911">
        <h1 class="shn">609.8911 REPORTING VIOLATIONS.</h1>
        <p>A person who has reason to believe that any provision of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.88">609.88</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.89">609.89</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.891">609.891</a> is being or has been violated shall report the suspected violation to the prosecuting authority in the county in which all or part of the suspected violation occurred. A person who makes a report under this section is immune from any criminal or civil liability that otherwise might result from the person's action, if the person is acting in good faith.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.8911.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.53.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 53</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.8912">
        <h1 class="shn">609.8912 CRIMINAL USE OF ENCRYPTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.8912.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever intentionally uses or attempts to use encryption to do any of the following is guilty of criminal use of encryption and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 2:</p>
          <p>(1) to commit, further, or facilitate conduct constituting a crime;</p>
          <p>(2) to conceal the commission of any crime;</p>
          <p>(3) to conceal or protect the identity of a person who has committed any crime; or</p>
          <p>(4) to prevent, impede, delay, or disrupt the normal operation or use of another's computer, computer program, or computer system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.8912.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who violates subdivision 1 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the crime referenced in subdivision 1, clause (1), (2), or (3), is a felony; or</p>
          <p>(2) the person has two or more prior convictions for an offense under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.88">609.88</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.89">609.89</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.891">609.891</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.8913">609.8913</a>, or similar laws of other states, the United States, the District of Columbia, tribal lands, and United States territories.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates subdivision 1, under circumstances not described in paragraph (a), is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.8912.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.36.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.8913">
        <h1 class="shn">609.8913 FACILITATING ACCESS TO COMPUTER SECURITY SYSTEM.</h1>
        <p>A person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the person knows or has reason to know that by facilitating access to a computer security system the person is aiding another who intends to commit a crime and in fact commits a crime. For purposes of this section, "facilitating access" includes the intentional disclosure of a computer password, identifying code, personal information number, or other confidential information about a computer security system which provides a person with the means or opportunity for the commission of a crime.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.8913.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.1.37.0">2006 c 260 art 1 s 37</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.892">
        <h1 class="shn">609.892 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this section apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/237.73">237.73</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.892">609.892</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.893">609.893</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Access device.</span></h2>
          <p>"Access device" means a card, plate, code, account number, or other means of account access that can be used, alone or in conjunction with another access device, to obtain telecommunications service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Credit card number.</span></h2>
          <p>"Credit card number" means the card number appearing on a credit card that is an identification card or plate issued to a person by a supplier of telecommunications service that permits the person to whom the card has been issued to obtain telecommunications service on credit. The term includes the number or description of the card or plate even if the card or plate itself is not produced when obtaining telecommunications service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Telecommunications device.</span></h2>
