          <p>"Telecommunications device" means an instrument, apparatus, equipment mechanism, operating procedure, or code designed or adapted for a particular use and that is intended or can be used in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.893">609.893</a>. The term includes but is not limited to computer hardware, software, programs, electronic mail system, voice mail system, identification validation system, private branch exchange, or any other means of facilitating telecommunications service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Telecommunications provider.</span></h2>
          <p>"Telecommunications provider" means a person, firm, association, or a corporation, private or municipal, owning, operating, or managing facilities used to provide telecommunications service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Telecommunications service.</span></h2>
          <p>"Telecommunications service" means a service that, in exchange for a pecuniary consideration, provides or offers to provide transmission of messages, signals, facsimiles, or other communication between persons who are physically separated from each other by telephone, telegraph, cable, wire, fiber optic cable, or the projection of energy without physical connection. This term applies when the telecommunications service originates or ends or both originates and ends in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.892.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Telephone company.</span></h2>
          <p>"Telephone company" means a telecommunications provider that provides local exchange telecommunications service.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.892.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/494/#laws.0.5.0">1990 c 494 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/199/#laws.1.86.0">1991 c 199 art 1 s 86</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.893">
        <h1 class="shn">609.893 TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION SERVICES FRAUD; CRIME DEFINED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.893.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Obtaining services by fraud.</span></h2>
          <p>A person commits telecommunications and information services fraud and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 3 if the person, with intent to evade a lawful charge, obtains telecommunications service for the person's own use by any fraudulent means.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.893.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Facilitation of telecommunications fraud.</span></h2>
          <p>A person commits a felony and may be sentenced as provided in subdivision 4 who:</p>
          <p>(1) makes available to another, or offers or advertises to make available, a telecommunications device or information in order to facilitate violation of subdivision 1 by another; or</p>
          <p>(2) makes, assembles, or possesses a telecommunications device that is designed or adapted to violate subdivision 1 or to conceal from a provider of telecommunications service or from a lawful authority, the existence or place of origin or destination of telecommunications service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.893.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Fraud.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Whoever commits telecommunications and information services fraud in violation of subdivision 1 may be sentenced as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both, if the value of the services is in excess of $2,500;</p>
          <p>(2) to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both, if the value of the services is more than $500 but not more than $2,500; or</p>
          <p>(3) in all other cases, to imprisonment for not more than 90 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000, or both.</p>
          <p>(b) Amounts involved in a violation of paragraph (a) under one scheme or course of conduct, whether from the same credit card number or several credit card numbers, may be aggregated in determining the classification of the offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.893.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Facilitation of fraud.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.893.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/494/#laws.0.6.0">1990 c 494 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.72.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 72</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.894">
        <h1 class="shn">609.894 CELLULAR TELEPHONE COUNTERFEITING; CRIMES DEFINED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.894.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this subdivision apply to this section.</p>
          <p>(a) "Cellular telephone" means a radio telecommunications device that may be used to obtain access to the public and cellular switch telephone networks and that is programmed by the manufacturer with an electronic serial number.</p>
          <p>(b) "Cellular telephone service" means all services and cellular telephone equipment and capabilities available from a provider to an end user for a fee.</p>
          <p>(c) "Cloned cellular telephone" or "counterfeit cellular telephone" means a cellular telephone, the electronic serial number of which has been altered by someone other than the manufacturer.</p>
          <p>(d) "Telephone cloning paraphernalia" means materials that, when possessed in combination, are capable of creating a cloned cellular telephone. Telephone cloning paraphernalia includes, but is not limited to:</p>
          <p>(1) scanners to intercept electronic serial numbers and mobile identification numbers;</p>
          <p>(2) cellular telephones;</p>
          <p>(3) cables;</p>
          <p>(4) EPROM chips;</p>
          <p>(5) EPROM burners;</p>
          <p>(6) software for programming the cellular telephone with a false electronic serial number, mobile identification number, other identifiable data, or a combination of those items;</p>
          <p>(7) computers containing software described in clause (6); and</p>
          <p>(8) lists of electronic serial number and mobile identification number combinations.</p>
          <p>(e) "Electronic serial number" means a unique number that is programmed into a cellular telephone by the manufacturer, transmitted by the cellular telephone, and used by cellular telephone providers to validate radio transmissions to the system as having been made by an authorized device.</p>
          <p>(f) "End user" is a person who pays a fee to subscribe to cellular telephone service from a provider or a person receiving a call from or sending a call to the person paying or subscribing for cellular telephone service.</p>
          <p>(g) "Intercept" means to electronically capture, record, reveal, or otherwise access the signals emitted or received during the operation of a cellular telephone by any instrument, device, or equipment without the consent of the sender or receiver.</p>
          <p>(h) "Mobile identification number" means the cellular telephone number assigned to the cellular telephone by the cellular telephone provider.</p>
          <p>(i) "Provider" means a licensed seller of cellular telephone service or a reselling agent authorized by a licensed seller.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.894.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Cellular counterfeiting in the third degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person commits the crime of cellular counterfeiting in the third degree if the person knowingly possesses a cloned cellular telephone and knows that the telephone is unlawfully cloned.</p>
          <p>(b) Cellular counterfeiting in the third degree is a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.894.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Cellular counterfeiting in the second degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person commits the crime of cellular counterfeiting in the second degree if the person knowingly possesses, and knows the unlawful nature of using, any telephone cloning paraphernalia or any instrument capable of intercepting or manipulating electronic serial numbers, mobile identification numbers, other identifiable data, or a combination of those items.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates paragraph (a) may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years and may be fined up to $7,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.894.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Cellular counterfeiting in the first degree.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person commits the crime of cellular counterfeiting in the first degree if the person knowingly possesses or distributes, and knows the unlawful nature of using, any telephone cloning paraphernalia or any instrument capable of intercepting or manipulating electronic serial numbers, mobile identification numbers, other identifiable data, or a combination of those items, and agrees with, encourages, solicits, or permits one or more other persons to engage in or cause, or obtain cellular telephone service through, cellular counterfeiting.</p>
          <p>(b) A person who violates paragraph (a) may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years and may be fined up to $10,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.894.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exclusions.</span></h2>
          <p>The provisions of subdivisions 2 to 4 do not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) officers, employees, or agents of cellular telephone service providers who engage in conduct prohibited by this section for the purpose of constructing, maintaining, or conducting the radio telecommunication service or for law enforcement purposes;</p>
          <p>(2) law enforcement officers and public officials in charge of jails, police premises, sheriffs' offices, Department of Corrections institutions, and other penal or correctional institutions, or any other person under the color of law, who engages in conduct prohibited by this section for the purpose of law enforcement or in the normal course of the officer's or official's employment activities or duties; and</p>
          <p>(3) officers, employees, or agents of federal or state agencies that are authorized to monitor or intercept cellular telephone service in the normal course of the officer's, employee's, or agent's employment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.894.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Civil liability.</span></h2>
          <p>A prosecution under this section does not preclude civil liability under any applicable provision of law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.894.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/331/#laws.0.2.0">1996 c 331 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.895">
        <h1 class="shn">609.895 COUNTERFEITED INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.895.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(b) "Counterfeit mark" means:</p>
          <p>(1) any unauthorized reproduction or copy of intellectual property; or</p>
          <p>(2) intellectual property affixed to any item without the authority of the owner of the intellectual property.</p>
          <p>(c) "Counterfeited item or service" means an item or service bearing or identified by a counterfeit mark.</p>
          <p>(d) "Intellectual property" means any trademark, service mark, or trade name.</p>
          <p>(e) "Retail value" means:</p>
          <p>(1) the usual selling price of the article or service bearing or identified by the counterfeit mark; or</p>
          <p>(2) the usual selling price of a finished product on or in which components bearing or identified by a counterfeit mark are used.</p>
          <p>(f) "Service mark" means a mark used by a person to identify services and to distinguish them from the services of others.</p>
          <p>(g) "Trademark" means a mark used by a person to identify goods and to distinguish them from the goods of others.</p>
          <p>(h) "Trade name" means a word, name, symbol, device, or any combination of the foregoing in any form or arrangement, used by a person to identify the person's business, vocation, or occupation and to distinguish it from the business, vocation, or occupation of others.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.895.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally manufactures, produces, distributes, offers for sale, sells, or possesses with intent to sell or distribute any counterfeited item or service, knowing or having reason to know that the item or service is counterfeit, is guilty of counterfeiting intellectual property and may be punished as provided in subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.895.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who is convicted of violating subdivision 2 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $100,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the violation involves the manufacture or production of a counterfeited item or items;</p>
          <p>(2) the violation involves the distribution, offer for sale, sale, or possession with intent to sell or distribute 1,000 or more counterfeited items;</p>
          <p>(3) the violation involves the distribution, offer for sale, sale, or possession with intent to sell or distribute counterfeited items or services having a retail value of more than $10,000; or</p>
          <p>(4) the defendant has two or more prior convictions for violating this section or a law of another state or the United States that provides criminal penalties for counterfeiting intellectual property.</p>
          <p>(b) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (a), a person who is convicted of violating subdivision 2 may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of not more than $50,000, or both, if:</p>
          <p>(1) the violation involves more than 100 but fewer than 1,000 counterfeited items;</p>
          <p>(2) the violation involves counterfeited items or services having a retail value of more than $1,000 but not more than $10,000; or</p>
          <p>(3) the defendant has one prior conviction for violating this section or a law of another state or the United States that provides criminal penalties for counterfeiting intellectual property.</p>
          <p>(c) A person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 364 days or to payment of a fine of not more than $3,000, or both, if the person is convicted of violating subdivision 2, under circumstances not described in paragraph (a) or (b).</p>
          <p>(d) If the defendant distributes, sells, offers for sale, or possesses with intent to sell or distribute more than one item or service bearing or identified by more than one counterfeit mark, the quantity or retail value of these items and services may be aggregated for purposes of determining penalties under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.895.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Alternative fine.</span></h2>
          <p>In lieu of the fine authorized by subdivision 3, a person convicted of violating this section who received economic gain from the act or caused economic loss during the act may be sentenced to pay a fine calculated in the manner provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.904#stat.609.904.2">609.904, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.895.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>Property used to commit or facilitate the commission of a violation of this section, and all money and property representing proceeds of a violation of this section, shall be forfeited in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.531">609.531</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5316">609.5316</a>. Notwithstanding any provision of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315">609.5315</a> to the contrary, forfeited items bearing or identified by a counterfeit mark must be destroyed unless the intellectual property owner consents to another disposition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.895.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Prima facie evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>A Minnesota or federal certificate of registration of an intellectual property is prima facie evidence of the registrant's ownership and exclusive right to use the intellectual property in connection with the goods or services described in the certificate.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.895.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/142/#laws.0.2.0">1999 c 142 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.896">
        <h1 class="shn">609.896 CRIMINAL USE OF REAL PROPERTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.896.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(b) "Audiovisual recording function" means the capability of a device to record or transmit a motion picture or any part of a motion picture by means of any technology now known or later developed.</p>
          <p>(c) "Convicted" includes a conviction for a similar offense under the law of another state or the federal government.</p>
          <p>(d) "Motion picture theater" means a movie theater, screening room, or other venue when used primarily for the exhibition of a motion picture.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.896.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any person in a motion picture theater while a motion picture is being exhibited who knowingly operates an audiovisual recording function of a device without the consent of the owner or lessee of the motion picture theater is guilty of criminal use of real property.</p>
          <p>(b) If a person is convicted of a first offense, it is a misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(c) If a person is convicted of a second offense, it is a gross misdemeanor.</p>
          <p>(d) If a person is convicted of a third or subsequent offense, it is a felony and the person may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.896.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Detaining suspects.</span></h2>
          <p>An owner or lessee of a motion picture theater is a merchant for purposes of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.366">629.366</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.896.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Exception.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not prevent any lawfully authorized investigative, law enforcement protective, or intelligence-gathering employee or agent of the state or federal government from operating any audiovisual recording device in a motion picture theater where a motion picture is being exhibited, as part of lawfully authorized investigative, law enforcement protective, or intelligence gathering activities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.896.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Not preclude alternative prosecution.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in this section prevents prosecution under any other provision of law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.896.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/136/#laws.17.51.0">2005 c 136 art 17 s 51</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">RACKETEER INFLUENCED AND CORRUPT ORGANIZATIONS (RICO)</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.901">
        <h1 class="shn">609.901 CONSTRUCTION OF RACKETEERING PROVISIONS.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.902">609.902</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.912">609.912</a> shall be liberally construed to achieve their remedial purposes of curtailing racketeering activity and controlled substance crime and lessening their economic and political power in Minnesota.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.901.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.5.0">1989 c 286 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.902">
        <h1 class="shn">609.902 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.901">609.901</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.912">609.912</a>, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Criminal proceeding.</span></h2>
          <p>"Criminal proceeding" means a criminal proceeding begun under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Enterprise.</span></h2>
          <p>"Enterprise" means a sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, trust, or other legal entity, or a union, governmental entity, association, or group of persons, associated in fact although not a legal entity, and includes illicit as well as legitimate enterprises.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Criminal act.</span></h2>
          <p>"Criminal act" means conduct constituting, or a conspiracy or attempt to commit, a felony violation of chapter 152, or a felony violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/297D.09">297D.09</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299F.79">299F.79</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299F.80">299F.80</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299F.82">299F.82</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.185">609.185</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.19">609.19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.195">609.195</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.20">609.20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.205">609.205</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.221">609.221</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.222">609.222</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.223">609.223</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2231">609.2231</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.228">609.228</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.235">609.235</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.245">609.245</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.25">609.25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.27">609.27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.322">609.322</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342">609.342</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343">609.343</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344">609.344</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345">609.345</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.42">609.42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.48">609.48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.485">609.485</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.495">609.495</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.496">609.496</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.497">609.497</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.498">609.498</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, if the offense is punishable under subdivision 3, clause (1), if the property is a firearm, clause (3)(b), or clause (3)(d)(v); section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (1) or (4); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.527">609.527</a>, if the crime is punishable under subdivision 3, clause (4); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.528">609.528</a>, if the crime is punishable under subdivision 3, clause (4); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.53">609.53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.561">609.561</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.562">609.562</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.582#stat.609.582.1">609.582, subdivision 1</a> or 2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.668#stat.609.668.6">609.668, subdivision 6</a>, paragraph (a); <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.67">609.67</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.687">609.687</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.713">609.713</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.86">609.86</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.894#stat.609.894.3">609.894, subdivision 3</a> or 4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.895">609.895</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.713">624.713</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.7191">624.7191</a>; or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626A.02#stat.626A.02.1">626A.02, subdivision 1</a>, if the offense is punishable under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626A.02#stat.626A.02.4">626A.02, subdivision 4</a>, paragraph (a). "Criminal act" also includes conduct constituting, or a conspiracy or attempt to commit, a felony violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.52#stat.609.52.2">609.52, subdivision 2</a>, clause (3), (4), (15), or (16), if the violation involves an insurance company as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.02#stat.60A.02.4">60A.02, subdivision 4</a>, a nonprofit health service plan corporation regulated under chapter 62C, a health maintenance organization regulated under chapter 62D, or a fraternal benefit society regulated under chapter 64B.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Participation in a pattern of criminal activity.</span></h2>
          <p>A person "participates in a pattern of criminal activity" when the person is a principal with respect to conduct constituting at least three of the criminal acts included in the pattern and two of the acts constitute felonies other than conspiracy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Pattern of criminal activity.</span></h2>
          <p>"Pattern of criminal activity" means conduct constituting three or more criminal acts that:</p>
          <p>(1) were committed within ten years of the commencement of the criminal proceeding;</p>
          <p>(2) are neither isolated incidents, nor so closely related and connected in point of time or circumstance of commission as to constitute a single criminal offense; and</p>
          <p>(3) were either: (i) related to one another through a common scheme or plan or a shared criminal purpose or (ii) committed, solicited, requested, importuned, or intentionally aided by persons acting with the mental culpability required for the commission of the criminal acts and associated with or in an enterprise involved in those activities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Personal property.</span></h2>
          <p>"Personal property" includes personal property, an interest in personal property, or a right, including a bank account, debt, corporate stock, patent, or copyright. Personal property and a beneficial interest in personal property are deemed to be located where the trustee is, the personal property is, or the instrument evidencing the right is.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Principal.</span></h2>
          <p>"Principal" means a person who personally engages in conduct constituting a violation or who is criminally liable under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.05">609.05</a> for the conduct of another constituting a violation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Prosecuting authority.</span></h2>
          <p>"Prosecuting authority" means the office of a county attorney or office of the attorney general.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.902.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Real property.</span></h2>
          <p>"Real property" means any real property or an interest in real property, including a lease of, or mortgage on, real property. A beneficial interest in real property is deemed to be located where the real property is located.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.902.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.6.0">1989 c 286 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.17.1.0">1991 c 325 art 17 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/564/#laws.1.54.0">1992 c 564 art 1 s 54</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/326/#laws.5.11.0">1993 c 326 art 5 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.5.16.0">1994 c 636 art 5 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/239/#laws.3.20.0">1997 c 239 art 3 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/367/#laws.2.32.0">1998 c 367 art 2 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/142/#laws.0.3.0">1999 c 142 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/244/#laws.0.4.0">1999 c 244 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/354/#laws.0.6.0">2000 c 354 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/76/#laws.1.68.0">2011 c 76 art 1 s 68</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/81/#laws.0.1.0">2011 c 81 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.96.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 96</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.903">
        <h1 class="shn">609.903 RACKETEERING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.903.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Crime.</span></h2>
          <p>A person is guilty of racketeering if the person:</p>
          <p>(1) is employed by or associated with an enterprise and intentionally conducts or participates in the affairs of the enterprise by participating in a pattern of criminal activity;</p>
          <p>(2) acquires or maintains an interest in or control of an enterprise, or an interest in real property, by participating in a pattern of criminal activity; or</p>
          <p>(3) participates in a pattern of criminal activity and knowingly invests any proceeds derived from that conduct, or any proceeds derived from the investment or use of those proceeds, in an enterprise or in real property.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.903.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Permitted activities.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, it is not unlawful to:</p>
          <p>(1) purchase securities on the open market with intent to make an investment, and without the intent of controlling or participating in the control of the issuer, or of assisting another to do so, if the securities of the issuer held by the purchaser, the members of the purchaser's immediate family, and the purchaser's accomplices in a pattern of criminal activity do not amount in the aggregate to five percent of the outstanding securities of any one class and do not confer, either in the law or in fact, the power to elect one or more directors of the issuer;</p>
          <p>(2) make a deposit in an account maintained in a savings association, or a deposit in any other financial institution, that creates an ownership interest in that association or institution; or</p>
          <p>(3) purchase nonvoting shares in a limited partnership, with intent to make an investment, and without the intent of controlling or participating in the control of the partnership.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.903.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.7.0">1989 c 286 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/202/#laws.1.25.0">1995 c 202 art 1 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.904">
        <h1 class="shn">609.904 CRIMINAL PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.904.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than 20 years or to payment of a fine of not more than $1,000,000, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.904.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fine.</span></h2>
          <p>In lieu of the fine authorized by subdivision 1, a person convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>, who received economic gain from the act or caused economic loss or personal injury during the act, may be sentenced to pay a fine calculated under this subdivision. The maximum fine is three times the gross value gained or three times the gross loss caused, whichever is greater, plus court costs and the costs of investigation and prosecution reasonably incurred, less the value of any property forfeited under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a>. The district court shall hold a hearing to determine the amount of the fine authorized by this subdivision. In imposing a fine, the court shall consider the seriousness of the conduct, whether the amount of the fine is disproportionate to the conduct in which the person engaged, its impact on victims and any legitimate enterprise involved in that conduct, as well as the economic circumstances of the convicted person, including the effect of the imposition of the fine on the person's immediate family. For purposes of this subdivision, loss does not include pain and suffering.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.904.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Injunctive relief.</span></h2>
          <p>After the entry of a judgment that includes a fine or an order of criminal forfeiture under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a>, the district court may enter a restraining order or injunction, require the execution of a satisfactory performance bond, or take other action, including the appointment of a receiver, that the court deems proper to protect the interests of the prosecuting authority in collecting the money or forfeiture or an innocent party.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.904.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Disposition of fine proceeds.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall apply fines collected under this section to the costs and expenses of investigation and prosecution, including costs of resources and personnel incurred in investigation and prosecution and the balance, if any, as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/574.34">574.34</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.904.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>In a settlement discussion or before the imposition of a sentence under this section, the prosecuting authority shall vigorously advocate full and complete restitution to an aggrieved person. Before the acceptance of a plea or after a verdict but before the imposition of a sentence under this section, the district court must ensure that full and complete restitution has been duly effected or that a satisfactory explanation of why it is impractical has been made to the court.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.904.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.8.0">1989 c 286 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.905">
        <h1 class="shn">609.905 CRIMINAL FORFEITURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.905.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Forfeiture.</span></h2>
          <p>When a person is convicted of violating section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>, the court may order the person to forfeit to the prosecuting authority any real or personal property subject to forfeiture under this section. Property subject to forfeiture is real and personal property that was used in the course of, intended for use in the course of, derived from, or realized through conduct in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>. A court may not order the forfeiture of property that has been used to pay reasonable attorney fees in connection with a criminal proceeding under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>. The term includes property constituting an interest in or means of control or influence over the enterprise involved in the violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.902">609.902</a> and any property constituting proceeds derived from the violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.902">609.902</a>, including:</p>
          <p>(1) a position, office, appointment, tenure, commission, or employment contract that was acquired or maintained in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> or through which the person conducted or participated in the conduct of the affairs of an enterprise in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> or that afforded the person a source of influence or control over the affairs of an enterprise that the person exercised in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) any compensation, right, or benefit derived from a position, office, appointment, tenure, commission, or employment contract described in this section that accrued to the person during the period of conduct in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) any interest in, security of, claim against, or property or contractual right affording the person a source of influence or control over the affairs of an enterprise that the person exercised in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) any amount payable or paid under any contract for goods or services that was awarded or performed in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.905.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Other property of defendant.</span></h2>
          <p>The district court may order criminal forfeiture of any other property of the defendant up to the value of the property that is unreachable if any property subject to criminal forfeiture under subdivision 1:</p>
          <p>(1) cannot be located;</p>
          <p>(2) has been sold to a bona fide purchaser for value;</p>
          <p>(3) has been placed beyond the jurisdiction of the court;</p>
          <p>(4) has been substantially diminished in value by the conduct of the defendant;</p>
          <p>(5) has been commingled with other property that cannot be divided without difficulty or undue injury to innocent persons; or</p>
          <p>(6) is otherwise unreachable without undue injury to an innocent person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.905.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecuting authority shall report on forfeitures occurring under this section as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315">609.5315</a>, subdivision 6.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.905.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.9.0">1989 c 286 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/391/#laws.0.20.0">2010 c 391 s 20</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.907">
        <h1 class="shn">609.907 PRESERVATION OF PROPERTY SUBJECT TO FORFEITURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.907.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Temporary restraining order.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) When an indictment or complaint is filed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>, the district court may take any of the following actions if the prosecuting authority shows by a preponderance of the evidence that the action is necessary to preserve the reachability of property subject to criminal forfeiture:</p>
          <p>(1) enter a restraining order or injunction;</p>
          <p>(2) require the execution of a satisfactory performance bond; or</p>
          <p>(3) take any other reasonable action, including the appointment of a receiver.</p>
          <p>(b) Before granting the remedies provided by this subdivision, the court shall hold a hearing, after notice to all affected persons, giving them a reasonable opportunity to respond. At the hearing, the rules of evidence do not apply.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.907.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Preindictment order.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If no indictment or complaint has been filed, the district court may take actions provided in subdivision 1 if the prosecuting authority makes the showing required by subdivision 1 and also shows that:</p>
          <p>(1) there is probable cause to believe that the property with respect to which the order is sought would, in the event of a conviction, be subject to criminal forfeiture under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.904">609.904</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) the requested order would not result in substantial and irreparable harm or injury to the party against whom the order is to be entered, or to other affected persons, that outweighs the need to preserve the reachability of the property.</p>
          <p>(b) An order entered under this subdivision is effective for a maximum of 90 days unless:</p>
          <p>(1) extended by the district court for good cause; or</p>
          <p>(2) terminated by the filing of an indictment or complaint alleging that the property is subject to forfeiture.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.907.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Restraining order without notice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) On application by the prosecuting authority, the district court may grant, without notice to any party, a temporary restraining order to preserve the reachability of property subject to criminal forfeiture under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a> if:</p>
          <p>(1) an indictment or complaint alleging that property is subject to criminal forfeiture has been filed or the district court determines that there is probable cause to believe that property with respect to which the order is sought would, in the event of a conviction, be subject to criminal forfeiture under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) the property is in the possession or control of the party against whom the order is to be entered; and</p>
          <p>(3) the district court makes a specific finding in writing that the property can be concealed, disposed of, or placed beyond the jurisdiction of the court before any party may be heard in opposition.</p>
          <p>(b) A temporary restraining order granted without notice to any party under this subdivision expires within the time fixed by the court, not to exceed ten days. The court may extend the order for good cause shown, or if the party against whom it is entered consents to an extension. After a temporary restraining order is granted under this subdivision, a hearing concerning the entry of an order under this section shall be held at the earliest practicable time and before the temporary order expires.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.907.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.10.0">1989 c 286 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.908">
        <h1 class="shn">609.908 DISPOSITION OF FORFEITURE PROCEEDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.908.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Disposition alternatives.</span></h2>
          <p>After making due provisions for the rights of innocent persons, the prosecuting authority shall, as soon as feasible, dispose of all property ordered forfeited under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a> by:</p>
          <p>(1) public sale;</p>
          <p>(2) transfer to a state governmental agency for official use;</p>
          <p>(3) sale or transfer to an innocent person; or</p>
          <p>(4) destruction, if the property is not needed for evidence in a pending criminal or civil proceeding.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.908.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">No reversion to defendant.</span></h2>
          <p>An interest in personal or real property not exercisable by or transferable for value by the prosecuting authority expires and does not revert to the defendant. Forfeited property may not be purchased by the defendant, relative of the defendant, or any person acting in concert with the defendant or on the defendant's behalf.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.908.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sale proceeds.</span></h2>
          <p>The proceeds of a sale or other disposition of forfeited property under this section whether by final judgment, settlement, or otherwise, must be applied as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to the fees and costs of the forfeiture and sale including expenses of seizure, maintenance, and custody of the property pending its disposition, advertising, and court costs;</p>
          <p>(2) to all costs and expenses of investigation and prosecution including costs of resources and personnel incurred in investigation and prosecution; and</p>
          <p>(3) the balance to the appropriate agencies under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.5315#stat.609.5315.5">609.5315, subdivision 5</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.908.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.11.0">1989 c 286 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.909">
        <h1 class="shn">609.909 ADDITIONAL RELIEF AVAILABLE.</h1>
        <p>With respect to property ordered forfeited, fine imposed, or civil penalty imposed in a criminal proceeding under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> or civil proceeding under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.911">609.911</a>, the district court may, on petition of the prosecuting authority or any other person within 60 days of a final order:</p>
        <p>(1) authorize the compromise of claims;</p>
        <p>(2) award compensation to persons providing information that results in a forfeiture under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a>;</p>
        <p>(3) grant petitions for mitigation or remission of forfeiture or fines;</p>
        <p>(4) restore forfeited property or imposed fines to victims of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>; and</p>
        <p>(5) take any other action to protect the rights of innocent persons that is in the interest of justice and is consistent with the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.901">609.901</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.912">609.912</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.909.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.12.0">1989 c 286 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.910">
        <h1 class="shn">609.910 RELATION TO OTHER SANCTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.910.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Remedy not exclusive.</span></h2>
          <p>Except as provided in this section, a criminal penalty, forfeiture, or fine imposed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.904">609.904</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.905">609.905</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.911">609.911</a> does not preclude the application of any other criminal penalty or civil remedy for the separate criminal acts. A prosecuting authority may not file a civil action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.911">609.911</a> if any prosecuting authority has filed a previous criminal proceeding under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> against the same person based on the same criminal conduct and the charges were dismissed after jeopardy attached or the person acquitted.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.910.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Restitution.</span></h2>
          <p>A restitution payment to a victim under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.904">609.904</a> does not limit the liability for damages in a civil action or proceeding for an amount greater than the restitution payment.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.910.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.13.0">1989 c 286 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.911">
        <h1 class="shn">609.911 CIVIL REMEDIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.911.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Relief available.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecuting authority may institute civil proceedings in district court against a person seeking relief from conduct constituting a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> or to prevent or restrain future violations. If the prosecuting authority proves the alleged violation by a preponderance of the evidence, and the court has made due provision for the rights of innocent persons, the court may:</p>
          <p>(1) order a defendant to divest an interest in an enterprise or in real property;</p>
          <p>(2) impose reasonable restrictions on the future activities or investments of a defendant, including prohibiting a defendant from engaging in the same type of endeavor as the enterprise in which the defendant was engaged in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) order the dissolution or reorganization of an enterprise;</p>
          <p>(4) order the suspension or revocation of a license, permit, or prior approval granted to an enterprise by a state agency; or</p>
          <p>(5) order the surrender of the charter of a corporation organized under Minnesota law, dissolution of an enterprise, or the revocation of a certificate authorizing a foreign corporation to conduct business in Minnesota, if the court finds that:</p>
          <p>(i) the board of directors or a managerial agent acting on behalf of the corporation, in conducting the affairs of the corporation, authorized or engaged in conduct prohibited by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>; and</p>
          <p>(ii) the public interest in preventing future criminal conduct requires the action.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.911.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Injunctive relief.</span></h2>
          <p>In a proceeding under this section, the court may grant injunctive relief.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.911.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Civil penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>The prosecuting authority may institute proceedings against an enterprise or an individual to recover a civil penalty. The penalty may be imposed in the discretion of the district court for conduct constituting a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>. The civil penalty may not exceed $1,000,000 less a fine imposed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a>. Penalties collected under this section must be applied to the costs and expenses of investigation and prosecution, including costs of resources and personnel incurred in investigation and prosecution, and the balance, if any, to the state general fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.911.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Attorney fees.</span></h2>
          <p>If the district court issues an injunction, or grants other relief under this section, or the prosecuting authority otherwise substantially prevails, the prosecuting authority shall also recover reasonable attorney fees in the trial and appellate courts and costs of investigation and litigation reasonably incurred.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.609.911.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Personal jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>Personal service of process in a proceeding under this section may be made on any person outside of Minnesota if the person was a principal in any conduct constituting a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.903">609.903</a> in this state. The person is deemed to have submitted to the jurisdiction of the courts of this state for the purposes of this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.911.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.14.0">1989 c 286 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.609.912">
        <h1 class="shn">609.912 NOTICE TO OTHER PROSECUTING AUTHORITIES.</h1>
        <p>When a county attorney begins an investigation involving sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.901">609.901</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.911">609.911</a>, the county attorney shall notify the attorney general. When the attorney general begins an investigation involving sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.901">609.901</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.911">609.911</a>, the attorney general shall notify the county attorney of each county in which a substantial part of the investigation is likely to be conducted.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.609.912.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/286/#laws.0.15.0">1989 c 286 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
